air:驼峰航线（北线）.note: After the Burma Road was cut, the only route for the Chinese and US airlift of supplies; flying from Dinjan and other airfields in Assam over peaks of the Hengduan Mountains higher than 4,500 metres, it carried about 650,000 tonnes in three years, at the cost of more than 600 aircraft.

air:驼峰航线（南线）.mod: Dinjan, Assam, India – Myitkyina – Kunming, Yunnan
air:驼峰航线（南线）.note: After the Allies took Myitkyina in August 1944, removing the threat from Japanese fighters, aircraft switched to the lower southern route and the tonnage carried rose sharply.

battle:“伤心岭”之战.cmd: Young vs. Korean People's Army and CPV 68th Army
battle:“伤心岭”之战.note: “Heartbreak Ridge” is the American name. On this ridge north of Bloody Ridge the US 2nd Division and the attached French Battalion fought hard for a month; from October they sent tanks up the Mundung-ni valley to break into the flank and rear, disrupting the CPV 68th Army's relief of the Korean People's Army, and took the ridge on the 15th. After this the eastern front became largely fixed, and both sides turned to positional warfare.
battle:“伤心岭”之战.sides: US and French forces defeated Korean People's Army and Chinese People's Volunteers

battle:“血岭”之战.note: “Bloody Ridge” is the American name; for the Chinese and Korean side it was part of the summer and autumn defensive operations. During the armistice talks, to improve their positions on the eastern front, the “UN Command” forces used the US 2nd Division, with the attached 36th Regiment of the ROK 5th Division, to fight again and again for three hilltops north of Yanggu, suffering about 2,700 casualties; the Korean People's Army also suffered heavily and fell back to “Heartbreak Ridge” to the north.
battle:“血岭”之战.sides: US and ROK forces defeated Korean People's Army

battle:一·二八淞沪抗战.cmd: Jiang Guangnai, Cai Tingkai and Zhang Zhizhong vs. Shiozawa Kōichi, Ueda Kenkichi and Shirakawa Yoshinori
battle:一·二八淞沪抗战.note: Japanese forces attacked Shanghai; the 19th Route Army and the Fifth Army rose to resist, fighting the Japanese hard for more than a month at Zhabei, Wusong and Miaohang, and the Japanese side changed its commander three times. In early March Japanese forces landed at Liuhe, the Chinese forces withdrew to the Jiading–Huangdu line, and in May the Nationalist Government signed the Songhu Ceasefire Agreement.

battle:一二军之战.cmd: Xiong Kewu, Dan Maoxin and Liu Chengxun vs. Yang Sen
battle:一二军之战.note: After Liu Xiang stepped down, the Sichuan Army's First Army (Xiong Kewu's faction) and Third Army (Liu Chengxun) jointly attacked Yang Sen, acting commander of the Second Army; the Second Army was defeated in Sichuan, and Yang Sen abandoned Chongqing and went east to Yichang to join Wu Peifu. The Sichuan self-government alliance broke apart, and Wu Peifu used the opportunity to meddle in Sichuan affairs.
battle:一二军之战.old: War of the First and Second Armies
battle:一二军之战.sides: First and Third Armies defeated Second Army

battle:一渡赤水.cmd: Mao Zedong and Zhu De vs. Liu Xiang
battle:一渡赤水.note: After the setback at Tucheng the Central Red Army built pontoon bridges around Tucheng and Yuanhou, crossed the Chishui River to the west and moved towards Gulin and Xuyong in southern Sichuan; the original plan to cross the Yangtze northward was abandoned because of blocking by the Sichuan Army, and the army turned towards Zhaxi.
battle:一渡赤水.old: First crossing of the Chishui River

battle:七亘村伏击战.cmd: Liu Bocheng and Chen Geng vs. Japanese 20th Division supply train
battle:七亘村伏击战.note: The 772nd Regiment of the Eighth Route Army's 129th Division twice ambushed Japanese supply columns at the same spot, exploiting the enemy's belief that “no one sets a second ambush in the same place”; it became a classic case of the repeated ambush.
battle:七亘村伏击战.sides: Eighth Route Army defeated Japanese forces

battle:万家岭大捷.note: The Japanese 106th Division thrust into the hills west of De'an and was surrounded at Wanjialing by more than ten divisions brought together by Xue Yue; it was almost completely wiped out. The victory is ranked alongside Pingxingguan and Tai'erzhuang.

battle:万山群岛战役.cmd: South China Military Region forces vs. KMT garrison of the Wanshan Islands
battle:万山群岛战役.note: Newly formed naval vessels, acting together with the army, liberated the Wanshan Islands off the mouth of the Pearl River one island at a time, lifting the blockade of Guangzhou's outlet to the sea; it is regarded as the first battle of the People's Navy.

battle:万源保卫战.cmd: Xu Xiangqian and Xu Shiyou vs. Liu Xiang (Wang Lingji and Tang Shizun)
battle:万源保卫战.note: The climax of Liu Xiang's six-route siege: 200,000 Sichuan troops stormed the line of Wanyuan and Damianshan for more than seventy days without taking it. The Red Army went over to the counter-offensive and the Sichuan-Shaanxi Soviet Area came through the danger, but its population and material resources had been heavily drained.
battle:万源保卫战.sides: Red Fourth Front Army defeated Sichuan Army

battle:三下江南、四保临江.cmd: Lin Biao and Chen Yun vs. Du Yuming
battle:三下江南、四保临江.note: The forces in southern Northeast China defended Linjiang four times, while the main force in northern Northeast China crossed south over the Songhua River three times in support, smashing Du Yuming's plan of “south first, then north”; the war in the Northeast turned from defence to offence.
battle:三下江南、四保临江.old: Three crossings south of the Songhua and four defences of Linjiang
battle:三下江南、四保临江.sides: Northeast Democratic Allied Army defeated KMT forces

battle:三渡赤水.cmd: Mao Zedong and Zhu De vs. Chiang Kai-shek (Zhou Hunyuan and Wu Qiwei)
battle:三渡赤水.note: After the failed assault at Lubanchang, the Red Army crossed the Chishui River westward for the third time at the Maotai ferry and re-entered southern Sichuan with great fanfare, luring the KMT columns to shift west.
battle:三渡赤水.old: Third crossing of the Chishui River

battle:上党战役.cmd: Liu Bocheng and Deng Xiaoping vs. Shi Zebo and Peng Yubin
battle:上党战役.note: Taking advantage of the Japanese surrender, Yan Xishan's forces invaded the Changzhi area; troops of the Shanxi-Hebei-Shandong-Henan Military Region struck back in self-defence, besieging the town and attacking the relief forces, wiping out more than 30,000 of them and capturing Shi Zebo. Fought during the Chongqing Negotiations, the campaign gave strong support to the CPC delegation at the talks.
battle:上党战役.sides: Eighth Route Army defeated Yan Xishan's forces

battle:上寮战役.cmd: Võ Nguyên Giáp and Souphanouvong vs. Salan
battle:上寮战役.note: Three divisions of the Vietnam People's Army and Pathet Lao forces advanced into Laos along several routes; in mid-April the French and Lao garrison abandoned Sam Neua and withdrew south, much of it intercepted on the way. The Vietnamese forces reached the Plain of Jars and the outskirts of Luang Prabang; the French flew in troops and built fortified camps to hold out, and the garrison of Muang Khoua held on for more than a month. Before the rainy season the Vietnamese pulled back, and Souphanouvong's resistance government remained at Sam Neua.
battle:上寮战役.sides: Vietnam People's Army and Pathet Lao defeated French and Royal Lao forces

battle:上海制造局之战.cmd: Zheng Rucheng vs. Chen Qimei and Niu Yongjian
battle:上海制造局之战.note: The Anti-Yuan Army made several night attacks on the Jiangnan Arsenal, all beaten off by Zheng Rucheng's forces and the guns of the navy's ships; the Wusong forts were lost soon afterwards. The anti-Yuan rising in Shanghai failed, and the gateway to the lower Yangtze fell into the hands of the Beiyang Army.

battle:上海工人第三次武装起义.cmd: Zhou Enlai and Zhao Shiyan vs. Bi Shucheng
battle:上海工人第三次武装起义.note: As the Northern Expedition Army neared Shanghai, the CPC led a city-wide general strike and armed uprising; after thirty hours of fierce fighting the workers took the North Station in Zhabei, drove out the Zhili-Shandong Allied Army and welcomed the Eastern Route Army into the city. Three weeks later Chiang Kai-shek launched the April 12 Counter-revolutionary Coup, and the workers' pickets were disarmed.
battle:上海工人第三次武装起义.old: Third Armed Uprising of the Shanghai Workers
battle:上海工人第三次武装起义.sides: Shanghai workers' pickets defeated Zhili-Shandong Allied Army

battle:上海战役.cmd: Chen Yi and Su Yu vs. Tang Enbo
battle:上海战役.note: The Third Field Army attacked Yuepu, Gaoqiao and Wusong first, so as to avoid shelling the urban area; Shanghai was liberated on 27 May. Tang Enbo's forces withdrew to Zhoushan and Taiwan, and the people's government took over China's largest industrial and commercial city.
battle:上海战役.sides: Third Field Army defeated KMT forces

battle:上海起义.note: Merchant militia and dare-to-die squads attacked the Jiangnan Arsenal; Chen Qimei was captured for a time, but a renewed attack the next day succeeded, and the Shanghai Military Governorate was established. The revolutionaries thus gained control of the largest arsenal in the country and of Shanghai's financial resources and press.

battle:上甘岭战役.mod: southern slopes of Mount Osong, Kimhwa County, North Korea
battle:上甘岭战役.note: The “UN Command” forces launched Operation Showdown to seize Hills 597.9 and 537.7 on the southern slopes of Mount Osong north of Gimhwa; the CPV 15th Army held out from its tunnels for 43 days. The density of artillery fire on both sides was unprecedented and both suffered heavy casualties; the positions finally remained with the CPV, and the enemy offensive was smashed.
battle:上甘岭战役.sides: Chinese People's Volunteers defeated US and ROK forces

battle:上蔡、临颍战役.cmd: Tang Shengzhi and Zhang Fakui vs. Zhang Xueliang and Han Linchun
battle:上蔡、临颍战役.note: The Wuhan Nationalist Government continued the Northern Expedition north along the Beijing–Hankou Railway; the Fourth Front Army fought bloody battles with the Fengtian Army's elite at Shangcai and Linying, suffering more than 10,000 casualties. The Fengtian Army withdrew north while Feng Yuxiang came out through Tong Pass, and the two armies joined forces at Zhengzhou in early June.
battle:上蔡、临颍战役.sides: National Revolutionary Army defeated Fengtian Army

battle:上高会战.note: Japanese forces attacked west towards Shanggao in northern Jiangxi in three columns; the 19th Army Group lured them in deep and then encircled them, mauling the 34th Division and killing a brigade commander. It was one of the most successful battles on the frontal battlefield in the middle period of the War of Resistance.

battle:东宁要塞战斗.note: The Dongning fortress complex was the Kwantung Army's largest permanent fortification on the eastern sector of the Sino-Soviet border. The Soviet 25th Army bypassed the fortresses and pushed deep; the remnants of the garrison held out in the tunnels until after Japan's surrender and laid down their arms only at the end of the month.

battle:东山岛战役.cmd: Ye Fei and You Meiyao vs. Hu Lian
battle:东山岛战役.note: KMT forces nearly 10,000 strong, supported by paratroopers, attacked Dongshan Island in southern Fujian; the island's garrison, the 80th Public Security Regiment, held Gongyunshan and other positions together with the militia, the 31st Army crossed the sea as reinforcements, and the KMT forces withdrew after losing more than 3,000 killed, wounded and captured. After this the KMT forces made no further large-scale attacks on the mainland.

battle:东征.cmd: Mao Zedong and Peng Dehuai vs. Yan Xishan and Chen Cheng
battle:东征.note: Under the name of the “Anti-Japanese Vanguard Army”, the Red First Front Army crossed the Yellow River east into Shanxi and fought its way across more than fifty counties of western and southern Shanxi, adding 8,000 men to its ranks and raising several hundred thousand in funds. After KMT Central Army reinforcements entered Shanxi it returned to northern Shaanxi; Liu Zhidan laid down his life at Sanjiao.

battle:东韶战斗.cmd: Mao Zedong and Zhu De vs. Tan Daoyuan
battle:东韶战斗.note: After the Longgang battle the Red Army pursued Tan Daoyuan's 50th Division as it withdrew east and wiped out half of it at Dongshao; the KMT columns pulled back one after another, and the first “encirclement” campaign was smashed.
battle:东韶战斗.sides: Red First Front Army defeated KMT 50th Division

battle:两淮之战.cmd: Li Yannian and Zhang Lingfu vs. Zhang Dingcheng and Su Yu
battle:两淮之战.note: KMT forces closed in along two routes, from south and north of the Huai River, occupying Huaiyin, capital of the Jiangsu-Anhui Border Region, on 19 September and Huai'an on the 22nd. The Central China forces moved north to draw close to the Shandong forces.
battle:两淮之战.sides: KMT forces defeated Central China Military Region forces

battle:中原突围.cmd: Li Xiannian and Wang Zhen vs. Liu Zhi
battle:中原突围.note: KMT forces 300,000 strong besieged the Central Plains Liberated Area centred on Xuanhuadian; Li Xiannian's forces broke out in several columns, the main body heading west into southern Shaanxi and western Henan and Wang Zhen's forces returning north to the Shaanxi-Gansu-Ningxia Border Region. With this as its starting point the KMT launched a full-scale civil war, and the War of Liberation began.
battle:中原突围.sides: Central Plains Military Region forces broke out

battle:中寮战役.note: Part of the Vietnamese forces, together with Lao troops, attacked through the Mụ Giạ Pass into Khammouane; on 23 December the French and Lao forces abandoned Thakhek, and the Vietnamese reached the Mekong River, cutting river traffic between Vientiane and Savannakhet. Navarre was forced to divert troops to hold Seno.
battle:中寮战役.sides: Vietnam People's Army and Pathet Lao defeated French and Royal Lao forces

battle:中条山战役.cmd: Wei Lihuang (Zeng Wanzhong and Tang Huaiyuan) vs. Tada Hayao
battle:中条山战役.note: Japanese forces concentrated more than 100,000 troops to converge on the Zhongtiao Mountains from several directions; attacked front and rear, the KMT forces lost more than 70,000 killed, wounded or captured, and Tang Huaiyuan, commander of the Third Army, took his own life, dying for his country. The KMT forces lost their last foothold north of the Yellow River, the Japanese consolidated their hold on southern Shanxi, and the Zhongtiao Mountains later became an area of operations for the Eighth Route Army's Taiyue forces.

battle:中途岛海战.cmd: Nimitz, Spruance and Fletcher vs. Yamamoto Isoroku and Nagumo Chūichi
battle:中途岛海战.note: Having broken the Japanese codes, the Americans laid an ambush northeast of Midway; their dive bombers sank four Japanese aircraft carriers, the Akagi, Kaga, Sōryū and Hiryū, for the loss of the Yorktown. The Japanese navy's offensive was brought to an end, and the tide of the Pacific War turned.

battle:临汾战役.note: Xu Xiangqian's forces breached the strongly fortified city of Linfen with tunnelling and demolitions after seventy-two days; Liang Peihuang was captured and all of southern Shanxi was liberated.

battle:临沂保卫战.cmd: Pang Bingxun and Zhang Zizhong vs. Itagaki Seishirō
battle:临沂保卫战.note: Pang Bingxun's forces held Linyi, and Zhang Zizhong hurried to their aid with the 59th Army; they beat back the Sakamoto Detachment of the Japanese 5th Division, wrecking its plan to converge on Tai'erzhuang from the east.

battle:临津江之战.note: In the first phase of the Fifth Campaign the CPV 19th Army Group forced a crossing of the Imjin River; the 1st Battalion, Gloucestershire Regiment, of the British 29th Brigade was surrounded on the heights at Seolma-ri, and only a few dozen men broke out alive. The British held up the advance for three days, covering the withdrawal of the “UN Command” forces to north of Seoul.
battle:临津江之战.sides: Chinese People's Volunteers defeated British and Belgian forces

battle:丹尼行动.cmd: Yigal Allon and Rabin vs. Arab Legion
battle:丹尼行动.note: After the first truce ended, Israeli forces seized Lydda airport and the towns of Lydda and Ramle, forcing more than 50,000 Arab inhabitants to leave, and widened the corridor to Jerusalem; at the same time Nazareth was taken on the northern front.
battle:丹尼行动.sides: Israel defeated Jordan and Arab forces

battle:义路之战（1951）.cmd: de Lattre vs. Võ Nguyên Giáp
battle:义路之战（1951）.note: Vietnamese forces attacked Nghĩa Lộ, the gateway to the Thái areas of the northwest; the French dropped in paratroopers as reinforcements, and the Vietnamese pulled back. A year later they returned, and Nghĩa Lộ was lost.
battle:义路之战（1951）.sides: French forces defeated Vietnam People's Army

battle:乌山之战.note: After the United States launched its armed intervention in Korea, Task Force Smith of the US 24th Division, about 400 men, engaged the Korean People's Army for the first time; its bazookas could not penetrate the T-34s, and it broke and fell back within half a day, shattering the Americans' contempt for their enemy.
battle:乌山之战.sides: Korean People's Army defeated US forces

battle:乌泰之役.note: Utai, jasagh of the Khorchin Right Front Banner, rebelled in response to Outer Mongolian “independence”; he attacked Taonan and Zhendong, was defeated by the Fengtian patrol and defence forces of Wu Junsheng and others, and fled to Outer Mongolia. Most of the eastern Mongol banners did not join him, and the frontier defences of the Northeast held firm.

battle:乌蒙山回旋战.cmd: He Long, Ren Bishi and Xiao Ke vs. Sun Du, Wan Yaohuang and Fan Songfu
battle:乌蒙山回旋战.mod: between Weining, Guizhou, and Zhenxiong, Yunnan
battle:乌蒙山回旋战.note: After leaving the Qianxi–Dading–Bijie area of Guizhou, the Red Second and Sixth Army Groups manoeuvred for nearly a month in the Wumeng Mountains against more than 100,000 pursuers, now east, now west, finally shaking off the encirclement in eastern Yunnan; they then moved south to fight their way through central Yunnan, and at the end of April forced a crossing of the Jinsha River.

battle:乾州之战.cmd: Zhang Yunshan vs. Shengyun and Ma Anliang
battle:乾州之战.note: Shengyun, Governor of Shaanxi, led the Gansu Army east, took Changwu and Binzhou in succession and besieged Qianzhou for several dozen days. Even after the abdication of the Qing emperor Shengyun did not stop fighting, lifting the siege only in March; the Shaanxi revolutionary army held on to Guanzhong.

battle:二刘大战.cmd: Liu Xiang and Deng Xihou vs. Liu Wenhui
battle:二刘大战.note: The last battle in the contest between uncle and nephew for mastery of Sichuan, fought first in southern Sichuan and then on the Pi River near Chengdu. Liu Wenhui was defeated and withdrew to Ya'an to build up Xikang; Liu Xiang unified the government of Sichuan and was soon charged with the “encirclement” of the Sichuan-Shaanxi Soviet Area.

battle:二渡赤水.cmd: Mao Zedong and Zhu De vs. Liu Xiang and Wang Jialie
battle:二渡赤水.note: After the Zhaxi reorganization the Red Army, catching the enemy off guard, turned back east across the Chishui River, heading straight for Tongzi and Zunyi in thinly defended northern Guizhou, and threw the KMT forces' plans for blocking and encircling it in southern Sichuan into disarray.
battle:二渡赤水.old: Second crossing of the Chishui River
battle:二渡赤水.sides: Red Army defeated Sichuan and Guizhou Armies

battle:云山战斗.note: The main battlefield of the CPV's First Campaign. The ROK 1st Division was checked at Unsan, and on 1–2 November the CPV 39th Army mauled the 8th Regiment of the US 1st Cavalry Division in the CPV's first clash with US forces. The “UN Command” forces fell back south of the Chongchon River.
battle:云山战斗.sides: Chinese People's Volunteers defeated US and ROK forces

battle:五原战役.note: In February Japanese forces pushed west into the Hetao and took Wuyuan; when their main force withdrew east, Fu Zuoyi made a night raid on Wuyuan New City, killing Mizukawa Yorio, head of the special service agency, and recovered the Hetao. It is known as the Wuyuan Victory.

battle:五路之战.cmd: Wang Huaiqing and others vs. Togtokh and Magsarjav
battle:五路之战.note: The Outer Mongolian “independence” regime invaded Inner Mongolia along five routes, at one point thrusting deep into Xilingol and Ulanqab and nearing Duolun. The Beijing Government massed large forces to counter-attack, and tsarist Russia did not back the southward push either; the Outer Mongolian army withdrew at the end of the year and Inner Mongolia was preserved.
battle:五路之战.sides: Beiyang Army defeated Outer Mongolian army

battle:亚喀巴之战.cmd: Auda abu Tayi and Lawrence vs. Aqaba garrison
battle:亚喀巴之战.note: Arab cavalry crossed the desert to come round behind Aqaba and destroyed an Ottoman relief force at Aba el Lissan on 2 July; on the 6th the Aqaba garrison surrendered. The rebels gained a port for supply by sea, and thereafter advanced north as the right wing of Allenby's army.

battle:亚特兰特行动.cmd: Navarre vs. Viet Minh Interzone V forces
battle:亚特兰特行动.note: Navarre aimed to clear the Viet Minh's Interzone V from Quảng Ngãi to Phú Yên; on 20 January his forces landed from the sea around Tuy Hòa and occupied the Phú Yên coast, but troops were drawn off one after another as the situation at Điện Biên Phủ and in the Central Highlands grew tight, and the follow-up operations north into Bình Định never got under way.

battle:仁安羌大捷.cmd: Sun Liren and Liu Fangwu vs. Japanese 33rd Division
battle:仁安羌大捷.note: More than 7,000 men of the 1st Burma Division had their line of retreat cut by the Japanese in the Yenangyaung oilfields; the 113th Regiment of the Chinese Expeditionary Force's New 38th Division rushed to their aid, broke the encirclement after two days and nights of hard fighting, and also rescued more than 500 captured British soldiers, missionaries and journalists. It was the first victory won by Chinese forces abroad.
battle:仁安羌大捷.sides: Chinese Expeditionary Force and British forces defeated Japanese forces

battle:仁川登陆.cmd: MacArthur and Almond vs. Korean People's Army
battle:仁川登陆.note: Disregarding the risks of the great tidal range and the narrow channel, MacArthur landed the US X Corps at Incheon, cutting the supply lines of the Korean People's Army in the south; its main force there was thrown on the defensive and forced into a strategic withdrawal.
battle:仁川登陆.sides: “UN Command” forces defeated Korean People's Army

battle:仰光之战.note: On 23 February, with the Japanese closing in, the British blew up the Sittang River bridge, leaving more than half of the 17th Indian Division cut off on the east bank. On 7 March the British destroyed the port installations and abandoned Rangoon, breaking through a Japanese roadblock near Taukkyan to withdraw north; the loss of Rangoon closed the sea entrance for aid to China through Burma.

battle:仰光收复.cmd: Slim and Mountbatten vs. Kimura Heitarō
battle:仰光收复.note: The British raced south ahead of the monsoon and attacked Rangoon from the sea and from the air in Operation Dracula; the Japanese had already pulled out at the end of April, and on 3 May the 26th Indian Division entered the city. The outcome of the Burma campaign was settled, with the remaining Japanese trapped in the Pegu Yomas and east of the Sittang River.

battle:伊尔库茨克起义.cmd: Political Centre (Socialist Revolutionaries and others) vs. Skipetrov (Semyonov's forces)
battle:伊尔库茨克起义.note: The “Political Centre”, led by the Socialist Revolutionaries, seized Irkutsk while the Czechoslovak Legion stood neutral, and Semyonov's relief force was blocked. Kolchak was handed over by the Czechoslovak Legion on 15 January, and on the 21st power passed to the Bolshevik Revolutionary Committee.

battle:会昌战斗.cmd: Zhu De and Ye Ting vs. Qian Dajun
battle:会昌战斗.note: The fiercest battle of the Nanchang Uprising forces' march south: they routed Qian Dajun's forces and opened the way into Guangdong, but suffered heavy losses themselves, and then changed course to enter the Chaozhou–Shantou region by way of Changting and Shanghang in Fujian.
battle:会昌战斗.sides: Nanchang Uprising forces defeated Qian Dajun's forces

battle:佐吉拉山口之战.cmd: Thimayya vs. Pakistani tribal lashkars and Scouts
battle:佐吉拉山口之战.note: The Indian army dismantled Stuart light tanks and hauled them up to the 3,500-metre Zoji La for an assault, taking the pass on 1 November and recovering Kargil on the 24th, opening the road to Leh.

battle:倒杨之战.cmd: Liu Xiang, Yuan Zuming, Liu Wenhui and Deng Xihou vs. Yang Sen
battle:倒杨之战.note: In the name of “unifying Sichuan”, Yang Sen attacked the forces of Liu Chengxun, Lai Xinhui and others; these armies allied with Liu Xiang and Yuan Zuming's Guizhou Army to bring Yang down, and Yang Sen fled in defeat to Hubei to join Wu Peifu. Sichuan reverted to a division into garrison zones among warlords such as Liu Xiang, Liu Wenhui, Deng Xihou and Tian Songyao.
battle:倒杨之战.sides: Anti-Yang Allied Army defeated Yang Sen

battle:倪家营子战斗.cmd: Xu Xiangqian and Chen Changhao vs. Ma Yuanhai and Ma Buqing
battle:倪家营子战斗.note: The Western Route Army fought the Ma cavalry back and forth for forty days over more than seventy fortified hamlets at Nijiayingzi; with its ammunition and food exhausted it broke out, was defeated again at Liyuankou, and on 14 March the Shiwo Meeting decided to disperse into guerrilla groups. The Western Route Army had failed.
battle:倪家营子战斗.sides: Ma Bufang's and Ma Buqing's forces defeated Western Route Army

battle:克拉斯诺亚尔斯克之战.note: The garrison commander Zinevich went over to the insurgents; Kappel's forces failed to take the city and went round it to the east, and large numbers of their rearguard were captured. Organized White resistance west of the Yenisei River ended here.
battle:克拉斯诺亚尔斯克之战.sides: uprising forces and Red Army defeated Whites

battle:八莫之战.note: The New 38th Division of the New 1st Army besieged Bhamo, a strong Japanese position on the Irrawaddy River, for a month, and more than half of the Japanese garrison was killed. The Chinese Army in India then moved south to Namhkam, and in January 1945 it joined up with the Expeditionary Force from western Yunnan at Mong Yu.
battle:八莫之战.sides: Chinese Army in India defeated Japanese forces

battle:兰封会战.cmd: Xue Yue and Gui Yongqing vs. Doihara Kenji
battle:兰封会战.note: Chinese forces with superior numbers besieged the Japanese 14th Division, which had pushed deep on its own, but through faulty command failed to annihilate it; Japanese reinforcements raised the siege, Kaifeng fell soon after, and this precipitated the Huayuankou dyke breach.

battle:兰州战役.note: The First Field Army stormed Yingpanling and other positions in the hills south of Lanzhou, with heavy casualties on both sides; Lanzhou was liberated on 26 August, the main body of Ma Bufang's group was wiped out, and Xining and Yinchuan were liberated soon after.
battle:兰州战役.sides: First Field Army defeated Ma Bufang's forces

battle:关岛之战（1941）.note: Guam was surrounded by the Japanese-mandated Mariana Islands; its garrison numbered only a few hundred, with no coastal guns. The Japanese South Seas Detachment landed on 10 December, and the naval governor, McMillin, surrendered the same day.

battle:关岛之战（1944）.cmd: Geiger vs. Takashina Takeshi and Obata Hideyoshi
battle:关岛之战（1944）.note: The US 3rd Marine Division and the Army's 77th Division landed on Guam and beat off Japanese night attacks, declaring the island recaptured on 10 August; Obata Hideyoshi, commander of the 31st Army, killed himself. Guam was then built up as the forward headquarters of the Pacific Fleet and a B-29 base.

battle:冀中五一反“扫荡”.note: More than 50,000 Japanese troops swept the Central Hebei plain in a dragnet “mopping-up” operation, digging blockade trenches, building strongpoints and carrying out the “Three Alls Policy”; tens of thousands of the Eighth Route Army's Central Hebei troops and local people were killed, wounded or captured. Central Hebei changed from an anti-Japanese base area into a guerrilla zone, and from then on the tunnel warfare devised by the army and the people spread.
battle:冀中五一反“扫荡”.old: Central Hebei May First counter-“mopping-up” campaign
battle:冀中五一反“扫荡”.sides: Japanese forces defeated Eighth Route Army

battle:冲绳战役.note: The largest amphibious campaign of the Pacific War. US casualties were about 50,000, and the commander, Buckner, was killed; about 100,000 Japanese troops died, more than 90,000 Okinawan civilians lost their lives, and there were tragedies of “collective suicide” forced by the Japanese army. After the war US forces remained there for the long term.

battle:刘戴之战.note: During the restoration Zhang Xun named Liu Cunhou Governor of Sichuan; the acting military governor Dai Kan denounced him on these grounds, and the two armies fought street battles inside and outside Chengdu's Imperial City for more than ten days. Dai Kan was defeated and killed while breaking out, Liu Cunhou held Chengdu alone, and the Guizhou Army's presence in western Sichuan came to an end.

battle:加平之战.note: After the ROK 6th Division broke and fell back at Sachang-ri, the Australian and Canadian battalions held the heights on both sides of the Gapyeong Stream valley for two days and nights, blocking the CPV route south along the Bukhan River valley towards the eastern side of Seoul.
battle:加平之战.sides: Commonwealth forces defeated Chinese People's Volunteers

battle:加里波利之战.cmd: Hamilton vs. Liman von Sanders and Mustafa Kemal
battle:加里波利之战.note: In March the Allied fleet's attempt to force the Dardanelles failed; on 25 April British, ANZAC and French troops landed at Cape Helles and Anzac Cove, and Mustafa Kemal held the heights with the 19th Division. After eight months of stalemate, with about 250,000 casualties on each side, the Allies withdrew in January 1916; the campaign made Kemal's name.
battle:加里波利之战.sides: Ottoman Empire defeated Britain and France

battle:劳山战役.cmd: Xu Haidong and Liu Zhidan vs. He Lizhong
battle:劳山战役.note: The Red 15th Army Group ambushed the Northeastern Army's 110th Division at Laoshan on the Yan'an–Ganquan road, killing its commander He Lizhong and smashing the northern prong of the KMT forces' third “encirclement” campaign.

battle:包头战役.cmd: Fu Zuoyi vs. Mongolia Garrison Army
battle:包头战役.note: In the Winter Offensive Fu Zuoyi's forces made a surprise attack on Baotou, at one point breaking into the city, and after wiping out part of the Japanese and puppet troops withdrew to the Hetao.

battle:包座战役.cmd: Xu Xiangqian and Chen Changhao vs. Wu Chengren
battle:包座战役.note: After the Right Column came out of the grasslands, the Red Fourth Front Army's 30th Army and Fourth Army besieged Baozuo to strike at the relief force, wiping out most of the 49th Division of Hu Zongnan's KMT forces and opening the gateway north into southern Gansu.

battle:北西原战役.cmd: Viet Minh Interzone V forces vs. Navarre
battle:北西原战役.note: While the French were launching Operation Atlante on the coast of Interzone V, the Vietnamese forces struck in the opposite direction, into the northern Central Highlands, overrunning the posts north of Kon Tum; on 7 February the French evacuated Kon Tum, and the Vietnamese pressed on towards Pleiku, tying down Navarre's reserves in central Vietnam.
battle:北西原战役.sides: Vietnam People's Army defeated French forces

battle:南京之战.cmd: Xu Shaozhen vs. Zhang Xun, Tieliang and Zhang Renjun
battle:南京之战.note: The 9th Division's attack on Yuhuatai on 8 November failed; the Jiangsu, Zhejiang and Shanghai forces then formed an allied army and attacked again, taking Tianbao Fort on Zijin Mountain on 1 December, and the next day Zhang Xun withdrew to Xuzhou. Nanjing was won for the revolution and became the seat of the Provisional Government.
battle:南京之战.sides: Jiangsu-Zhejiang Allied Army defeated Qing forces

battle:南京之战（二次革命）.cmd: Zhang Xun and Feng Guozhang vs. He Haiming
battle:南京之战（二次革命）.note: After Huang Xing left Nanjing at the end of July, He Haiming declared independence once more and held the city for over twenty days. On 1 September Zhang Xun's Pigtail Army broke into the city and burned, killed and looted, killing Japanese residents by mistake and setting off a diplomatic dispute; the failure of the Second Revolution was now certain.

battle:南京保卫战.cmd: Tang Shengzhi vs. Matsui Iwane and Prince Asaka Yasuhiko
battle:南京保卫战.note: The Chinese defenders fought hard at Yuhuatai, Zijin Mountain and Zhonghua Gate; after the order to withdraw was issued on 12 December, order collapsed and large numbers of officers and men failed to cross the river. Nanjing fell on 13 December, and Japanese forces then perpetrated the Nanjing Massacre.

battle:南口之战.cmd: Zhang Xueliang, Han Linchun, Zhang Zongchang and Wu Peifu vs. Lu Zhonglin, Song Zheyuan and Liu Ruming
battle:南口之战.note: After withdrawing from Beijing, the Guominjun held out behind the natural barriers of Nankou and Juyong Pass, besieged on all sides by the Fengtian, Zhili, Zhili-Shandong and Shanxi armies; after more than three months of fierce fighting Nankou fell on 14 August, and the Guominjun withdrew west to Suiyuan and Gansu. The battle tied down the main forces of the Beiyang warlords and objectively helped the National Revolutionary Army's Northern Expedition.

battle:南口战役.cmd: Tang Enbo and Liu Ruming vs. Itagaki Seishirō and Tōjō Hideki
battle:南口战役.note: Tang Enbo's forces held the mountains of Juyong Pass and Nankou in bitter fighting for half a month; after Japanese forces outflanked them by way of Zhangjiakou the Chinese defenders withdrew, and the eastern section of the Beiping–Suiyuan Railway and southern Chahar soon fell.

battle:南宁围城.cmd: Huang Xuchu and Bai Chongxi vs. Lu Han
battle:南宁围城.note: On Nanjing's orders the Yunnan Army attacked Guangxi, advancing east down the You River and besieging Nanning for about three months, but Huang Xuchu held firm; in October Bai Chongxi returned to raise the siege, and the Yunnan Army withdrew to Yunnan.

battle:南库页岛战役.note: The Soviet 16th Army broke through the Koton fortified region south of the 50th parallel and landed at Esutoru and Maoka, occupying Toyohara and Odomari on 25 August. Many Japanese civilians were killed or injured in the evacuation, and nine women telephone operators at the Maoka post office took their own lives.

battle:南征之役.cmd: Li Jishen, Chen Mingshu and Yu Zuobai vs. Deng Benyin and Shen Baofan
battle:南征之役.note: The Nationalist Government sent the Fourth Army as its main force on a southern campaign against the Eight Prefectures Allied Army, while Yu Zuobai's New Guangxi Clique forces attacked from Guangxi in a pincer; they took Yangjiang, Gaozhou, Leizhou, Qinzhou and Lianzhou in succession, and in early 1926 crossed the sea to take Hainan Island, unifying the Guangdong revolutionary base.
battle:南征之役.sides: National Revolutionary Army defeated Deng Benyin

battle:南日岛战斗.note: KMT forces sent about 6,000 men from Kinmen to attack Nanri Island off Putian; most of the more than 1,000 men of the 28th Army holding the island were killed, wounded or captured, and the KMT forces withdrew to Kinmen before reinforcements arrived. It was one of the larger KMT raids on the southeast coast.

battle:南昌会战.cmd: Luo Zhuoying and Xue Yue vs. Okamura Yasuji
battle:南昌会战.note: Using tanks and poison gas, Japanese forces forced a crossing of the Xiu River and took Nanchang on 27 March; a Chinese counter-offensive in April at one point reached the outskirts of the city but failed to retake it, and the western section of the Zhejiang–Jiangxi Railway came under threat.

battle:南昌战役.cmd: Chiang Kai-shek, Zhu Peide and Li Zongren vs. Sun Chuanfang and Deng Ruzhuo
battle:南昌战役.note: The Northern Expedition Army broke into the city briefly in September but was soon driven out, and its assault in October failed again, the First Army suffering heavy casualties; after regrouping it first broke through at De'an and Jiujiang, cutting the Nanchang–Jiujiang Railway, and retook Nanchang on 8 November. Sun Chuanfang's main force never recovered.
battle:南昌战役.sides: National Revolutionary Army defeated Sun Chuanfang's army

battle:南昌起义.cmd: Zhou Enlai, He Long, Ye Ting, Zhu De and Liu Bocheng vs. Zhu Peide's garrison
battle:南昌起义.note: The CPC rose up with about 20,000 men, among them He Long's 20th Army and Ye Ting's 11th Army; after four hours of fierce fighting it wiped out the garrison, firing the first shot of armed resistance against the KMT reactionaries and marking the beginning of the CPC's creation of a people's army; 1 August was later designated Army Day. From 3 August the forces left Nanchang and moved south towards Guangdong.
battle:南昌起义.sides: Nanchang Uprising forces defeated KMT defenders

battle:南苑之战.cmd: Tong Linge and Zhao Dengyu vs. Katsuki Kiyoshi
battle:南苑之战.note: Japanese forces launched a general attack with aircraft and tanks on the 29th Army's camp at Nanyuan; the deputy army commander Tong Linge and the division commander Zhao Dengyu died heroically for their country. Song Zheyuan withdrew to Baoding that night, and Beiping fell the next day.

battle:占守岛之战.note: Three days after Japan announced its surrender, Soviet troops landed on Shimushu, at the northernmost end of the Kuril Islands, and met stubborn resistance from the Japanese 91st Division, suffering more casualties than the Japanese; the Japanese ceased fighting on orders and laid down their arms on 23 August. The Soviets then moved south and by early September had occupied all the Kurils.

battle:卡马格行动.cmd: Leblanc vs. Vietnam People's Army 95th Regiment
battle:卡马格行动.mod: Route 1 along the coast of Quảng Trị, Vietnam
battle:卡马格行动.note: The French closed in by sea and land on the Viet Minh villages on both sides of Route 1 between Quảng Trị and Huế; the main force of the Vietnam People's Army slipped out through the cordon, and the French came back empty-handed. The French called this stretch of road the “Street Without Joy”.

battle:县里之战.note: In the second phase of the Fifth Campaign the CPV 9th Army Group and the Korean People's Army drove through to cut the line of retreat behind Hyeon-ri; the two divisions of the ROK III Corps disintegrated, and the eastern front fell back several dozen kilometres. Afterwards the Americans disbanded the ROK III Corps.
battle:县里之战.sides: Chinese People's Volunteers and Korean People's Army defeated ROK Army

battle:双堆集战役.cmd: Liu Bocheng, Chen Yi and Deng Xiaoping vs. Huang Wei
battle:双堆集战役.note: Second phase of the Huaihai Campaign. The Central Plains Field Army and part of the East China Field Army encircled Huang Wei's 12th Army Group at Shuangduiji southwest of Suxian; Liao Yunzhou, commander of the 110th Division, led his forces in an uprising, the army group was wiped out completely on 15 December, and Huang Wei was captured.
battle:双堆集战役.sides: Central Plains and East China Field Armies defeated KMT forces

battle:双桥镇战斗.cmd: Xu Xiangqian and Zeng Zhongsheng vs. Yue Weijun
battle:双桥镇战斗.note: The Red Fourth Army of the Hubei-Henan-Anhui area wiped out the entire KMT 34th Division at Shuangqiao Town, capturing more than 5,000 men, including the division commander Yue Weijun; it was the first time the Red Army in this area had annihilated a whole KMT division, and it smashed the first “encirclement” campaign against the Hubei-Henan-Anhui Base Area.
battle:双桥镇战斗.sides: Red Fourth Army defeated KMT 34th Division

battle:叙利亚—黎巴嫩战役.note: To prevent the Axis from making use of Vichy-ruled Syria, Commonwealth and Free French forces invaded along several routes from Palestine, Transjordan and Iraq, taking Damascus on 21 June; under the Armistice of Acre of 14 July, Syria and Lebanon passed to Free France.
battle:叙利亚—黎巴嫩战役.sides: Britain and Free France defeated Vichy France

battle:叙州之战.cmd: Liu Yunfeng vs. Wu Xiangzhen and Feng Yuxiang
battle:叙州之战.note: Liu Yunfeng's left column of the First National Protection Army entered Sichuan from northeastern Yunnan and took Xuzhou in January, the National Protection Army's first victory; in early March Feng Yuxiang's Beiyang brigade counter-attacked and retook Xuzhou, and the two sides faced each other south of Xuzhou until the ceasefire.

battle:古北口之战.cmd: Xu Tingyao, Guan Linzheng and Huang Jie vs. Nishi Yoshikazu
battle:古北口之战.note: Three divisions of the Central Army's 17th Army fought bloody battles in turn at Gubeikou and Nantianmen for two months, suffering more than 10,000 casualties. In mid-May Japanese forces broke through at Nantianmen and drove straight on Miyun and Huairou, and the Nationalist Government compromised with Japan and sued for peace.

battle:古浪战斗.note: The Western Route Army's Ninth Army took Gulang and was immediately counter-attacked by the cavalry of Ma Bufang and Ma Buqing, suffering more than 2,000 casualties, a crippling blow. Thereafter the Western Route Army pushed west along the Hexi Corridor to Yongchang and Shandan.

battle:台儿庄战役.cmd: Li Zongren, Sun Lianzhong and Tang Enbo vs. Isogai Rensuke and Itagaki Seishirō
battle:台儿庄战役.note: Sun Lianzhong's forces fought house to house in the streets of Tai'erzhuang while Tang Enbo's corps closed the ring from outside; the Seya Detachment of the Japanese 10th Division and the Sakamoto Detachment of the 5th Division were defeated and fell back, with more than 10,000 killed or wounded. Known as the Tai'erzhuang Victory, it was the greatest victory won on the frontal battlefield since the War of Resistance began.

battle:叶卡捷琳堡之战.cmd: Czechoslovak Legion and Siberian Army vs. Ural Red Army
battle:叶卡捷琳堡之战.note: On 25 July the rebellious Czechoslovak Legion and the White Siberian Army broke into Yekaterinburg; eight days earlier the local Soviet had executed Nicholas II and his family, who were held there under house arrest. The eastern foothills of the Urals remained in White hands from then until July of the following year.
battle:叶卡捷琳堡之战.sides: Czechoslovak Legion and Whites defeated Red Army

battle:同古保卫战.note: The 200th Division of the Chinese Expeditionary Force held off the Japanese 55th Division at Toungoo for twelve days, the Expeditionary Force's first battle in Burma, covering the British withdrawal north. After the Japanese 56th Division came up as reinforcement, Dai Anlan's forces broke out to the north on orders, and Toungoo was lost.
battle:同古保卫战.sides: Japanese forces defeated Chinese Expeditionary Force

battle:同江之战.cmd: Soviet Amur Flotilla vs. Northeast Navy River Defence Fleet
battle:同江之战.note: The Northeastern authorities' forcible recovery of the Chinese Eastern Railway set off the Chinese Eastern Railway Incident. The Soviet Amur Flotilla and army attacked Lahasusu (Tongjiang) at the mouth of the Songhua River; the main force of the Northeast River Defence Fleet was sunk, Tongjiang fell for a time, and the river defence forces of the Northeast were all but wiped out.

battle:和平战役.cmd: de Lattre and Salan vs. Võ Nguyên Giáp
battle:和平战役.note: French paratroopers dropped on Hòa Bình on 14 November, aiming to cut the communications between Việt Bắc and central Vietnam and the delta. The Vietnamese forces besieged the French posts along the Black River and Route 6; de Lattre, gravely ill, went home and died in January 1952, and Salan withdrew from Hòa Bình on 22–24 February, restoring the Vietnamese-controlled area to its former state.
battle:和平战役.sides: Vietnam People's Army defeated French forces

battle:哈伊勒之战.cmd: Ibn Saud vs. Muhammad bin Talal
battle:哈伊勒之战.note: After proclaiming himself Sultan of Nejd, Ibn Saud besieged Ha'il; the city surrendered on 2 November, the Rashidi dynasty came to an end, and Jabal Shammar was absorbed into Nejd.

battle:哈尔滨保卫战.cmd: Li Du and Ding Chao vs. Tamon Jirō
battle:哈尔滨保卫战.note: The Jilin Self-Defence Army held Harbin against the Japanese 2nd Division and after several days of fierce fighting withdrew east to Yilan. With the hub of northern Northeast China lost, Japan promptly cobbled together Puppet Manchukuo.
battle:哈尔滨保卫战.sides: Japanese forces defeated Jilin Self-Defence Army

battle:响堂铺伏击战.cmd: Liu Bocheng and Xu Xiangqian vs. Japanese 14th Division supply train
battle:响堂铺伏击战.note: The Eighth Route Army's 129th Division ambushed a Japanese truck convoy at Xiangtangpu on the Handan–Changzhi road, burning 180 vehicles; it was a model of the Eighth Route Army's ambush warfare.
battle:响堂铺伏击战.sides: Eighth Route Army defeated Japanese forces

battle:哥打巴鲁登陆.note: The Japanese Takumi Detachment landed on the beaches at Kota Bharu under fire from British Indian troops, more than an hour before the air raid on Pearl Harbor—the first shot of the Pacific War. The next day the British abandoned the airfield, and the northeastern gateway to Malaya lay wide open.

battle:喀什之战.cmd: Ma Fuyuan and Ma Zhancang vs. Sabit Damolla
battle:喀什之战.note: The Dungan troops holding the New City of Kashi counter-attacked the Old City, and the leaders of the so-called “Islamic Republic of East Turkestan” fled to Yengisar and Hotan. In April Ma Zhongying came to Kashi in person and the Dungan troops also took Yarkant, and this separatist regime collapsed.
battle:喀什之战.sides: Ma Zhongying's forces defeated “East Turkestan” separatists

battle:喜峰口之战.cmd: Song Zheyuan and Zhao Dengyu vs. Suzuki Yoshiyuki
battle:喜峰口之战.note: In the Great Wall Resistance the 29th Army's broadsword squads raided Japanese artillery positions by night, forcing Japanese forces to switch their attack to Luowenyu and Lengkou. After Lengkou fell in April all the armies withdrew south, but from then on “Swing your broadswords at the devils' heads” was sung throughout the country.

battle:嘉陵江战役.cmd: Xu Xiangqian vs. Deng Xihou and Tian Songyao
battle:嘉陵江战役.note: The Red Fourth Front Army forced a crossing of the Jialing River at Tazishan in Cangxi, took Jiange, Langzhong, Nanbu and the outskirts of Jiangyou in succession, and gained control of the broad area between the Jialing and Fu Rivers; it then abandoned the Sichuan-Shaanxi Soviet Area and moved west to prepare to meet the Central Red Army.

battle:四平保卫战.cmd: Du Yuming and Zheng Dongguo vs. Lin Biao
battle:四平保卫战.note: The Northeast Democratic Allied Army held Siping and blocked the KMT advance north for a month; the New 1st Army broke through by an outflanking move, and on the night of 18 May Lin Biao led his forces out. KMT forces then occupied Changchun and Jilin; in June a ceasefire took effect in the Northeast, halting them south of the Songhua River.
battle:四平保卫战.sides: KMT forces defeated Northeast Democratic Allied Army

battle:四平战役（1948）.cmd: Northeast Field Army 1st, 3rd and 7th Columns vs. Peng E
battle:四平战役（1948）.note: In its winter offensive the Northeast Field Army took Siping with three columns, wiping out the defending 88th Division. This ended the “four battles of Siping”: Siping was liberated, and Changchun was cut off from Shenyang.
battle:四平战役（1948）.sides: Northeast Field Army defeated KMT forces

battle:四平攻坚战.cmd: Lin Biao and Li Tianyou vs. Chen Mingren
battle:四平攻坚战.note: The last battle of the Northeast Democratic Allied Army's summer offensive: it broke into most of Siping, but Chen Mingren held on to the death awaiting relief, and after heavy casualties the Allied Army lifted the siege.
battle:四平攻坚战.sides: KMT forces defeated Northeast Democratic Allied Army

battle:四月事变.cmd: Japanese Vladivostok Expeditionary Army vs. Lazo
battle:四月事变.note: After the Nikolayevsk Incident, the Japanese interventionist forces simultaneously attacked Russian troops and partisans in Vladivostok, Nikolsk-Ussuriysky, Khabarovsk and elsewhere; Lazo and other revolutionaries were captured and killed. Japan used this to consolidate its occupation of southern Primorye, and Soviet Russia then set up the Far Eastern Republic as a buffer.

battle:四渡赤水.cmd: Mao Zedong and Zhu De vs. Chiang Kai-shek
battle:四渡赤水.note: The Red Army suddenly doubled back and crossed the Chishui River eastward for the fourth time at Erlangtan and Taipingdu; on 31 March it crossed the Wu River southward, feinting at Guiyang and making a show of heading for Kunming, and slipped out of the encirclement by several hundred thousand men of the KMT forces. The four crossings of the Chishui River were the masterstroke of Mao Zedong's art of military command.
battle:四渡赤水.old: Fourth crossing of the Chishui River

battle:四行仓库保卫战.cmd: Xie Jinyuan vs. part of the Japanese 3rd Division
battle:四行仓库保卫战.note: After the Chinese forces withdrew west, Xie Jinyuan and a battalion of the 88th Division held the Sihang Warehouse on the north bank of Suzhou Creek for four days and nights; hailed as the “Eight Hundred Heroes”, they withdrew into the International Settlement on orders.

battle:围困长春.cmd: Xiao Jingguang and Xiao Hua vs. Zheng Dongguo
battle:围困长春.note: The Northeast Field Army kept Changchun under a long siege for five months, cutting off its food supplies; famine in the city was severe and very many civilians died. After the liberation of Jinzhou, Zeng Zesheng, commander of the 60th Army, led his forces in an uprising, the New 7th Army came over, and Changchun was peacefully liberated.
battle:围困长春.sides: Northeast Field Army defeated KMT forces

battle:图拉巴之战.cmd: Khalid bin Luay vs. Abdullah bin Hussein
battle:图拉巴之战.note: Hejaz and Nejd contested the oases of Khurmah and Turabah; the Ikhwan made a night attack on Abdullah's camp, and the Hejazi army was almost wiped out. Britain stepped in to stop Ibn Saud from following up his victory with an attack on Hejaz.

battle:土亚战争.note: The Ankara government's Eastern Army took Kars on 30 October and Alexandropol on 7 November. Under the Treaty of Alexandropol of 2 December Armenia gave up Kars and Ardahan; at the same time Soviet power was established in Erivan.

battle:土城战役.cmd: Mao Zedong and Zhu De vs. Guo Xunqi
battle:土城战役.note: Misjudging the strength of the Sichuan Army, the Red Army fought a fierce day-long battle at Qinggangpo against Guo Xunqi's and other units without winning; the next morning it broke off the battle of its own accord and crossed the Chishui River westward into southern Sichuan.

battle:埃尔祖鲁姆战役.note: The Russian winter offensive broke through the Köprüköy line and took the fortress city of Erzurum on 16 February, then Bitlis and Trebizond; Russian-occupied Turkish Armenia reached its greatest extent.

battle:塔山阻击战.cmd: Cheng Zihua vs. Hou Jingru and Que Hanqian
battle:塔山阻击战.note: The 4th and 11th Columns of the Northeast Field Army held the Tashan line between Jinxi and Huludao against the KMT Eastern Advance Army Group for six days and nights, securing the assault on Jinzhou.
battle:塔山阻击战.sides: Northeast Field Army defeated KMT forces

battle:塔拉瓦之战.note: The US 2nd Marine Division stormed the fortified islet of Betio; its landing craft grounded on the reef, and it suffered more than 3,000 casualties in three days, while almost all of the Japanese garrison of more than 4,000 were killed. It opened the Central Pacific offensive, and its lessons in amphibious warfare were applied in all the landings that followed.

battle:塞班岛之战.cmd: Holland Smith and Turner vs. Saitō Yoshitsugu and Nagumo Chūichi
battle:塞班岛之战.note: Three US divisions landed on Saipan, and the Japanese garrison of more than 30,000 was almost entirely wiped out; Saitō and Nagumo killed themselves, and large numbers of Japanese civilians leapt into the sea from the cliffs at the north of the island. The loss of the Marianas allowed B-29s to bomb the Japanese home islands directly, and the Tōjō Hideki cabinet fell soon after.

battle:多伦之战.cmd: Ji Hongchang and Fang Zhenwu vs. Mogi Kennosuke and Li Shouxin
battle:多伦之战.note: The Chahar People's Anti-Japanese Allied Army took Kangbao, Baochang and Guyuan in succession and then besieged Duolun, taking it after five days and nights; it was the first time since the September 18 Incident that Chinese forces had recovered lost territory from the Japanese and their puppets. In August the Allied Army was defeated under a pincer attack by Japanese forces and KMT forces, and Duolun fell again.
battle:多伦之战.sides: Anti-Japanese Allied Army defeated Japanese and puppet troops

battle:夜袭阳明堡机场.cmd: Chen Xilian vs. Japanese garrison of Yangmingbao airfield
battle:夜袭阳明堡机场.note: The 769th Regiment of the Eighth Route Army's 129th Division raided Yangmingbao airfield by night, destroying or damaging more than twenty Japanese aircraft and weakening Japanese air strikes against the Chinese defenders at Xinkou.
battle:夜袭阳明堡机场.sides: Eighth Route Army defeated Japanese forces

battle:大柏地战斗.cmd: Zhu De and Mao Zedong vs. Liu Shiyi
battle:大柏地战斗.note: Leaving Jinggangshan, the Red Fourth Army marched into southern Jiangxi; after a string of defeats, with pursuers close behind, it laid an ambush at Mazi'ao, Dabaidi, wiping out two regiments of Liu Shiyi's Jiangxi Army and capturing more than 800 men, which reversed the passive situation it had been in since coming down the mountain.
battle:大柏地战斗.sides: Red Fourth Army defeated Jiangxi Army

battle:大田战役.note: The US 24th Division delayed the Korean People's Army on the Geum River–Daejeon line; on 20 July the Korean People's Army took Daejeon, and the US division commander, Major General Dean, became separated while breaking out and was captured on 25 August. The US delaying action bought time to assemble reinforcements on the Busan perimeter.
battle:大田战役.sides: Korean People's Army defeated US forces

battle:大马士革之战.cmd: Chauvel and Faisal vs. Ottoman Fourth Army
battle:大马士革之战.note: After Megiddo the Desert Mounted Corps and the Arab Northern Army pursued along separate routes; on 1 October Australian light horsemen and Arab troops entered the city one after the other, and Faisal promptly set up an Arab government. On 26 October Arab and British troops took Aleppo.
battle:大马士革之战.sides: Britain and Arab rebels defeated Ottoman Empire

battle:天津之战.cmd: Li Wentian and Zhang Zizhong's forces vs. Katsuki Kiyoshi
battle:天津之战.note: The 38th Division troops remaining in Tianjin and the Peace Preservation Corps took the offensive against the Japanese barracks at Haiguang Temple, the Dongjuzi airfield and Tianjin Station; Japanese aircraft bombed Nankai University and the city, and on 30 July the Chinese forces withdrew and Tianjin fell.

battle:天津之战（1925）.cmd: Zhang Zhijiang and Lu Zhonglin vs. Li Jinglin
battle:天津之战（1925）.note: After Guo Songling's revolt against Fengtian, the Guominjun seized the moment to attack Li Jinglin, Military Commissioner of Zhili; after half a month of fierce fighting at Yangcun and Beicang it took Tianjin on 24 December. Li Jinglin withdrew to Shandong and formed the Zhili-Shandong Allied Army with Zhang Zongchang. With Beijing and Tianjin in its hands, the Guominjun was at the height of its power.

battle:天津战役.note: With 340,000 men the Northeast Field Army took Tianjin in twenty-nine hours; Chen Changjie was captured and Tianjin was liberated. The Beiping garrison was left isolated, and Fu Zuoyi accepted peaceful reorganization.
battle:天津战役.sides: Northeast Field Army defeated KMT forces

battle:太原保卫战.cmd: Fu Zuoyi vs. Itagaki Seishirō and Kawagishi Bunzaburō
battle:太原保卫战.note: The Japanese forces from Xinkou and Niangzi Pass converged on Taiyuan; Fu Zuoyi held the city for several days and then broke out, and Taiyuan fell on 8 November. In North China, regular warfare with the KMT forces as the main body basically came to an end, and guerrilla warfare behind enemy lines with the Eighth Route Army as the main body rose to the primary position.

battle:太原战役.cmd: Xu Xiangqian and Peng Dehuai vs. Yan Xishan and Sun Chu
battle:太原战役.note: North China forces besieged Taiyuan for more than six months, for a time halting the attack to await the end of the Pingjin Campaign. The general assault broke into the city on 24 April; Sun Chu and others were captured and Taiyuan was liberated. Yan Xishan had already flown out in March.

battle:太行五月反“扫荡”.cmd: Peng Dehuai and Zuo Quan vs. Okamura Yasuji
battle:太行五月反“扫荡”.note: Japanese forces made a lightning raid on the Matian area of Liaoxian, where Eighth Route Army Headquarters was stationed. On 25 May the headquarters organs broke out at Shiziling, and the deputy chief of staff Zuo Quan died heroically for his country, the highest-ranking Eighth Route Army general to fall in the War of Resistance; Liaoxian was later renamed Zuoquan County.

battle:奠边府战役.cmd: Võ Nguyên Giáp vs. Navarre and de Castries
battle:奠边府战役.note: The Vietnam People's Army surrounded the French entrenched camp in the Điện Biên Phủ valley with four infantry divisions and heavy artillery; within two days of the opening of the battle it took the two strongpoints to the north, and the airfield was soon put out of action. After nearly two months of fighting for one strongpoint after another, de Castries surrendered on 7 May and more than 10,000 French troops were taken prisoner—a great victory for the Vietnam People's Army. The next day the Geneva Conference began discussing the restoration of peace in Indochina.
battle:奠边府战役.sides: Vietnam People's Army defeated French forces

battle:威克岛之战.cmd: Kajioka Sadamichi vs. Cunningham and Devereux
battle:威克岛之战.note: On 11 December the Marines' shore guns and fighters each sank a Japanese destroyer and beat off the first landing—the first small US victory after the outbreak of war. On the 23rd the Japanese landed again, now supported by aircraft carriers sent as reinforcement, and the garrison surrendered.

battle:娄山关战斗.cmd: Peng Dehuai and Yang Shangkun vs. Wang Jialie (Du Zhaohua)
battle:娄山关战斗.note: The Red Third Army Group took Loushan Pass, the natural stronghold of northern Guizhou, in the rain, opening the gateway to Zunyi. Mao Zedong's poem Loushan Pass, to the tune of Yiqin'e, is about this battle.

battle:娘子关之战.cmd: Cao Kun and Lu Yongxiang vs. Yan Xishan
battle:娘子关之战.note: Wu Luzhen was assassinated at Shijiazhuang on 7 November, and the plan for a combined Zhili–Shanxi army came to nothing. The Beiyang 3rd Division stormed Niangzi Pass, which fell on 12 December; the Shanxi Military Government withdrew from Taiyuan and Yan Xishan went north to Suiyuan, while the revolutionary forces in Hedong and Datong fought on.
battle:娘子关之战.sides: Qing forces defeated Shanxi revolutionary army

battle:娘子关战役.cmd: Huang Shaohong and Sun Lianzhong vs. Kawagishi Bunzaburō
battle:娘子关战役.note: The Japanese 20th Division advanced west along the Zhengding–Taiyuan Railway and outflanked the defences by way of Jiuguan and Ceyu Town; Niangzi Pass fell on 26 October, the eastern gateway to Taiyuan lay wide open, and the Xinkou defence line was shaken in turn.

battle:孙殿英西进之战.cmd: Ma Hongkui, Ma Bufang and Ma Hongbin vs. Sun Dianying
battle:孙殿英西进之战.note: Under the title of “Commissioner for Land Reclamation in Qinghai”, Sun Dianying led his troops west and stormed the city of Ningxia without success; the Ma warlords joined forces, with the Central air force joining in, and Sun's forces disintegrated in Alxa. Ma Hongkui's rule over Ningxia was thereby consolidated.
battle:孙殿英西进之战.sides: Ningxia Ma army defeated Sun Dianying's forces

battle:孟良崮战役.cmd: Chen Yi and Su Yu vs. Zhang Lingfu
battle:孟良崮战役.note: The East China Field Army cut the Reorganized 74th Division off from the massed KMT forces and wiped it out at Menglianggu; Zhang Lingfu was killed. The KMT forces' offensive against key areas in Shandong was dealt a heavy blow.
battle:孟良崮战役.sides: East China Field Army defeated KMT forces

battle:宁绍战役.note: To blockade the seaports of eastern Zhejiang, Japanese forces landed simultaneously at Zhenhai, Shipu, Wenzhou and the mouth of the Min River; Shaoxing, Ningbo and Fenghua fell in succession, and Fuzhou too was lost on 21 April. Most of the smuggling routes along the southeast coast were cut.

battle:安顺场战斗.cmd: Liu Bocheng and Nie Rongzhen vs. Liu Wenhui (Lai Zhizhong)
battle:安顺场战斗.note: Seventeen heroes of the Red 1st Regiment forced a crossing of the Dadu River in a single ferry boat and seized the landing on the far bank. Shi Dakai had met his end here in 1863; with too few boats for the whole army to cross, the Red Army pushed north along the river to seize Luding Bridge.

battle:定桂讨贼之役.cmd: Li Zongren, Huang Shaohong and Bai Chongxi vs. Lu Rongting and Lin Junting
battle:定桂讨贼之役.note: While Lu Rongting was besieged in Guilin by Shen Hongying, Li Zongren's Guangxi Pacification Army and Huang Shaohong's Anti-Rebel Army joined to form the Allied Army to Pacify Guangxi and Punish the Rebels; it took Nanning and swept away the remnants of Lu's faction along the Zuo and You Rivers. Lu Rongting announced his resignation by circular telegram in October, and the Old Guangxi Clique was finished.
battle:定桂讨贼之役.sides: New Guangxi Clique defeated Lu Rongting

battle:定陶战役.cmd: Liu Bocheng and Deng Xiaoping vs. Liu Zhi and Zhao Xitian
battle:定陶战役.note: The Shanxi-Hebei-Shandong-Henan Field Army wiped out the Reorganized 3rd Division around Dayanghu near Dingtao and captured its commander Zhao Xitian; a model, in the early War of Liberation, of concentrating superior forces to fight a war of movement.
battle:定陶战役.sides: Shanxi-Hebei-Shandong-Henan Field Army defeated KMT forces

battle:宜川战役.note: The Northwest Field Army besieged Yichuan and struck the relief forces, wiping out the Reorganized 29th Army at Wazijie; its commander Liu Kan killed himself, and Yichuan was liberated soon after. Hu Zongnan's group was gravely weakened, and in April the Northwest Field Army recovered Yan'an.
battle:宜川战役.sides: Northwest Field Army defeated KMT forces

battle:宿北战役.cmd: Chen Yi and Su Yu vs. Dai Zhiqi
battle:宿北战役.note: The Shandong and Central China Field Armies jointly struck the Reorganized 69th Division as it advanced north from Suqian; its commander Dai Zhiqi killed himself. The two armies were afterwards merged into the East China Field Army.
battle:宿北战役.sides: Shandong and Central China Field Armies defeated KMT forces

battle:宿州之战.note: The Guangdong Army's Northern Expedition force and the Jiangsu and Zhejiang armies advanced north along the Tianjin–Pukou line, defeated Zhang Xun's forces at Guzhen and Suzhou, and turned their spearhead towards Xuzhou. The Northern Expedition Army's advance strengthened the South's hand in the peace talks.
battle:宿州之战.sides: Northern Expedition Army defeated Zhang Xun's forces

battle:密支那之战.cmd: Stilwell, Zheng Dongguo and Merrill vs. Maruyama Fusayasu and Mizukami Genzō
battle:密支那之战.note: A combined Chinese–American raiding force crossed the Kumon Range and seized Myitkyina airfield in a surprise attack, but the siege of the town dragged on for nearly eighty days. On 3 August the Chinese Army in India took the town, and Mizukami Genzō killed himself. The Hump route could now be shifted south, and the China–India Road was past its most difficult stretch.
battle:密支那之战.sides: Chinese Army in India and US forces defeated Japanese forces

battle:富田战斗.cmd: Mao Zedong and Zhu De vs. Gong Bingfan
battle:富田战斗.note: The first battle of the second counter-“encirclement” campaign. After lying hidden in the Donggu hills for more than twenty days, the Red Army suddenly struck at Futian and Jiucunling and wiped out most of Gong Bingfan's 28th Division; thereafter it won battle after battle from west to east.
battle:富田战斗.sides: Red First Front Army defeated KMT 28th Division

battle:山城堡战役.cmd: Peng Dehuai vs. Hu Zongnan (Ding Delong)
battle:山城堡战役.note: The last battle after the rendezvous of the three main Red Army forces: the Red Army ambushed a brigade of Hu Zongnan's 78th Division at Shanchengbao and forced the KMT forces to halt their pursuit. With this the last major battle of the ten-year civil war came to an end.

battle:山海关之战.cmd: Du Yuming vs. Yang Guofu and Li Yunchang
battle:山海关之战.note: The KMT 13th and 52nd Armies, carried by US ships, landed at Qinhuangdao and stormed Shanhaiguan, occupying it on 16 November; they then pushed north along the Beining Railway, occupied Jinzhou on 26 November and opened the passage into the Northeast.
battle:山海关之战.sides: KMT forces defeated Northeast People's Autonomous Army

battle:岳州之战.cmd: Cao Kun, Wu Peifu and Zhang Huaizhi vs. Tan Haoming and Cheng Qian
battle:岳州之战.note: The Hunan-Guangxi Allied Army took Yuezhou on 27 January, threatening Wuhan. Back in office, Duan Qirui sent large forces south under Cao Kun and Zhang Huaizhi as commanders of two routes; Wu Peifu's forces retook Yuezhou on 18 March, entered Changsha on 26 March and took Hengyang as well in late April. The Hunan and Guangxi troops fell back to southern Hunan, and Wu Peifu then halted his advance and stopped fighting.
battle:岳州之战.sides: Beiyang Army defeated Hunan-Guangxi Allied Army

battle:川军驱逐滇黔军之战.cmd: Xiong Kewu, Liu Xiang and Liu Cunhou vs. Gu Pinzhen, Zhao Youxin and Lü Chao
battle:川军驱逐滇黔军之战.note: Tang Jiyao sought to control Sichuan through Lü Chao; Xiong Kewu joined forces with Liu Xiang and Liu Cunhou to counter-attack, re-entering Chengdu in August and taking Chongqing in October, while the Yunnan Army was defeated and fell back along the Luzhou–Xufu line. By the end of the year all the Yunnan and Guizhou troops had withdrawn from Sichuan, and the Sichuan generals promptly declared self-government.
battle:川军驱逐滇黔军之战.old: Sichuan Army's expulsion of the Yunnan and Guizhou Armies

battle:川边西征.cmd: Yin Changheng vs. Tibetan army in Kham
battle:川边西征.note: In the early years of the Republic the Xizang local authorities seized the chance to push east, and the armed forces of some native chieftains and monasteries in Kham rose to besiege the Sichuan Army at Litang, Batang, Qamdo and elsewhere. Yin Changheng, Military Governor of Sichuan, led an army west in July, relieved Batang and Qamdo and regained control of most of the Sichuan Frontier, but halted east of Jomda because of British interference.
battle:川边西征.old: Western Expedition into the Sichuan Frontier

battle:巧渡金沙江.cmd: Liu Bocheng (Cadre Regiment) vs. Liu Wenhui (Liu Yuanzhang)
battle:巧渡金沙江.note: The Cadre Regiment raided Jiaopingdu by night and seized seven wooden boats; in nine days and nine nights all 30,000 men of the Central Red Army crossed the Jinsha River, shook off their pursuers and headed north to Huili.
battle:巧渡金沙江.old: Skilful crossing of the Jinsha River
battle:巧渡金沙江.sides: Red Army defeated Sichuan and Yunnan Armies

battle:巨港空降.cmd: Kume Seiichi vs. Netherlands East Indies Army (KNIL)
battle:巨港空降.note: Paratroopers of a Japanese army raiding regiment dropped on the Palembang airfield and refineries, with the 38th Division following up the Musi River. The largest refining centre in the Netherlands East Indies fell into Japanese hands, and Java lost its western shield.

battle:巴丹之战.cmd: Homma Masaharu vs. Wainwright and King
battle:巴丹之战.note: MacArthur abandoned Manila and led the US and Filipino forces back into the Bataan Peninsula, where they held out for three months and upset the Japanese timetable. On 9 April Major General King surrendered with more than 70,000 men, and in the Bataan Death March that followed between several thousand and more than ten thousand died.
battle:巴丹之战.sides: Japan defeated United States and the Philippines

battle:巴勒斯坦阿拉伯大起义.cmd: Dill, Haining and Wingate vs. Abd al-Rahim al-Hajj Muhammad and Arif Abd al-Raziq
battle:巴勒斯坦阿拉伯大起义.note: The Arabs launched a general strike against British colonial rule and Jewish immigration, which turned into armed revolt after the Peel Commission proposed partition in 1937; at one point the rebels controlled the hill country and the Old City of Jerusalem. Britain sent more troops to suppress the revolt, and about 5,000 Arabs were killed; the White Paper of 1939 restricted immigration.

battle:巴厘巴板之战.note: Under heavy naval gunfire the Australian 7th Division landed at the refining centre on the east coast of Borneo, the last large-scale Allied amphibious landing of the Second World War. The Japanese withdrew inland and had still not been cleared out when they surrendered.

battle:巴士拉之战.cmd: Delamain and Barrett vs. Subhi Bey
battle:巴士拉之战.note: After the Ottoman Empire entered the war, British Indian troops set out from Bahrain, landed at Fao on 6 November and entered Basra on the 22nd, securing the Abadan refinery and the shipping lanes of the Gulf. This began the Mesopotamian campaign.

battle:巴库之战.note: The Ottoman “Army of Islam” and Azerbaijani troops attacked the Baku oilfields; the British Dunsterforce crossed the sea from Enzeli to help defend the city but withdrew on 14 September. Baku fell on the 15th, and its Armenian inhabitants were massacred in reprisal.
battle:巴库之战.sides: Ottoman Empire and Azerbaijan defeated Britain and Baku defenders

battle:巴格达陷落.note: Reorganized, the British Indian forces retook Kut, forced a crossing of the Tigris River and entered Baghdad on 11 March, where Maude issued a proclamation declaring “our armies do not come into your cities and lands as conquerors or enemies, but as liberators”. In November Maude died of illness in Baghdad.

battle:布哈拉战役.note: The Bukharan Revolution: the Young Bukharans rose up, and the Red Army, invited to help, attacked the city, breaking in on 2 September after artillery and air bombardment; the Emir fled east. The Bukharan People's Soviet Republic was established in October.
battle:布哈拉战役.sides: Soviet Russia and Young Bukharans defeated Emir of Bukhara

battle:布干维尔之战.cmd: Geiger, Griswold and Savige vs. Hyakutake Harukichi
battle:布干维尔之战.note: US forces landed at Empress Augusta Bay and built airfields from which to bomb Rabaul, beating off a counter-offensive by the Japanese 17th Army in March 1944. At the end of the year the Australians took over and pushed towards both the northern and southern ends of the island; when Japan surrendered, the Japanese still held the Buin area.

battle:布纳—戈纳之战.cmd: Eichelberger and Vasey vs. Yamagata Tsuyuo and Yasuda Yoshitatsu
battle:布纳—戈纳之战.mod: Buna, Oro Province, Papua New Guinea
battle:布纳—戈纳之战.note: US and Australian troops stormed the Japanese beachhead strongpoints amid swamps and fever, their battle casualties and sick together outnumbering the entire garrison. Buna was taken on 2 January 1943 and Sanananda on the 22nd, and all the Japanese strongpoints in Papua were cleared.
battle:布纳—戈纳之战.sides: United States and Australia defeated Japan

battle:常德会战.cmd: Sun Lianzhong and Yu Chengwan vs. Yokoyama Isamu
battle:常德会战.note: Yu Chengwan's 57th Division, 8,000 strong, held Changde to the death for sixteen days, with almost all its men killed or wounded; the city fell on 3 December, Chinese forces counter-attacked and retook it on 9 December, and Japanese forces returned to their original positions. Fought at the same time as the Cairo Conference, the battle drew the attention of the Allies.

battle:平型关大捷.cmd: Lin Biao and Nie Rongzhen vs. Itagaki Seishirō
battle:平型关大捷.note: The Eighth Route Army's 115th Division ambushed the supply train and follow-up units of the Japanese 5th Division at Qiaogou, northeast of Pingxing Pass, wiping out more than 1,000 of the enemy. It was the first major victory won by Chinese forces since the start of the nationwide War of Resistance, and it shattered the myth that “the Japanese army is invincible”.
battle:平型关大捷.sides: Eighth Route Army defeated Japanese forces

battle:平壤战役.cmd: Paik Sun-yup and Gay vs. Korean People's Army
battle:平壤战役.note: After the “UN Command” forces crossed the 38th parallel, the ROK 1st Division and the US 1st Cavalry Division raced each other north and broke into Pyongyang on 19 October, the DPRK government withdrawing north; on the 20th US airborne troops dropped at Sukchon and Sunchon to cut off the withdrawing forces.
battle:平壤战役.sides: “UN Command” forces defeated Korean People's Army

battle:平定杨刘叛乱.cmd: Chiang Kai-shek, Tan Yankai, Zhu Peide and Xu Chongzhi vs. Yang Ximin and Liu Zhenhuan
battle:平定杨刘叛乱.note: During the Eastern Expedition, Yang Ximin of the Yunnan Army and Liu Zhenhuan of the Guangxi Army colluded with Duan Qirui and Tang Jiyao and launched a rebellion in Guangzhou in June. The Eastern Expedition Army turned back and, together with the Hunan, Guangdong and Yunnan (Zhu Peide) armies, attacked them, breaking into Guangzhou on 12 June; Yang and Liu fled, the guest armies ceased to be a force, and the way was cleared for the founding of the Nationalist Government.
battle:平定杨刘叛乱.sides: Guangzhou revolutionary government defeated Yang Ximin's and Liu Zhenhuan's forces

battle:平汉线会战.cmd: He Chengjun vs. Fan Zhongxiu and Lu Zhonglin
battle:平汉线会战.note: The Northwestern Army attacked fiercely along the Beiping–Hankou Railway, at one point pushing south to Luohe; in June Fan Zhongxiu was killed in an air raid at Xuchang. After the Northeastern Army came inside the Great Wall in September, Feng's forces wavered along the whole front; on 6 October the Central Army entered Zhengzhou, and the Northwestern Army disintegrated.
battle:平汉线会战.sides: Chiang Kai-shek's Central Army defeated Northwestern Army

battle:平江之战.cmd: Li Zongren and Chen Mingshu vs. Lu Yun
battle:平江之战.note: The Fourth and Seventh Armies forced a crossing of the Miluo River and broke through Pingjiang, the gateway between Hunan and Hubei; its commander Lu Yun killed himself. The Northern Expedition Army thus drove straight into southern Hubei, opening the way for the attack on Wuhan.
battle:平江之战.sides: National Revolutionary Army defeated Wu Peifu's army

battle:平江起义.cmd: Peng Dehuai and Teng Daiyuan vs. Pingjiang county authorities
battle:平江起义.note: The 1st Regiment of the Hunan Army's Independent 5th Division, led by its commander Peng Dehuai, rose at Pingjiang and formed the Red Fifth Army; soon besieged by KMT forces from the three provinces of Hunan, Hubei and Jiangxi, it withdrew into the Hunan–Hubei–Jiangxi border area, and in December went up Jinggangshan to join the Red Fourth Army.
battle:平江起义.sides: Pingjiang Uprising forces defeated Pingjiang county garrison

battle:广东战役.cmd: Ye Jianying and Chen Geng vs. Yu Hanmou
battle:广东战役.note: The Fourth Field Army and the Second Field Army's 4th Army Group advanced into Guangdong; Guangzhou was liberated on 14 October, and Yu Hanmou's forces withdrew south and were wiped out around Yangjiang. Central and eastern Guangdong were liberated in turn.

battle:广州战役.note: The Japanese 21st Army landed at Daya Bay and took Guangzhou within ten days; most of the main Guangdong defence forces had been sent north, resistance was feeble, and the international supply line through South China was cut.

battle:广州起义.cmd: Zhang Tailei, Ye Ting and Ye Jianying vs. Zhang Fakui and Li Fulin
battle:广州起义.note: Taking advantage of Zhang Fakui's main force being engaged against the Guangxi Clique on the Xi River, the CPC launched an uprising in Guangzhou with the Training Regiment as its backbone and set up the Guangzhou Soviet Government. When Zhang Fakui's troops returned Zhang Tailei laid down his life; the uprising failed after holding out for three days, and several thousand insurgent soldiers and civilians were killed. The Nanjing Nationalist Government then severed relations with the Soviet Union.
battle:广州起义.sides: Guangdong Army defeated Guangzhou Uprising forces

battle:广昌战役.cmd: Chen Cheng and Luo Zhuoying vs. Peng Dehuai and Lin Biao (Bo Gu and Otto Braun)
battle:广昌战役.note: Bo Gu and Otto Braun pursued “Left” military adventurism and advocated “engaging the enemy outside the gates”; pitting blockhouse against blockhouse and using “short, swift thrusts”, the Red Army fought eleven of Chen Cheng's divisions head-on for eighteen days, suffering more than 5,000 casualties, and Guangchang was lost. Thereafter the Central Soviet Area shrank steadily, and the Red Army was finally forced to withdraw and set out on the Long March.

battle:广西反攻.cmd: Zhang Fakui and Tang Enbo vs. Japanese 11th and 23rd Armies
battle:广西反攻.note: As the Japanese began withdrawing from Guangxi to concentrate their forces, Chinese forces followed in pursuit, retaking Nanning on 27 May, Liuzhou on 30 June, Guilin on 28 July and Wuzhou and Quanzhou in mid-August; all of Guangxi was recovered.

battle:广西战役.cmd: Lin Biao and Chen Geng vs. Bai Chongxi
battle:广西战役.note: The Fourth Field Army and part of the Second Field Army advanced into Guangxi along several routes; Guilin, Liuzhou and Nanning were liberated one after another, the main body of Bai Chongxi's group was wiped out on the Guangdong–Guangxi border and around Qinzhou and Lianzhou, and its remnants fell back to Vietnam and Hainan.

battle:广阳伏击战.cmd: Liu Bocheng and Chen Geng vs. part of the Japanese 109th Division
battle:广阳伏击战.note: The 386th Brigade of the Eighth Route Army's 129th Division ambushed Japanese troops advancing on Taiyuan by the eastern route at Guangyang in Xiyang, killing or wounding several hundred; it was the Eighth Route Army's last battle in eastern Shanxi before the fall of Taiyuan.
battle:广阳伏击战.sides: Eighth Route Army defeated Japanese forces

battle:库伦之役.cmd: Ungern vs. Chu Qixiang and Chen Yi
battle:库伦之役.note: Ungern's Russian White Guard force invaded Outer Mongolia from Transbaikalia; after two failed attacks on Urga in October–November 1920, it attacked again in early February 1921 and took the city. The Chinese defenders broke and withdrew north, the Beijing Government's jurisdiction over Outer Mongolia was cut off, and the Bogd Khan was restored.
battle:库伦之役.sides: Ungern's White Russians defeated Chinese defenders

battle:库特之围.cmd: Townshend vs. von der Goltz and Halil Pasha
battle:库特之围.note: The British Indian force was besieged for 147 days; the relief forces' repeated attacks failed at a cost of more than 20,000 casualties, and on 29 April Townshend surrendered with about 13,000 men. Large numbers of the prisoners died on the march and in forced labour.

battle:底江战役.cmd: de Lattre vs. Võ Nguyên Giáp
battle:底江战役.note: Called the “Quang Trung Campaign” by the Vietnamese: the Vietnamese forces crossed the Đáy River to attack the Ninh Bình–Phủ Lý line; de Lattre's only son, Bernard, was killed at Ninh Bình on 30 May. French river flotillas cut the Vietnamese water-borne supplies, the Vietnamese forces pulled back in mid-June, and their attempts to attack the delta came to an end.
battle:底江战役.sides: French forces defeated Vietnam People's Army

battle:延安保卫战.note: Hu Zongnan's group attacked along several routes; the Northwest Field Corps fought a blocking action for six days and then withdrew, the CPC Central Committee left Yan'an of its own accord, and KMT forces occupied the empty city on 19 March. Whether Yan'an was held or lost became a focus of both sides' propaganda.
battle:延安保卫战.sides: KMT forces defeated Northwest Field Corps

battle:延平之战.cmd: Jiang Dingwen and Wei Lihuang vs. Cai Tingkai
battle:延平之战.note: Chiang Kai-shek sent the Central Army into Fujian from Zhejiang and Jiangxi; after taking Yanping (Nanping) it headed straight for Fuzhou, and the 19th Route Army hastily withdrew south and was split up and reorganized around Quanzhou and Zhangzhou. The Fujian People's Government collapsed after only two months.

battle:建宁战斗.cmd: Mao Zedong and Zhu De vs. Liu Heding
battle:建宁战斗.note: The final battle of the second counter-“encirclement” campaign. In fifteen days the Red Army swept 700 li from the banks of the Gan River to northwestern Fujian, fighting five battles in a row at Futian, Baisha, Zhongcun, Guangchang and Jianning and wiping out more than 30,000 men of the KMT forces.
battle:建宁战斗.sides: Red First Front Army defeated KMT 56th Division

battle:开封战役.cmd: Chen Shiju and Tang Liang vs. Li Zhongxin
battle:开封战役.note: The East China Field Army took Kaifeng, the provincial capital of Henan, and the defending commander Li Zhongxin was killed. To draw out the KMT relief forces, the PLA withdrew of its own accord on 25 June, and KMT forces reoccupied the city the next day.
battle:开封战役.sides: East China Field Army defeated KMT forces

battle:张家口战役.cmd: Fu Zuoyi and Sun Lianzhong vs. Nie Rongzhen
battle:张家口战役.note: Sun Lianzhong's forces attacked Huailai from the east while Fu Zuoyi made a rapid strike from Jining, and on 11 October they occupied Zhangjiakou, capital of the Shanxi-Chahar-Hebei Border Region. The same day the Nationalist Government ordered the convening of the National Assembly, closing the door to peace talks still further.
