battle:张家口战役.sides: KMT forces defeated Shanxi-Chahar-Hebei Military Region forces

battle:张鼓峰事件.cmd: Blyukher and Shtern vs. Suetaka Kamezō
battle:张鼓峰事件.mod: Zhanggufeng, Jingxin, Hunchun, Jilin (west of Lake Khasan, Russia)
battle:张鼓峰事件.note: The 19th Division of Japan's Korea Army fought Soviet troops for the heights west of Lake Khasan near the mouth of the Tumen River; the Soviets committed tanks and aircraft, a ceasefire was agreed in Moscow on 10 August, and the heights stayed in Soviet hands. The Japanese army used the clash to probe the Soviet attitude towards Japan.

battle:强渡乌江.cmd: Liu Bocheng and Lin Biao vs. Hou Zhidan
battle:强渡乌江.note: The Red First and Third Army Groups forced crossings at three points, Jiangjiehe, Huilongchang and Chashanguan, crossing at night on bamboo rafts to seize the far bank, and the Guizhou Army fled. On 7 January the Red Army occupied Zunyi.
battle:强渡乌江.old: Forced crossing of the Wu River

battle:徐州之战.cmd: Feng Guozhang and Zhang Xun vs. Leng Yu
battle:徐州之战.note: Leng Yu's 3rd Division of the Jiangsu Anti-Yuan Army attacked north towards Hanzhuang and Liguoyi but was defeated by the armies of Zhang Xun and Feng Guozhang coming south, and fell back to Nanjing on 22 July. The Beiyang Army then drove straight on Nanjing along the Tianjin–Pukou Railway.

battle:徐州之战（1927）.cmd: Zhang Zongchang and Sun Chuanfang vs. Wang Tianpei
battle:徐州之战（1927）.note: The Nanjing side's Northern Expedition Army took Xuzhou on 2 June, but in late July Zhang Zongchang and Sun Chuanfang counter-attacked and retook it; Chiang Kai-shek went in person to direct the fighting but was also defeated, and laid the blame on Wang Tianpei, commander of the Tenth Army. On 13 August Chiang was forced to step down.
battle:徐州之战（1927）.sides: Zhili-Shandong Allied Army and Sun Chuanfang's army defeated National Revolutionary Army

battle:徐州会战.cmd: Li Zongren vs. Hata Shunroku and Terauchi Hisaichi
battle:徐州会战.note: Japanese forces advanced towards each other from north and south to open up the Tianjin–Pukou Railway; after the Tai'erzhuang Victory they brought in more troops to encircle the Chinese, but the Chinese main forces broke out along separate routes. Xuzhou fell on 19 May, and the Japanese failed to achieve their aim of annihilation.

battle:忻口会战.cmd: Wei Lihuang and Hao Mengling vs. Itagaki Seishirō
battle:忻口会战.note: Chinese forces fought the Japanese fiercely for more than twenty days around Nanhuaihua at Xinkou; Hao Mengling and Liu Jiaqi died heroically for their country, the Eighth Route Army operated in support on the Japanese flank and rear, and the Japanese offensive was checked. With the fall of Niangzi Pass, the defenders were ordered to withdraw south to Taiyuan.

battle:怀玉山之战.cmd: Fang Zhimin and Liu Chouxi vs. Yu Jishi
battle:怀玉山之战.note: On its way back to the Fujian-Zhejiang-Jiangxi area, the Red Tenth Army Group (the Northward Anti-Japanese Vanguard Detachment) was surrounded in the Huaiyu Mountains by heavy KMT forces; Su Yu broke out with the advance units, but Fang Zhimin and Liu Chouxi were captured, and in August of the same year they met a heroic martyr's death in Nanchang.

battle:惠州之战.cmd: Chiang Kai-shek, He Yingqin and Cheng Qian vs. Yang Kunru
battle:惠州之战.note: Chen Jiongming's remnants took advantage of the Yang–Liu rebellion to reoccupy the Chaozhou–Shantou region, and the Nationalist Government launched its Second Eastern Expedition. Huizhou, bordered by water on three sides, was reputed to be impregnable; it was shelled on 13 October and taken by escalade on 14 October. In early November the Eastern Expedition Army retook the Chaozhou–Meixian region, and Chen Jiongming's power was wiped out completely.
battle:惠州之战.sides: National Revolutionary Army defeated Chen Jiongming's forces

battle:成都战役.cmd: Liu Bocheng and He Long vs. Hu Zongnan
battle:成都战役.note: After Liu Wenhui, Deng Xihou and Pan Wenhua declared their uprising by circular telegram from Pengxian, the Second and First Field Armies closed in on the Chengdu Plain from south and north; Li Wen's army group came over, Pei Changhui and others led their forces in uprisings, and Chengdu was liberated on 27 December. Hu Zongnan flew to Xichang.

battle:扎赉诺尔战斗.note: The Soviet Special Far Eastern Army attacked Jalainur with tanks and aircraft; the Northeastern Army's 17th Brigade fought desperately for two days, its commander Han Guangdi and a great many officers and men were killed, and the brigade was almost entirely destroyed.

battle:打拉根之战.note: The Australian 26th Brigade landed on the oil island of Tarakan to seize its airfield in support of later operations, but had to fight hard for seven weeks, and the airfield was too badly damaged to be used in time. This battle and the landings at Brunei Bay and Balikpapan are together known as Operation Oboe.

battle:扶眉战役.note: The First Field Army wiped out four armies of Hu Zongnan's forces, more than 40,000 men, between Fufeng and Meixian; Baoji was liberated, Hu Zongnan retreated into the Qinling Mountains, and Ma Bufang and Ma Hongkui lost the support on their flank.
battle:扶眉战役.sides: First Field Army defeated KMT forces

battle:拉特伦之战.cmd: Shamir and Marcus vs. Habis al-Majali
battle:拉特伦之战.note: Israeli forces repeatedly stormed the Latrun police fort commanding the Tel Aviv–Jerusalem road, and were each time beaten back by the Arab Legion with heavy casualties. Latrun remained in Jordanian hands for the next nineteen years.

battle:拉萨之战.note: Pro-British elements among the ruling stratum of Xizang seized the opportunity of the 1911 Revolution to launch the “expulsion of the Han”; the Tibetan army fought the mutinous Sichuan Army inside Lhasa and around Sera Monastery, and the garrisons of Gyangze and Xigaze surrendered one after another. After two ceasefires mediated by Nepalese representatives the Sichuan Army laid down its arms, and in December Zhong Ying led the remnants out of Lhasa, returning to the interior by way of India.
battle:拉萨之战.sides: Tibetan army defeated Sichuan Army stationed in Xizang

battle:援闽之役.cmd: Chen Jiongming and Xu Chongzhi vs. Li Houji
battle:援闽之役.note: Chen Jiongming led the Guangdong Army to Aid Fujian from the Chaozhou–Meixian region into Fujian against Li Houji, the Beiyang Military Governor of Fujian; on 31 August he took Zhangzhou and set up the “Southern Fujian Constitution Protection Zone” of some twenty-six counties. The Guangdong Army rested and regrouped here for two years and became the core armed force behind Sun Yat-sen's later return to Guangdong.

battle:收复士麦那.note: Turkish cavalry entered the city on 9 September, the Greek army having already left by sea. From the 13th a great fire destroyed the Armenian and Greek quarters, and large numbers of Christian inhabitants were killed or fled by ship. The Chanak Crisis followed, and the Armistice of Mudanya was concluded on 11 October.

battle:攻克吉安.cmd: Mao Zedong and Zhu De vs. Deng Ying
battle:攻克吉安.note: The Red Army of southwestern Jiangxi had attacked Ji'an eight times without taking it; the Red First Front Army succeeded on the ninth attempt and set up the Jiangxi Provincial Soviet Government. In November, before the KMT forces closed in, it withdrew of its own accord, carrying out the policy of “luring the enemy in deep”.
battle:攻克吉安.sides: Red First Front Army defeated Jiangxi Army

battle:斯卡都之围.cmd: Gilgit Scouts vs. Sher Jung Thapa
battle:斯卡都之围.note: The Jammu and Kashmir State Forces held Skardu for six months while relief columns were repeatedly intercepted, and surrendered on 14 August. Baltistan went to the Pakistani side, and the northern front advanced to Kargil and the edge of Ladakh.

battle:斯帕斯克之战.note: The People's Revolutionary Army and partisans stormed the Spassk fortress, and Diterikhs's White Guard “Zemstvo Army” was routed and fled south. The Japanese were forced to withdraw on schedule; on 25 October the People's Revolutionary Army entered Vladivostok, and the civil war in the Russian Far East essentially came to an end.

battle:新保安战役.cmd: Yang Dezhi and Yang Chengwu vs. Guo Jingyun
battle:新保安战役.note: The North China Field Army encircled and wiped out the 35th Army, Fu Zuoyi's own core force, and its commander Guo Jingyun killed himself; Zhangjiakou was liberated on 24 December, cutting off the route by which Fu Zuoyi's forces could retreat west to Suiyuan.
battle:新保安战役.sides: North China Field Army defeated Fu Zuoyi's forces

battle:新加坡之战.note: The Japanese 25th Army crossed the Johore Strait by night and within a week seized the Bukit Timah heights and the reservoirs; Percival surrendered with more than 80,000 British, Indian and Australian troops, a defeat Churchill called the worst disaster in British history. The Japanese then massacred tens of thousands of overseas Chinese in the city in the “Sook Ching” screening.

battle:方石岭战斗.cmd: Mao Zedong and Zhu De vs. Han Deqin
battle:方石岭战斗.note: With Guangdong and Guangxi sending troops into Hunan, the KMT forces began to withdraw; the Red Army intercepted and wiped out Han Deqin's 52nd Division at Fangshiling, and Han Deqin, taken prisoner, escaped in disguise. The third counter-“encirclement” campaign ended in victory.
battle:方石岭战斗.sides: Red First Front Army defeated KMT 52nd Division

battle:日军偷袭珍珠港.cmd: Nagumo Chūichi vs. Kimmel and Short
battle:日军偷袭珍珠港.mod: Pearl Harbor, Oahu, Hawaii, United States
battle:日军偷袭珍珠港.note: Carrier aircraft from six Japanese navy aircraft carriers made a surprise attack in two waves on the anchorage of the US Pacific Fleet, sinking or damaging eight battleships and killing more than 2,400 Americans; the US carriers escaped because they were away at sea. The next day the United States declared war on Japan, and the Pacific War broke out in full.

battle:日得拉之战.note: The Saeki Detachment, the vanguard of the Japanese 5th Division, broke through the prepared positions of the 11th Indian Division with a handful of tanks; the British fell back south in haste, losing large numbers of guns and vehicles. The Kedah airfields fell in turn, and northern Malaya was lost in a single battle.

battle:昆仑关战役.cmd: Du Yuming and Zheng Dongguo vs. Nakamura Masao
battle:昆仑关战役.mod: Kunlun Pass, Xingning District, Nanning, Guangxi
battle:昆仑关战役.note: The Fifth Army stormed Kunlun Pass with mechanized units, killing Nakamura Masao, commander of the Japanese 12th Brigade, and recaptured the pass on 31 December. Known as the Kunlun Pass Victory, it was a major success of the Winter Offensive.

battle:昆明重九起义.cmd: Cai E and Li Genyuan vs. Li Jingxi
battle:昆明重九起义.note: On the ninth day of the ninth lunar month the New Army's 19th Division rose in revolt; after a night of fierce fighting it took the arsenal and the viceroy's yamen, and Li Jingxi, Viceroy of Yunnan and Guizhou, was courteously escorted out of the province. The Yunnan Military Government was set up with Cai E as military governor, and the Southwest followed suit.

battle:昌都之役.cmd: Kalön Lama Jampa Tendar vs. Peng Risheng
battle:昌都之役.note: The Sichuan Frontier Army clashed with the Tibetan army at Riwoqe; taking advantage of the civil war in Sichuan, the Tibetan army pushed east in force, taking Zhag'yab, Ningjing and Gonjo in succession. In April 1918 it besieged Qamdo, and the commander Peng Risheng, his provisions exhausted, came out and surrendered; the western part of the Sichuan Frontier was entirely lost. Teichman, the British vice-consul at Dajianlu, promptly stepped in under the name of “mediation”.
battle:昌都之役.sides: Tibetan army defeated Sichuan Frontier Army

battle:昌都战役.cmd: Zhang Guohua and Wang Qimei vs. Ngapoi Ngawang Jigme
battle:昌都战役.note: The 18th Army, together with troops from Qinghai and Yunnan, crossed the Jinsha River along several routes and wiped out more than 5,000 men of the main force of the Tibetan army; Ngapoi Ngawang Jigme, Governor-General of Qamdo, led his forces in laying down their arms, Qamdo was liberated, and conditions were created for the peaceful liberation of Xizang.

battle:晋中战役.note: The North China 1st Army Group, 60,000 strong, wiped out 100,000 of Yan Xishan's forces between Pingyao, Jiexiu and Qixian; his field army commander-in-chief Zhao Chengshou was captured, more than ten towns in central Shanxi were liberated, and Taiyuan was left isolated.
battle:晋中战役.sides: North China 1st Army Group defeated Yan Xishan's forces

battle:晋察冀秋季反“扫荡”.note: After Okamura Yasuji took command of the North China Area Army, he threw 70,000 troops into an “iron-wall encirclement” of the Beiyue area and carried out the “Three Alls Policy” of burning all, killing all and looting all. The organs of the Border Region slipped out of the encirclement, suffering heavy losses but escaping destruction; the Five Heroes of Langya Mountain came from this campaign.

battle:曹甸战役.cmd: Chen Yi and Huang Kecheng vs. Han Deqin
battle:曹甸战役.note: To counter the anti-Communist activities of Han Deqin's forces, the New Fourth Army and the Eighth Route Army's Fifth Column besieged the Caodian–Cheqiao line to which he had withdrawn, but lifted the siege after a long assault failed. Friction between the KMT and the CPC in northern Jiangsu continued, and before long the KMT diehards engineered the Southern Anhui Incident.
battle:曹甸战役.sides: KMT forces under Han Deqin defeated New Fourth Army

battle:曼德勒—密铁拉战役.note: The British Fourteenth Army feinted at Mandalay while its main mechanized force crossed the Irrawaddy River to the south and struck at the communications hub of Meiktila, taking it on 3 March; the rear of the Japanese Burma Area Army collapsed. On the 20th the British took Mandalay and recaptured Mandalay Palace (Fort Dufferin).

battle:杜姆卢珀纳尔战役.cmd: Mustafa Kemal and İsmet vs. Hatzianestis and Trikoupis
battle:杜姆卢珀纳尔战役.note: The Turkish army launched its great offensive from south of Afyon and on 30 August encircled the main Greek force at Dumlupınar, capturing Trikoupis. The Greek army fell back in rout all along the line to the coast.

battle:杜霍夫斯卡亚之战.cmd: Ōi Shigemoto vs. Far Eastern Soviet Red Army
battle:杜霍夫斯卡亚之战.mod: north of Spassk, Primorsky Krai, Russia
battle:杜霍夫斯卡亚之战.note: The first major battle fought by the Allied interventionist forces on the Ussuri Railway: the Japanese 12th Division, with British and Czechoslovak troops, routed the Far Eastern Red Army and went on north to take Khabarovsk (5 September); Soviet power in the Far East was overthrown for a time.
battle:杜霍夫斯卡亚之战.sides: Japan, Britain and the Czechoslovak Legion defeated Red Army

battle:松山战役.cmd: He Shaozhou and Li Mi vs. Kanemitsu Keijirō
battle:松山战役.note: Songshan commanded the west bank at the Huitong Bridge on the Burma Road, and more than 1,000 Japanese held it in tunnelled fortifications. The Expeditionary Force's Eighth Army assaulted it for three months, dug tunnels and blew up the main peak, and the defenders were almost entirely wiped out; the Burma Road was thereby opened.

battle:枣宜会战.cmd: Li Zongren, Chen Cheng and Zhang Zizhong vs. Sonobe Waichirō
battle:枣宜会战.note: Japanese forces first attacked Zaoyang, then crossed the Han River westward to take Yichang; Zhang Zizhong died heroically for his country at Nanguadian. Yichang fell on 12 June, giving the Japanese a forward base for bombing Chongqing and threatening the gateway to eastern Sichuan.

battle:柳州之战.note: While Guilin was under siege, the Japanese closed on Liuzhou from the direction of Xiangzhou and Wuxuan; the 26th Army withdrew, and Liuzhou airfield and city were lost around 10 November. The US Fourteenth Air Force lost another forward base.

battle:桂南会战.cmd: Bai Chongxi vs. Imamura Hitoshi and Andō Rikichi
battle:桂南会战.note: Japanese forces landed at Qinzhou Bay and took Nanning on 24 November, cutting the international route between Guangxi and Vietnam; Chinese forces counter-attacked and recovered Kunlun Pass, but after the setback at Binyang in February 1940 Nanning remained in Japanese hands.

battle:桂林保卫战.cmd: Wei Yunsong and Kan Weiyong vs. Yokoyama Isamu
battle:桂林保卫战.note: Wei Yunsong, commander of the Guilin city defences, held the city with the 131st Division and other units; after encircling it, the Japanese attacked the cave works at Qixingyan and elsewhere with poison gas and flame. The city fell on 10 November, and the division commander Kan Weiyong took his own life, dying for his country.

battle:桂柳会战.cmd: Zhang Fakui and Bai Chongxi vs. Yokoyama Isamu and Tanaka Hisakazu
battle:桂柳会战.note: Third phase of the Henan–Hunan–Guangxi Campaign: the Japanese 11th Army advanced along the Hunan–Guangxi Railway and the 23rd Army up the Xi River, converging on Guilin and Liuzhou. KMT forces, worn down and badly directed, lost most of Guangxi in three months, and the Japanese opened a line of communication through to Vietnam.

battle:梁山战斗.cmd: Chen Guang and Yang Yong vs. Nagata Toshie
battle:梁山战斗.note: After the main force of the Eighth Route Army's 115th Division entered Shandong, it wiped out an entire reinforced Japanese battalion at Dushanzhuang in Liangshan, consolidating the Western Shandong Anti-Japanese Base Area.
battle:梁山战斗.sides: Eighth Route Army defeated Japanese forces

battle:棉湖之战.cmd: Chiang Kai-shek and He Yingqin vs. Lin Hu
battle:棉湖之战.note: Lin Hu led his main force south from Xingning to cut off the Eastern Expedition Army; the Whampoa 1st Training Regiment, a little over 1,000 strong, fought his more than 10,000 men at Mianhu all day and, when reinforcements arrived, routed them. Chen Jiongming's main force disintegrated, and the Eastern Expedition Army soon took Xingning and Meixian.
battle:棉湖之战.sides: Eastern Expedition Army defeated Lin Hu

battle:棉花坡之战.cmd: Zhu De and Zhao Youxin vs. Zhang Jingyao
battle:棉花坡之战.note: Mianhuapo was the key point of the National Protection Army's line east of Naxi town; Zhu De's detachment fought the Beiyang Army here for several days and nights without losing its positions. It was here that Zhu De made his name.

battle:榆关抗战.cmd: He Zhuguo and An Dexin vs. Nishi Yoshikazu
battle:榆关抗战.note: Japanese forces deliberately provoked an incident and attacked Yuguan by land, sea and air; An Dexin, the battalion commander defending the town, died heroically for his country together with his whole battalion. The gateway to North China lay wide open, and Japanese forces went on to invade Rehe.

battle:榆林桥战斗.note: The Red 15th Army Group wiped out the entire 619th Regiment of the Northeastern Army's 107th Division and captured its commander Gao Fuyuan. Gao Fuyuan later returned to the Northeastern Army and acted as go-between for Zhang Xueliang and the CPC.

battle:横城反击战.note: During the Fourth Campaign the CPV concentrated several armies to counter-attack the US X Corps advancing north from Hoengseong; most of the ROK 8th Division was wiped out, the US supporting units suffered heavy losses, and the “UN Command” forces fell back to the Wonju line.
battle:横城反击战.sides: Chinese People's Volunteers and Korean People's Army defeated ROK and US forces

battle:武昌战役.cmd: Deng Yanda and Chen Keyu vs. Liu Yuchun and Chen Jiamo
battle:武昌战役.note: Two attempts by the Northern Expedition Army to storm the walls were repulsed, and it switched to a close siege; with the city's food exhausted, part of the garrison opened a gate to let it in, and Wuchang was taken on 10 October. Liu Yuchun and Chen Jiamo were captured, and Wu Peifu's warlord power in Hunan and Hubei was destroyed.
battle:武昌战役.sides: National Revolutionary Army defeated Wu Peifu's army

battle:武汉会战.cmd: Chen Cheng, Li Zongren and Xue Yue vs. Hata Shunroku, Okamura Yasuji and Prince Higashikuni Naruhiko
battle:武汉会战.note: Chinese forces resisted step by step along both banks of the Yangtze and in the Dabie Mountains for four and a half months, inflicting more than 100,000 casualties on the Japanese; after occupying Wuhan the Japanese no longer had the strength to launch large-scale strategic offensives, and the War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression entered the stage of strategic stalemate.

battle:武汉四二九空战.cmd: Chinese Air Force and Soviet Volunteer Group vs. Japanese naval air units
battle:武汉四二九空战.note: Japanese forces raided Wuhan to mark the “Emperor's Birthday”; Chinese and Soviet pilots fought side by side to meet them and shot down more than twenty Japanese aircraft. It was one of the largest air battles of the early War of Resistance.
battle:武汉四二九空战.sides: Chinese Air Force and Soviet Volunteer Group defeated Japanese forces

battle:比塔帕卡之战.cmd: Holmes vs. German New Guinea police force
battle:比塔帕卡之战.mod: Kokopo, New Britain, Papua New Guinea
battle:比塔帕卡之战.note: The Australian Naval and Military Expeditionary Force landed near Rabaul and captured the German wireless station; the Germans surrendered on 17 September. It was the Australians' first battle of the First World War, and from then on German New Guinea belonged to Australia.

battle:永安战役.cmd: de Lattre vs. Võ Nguyên Giáp
battle:永安战役.note: Called the “Trần Hưng Đạo Campaign” by the Vietnamese: two divisions attacked Vĩnh Yên northwest of Hà Nội in an attempt to break into the Red River Delta. De Lattre flew in reinforcements and bombed the massed Vietnamese assaults with napalm; the Vietnamese forces withdrew after heavy losses, the first setback for the Vietnam People's Army since the Border Campaign.
battle:永安战役.sides: French forces defeated Vietnam People's Army

battle:汀泗桥战役.cmd: Chen Keyu and Zhang Fakui vs. Song Dapei and Dong Zhengguo
battle:汀泗桥战役.note: With water on three sides and hills on the fourth, Tingsiqiao was the first gateway into Wuhan on the Guangzhou–Hankou Railway. The Fourth Army outflanked it by mountain paths and took it in one stroke, and from here the name “Iron Army” spread.
battle:汀泗桥战役.sides: National Revolutionary Army defeated Wu Peifu's army

battle:汉城之战.note: When the Korean civil war broke out, the Korean People's Army, led by T-34 tanks, crossed the 38th parallel and broke into Seoul in three days; the ROK Army hastily blew up the Han River bridge, stranding large numbers of troops and citizens on the north bank, and the Syngman Rhee government moved south to Daejeon.
battle:汉城之战.sides: Korean People's Army defeated ROK Army

battle:汉城争夺战.cmd: Almond vs. Korean People's Army garrison
battle:汉城争夺战.note: The US 1st Marine Division and 7th Infantry Division forced a crossing of the Han River, and the Korean People's Army resisted street by street; on 28 September the “UN Command” forces reoccupied Seoul, and on the 29th Syngman Rhee held a ceremony marking the government's return to the capital.
battle:汉城争夺战.sides: “UN Command” forces defeated Korean People's Army

battle:江桥抗战.cmd: Ma Zhanshan and Xie Ke vs. Tamon Jirō
battle:江桥抗战.note: Defying the non-resistance order, Ma Zhanshan, acting chairman of Heilongjiang, held off the Japanese forces and the puppet troops of Zhang Haipeng, who had gone over to the enemy, at the Nen River railway bridge for half a month, firing the first shot of organized resistance by Chinese forces against Japanese aggression and lifting the spirits of the whole nation; Qiqihar fell on 19 November, and Ma's forces withdrew to Hailun.

battle:江浙战争.cmd: Qi Xieyuan and Sun Chuanfang vs. Lu Yongxiang and He Fenglin
battle:江浙战争.note: Qi Xieyuan, the Zhili Clique's Military Governor of Jiangsu, and Lu Yongxiang, the Anhui Clique's Military Governor of Zhejiang, fought for control of Shanghai. War broke out on 3 September and the two sides were deadlocked around Yixing, Jiading and Liuhe; Sun Chuanfang of Fujian then entered Zhejiang through the Xianxia Mountains, and Lu Yongxiang, attacked front and rear, abandoned Hangzhou and fell back on Shanghai, announcing his resignation by circular telegram on 13 October. The fighting touched off the Second Zhili–Fengtian War.
battle:江浙战争.sides: Qi Xieyuan and Sun Chuanfang defeated Lu Yongxiang

battle:汤坑战役.cmd: Ye Ting and He Long vs. Chen Jitang and others
battle:汤坑战役.note: The uprising forces occupied Chaozhou and Shantou in late September; the main force pushed west to Tangkeng and was defeated in fierce fighting with the Guangdong Army. In early October Chaozhou and Shantou were lost; after the Liusha Meeting most of the troops were scattered, one part entering Hailufeng and another, led by Zhu De, moving into the Fujian–Jiangxi–Guangdong border area, preserving the spark of revolution.
battle:汤坑战役.sides: Guangdong Army defeated Nanchang Uprising forces

battle:沂蒙反“扫荡”·大青山突围.note: More than 50,000 Japanese troops threw an “iron-wall encirclement” around the Yimeng Mountains. On 30 November the Shandong Sub-bureau, the First Branch of the Anti-Japanese Military and Political College and other organs were trapped at Daqingshan and broke out at a cost of several hundred casualties. Luo Ronghuan led his forces out of the encirclement with “edge-turning tactics”, and the anti-Japanese base area was preserved.
battle:沂蒙反“扫荡”·大青山突围.old: Yimeng counter-“mopping-up” campaign: breakout at Daqingshan

battle:沃洛恰耶夫卡之战.note: The Whites took Khabarovsk in December 1921; in bitter cold of thirty to forty degrees below zero the People's Revolutionary Army stormed the positions on June-Koran Hill at Volochayevka, and recovered Khabarovsk on 14 February; the Whites fell back into the Japanese-controlled zone.

battle:沙家店战役.note: The Northwest Field Army wiped out more than 6,000 men of the main body of the Reorganized 36th Division at Shajiadian, turning the tide in northern Shaanxi and going over to the counter-offensive on interior lines.
battle:沙家店战役.sides: Northwest Field Army defeated KMT forces

battle:沙特—也门战争.cmd: Crown Prince Saud and Faisal vs. Yahya
battle:沙特—也门战争.note: The two countries contested Asir and Najran. Faisal led an army south along the Tihama coast and occupied Hodeidah in early May, while Crown Prince Saud's column was held up in the mountains. Under the Treaty of Taif of 20 May, Yemen recognized Saudi sovereignty over Asir, Jizan and Najran, and the Saudi forces withdrew from Hodeidah.

battle:沙特攻取汉志.cmd: Ibn Saud and Khalid bin Luay vs. Hussein and Ali
battle:沙特攻取汉志.note: After Hussein proclaimed himself caliph, the Ikhwan took Taif in September; Hussein abdicated on 3 October, and on the 13th the Ikhwan entered Mecca. His son Ali held out in Jeddah for a year, and in December 1925 Medina and then Jeddah surrendered.

battle:河内之战.note: As the French pressed in step by step, on the night of 19 December the Vietnamese soldiers and people in Hà Nội attacked the French; Hồ Chí Minh called for nationwide resistance, and the Vietnamese people's war of resistance against France broke out in full. The Capital Self-Defence Regiment held out in the Old Quarter for two months before withdrawing, and the central leadership of the Democratic Republic of Vietnam moved to the Việt Bắc Base Area.
battle:河内之战.sides: French forces defeated Vietnam People's Army

battle:泗水之战.note: British Indian troops entered Surabaya to take over from the Japanese and clashed with armed Indonesian youths; on 30 October the British brigade commander Mallaby was killed. From 10 November the British launched an all-out attack with naval and air firepower; the soldiers and people of Surabaya resisted heroically, and the British occupied the whole city only after three weeks. Indonesian dead are estimated at between 6,000 and more than 10,000. 10 November was later made Indonesia's Heroes' Day.
battle:泗水之战.sides: British forces defeated Indonesian people's forces

battle:波罗行动.note: India sent in troops on the grounds of harassment by the armed Razakars, calling it a “police action”; columns broke in from all directions within five days, the Nizam announced his surrender on 17 September, and Indian troops entered the city on the 18th. During and after the operation large-scale communal killings took place in many areas.

battle:泰法战争.note: Taking advantage of France's defeat, Thailand invaded Laos and northwestern Cambodia in the name of “recovering lost territories”; on 16 January a French counter-attack at Yang Dang Khum was checked. Japan stepped in to mediate a ceasefire, and in May the Treaty of Tokyo assigned Battambang, Siem Reap and the Laotian lands west of the Mekong River to Thailand.

battle:泰西封战役.note: The 6th Indian Division pushed rashly up the Tigris River to Ctesiphon southeast of Baghdad, lost nearly half its men and was forced back to Kut.

battle:洛东江战役.note: Also known as the Battle of the Busan Perimeter. The “UN Command” forces formed a line of about 230 kilometres along the Nakdong River and the eastern mountains and, relying on movement along interior lines and on air and naval superiority, withstood two general offensives by the Korean People's Army in August and September, going over to the counter-attack after the Incheon landing.
battle:洛东江战役.sides: “UN Command” forces defeated Korean People's Army

battle:洛林行动.note: Thirty thousand French troops pushed north up the Red River and captured Vietnamese depots around Phú Thọ and Phú Đoan, hoping to draw the main Vietnamese force back from the northwest. Võ Nguyên Giáp refused to be drawn, and the French pulled back in mid-November, being ambushed on the way in the Chân Mộng valley.

battle:洛阳保卫战.note: Wu Tinglin's 15th Army defended Luoyang with three divisions; Japanese forces encircled it with the 3rd Tank Division and infantry, and the city fell after holding out for more than ten days. The First War Zone withdrew to western Henan, and most of Henan fell.

battle:洛阳战役.cmd: Chen Geng and Chen Shiju vs. Qiu Xingxiang
battle:洛阳战役.note: The Chen-Xie Group and the 3rd and 8th Columns of the East China Field Army took Luoyang and captured Qiu Xingxiang; the PLA soon withdrew of its own accord and liberated Luoyang again on 5 April.
battle:洛阳战役.sides: Chen-Xie Group and East China Field Army defeated KMT forces

battle:济南之战（1928）.cmd: Chiang Kai-shek and Liu Zhi vs. Zhang Zongchang and Sun Chuanfang
battle:济南之战（1928）.note: In the Second Northern Expedition the First Army Group advanced north along the Tianjin–Pukou Railway; after it took Tai'an, Zhang Zongchang abandoned Jinan and fled north, and on 1 May the Northern Expedition Army entered Jinan. Two days later Japanese forces perpetrated the Jinan Massacre, and the Northern Expedition Army was forced to make a detour, cross the river and push north.
battle:济南之战（1928）.sides: National Revolutionary Army defeated Zhili-Shandong Allied Army

battle:济南反攻战（1930）.cmd: Jiang Guangnai, Cai Tingkai and Han Fuju vs. Fu Zuoyi
battle:济南反攻战（1930）.note: The Shanxi Army took Jinan on 25 June and then attacked south towards Qufu without success; Chiang Kai-shek shipped the 19th Route Army by sea to Qingdao, and together with Han Fuju it counter-attacked and retook Jinan on 15 August. The Shanxi Army fell back across the Yellow River, and the outcome on the Tianjin–Pukou front was settled.
battle:济南反攻战（1930）.sides: Chiang Kai-shek's Central Army defeated Shanxi Army

battle:济南战役.cmd: Su Yu and Xu Shiyou vs. Wang Yaowu
battle:济南战役.note: The East China Field Army took Jinan in eight days; Wu Huawen, commander of the 96th Army, led his forces in an uprising, and Wang Yaowu was captured fleeing in disguise. It was the first time the People's Liberation Army had taken a fortified provincial capital held by 100,000 defenders, and it shook the KMT forces' system of defending key cities.
battle:济南战役.sides: East China Field Army defeated KMT forces

battle:浙奉战争.cmd: Sun Chuanfang vs. Yang Yuting, Xing Shilian and Shi Congbin
battle:浙奉战争.note: In the name of the Five-Province Allied Army, Sun Chuanfang launched a surprise attack on Shanghai, and the Fengtian Army withdrew from Shanghai and Nanjing without a fight. Sun's army advanced north along the Tianjin–Pukou line, routed Zhang Zongchang's forces at Guzhen on 8 November, captured and killed Shi Congbin and went on to occupy Xuzhou; the power of the Fengtian Clique withdrew from the Yangtze valley.

battle:浙赣会战.cmd: Gu Zhutong vs. Sawada Shigeru and Anami Korechika
battle:浙赣会战.note: After the Doolittle Raid Japanese forces advanced towards each other from east and west to open up the Zhejiang–Jiangxi Railway, destroyed the airfields at Quzhou, Lishui, Yushan and elsewhere, and carried out retaliatory massacres and germ warfare in the towns and villages along the line. From mid-August the Japanese pulled back, keeping only the Jinhua–Lanxi area.

battle:海南岛战役.note: The 40th and 43rd Armies of the Fourth Field Army slipped across the Qiongzhou Strait in wooden sailing junks in successive groups and joined up with the Qiongya Column; the main landing came on 16 April, Haikou was liberated on the 23rd, and the whole of Hainan Island was liberated on 1 May.
battle:海南岛战役.sides: Fourth Field Army and Qiongya Column defeated KMT forces

battle:海拉尔战斗.cmd: Luchinsky vs. Japanese 80th Independent Mixed Brigade
battle:海拉尔战斗.note: The 36th Army of the Transbaikal Front attacked Hailar; the Japanese held out stubbornly for nine days in the permanent fortifications on Beishan and surrendered only after the Emperor's rescript had been issued. Hailar commanded the western section of the Chinese Eastern Railway and was the first barrier on the Soviet advance to the Greater Hinggan Mountains.

battle:海满抗战.cmd: Su Bingwen and Ma Zhanshan vs. Matsuki Naosuke
battle:海满抗战.note: Su Bingwen of the Chinese Eastern Railway Guard Army held Hailar and Manzhouli against Japan and detained Japanese residents. Japanese forces pushed west with aircraft and tanks; in early December Su Bingwen and Ma Zhanshan withdrew into the Soviet Union, and the main force of the volunteer armies in northern Northeast China was thus defeated.
battle:海满抗战.sides: Japanese forces defeated Northeast Anti-Japanese Volunteer Army

battle:涿州之战.note: In the Shanxi–Fengtian War Fu Zuoyi led a division in a surprise seizure of Zhuozhou, a key point on the Beijing–Hankou line, and held it for nearly three months under close Fengtian siege; the Fengtian Army's repeated assaults failed, and in the end he left the city under a negotiated settlement and accepted reorganization. Fu Zuoyi made his name here.

battle:淞沪会战.cmd: Zhang Zhizhong, Chen Cheng and Gu Zhutong vs. Matsui Iwane and Yanagawa Heisuke
battle:淞沪会战.note: More than 700,000 Chinese troops fought bloody battles with the Japanese at Shanghai for three months, shattering Japan's arrogant plan to “subjugate China in three months” and buying time for coastal factories to move inland; after the Japanese landed at Hangzhou Bay the Chinese forces retreated along the whole front.

battle:淡水之战.cmd: Chiang Kai-shek, He Yingqin and Xu Chongzhi vs. Hong Zhaolin
battle:淡水之战.note: In the First Eastern Expedition the Whampoa cadet army made its first assault on a fortified position: a dare-to-die squad scaled the walls with ladders and took Danshui, then beat off Hong Zhaolin's relief force, and the Eastern Expedition Army drove on unchecked into the Chaozhou–Shantou region.
battle:淡水之战.sides: Eastern Expedition Army defeated Chen Jiongming's forces

battle:清川江战役.note: Western front of the Second Campaign. The CPV broke through the ROK II Corps at Tokchon and Nyongwon and drove deep to Samso-ri and Ryongwon-ri, and the US 2nd Division was mauled at Kunu-ri as it withdrew south. The “UN Command” forces fell back all along the line, and on 6 December Chinese and Korean forces recovered Pyongyang.
battle:清川江战役.sides: Chinese People's Volunteers defeated US, ROK and Turkish forces

battle:清津登陆战.cmd: Yumashev vs. Japanese Ranam Divisional District troops
battle:清津登陆战.note: The Soviet Pacific Fleet landed at the port of Chongjin and linked up with the 25th Army coming south along the coast, cutting the line of retreat of the Japanese in northeastern Korea; it was the main battle of the Soviet entry into Korea.

battle:清风店战役.cmd: Yang Dezhi and Luo Ruiqing vs. Luo Lirong
battle:清风店战役.note: The Shanxi-Chahar-Hebei Field Army hurried south and intercepted at Qingfengdian the 3rd Army, which was moving north from Shijiazhuang to relieve Baoding; its commander Luo Lirong was captured, leaving Shijiazhuang thinly defended.
battle:清风店战役.sides: Shanxi-Chahar-Hebei Field Army defeated KMT forces

battle:渡江战役.cmd: Liu Bocheng, Deng Xiaoping, Chen Yi and Su Yu vs. Tang Enbo and Bai Chongxi
battle:渡江战役.mod: middle and lower Yangtze (from Digang, Anhui, to Jiangyin, Jiangsu)
battle:渡江战役.note: A million men of the Second and Third Field Armies forced a crossing along a thousand-li stretch of the river from Hukou in the west to Jiangyin in the east; the garrison of the Jiangyin Fortress rose up, Nanjing was liberated on 23 April, and the Shanghai–Hangzhou area, the Zhejiang–Jiangxi area and southern Anhui were liberated one after another.

battle:湖口之战.note: Li Liejun declared Jiangxi independent at Hukou and took up arms against Yuan Shikai, and the Second Revolution broke out. Li Chun's Beiyang 6th Division, together with the navy, launched a fierce attack; Hukou fell on 25 July and Nanchang on 18 August.

battle:湘军驱张之战.cmd: Tan Yankai and Zhao Hengti vs. Zhang Jingyao
battle:湘军驱张之战.note: Wu Peifu withdrew north from Hengyang in May, and the Hunan Army followed on his heels; on 11 June Zhang Jingyao abandoned Changsha and fled, and at the end of the month the Hunan Army took Yuezhou. The movement to expel Zhang had long since swept the whole country; from then on Hunan was run by Hunanese themselves.
battle:湘军驱张之战.old: Hunan Army's campaign to expel Zhang Jingyao

battle:湘南护法之战.cmd: Cheng Qian, Liu Jianfan, Lin Xiumei and Tan Haoming vs. Fu Liangzuo, Wang Ruxian and Fan Guozhang
battle:湘南护法之战.note: Duan Qirui pursued “unification by force” and sent Fu Liangzuo to govern Hunan as military governor; in September Liu Jianfan, Garrison Commissioner of Lingling, and the brigade commander Lin Xiumei declared autonomy, and Cheng Qian came to their support with the Hunan and Guangxi Armies, fighting fiercely around Hengshan and Baoqing. In November the Beiyang commanders Wang Ruxian and Fan Guozhang called for a ceasefire by circular telegram, Fu Liangzuo abandoned Changsha and fled, and Duan Qirui resigned soon afterwards.
battle:湘南护法之战.old: Constitution Protection War in Southern Hunan
battle:湘南护法之战.sides: Hunan-Guangxi Allied Army defeated Beiyang Army

battle:湘南起义.cmd: Zhu De and Chen Yi vs. Xu Kexiang
battle:湘南起义.note: Zhu De and Chen Yi led the remnants of the Nanchang Uprising forces to take the county town of Yizhang by stratagem and routed Xu Kexiang in a battle at Pingshi, and more than ten counties, including Chenzhou, Leiyang, Yongxing and Zixing, rose in armed uprisings one after another; in April, under a pincer attack by the Hunan and Guangdong armies, the forces withdrew up Jinggangshan.
battle:湘南起义.sides: Workers' and Peasants' Revolutionary Army defeated Xu Kexiang's forces

battle:湘江战役.cmd: Zhu De and Zhou Enlai (Bo Gu and Otto Braun) vs. He Jian and Bai Chongxi
battle:湘江战役.note: The Central Red Army fought blocking actions at three places, Jiaoshanpu in Quanzhou, Xinxu in Guanyang and Guanghuapu in Xing'an, covering the Central Column as it forced a crossing of the Xiang River and broke through the fourth blockade line. Its strength fell sharply from more than 80,000 to just over 30,000, and the Red 34th Division, serving as rearguard, died heroically almost to a man.

battle:湘西之战.note: After Guizhou declared independence, Wang Wenhua led the eastern column of the Guizhou Army into western Hunan, taking Huangxian, Yuanzhou, Qianyang, Hongjiang and other places in succession; Ma Jizeng, commander of the Beiyang 6th Division, died at Chenzhou. The fighting in western Hunan threatened the flank and rear of the Beiyang Army and helped bring about Hunan's later declaration of independence.
battle:湘西之战.sides: National Protection Army defeated Beiyang Army

battle:湘西会战.cmd: He Yingqin and Wang Yaowu vs. Banzai Ichirō
battle:湘西会战.mod: around Dongkou and Suining, Hunan (Xuefeng Mountains)
battle:湘西会战.note: The Japanese 20th Army struck west from Shaoyang at Zhijiang airfield; Chinese forces blocked it line after line in the Xuefeng Mountains and, supported by US air power, counter-attacked, and the Japanese fell back to Shaoyang. It was the last major battle on the frontal battlefield of the War of Resistance, and the first in which Chinese forces held the advantage in equipment.

battle:湘鄂战争.cmd: Wu Peifu and Xiao Yaonan vs. Zhao Hengti and Song Hegeng
battle:湘鄂战争.note: People in Hubei invited the Hunan Army to “aid Hubei's self-government” and drive out Wang Zhanyuan; in late July the Hunan Army attacked north towards Puqi and Yangloudong, and Wang Zhanyuan left office. Wu Peifu led the Zhili Army south to counter-attack, defeated the Hunan Army in late August and went on to occupy Yuezhou; a ceasefire followed in early September, and from then on Yuezhou belonged to the Zhili Clique.

battle:滇桂战争.cmd: Li Zongren, Huang Shaohong and Bai Chongxi vs. Tang Jiyu, Long Yun and Shen Hongying
battle:滇桂战争.note: Appointed by the Beijing Government, Shen Hongying attacked the New Guangxi Clique and was crushed along the Guilin–Liuzhou line; Tang Jiyao then proclaimed himself deputy generalissimo and sent the Yunnan Army into Guangxi along two routes, Long Yun's column occupying Nanning. The New Guangxi Clique turned back to besiege it and in July defeated Tang Jiyu's forces at Shapu and elsewhere; the Yunnan Army withdrew to Yunnan, and Guangxi was unified under the New Guangxi Clique.
battle:滇桂战争.sides: New Guangxi Clique defeated Yunnan Army and Shen Hongying

battle:滇西反攻.note: More than 100,000 men of the Chinese Expeditionary Force forced a crossing of the Nu River, attacked uphill into the Gaoligong Mountains, took Songshan, Tengchong, Longling, Mangshi and Wanding one by one, and joined up with the Chinese Army in India at Mong Yu. Western Yunnan was the region where Chinese forces recovered lost territory most completely in the War of Resistance.

battle:滕县保卫战.note: Wang Mingzhang, commander of the Sichuan Army's 122nd Division, led his troops in a fight to the death at Tengxian and died for his country when the town fell; they held up the Japanese 10th Division for several days, gaining time to prepare the defences of Tai'erzhuang.

battle:满洲里战斗.note: Liang Zhongjia, commander of the 15th Brigade, was surrounded at Manzhouli for several days and then surrendered with his troops and was taken prisoner, and Soviet forces drove straight on Hailar. The Northeastern authorities were forced to sue for peace; on 22 December the Khabarovsk Protocol was signed, and the Chinese Eastern Railway reverted to its former status.

battle:滦东之战.cmd: Bai Chongxi vs. Zhang Zongchang and Chu Yupu
battle:滦东之战.note: After the Northern Expedition the Zhili-Shandong warlords Zhang Zongchang and Chu Yupu refused to accept reorganization and held out east of the Luan River with their remnants; Bai Chongxi's forces attacked from the west and the Fengtian Army from the east, the Zhili-Shandong Allied Army was entirely disarmed, and Zhang Zongchang fled to Dalian. With this the last battle of the Northern Expedition was over.
battle:滦东之战.sides: National Revolutionary Army and Fengtian Army defeated Zhili-Shandong Allied Army

battle:滦州起义.cmd: Wang Huaiqing vs. Wang Jinming and Shi Congyun
battle:滦州起义.note: Part of the 20th Division stationed at Luanzhou declared independence and set up the Northern Revolutionary Military Government; marching west, it was intercepted by Qing forces at Leizhuang, and Wang Jinming and Shi Congyun were lured into a trap and killed. The uprisings around the capital all failed, and the north remained under the control of the Qing court and Yuan Shikai.

battle:漳州战役.cmd: Mao Zedong and Lin Biao vs. Zhang Zhen
battle:漳州战役.note: The Red Army's Eastern Route Army entered Fujian, routed Zhang Zhen's 49th Division outside Zhangzhou and entered the city on 20 April, raising large quantities of supplies; at the end of May it withdrew to the Soviet Area.

battle:潍县之战.note: The Chinese Revolutionary Party organized its Northeast Army with Japanese-occupied Qingdao as its rear base; in early May the army rode special trains along the Qingdao–Jinan Railway to Weixian, attacked the town and then set up its general headquarters there. Shandong thus gained a base for the struggle against Yuan; after Yuan Shikai's death the army was reorganized and disbanded.
battle:潍县之战.sides: Chinese Revolutionary Army defeated Beiyang Army

battle:潍县战役.cmd: Xu Shiyou and Tan Zhenlin vs. Chen Jincheng
battle:潍县战役.note: The Shandong Army Group of the East China Field Army took Weixian and captured Chen Jincheng; the middle section of the Qingdao–Jinan Railway was liberated, and Jinan and Qingdao were cut off from each other by land.
battle:潍县战役.sides: East China Field Army defeated KMT forces

battle:热河之战.cmd: Tang Yulin and Zhang Xueliang vs. Mutō Nobuyoshi
battle:热河之战.note: The Japanese Kwantung Army and Puppet Manchukuo troops invaded Rehe along three routes; Tang Yulin fled without a fight, and on 4 March 128 Japanese cavalrymen seized Chengde. The whole country was in uproar; Zhang Xueliang took the blame and resigned, and Rehe fell and was incorporated into Puppet Manchukuo.
battle:热河之战.sides: Japanese and puppet troops defeated Chinese defenders

battle:爪哇海海战.mod: Java Sea north of Surabaya, Indonesia
battle:爪哇海海战.note: The combined American, British, Dutch and Australian fleet tried to intercept the Japanese invasion convoys bound for Java but was routed by long-range Japanese torpedoes and night fighting; Doorman went down with two Dutch cruisers, and the remaining ships were destroyed one after another in the Sunda Strait and the sea south of Java. The Japanese landed on Java on 1 March, and the Dutch forces surrendered on the 8th.
battle:爪哇海海战.sides: Japan defeated United States, Britain, Netherlands and Australia

battle:牡丹江战役.cmd: Beloborodov and Krylov vs. Shimizu Noritsune
battle:牡丹江战役.note: The 1st Far Eastern Front advanced west along the eastern section of the Chinese Eastern Railway and fought the Japanese 5th Army fiercely on the approaches to Mudanjiang, the hardest fighting of the Soviet operations in Northeast China. After taking Mudanjiang the Soviets drove straight on Harbin and Jilin.

battle:独山战役.cmd: Tang Enbo vs. Japanese 3rd and 13th Divisions
battle:独山战役.note: The Japanese pushed along the Guizhou–Guangxi Railway into southern Guizhou and took Dushan around 2 December; Chongqing was shaken, and the Nationalist Government for a time discussed moving to Xichang. Their supplies exhausted, the Japanese soon fell back to Hechi, and Chinese forces recovered Dushan. The episode is known as the “Southern Guizhou Incident”.

battle:独树镇战斗.cmd: Wu Huanxian and Xu Haidong vs. Pang Bingxun
battle:独树镇战斗.note: On the Long March the Red 25th Army was blocked by the 40th Army on the Xuchang–Nanyang Highway in wind and snow; its political commissar Wu Huanxian, sword in hand, led a counter-charge, and that night the army broke out of the encirclement, went west into the Funiu Mountains and moved on into southern Shaanxi.

battle:珊瑚海海战.cmd: Inoue Shigeyoshi and Takagi Takeo vs. Fletcher
battle:珊瑚海海战.note: The first carrier-versus-carrier battle in history, in which the two fleets never came within sight of each other. The Americans lost the Lexington and the Japanese the Shōhō; the Shōkaku was badly damaged and the Zuikaku lost more than half its aircraft, so neither could take part in the Battle of Midway, and the Japanese called off the seaborne attack on Port Moresby.

battle:瓜达尔卡纳尔之战.cmd: Vandegrift and Halsey vs. Hyakutake Harukichi and Yamamoto Isoroku
battle:瓜达尔卡纳尔之战.note: The US 1st Marine Division landed and seized the airfield the Japanese were about to complete (Henderson Field), and the two sides fought a six-month war of attrition on land, at sea and in the air around the island, with seven naval battles large and small. The Japanese committed more than 30,000 men in all, about 20,000 of whom were killed or starved to death, and withdrew in February 1943; from then on the Allies went over to the counter-offensive.

battle:瓦济里斯坦战役.cmd: British Indian Army vs. Faqir of Ipi
battle:瓦济里斯坦战役.note: The Faqir of Ipi used a marriage case involving a religious conversion to call the Tori Khel tribe to arms; the British Indian Army committed some 40,000 troops in all, together with air power, to hunt him down but never caught him, and he remained active on the frontier until after the end of the Second World War.

battle:甘孜之战.cmd: Demo and Kemi vs. Sichuan-Xikang Frontier Defence Army
battle:甘孜之战.note: Dargye Monastery and the Beri chieftain quarrelled over monastery property; the Sichuan-Xikang Army backed Beri and the Tibetan army backed Dargye Monastery, and fighting broke out in June 1930, known as the “Dargye–Beri Incident”. In February 1931 the Tibetan army raided Garze by night and the Sichuan-Xikang Army fell back to hold Luhuo; in May the Tibetan army also took Zhanhua.

battle:甘溪战斗.cmd: Xiao Ke, Ren Bishi and Wang Zhen vs. Liao Lei
battle:甘溪战斗.note: The Red Sixth Army Group, on its Western March, was intercepted at Ganxi by the Guangxi Army's Seventh Army and cut into several sections; the main force broke out of the encirclement, but most of the 18th Division was lost. At the end of the month, after many twists and turns, it reached eastern Guizhou and joined the Red Third Army.

battle:田家镇要塞之战.note: Tianjiazhen commanded the north bank of the Yangtze; Li Yannian's Second Army held it for more than twenty days before the Japanese 6th Division broke through the fortress, and Wuhan lost its eastern shield.

battle:登步岛战斗.cmd: Shi Jue vs. PLA 7th Army Group
battle:登步岛战斗.note: The Third Field Army's 21st Army landed on Dengbu Island in the Zhoushan group, but KMT forces, reinforced with naval and air support, counter-attacked, and it withdrew to the mainland. Like Kinmen, it was a setback in cross-sea operations.

battle:白马山战斗.mod: White Horse Hill, Cheorwon, South Korea
battle:白马山战斗.note: In its autumn tactical counter-attacks the CPV attacked White Horse Hill (Hill 395) northwest of Cheorwon and fought the ROK 9th Division for it back and forth for ten days; the position changed hands more than twenty times and was finally left to the ROK Army, which kept its hold on the Cheorwon plain.
battle:白马山战斗.sides: ROK Army defeated Chinese People's Volunteers

battle:百丈关战役.cmd: Xu Xiangqian vs. Liu Xiang (Yang Sen and Tang Shizun)
battle:百丈关战役.note: Moving south, the Red Fourth Front Army bore down on Qionglai and Mingshan and fought a bloody seven-day battle at Baizhangguan with more than ten Sichuan Army brigades, suffering nearly 10,000 casualties; it was forced on to the defensive, and in spring 1936 withdrew west to northern Xikang. Zhang Guotao's policy of going south had thus failed.

battle:百团大战.cmd: Peng Dehuai and Zuo Quan vs. Tada Hayao
battle:百团大战.note: More than a hundred regiments of the Eighth Route Army raided and wrecked the Zhengding–Taiyuan, Datong–Puzhou, Beiping–Hankou, Tianjin–Pukou and other railways and Japanese strongpoints, at one point taking Niangzi Pass. It was the largest offensive the Eighth Route Army had launched against the Japanese since the War of Resistance began, and it dealt a heavy blow to the Japanese “cage policy”; the Japanese then subjected the anti-Japanese base areas to even more brutal “mopping-up” operations.
battle:百团大战.sides: Eighth Route Army defeated Japanese forces

battle:百灵庙战役.cmd: Fu Zuoyi (Sun Lanfeng and Dong Qiwu) vs. Prince De and Kwantung Army advisers
battle:百灵庙战役.mod: Bailingmiao, Darhan Muminggan United Banner, Inner Mongolia
battle:百灵庙战役.note: In the Suiyuan Resistance, after beating back the puppet Mongol army at Honggertu, Fu Zuoyi's forces made a lightning raid by truck through ice and snow on Bailingmiao and took the puppet Mongol army's base in a single night. A wave of support for the resistance in Suiyuan swept the country, and Japan's scheme to engineer “Inner Mongolian independence” was thwarted.
battle:百灵庙战役.sides: Chinese forces defeated puppet Mongol army

battle:盐阜反“扫荡”.cmd: Chen Yi and Huang Kecheng vs. Japanese and puppet troops
battle:盐阜反“扫荡”.note: More than 10,000 Japanese and puppet troops converged on Yan-Fu along several routes, aiming to destroy the newly established headquarters of the New Fourth Army. The headquarters moved away while the main force harassed the enemy on exterior lines; the Japanese and puppet troops occupied Yancheng, Funing and other towns, but the anti-Japanese base area in the countryside was preserved.

battle:直皖战争.cmd: Wu Peifu, Cao Kun and Zhang Zuolin vs. Duan Qirui, Duan Zhigui and Xu Shuzheng
battle:直皖战争.note: The first large-scale war among the Beiyang warlords. The Anhui Clique's National Stabilization Army attacked in separate columns along the Beijing–Hankou and Beijing–Fengtian lines; Wu Peifu routed the main force of the western column at Zhuozhou, Gaobeidian and Songlindian and captured Qu Tongfeng, while the Fengtian Army supported him on the eastern front. The war was decided in five days: Duan Qirui stepped down, the Anfu Clique was dissolved, and the Beijing Government passed under the control of the Zhili and Fengtian Cliques.
battle:直皖战争.sides: Zhili and Fengtian Cliques defeated Anhui Clique

battle:直罗镇战役.cmd: Mao Zedong and Peng Dehuai vs. Niu Yuanfeng
battle:直罗镇战役.note: The first battle after the Red First Front Army joined forces with the Red 15th Army Group: it encircled and wiped out the Northeastern Army's 109th Division at Zhiluo Town, killing its commander Niu Yuanfeng, smashed the KMT forces' third “encirclement” campaign against the Shaanxi-Gansu Soviet Area, and laid the foundation stone for the Party Central Committee's establishment of the national headquarters of the revolution in the Northwest.

battle:直鲁联军复津之战.cmd: Zhang Zongchang, Li Jinglin and Chu Yupu vs. Lu Zhonglin
battle:直鲁联军复津之战.note: The Zhili-Shandong Allied Army attacked north along the Tianjin–Pukou line while the Fengtian Army pushed west from Shanhaiguan; on 23 March the Guominjun abandoned Tianjin and fell back to hold the capital region. In the Dagukou Incident Japan joined with the other powers to present an ultimatum. On 15 April the Guominjun withdrew from Beijing.

battle:石家庄战役.cmd: Yang Dezhi and Luo Ruiqing vs. Liu Ying
battle:石家庄战役.note: Using tunnelling and demolitions, the Shanxi-Chahar-Hebei Field Army broke through the outer and inner city trenches of Shimen; the defending commander Liu Ying was captured and Shijiazhuang was liberated. It was the first large, strongly fortified city taken by the People's Liberation Army, and it joined Shanxi-Chahar-Hebei and Shanxi-Hebei-Shandong-Henan into one.
battle:石家庄战役.sides: Shanxi-Chahar-Hebei Field Army defeated KMT forces

battle:砥平里之战.note: After the Hoengseong counter-attack the CPV besieged Jipyeong-ri, where the US 23rd Regiment and the French Battalion held a perimeter for three days and nights until the US 5th Cavalry Regiment broke through to relieve them. The CPV attack failed, and the “UN Command” forces then went over to the counter-attack.
battle:砥平里之战.sides: US and French forces defeated Chinese People's Volunteers

battle:硫磺岛战役.cmd: Holland Smith and Schmidt vs. Kuribayashi Tadamichi
battle:硫磺岛战役.mod: Iwo To (Iwo Jima), Ogasawara Village, Tokyo, Japan
battle:硫磺岛战役.note: Kuribayashi Tadamichi gave up the idea of a decisive battle on the beaches and resisted stubbornly from tunnels; almost all of the more than 20,000 Japanese were killed, while US casualties were about 26,000, so that total US casualties exceeded those of the Japanese. Once the island was taken, B-29s could make emergency landings there and gained fighter escorts.

battle:碾庄战役.note: First phase of the Huaihai Campaign. He Jifeng and Zhang Kexia led the troops of the 3rd Pacification Zone in an uprising at Tai'erzhuang and Jiawang; the East China Field Army crossed the Grand Canal and encircled Huang Baitao's army group at Nianzhuangxu, and Huang Baitao killed himself.
battle:碾庄战役.sides: East China Field Army defeated KMT forces

battle:磁武涉林战役.cmd: Liu Bocheng and Deng Xiaoping vs. Zhu Huaibing
battle:磁武涉林战役.mod: from Cixian, Hebei, to Linzhou, Henan
battle:磁武涉林战役.note: Zhu Huaibing's forces of the KMT diehards invaded the Taihang Anti-Japanese Base Area; the Eighth Route Army struck back in self-defence and routed the KMT 97th Army. Thereafter the two sides divided their garrison zones along the line of the Linfen–Tunliu road, Changzhi and Pingshun, and the first anti-Communist upsurge was beaten back.
battle:磁武涉林战役.sides: Eighth Route Army defeated KMT forces under Zhu Huaibing

battle:神头岭伏击战.cmd: Xu Xiangqian and Chen Geng vs. part of the Japanese 108th Division
battle:神头岭伏击战.note: The Eighth Route Army's 129th Division ambushed Japanese forces at Shentouling on the Handan–Changzhi road, wiping out more than 1,000 of the enemy and tying down the Japanese forces pushing south along the Datong–Puzhou Railway towards the Yellow River.
battle:神头岭伏击战.sides: Eighth Route Army defeated Japanese forces

battle:福州之役.cmd: Xu Chongzhi and Wang Yongquan vs. Li Houji
battle:福州之役.note: The Northern Expedition Army moved into Fujian and, together with Wang Yongquan, who was in contact with Xu Shuzheng, attacked Fuzhou from two sides; Li Houji fled, and Xu Chongzhi's forces were renamed the Eastern Route Anti-Rebel Army. This was the first joint action of the “anti-Zhili triangular alliance” of Sun Yat-sen, Duan Qirui and Zhang Zuolin.

battle:福州于山之战.cmd: Sun Daoren and Xu Chongzhi vs. Pushou
battle:福州于山之战.note: The New Army's 10th Division set up guns on Yushan and shelled the banner garrison; after a day of fierce fighting the bannermen surrendered, Pushou, the Fuzhou General, was killed and Songshou, Viceroy of Fujian and Zhejiang, took his own life, and the whole of Fujian was won for the revolution.

battle:秋收起义.cmd: Mao Zedong and Lu Deming vs. KMT forces of Hunan and Jiangxi
battle:秋收起义.note: Mao Zedong led the Autumn Harvest Uprising on the Hunan–Jiangxi border; the First Division of the Workers' and Peasants' Revolutionary Army rose in separate columns at Xiushui, Tonggu and Anyuan, and its attacks towards Changsha met one setback after another. On 19 September the remaining forces assembled at Wenjiashi, where Mao Zedong decided to give up the attack on Changsha and turn to the countryside, where enemy rule was weak, moving south into the middle section of the Luoxiao Mountains.
battle:秋收起义.sides: KMT forces of Hunan and Jiangxi defeated Workers' and Peasants' Revolutionary Army

battle:科布多之战.note: The Outer Mongolian “independence” regime sent troops to besiege the city of Kobdo; relief forces from Xinjiang and Altay were driven back outside the city in early August. The city fell on 20 August, the Councillor Purun was escorted out of the territory by the Russian consul, and the whole of western Outer Mongolia fell into the regime's hands.
battle:科布多之战.sides: Outer Mongolian army defeated Kobdo garrison

battle:科希马之战.note: The Japanese 31st Division surrounded the hill town of Kohima, where the garrison faced the Japanese at close quarters across the tennis court of the Deputy Commissioner's bungalow for two weeks. The British 2nd Division relieved the town and counter-attacked; the division commander Satō retreated against orders, and the Imphal–Kohima road was reopened.

battle:科科达小道之战.cmd: Rowell, Allen and Vasey vs. Horii Tomitarō
battle:科科达小道之战.note: The Japanese South Seas Detachment crossed the Owen Stanley Range from Buna and in September reached Ioribaiwa, only a few dozen kilometres from Port Moresby. Ordered to fall back because of the crisis on Guadalcanal, it was pursued by the Australians along the muddy mountain track, and Kokoda was retaken on 2 November.

battle:科雷吉多之战.note: After the fall of Bataan, the island fortress at the mouth of Manila Bay endured nearly a month of bombardment, and on the night of 5 May the Japanese landed. Wainwright surrendered the next day and, as ordered, had the US and Filipino forces on Mindanao and elsewhere surrender with him; the US-ruled Philippines fell.
battle:科雷吉多之战.sides: Japan defeated United States and the Philippines

battle:空山坝战役.note: The decisive battle of the Sichuan-Shaanxi Soviet Area's struggle against the three-route siege: the Red Fourth Front Army counter-attacked in the dense forest of Kongshanba and wiped out seven of Tian Songyao's regiments. Tian's forces withdrew from the Tongjiang–Nanjiang–Bazhong area, and the Sichuan-Shaanxi Soviet Area gained a firm foothold.
battle:空山坝战役.sides: Red Fourth Front Army defeated Sichuan Army

battle:第一、二次加沙之战.cmd: Murray and Dobell vs. Kress von Kressenstein
battle:第一、二次加沙之战.note: Two British frontal assaults on the Gaza–Beersheba line both failed; Murray was removed, and in June Allenby took over as commander of the Egyptian Expeditionary Force.
battle:第一、二次加沙之战.old: First and Second Battles of Gaza

battle:第一次印巴战争.cmd: Cariappa and Thimayya vs. Akbar Khan
battle:第一次印巴战争.note: Also called the First Kashmir War, a conflict sparked by the Kashmir question left behind by Britain's “divide and rule”. On 22 October Pashtun tribal forces invaded Kashmir and sacked Baramula; the Maharaja acceded to India on the 26th, and on the 27th Indian troops were airlifted to Srinagar. The two sides then fought back and forth along the line of Uri, Poonch and Ladakh, and the Pakistani regular army openly entered the war in May 1948. A ceasefire was reached through UN mediation on 1 January 1949.

battle:第一次直奉战争.cmd: Wu Peifu vs. Zhang Zuolin and Zhang Jinghui
battle:第一次直奉战争.note: The Fengtian Army advanced inside the Great Wall along the Beijing–Hankou and Tianjin–Pukou lines; Wu Peifu concentrated his main force for a counter-attack along the Changxindian–Gu'an line. Zhang Jinghui's western Fengtian column broke and fled, the eastern column then fell back along its whole front, and the Fengtian Army withdrew beyond the Great Wall. The Zhili Clique took sole control of the Beijing Government, and Zhang Zuolin declared the “autonomy” of the Three Northeastern Provinces.

battle:第一次粤桂战争.cmd: Chen Jiongming and Xu Chongzhi vs. Mo Rongxin and Ma Ji
battle:第一次粤桂战争.note: Under the slogan “Guangdong for the Guangdong people”, the Guangdong Army to Aid Fujian marched back from Zhangzhou into the Chaozhou–Shantou area and advanced west along the Dong River, entering Guangzhou on 29 October; Mo Rongxin withdrew to Guangxi. Sun Yat-sen returned to Guangdong in November and re-established the Military Government.

battle:第一次长沙会战.note: Japanese forces crossed the Xinqiang and Miluo Rivers southward in three columns; after reaching the northern outskirts of Changsha their rear came under attack, and they were forced to pull back to their original positions. The Chinese side called it the “Northern Hunan Victory”.

battle:第三次战役.mod: Imjin River, Paju, South Korea (around the 38th parallel)
battle:第三次战役.note: At dusk on 31 December the Chinese People's Volunteers and the Korean People's Army attacked all along the 38th parallel, breaking through the Imjin River line; they entered Seoul on 4 January 1951 and reached the vicinity of the 37th parallel.
battle:第三次战役.sides: Chinese People's Volunteers and Korean People's Army defeated “UN Command” forces

battle:第三次英阿战争.cmd: Barrett and Dyer vs. Nadir Khan
battle:第三次英阿战争.note: Amanullah proclaimed full independence and the Afghan people rose against Britain; Afghan troops crossed the Durand Line and occupied Bagh Springs, the British bombed Jalalabad and Kabul from the air, and Nadir Khan besieged the fort at Thal. A ceasefire took effect on 3 June, and in August, in the Treaty of Rawalpindi, Britain recognized Afghan independence.

battle:第三次长沙会战.note: Japanese forces drove south to keep Chinese forces from moving south to relieve Hong Kong; Xue Yue held the city and awaited reinforcements with his “Heavenly Furnace” tactics, and the Japanese, unable to take Changsha, were intercepted by Chinese columns from all sides and retreated in defeat. It was one of the Allies' rare victories in the early Pacific War.

battle:第二次江浙战争.cmd: Zhang Zongchang and Lu Yongxiang vs. Qi Xieyuan
battle:第二次江浙战争.note: Duan Qirui removed Qi Xieyuan as Military Governor of Jiangsu and made Lu Yongxiang Pacification Commissioner for Jiangsu and Anhui, and Zhang Zongchang's Fengtian Army followed him south along the Tianjin–Pukou line. Qi Xieyuan abandoned Nanjing and fell back to Shanghai, but was soon defeated and fled; the Fengtian Army entered Shanghai on 28 January, and the power of the Fengtian Clique reached the lower Yangtze.

battle:第二次直奉战争.cmd: Zhang Zuolin, Zhang Xueliang, Guo Songling and Feng Yuxiang vs. Wu Peifu
battle:第二次直奉战争.note: The Fengtian Army attacked the Zhili forces along two routes, through Rehe and at Shanhaiguan, fighting fiercely at Jiumenkou and Shimenzhai and breaking through at Jiumenkou in early October. On 23 October Feng Yuxiang turned his army back and launched the Beijing Coup; attacked front and rear, the Zhili Army collapsed along its whole front, and on 3 November Wu Peifu fled south by sea from Tanggu.
battle:第二次直奉战争.sides: Fengtian Clique and Guominjun defeated Zhili Clique

battle:第二次粤桂战争.cmd: Chen Jiongming, Xu Chongzhi and Ye Ju vs. Lu Rongting, Tan Haoming and Shen Hongying
battle:第二次粤桂战争.note: Lu Rongting attacked Guangdong along several routes; the Guangdong Army went over from defence to attack and took Wuzhou in June, Liu Zhenhuan's Guangxi troops changed sides, and in early August the Guangdong Army entered Nanning; Lu Rongting fled. The Old Guangxi Clique's ten-year rule of Guangxi came to an end, and Guangxi was carved up among assorted Self-Government Armies.

battle:第二次郑州战役.note: Japanese forces crossed the Yellow River southward from Zhongmu and took Zhengzhou on 4 October; after setting up a bridgehead at Mangshantou they withdrew to the north bank at the end of the month. Zhengzhou was lost and regained, and did not fall again until the Battle of Central Henan in 1944.

battle:第二次长沙会战.note: Four Japanese divisions forced crossings of the Xinqiang and Miluo Rivers and on 27 September briefly broke into Changsha, but with their rear under attack and supplies failing they fell back to Yueyang in early October. Both sides claimed victory.

battle:米尔恩湾之战.cmd: Clowes vs. Japanese naval landing forces
battle:米尔恩湾之战.note: Japanese naval landing troops came ashore at the eastern tip of New Guinea, aiming to seize the airfields newly built by the Allies. Two Australian brigades, supported by US engineers and the Royal Australian Air Force, drove them back and the Japanese withdrew—the first time in the Pacific War that a Japanese landing operation had been completely defeated.

battle:粤北会战.note: Japanese forces drove north from Guangzhou, seeking to open the southern section of the Guangzhou–Hankou Railway and to support the operations in southern Guangxi; after reaching Yingde and Wengyuan they were checked by Chinese forces of the Fourth and Seventh War Zones and fell back.

battle:粤汉路南段作战.cmd: Xue Yue and Yu Hanmou vs. Japanese 20th and 23rd Armies
battle:粤汉路南段作战.note: To destroy the US airfields in the southeast and open the southern section of the Guangzhou–Hankou Railway, the Japanese advanced towards each other from north and south, taking Qujiang, Chenzhou and Lechang, and struck east at the airfields of Suichuan, Ganzhou and Nanxiong. Northern Guangdong and southern Jiangxi fell, and the Guangdong provincial government moved to Lianxian.
battle:粤汉路南段作战.old: Operations on the southern Guangzhou–Hankou Railway

battle:精河之战.cmd: Yang Zuanxu vs. Yuan Dahua and Yang Zengxin's forces
battle:精河之战.note: The Ili revolutionary army advanced east and fought fierce battles around Jinghe and Shaquanzi with Qing forces sent from Dihua, each side winning some and losing some. After the abdication of the Qing emperor a ceasefire was called and the two sides made peace; Ili was merged into Xinjiang, and Yang Zengxin took control of the whole province.

battle:红一方面军围攻长沙.cmd: Mao Zedong, Zhu De and Peng Dehuai vs. He Jian
battle:红一方面军围攻长沙.note: The Red First and Third Army Groups joined forces at Yonghe, Liuyang, to form the Red First Front Army and attacked Changsha again, but besieged it for more than ten days without taking it despite repeated assaults; Mao Zedong persuaded the Front Committee to lift the siege and turn to Jiangxi to attack Ji'an.
battle:红一方面军围攻长沙.old: Red First Front Army besieges Changsha
battle:红一方面军围攻长沙.sides: Hunan Army defeated Red First Front Army

battle:红三军团攻占长沙.cmd: Peng Dehuai and Teng Daiyuan vs. He Jian
battle:红三军团攻占长沙.note: Under the guidance of Li Lisan's “Left” adventurist errors, the Red Third Army Group moved south from Pingjiang and broke into Changsha on 27 July, setting up the Hunan Provincial Soviet Government; this was the only time during the Agrarian Revolutionary War that the Red Army captured a provincial capital. On 6 August it withdrew in the face of a Hunan Army counter-attack and shelling by imperialist warships.
battle:红三军团攻占长沙.old: Red Third Army Group captures Changsha
battle:红三军团攻占长沙.sides: Red Third Army Group defeated Hunan Army

battle:约阿夫行动.cmd: Yigal Allon vs. Egyptian Expeditionary Force
battle:约阿夫行动.note: Israeli forces broke through the Egyptian lines that cut off the Negev and took Beersheba on 21 October, splitting the Egyptian forces between the Gaza coast and the Faluja pocket; in early November the Egyptians withdrew from Majdal.

battle:纳溪之战.cmd: Cai E and Liu Cunhou vs. Zhang Jingyao and Wu Peifu
battle:纳溪之战.note: The main force of the National Protection Army, together with Liu Cunhou's Sichuan Army, attacked Luzhou without success and fell back to hold Naxi, fighting the Beiyang elite for more than a month; in mid-March it pulled back for a time to regroup, then counter-attacked successfully from 17 March, and at the end of the month the two sides ceased fire. Cai E took on a stronger enemy with weaker forces and pinned down the Beiyang main force.

battle:绥崇丹懋战役.cmd: Xu Xiangqian vs. Yang Sen and Liu Wenhui
battle:绥崇丹懋战役.note: Defying the Central Committee's policy of going north, Zhang Guotao led the Left Column south; the Red Fourth Front Army took Suijing, Chonghua, Danba and Maogong in succession, wiping out several thousand Sichuan troops, then turned east towards Tianquan and Lushan, bearing down on the Chengdu Plain.

battle:绥远战役.cmd: He Long and Nie Rongzhen vs. Fu Zuoyi
battle:绥远战役.note: Shanxi-Suiyuan and Shanxi-Chahar-Hebei troops advanced west along the Beiping–Suiyuan Railway and liberated Jining, Fengzhen and Zhuozishan, but failed to take Guisui and Baotou and lifted the sieges in December; Fu Zuoyi kept hold of Suiyuan.

battle:罗刘之战.note: Luo Peijin, Military Governor of Sichuan, sought to disband the Sichuan Army's 4th Division; Liu Cunhou led Sichuan troops to besiege the military governor's yamen, and street fighting raged in Chengdu for several days, burning down many homes. Beijing dismissed Luo Peijin and made Dai Kan acting military governor, and the Yunnan Army withdrew to southern Sichuan; so began the struggle of the Sichuan, Yunnan and Guizhou warlords for Sichuan.

battle:罗得岛登陆.note: Having launched the Italo-Turkish War, Italy landed troops on Rhodes, forced the garrison to surrender on 17 May and went on to occupy the Dodecanese islands one after another. After the Treaty of Ouchy in October, Italy stayed on in the name of “temporary occupation”, and formally acquired the islands under the Treaty of Lausanne in 1923.

battle:罗马尼之战.cmd: Murray and Chauvel vs. Kress von Kressenstein
battle:罗马尼之战.note: Ottoman and German forces moved on the canal again and were defeated by ANZAC mounted troops in the sand dunes at Romani. The British then advanced east, building a railway and a water pipeline as they went, took El Arish in December and Rafah in January 1917, and reached the border of Palestine.
battle:罗马尼之战.sides: Britain defeated Ottoman Empire and Germany

battle:美吉多战役.note: The British concentrated their forces on the coastal plain to break through, and the cavalry corps drove through the Carmel passes deep into the rear; the Ottoman Seventh and Eighth Armies were almost entirely destroyed. The Palestine front collapsed, and a month later the Ottomans sued for peace.
battle:美吉多战役.sides: Britain defeated Ottoman Empire and Germany

battle:耶路撒冷之战.cmd: Shaltiel vs. Abdullah al-Tall and Glubb
battle:耶路撒冷之战.note: After the British withdrew, the Haganah and the Arab Legion fought for Jerusalem; on 28 May the Arab Legion forced the Jewish Quarter of the Old City to surrender, while the Israelis built the “Burma Road” to bypass Latrun and supply the western city. After the ceasefire the city was divided into east and west.

battle:耶路撒冷战役.note: The British pressed forward through the Judaean Hills; on 9 December the mayor of Jerusalem came out of the city to surrender, and on the 11th Allenby entered on foot by the Jaffa Gate. At the end of the month the British beat off an Ottoman counter-attack.
battle:耶路撒冷战役.sides: Britain defeated Ottoman Empire and Germany

battle:聊城保卫战.cmd: Fan Zhuxian vs. Japanese and puppet troops
battle:聊城保卫战.note: Fan Zhuxian, Commissioner for Northwestern Shandong, refused to withdraw south and kept up the resistance behind enemy lines; he led his forces in a fight to the death at Liaocheng and died for his country when the town fell. The anti-Japanese guerrilla area of northwestern Shandong then passed under CPC leadership.

battle:胡康河谷之战.cmd: Sun Liren, Liao Yaoxiang and Stilwell vs. Tanaka Shin'ichi
battle:胡康河谷之战.note: The New 38th and New 22nd Divisions of the Chinese Army in India struck out from Ledo in a counter-offensive, defeating the Japanese 18th Division at Yupbang, Maingkwan and Walawbum in turn, with the American Merrill's Marauders making outflanking moves in support. The China–India Road advanced with the troops, and the counter-offensive in northern Burma got under way.
battle:胡康河谷之战.sides: Chinese Army in India and US forces defeated Japanese forces

battle:胡憨之战.cmd: Hu Jingyi and Yue Weijun vs. Han Yukun and Liu Zhenhua
battle:胡憨之战.note: Hu Jingyi of the Guominjun Second Army and Han Yukun of the Zhensong Army fought for Henan, clashing fiercely between Zhengzhou and Luoyang; in early April the Zhensong Army collapsed, Han Yukun killed himself and Liu Zhenhua withdrew from Shaanxi. Hu Jingyi died of illness on 10 April, and Yue Weijun succeeded him as Military Commissioner of Henan.

battle:腊子口战役.cmd: Lin Biao and Yang Chengwu vs. Lu Dachang
battle:腊子口战役.note: Lazikou was a natural stronghold on the Sichuan–Gansu border, where the mouth of the gorge was little more than 30 metres wide. The Red 4th Regiment combined a frontal assault with a flanking climb up the cliffs and broke through the line of Lu Dachang's KMT New 14th Division in a single night, clearing away the last natural barrier on the Central Red Army's march north.

battle:腊戍失守.cmd: Watanabe Masao vs. Zhang Zhen (66th Army) and Gan Lichu (6th Army)
battle:腊戍失守.note: The Japanese 56th Division, riding in lorries, struck east from Toungoo into the Shan States and drove north through Loikaw and Loilem, taking Lashio, the starting point of the Burma Road, on 29 April and cutting the Chinese Expeditionary Force's line of retreat. The main force of the Fifth Army was forced to withdraw to India through the Yeren Mountains instead, and in May the Japanese pursued as far as the Huitong Bridge on the Nu River.
battle:腊戍失守.sides: Japanese forces defeated Chinese Expeditionary Force

battle:腾冲战役.cmd: Huo Kuizhang vs. Kurashige Yasumi and Ōta Masato
battle:腾冲战役.note: After crossing the Gaoligong Mountains, the Expeditionary Force's 20th Army Group besieged Tengchong and fought house to house in its streets for more than forty days, wiping out the Japanese garrison. The town of Tengchong was almost reduced to scorched earth; it was the most savage assault on a city in the Western Yunnan counter-offensive.

battle:芒市、畹町之战.mod: from Mangshi to Wanding, Ruili, Yunnan
battle:芒市、畹町之战.note: On 20 November Chinese forces recovered Mangshi, and on 20 January 1945 they took Wanding; Japanese forces withdrew into Burma. All Chinese territory in western Yunnan had been recovered, and the China–India Road opened to traffic soon afterwards.

battle:芒扬山口之战.cmd: Barrou vs. Viet Minh Interzone V forces
battle:芒扬山口之战.mod: Mang Yang Pass, Gia Lai, Vietnam
battle:芒扬山口之战.note: French Groupement Mobile 100 was ordered to withdraw from An Khê and was ambushed on Route 19 on 24 June, losing all its vehicles and guns; its remnants were intercepted again at the Mang Yang Pass, and on 17 July they were hit once more at the Chu Dreh Pass on the road to Ban Mê Thuột, and the group was almost entirely destroyed. It was the last major battle of the Vietnamese people's war of resistance against France.
battle:芒扬山口之战.sides: Vietnam People's Army defeated French forces

battle:花县之战.cmd: Chen Jitang and Jiang Guangnai vs. Zhang Fakui and Li Zongren
battle:花县之战.note: Zhang Fakui's forces and the Guangxi Army formed the Party-Protecting National Salvation Army and attacked east towards Guangzhou, but were defeated around Huaxian and Conghua by the Guangdong Army and Central Army reinforcements and fell back to Guangxi; Chen Jitang thereby secured his hold on Guangdong.
battle:花县之战.sides: Guangdong Army defeated Zhang Fakui–Guangxi Allied Army

battle:苏中战役.cmd: Su Yu and Tan Zhenlin vs. Li Mo'an
battle:苏中战役.note: With a force of more than 30,000, the Central China Field Army won seven victories in seven battles at Xuanjiabu, south of Rugao, Hai'an, Libao, Dingyan, Shaobo and on the Rugao–Huangqiao road, wiping out more than 50,000 of the KMT forces, but in the end, heavily outnumbered, it withdrew from central Jiangsu.
battle:苏中战役.sides: Central China Field Army defeated KMT forces

battle:苏伊士运河之战.cmd: Maxwell vs. Djemal Pasha and Kress von Kressenstein
battle:苏伊士运河之战.note: The Ottoman Fourth Army crossed Sinai carrying pontoons, intending to force the canal and stir up a rising in Egypt, but was driven back by British Indian troops. Thereafter the two sides faced each other across Sinai for more than a year.

battle:苏军出兵东北.note: Three Soviet fronts, more than a million men, drove into Northeast China in a pincer from three sides—from Transbaikalia, from Primorye and across the Heilong River—while Mongolian troops entered northern Chahar. The Kwantung Army, its fighting strength hollowed out, collapsed within little more than ten days; from 19 August Japanese troops everywhere surrendered one after another.

battle:苏家埠战役.note: The Red Fourth Front Army besieged Sujiabu and Hanbaidu, besieging strongpoints to strike at relief forces, and wiped out more than 30,000 men of the KMT forces, capturing the commander-in-chief Li Shiding. The Hubei-Henan-Anhui Soviet Area reached its height, and the KMT forces promptly launched the fourth “encirclement” campaign.
battle:苏家埠战役.sides: Red Fourth Front Army defeated KMT forces

battle:英伊战争.cmd: Smart and Clark vs. Rashid Ali
battle:英伊战争.note: In April the pro-Axis Rashid Ali seized power in a coup, and Iraqi troops besieged RAF Habbaniya; the garrison struck out and counter-attacked, and British relief forces closed on Baghdad from Transjordan and from Basra. German and Italian air support was of no avail; an armistice was concluded on 31 May, followed at once by the “Farhud” riots against the Jews of Baghdad.

battle:英帕尔战役.cmd: Slim and Scoones vs. Mutaguchi Ren'ya
battle:英帕尔战役.note: Three divisions of the Japanese 15th Army crossed the Chindwin River and the Arakan Mountains to attack Imphal, aiming to cut off the Allied base area on the Indian side; the British, supplied by air, held the basin.
