When the monsoon came, the Japanese, out of food, broke and retreated, with more than 60,000 killed, wounded or dead of sickness and starvation—one of the worst defeats in the history of the Japanese army.

battle:英苏出兵伊朗.cmd: Quinan, Slim and Kozlov vs. Iranian army
battle:英苏出兵伊朗.note: On the grounds of expelling German nationals and opening a supply route to the Soviet Union, British forces invaded Khuzestan and Kermanshah from Iraq and the Persian Gulf, while Soviet forces came south from Transcaucasia and Central Asia. The Iranian army collapsed within days; Reza Shah abdicated on 16 September, and on the 17th British and Soviet troops entered Tehran.
battle:英苏出兵伊朗.sides: Britain and Soviet Union defeated Iran

battle:茅溪战役.cmd: de Lattre vs. Võ Nguyên Giáp
battle:茅溪战役.mod: Mạo Khê, Đông Triều, Quảng Ninh, Vietnam
battle:茅溪战役.note: Called the “Hoàng Hoa Thám Campaign” by the Vietnamese: the Vietnamese forces switched their attack to the coal-mining area of Mạo Khê on the northeastern edge of the delta; the French supported the garrison with naval guns and aircraft, and the Vietnamese forces withdrew after several assaults failed.
battle:茅溪战役.sides: French forces defeated Vietnam People's Army

battle:草台岗战斗.cmd: Zhou Enlai and Zhu De vs. Chen Cheng (Xiao Qian)
battle:草台岗战斗.note: The Red Army again ambushed Chen Cheng's 11th Division, at Caotaigang and Xuzhuang, mauling this main force of the “Tumu Clique”, and the fourth “encirclement” campaign collapsed. Chen Cheng wrote in a letter: “This defeat fills me with the deepest shame.”
battle:草台岗战斗.sides: Red First Front Army defeated KMT forces

battle:荷兰第一次殖民战争.note: Called a “police action” by the Netherlands and code-named Operation Product by the Dutch army. Tearing up the Linggadjati Agreement, the Dutch seized within two weeks the plantations, oilfields and ports of West Java, East Java and Sumatra, and the Republic fell back to Central Java and the interior of Sumatra. The UN Security Council intervened, a ceasefire took effect on 4 August, and the Renville Agreement was concluded in January of the following year.
battle:荷兰第一次殖民战争.sides: Dutch forces defeated Indonesian Republican Army

battle:荷兰第二次殖民战争.note: Called the second “police action” by the Netherlands and code-named Operation Kraai by the Dutch army: paratroopers dropped on Maguwo airfield at Yogyakarta and captured Sukarno, Hatta and other members of the cabinet, and the Dutch soon occupied all the Republic's cities. Sudirman, though ill, led a guerrilla war; the resistance of the Indonesian soldiers and people, together with international opinion and the pressure of a US suspension of aid, forced the Netherlands to withdraw from Yogyakarta in June 1949.
battle:荷兰第二次殖民战争.sides: Dutch forces defeated Indonesian Republican Army

battle:莱亚行动.note: Called the Việt Bắc Autumn–Winter Campaign by the Vietnamese. French paratroopers dropped on Bắc Kạn, while two columns advancing along the Lô River and the Cao Bằng road closed in on the Việt Bắc Base Area, almost capturing Hồ Chí Minh. The main force of the Vietnam People's Army dispersed, shifted its ground and counter-attacked; the French occupied Cao Bằng, Đông Khê and other posts on the Sino-Vietnamese border and then pulled back, and the Việt Bắc Base Area survived.

battle:莱城之战.cmd: Blamey and Vasey vs. Adachi Hatazō
battle:莱城之战.note: The Australian 9th Division landed from the sea and US paratroopers dropped at Nadzab, closing on Lae from two directions; the Japanese abandoned the town and fled north over the Saruwaged Range. The Allies went on to take Finschhafen and gained control of the Vitiaz Strait.
battle:莱城之战.sides: Australia and United States defeated Japan

battle:莱特湾海战.cmd: Halsey and Kinkaid vs. Kurita Takeo, Ozawa Jisaburō and Nishimura Shōji
battle:莱特湾海战.note: The largest naval battle in history. The Japanese used their aircraft carriers to lure away the US Third Fleet, and Kurita's force passed through the San Bernardino Strait to close on the landing area, only to turn back off Samar; the Musashi, four aircraft carriers and Nishimura's force were destroyed, and the Japanese Combined Fleet lost its fighting capacity for good. The kamikaze special attacks began with this battle.

battle:莱罗斯岛战役.note: After Italy's surrender the British hurried to occupy Kos, Leros and other Dodecanese islands, and Samos; the Germans retook Kos and then attacked Leros with paratroopers and landing forces, the British and Italian garrison surrendered, and the British then evacuated Samos. The Aegean islands remained in German hands until 1945.

battle:莱芜战役.cmd: Chen Yi and Su Yu vs. Li Xianzhou and Wang Yaowu
battle:莱芜战役.note: The East China Field Army gave up Linyi of its own accord, and its main force moved secretly north to encircle Li Xianzhou's group as it pushed south, wiping out more than 50,000 men in three days and capturing Li Xianzhou; the western section of the Qingdao–Jinan Railway was liberated for a time.
battle:莱芜战役.sides: East China Field Army defeated KMT forces

battle:莲塘、良村、黄陂战斗.cmd: Mao Zedong and Zhu De vs. Shangguan Yunxiang, Hao Mengling and Mao Bingwen
battle:莲塘、良村、黄陂战斗.note: In the third counter-“encirclement” campaign the Red Army marched back a thousand li and thrust east through a gap between heavy concentrations of KMT forces, winning three battles in five days at Liantang, Liangcun and Huangpi and wiping out more than 10,000 men of the KMT forces, which reversed its passive situation.
battle:莲塘、良村、黄陂战斗.old: Battles of Liantang, Liangcun and Huangpi
battle:莲塘、良村、黄陂战斗.sides: Red First Front Army defeated KMT forces

battle:菲律宾海海战.cmd: Spruance and Mitscher vs. Ozawa Jisaburō
battle:菲律宾海海战.mod: Philippine Sea (west of the Mariana Islands)
battle:菲律宾海海战.note: The Japanese navy threw all its aircraft carriers against the Saipan landing; its carrier aircraft were shot down in great numbers by radar-directed US fighters and the fleet's anti-aircraft fire, in what was dubbed the “Great Marianas Turkey Shoot”; the Taihō and Shōkaku were sunk by submarines and the Hiyō by US aircraft. From then on Japanese carrier aviation existed in name only.

battle:萨勒卡默什战役.note: Enver personally led the Third Army over the mountains in the depths of winter to outflank Sarıkamış, losing most of it to cold, hunger and battle; the Ottoman offensive in the Caucasus collapsed. Afterwards the authorities blamed the defeat on Armenian “collaboration with the enemy”.

battle:萨卡里亚战役.cmd: Mustafa Kemal and İsmet vs. Papoulas
battle:萨卡里亚战役.note: Having taken Eskişehir and Kütahya in July, the Greek army drove on Ankara and fought hard for twenty-two days along the Sakarya River before withdrawing, exhausted. The Grand National Assembly conferred on Kemal the title of “Gazi”; in October France made peace with Ankara.

battle:萨达拉巴德之战.cmd: Nazarbekian and Silikian vs. Vehip Pasha
battle:萨达拉巴德之战.note: Taking advantage of the disintegration of the Russian army, Ottoman forces invaded Transcaucasia; the Armenian soldiers and people made a last-ditch stand at Sardarabad west of Erivan and at the same time held the enemy at Bash Abaran and Karakilisa, saving Erivan. Armenia declared independence on 28 May.

battle:蒋冯战争.cmd: Chiang Kai-shek and Tang Shengzhi vs. Song Zheyuan and Sun Liangcheng
battle:蒋冯战争.note: Song Zheyuan and others denounced Chiang by circular telegram; the Northwestern Army came out through Tong Pass and pushed east into western Henan, fighting the Central Army and Tang Shengzhi's forces fiercely for more than a month around Luoyang, Dengfeng and Linru, and in late November was defeated and fell back west of Tong Pass.
battle:蒋冯战争.sides: Chiang Kai-shek's Central Army defeated Northwestern Army

battle:蒋桂战争.cmd: Chiang Kai-shek vs. Li Zongren, Hu Zongduo and Xia Wei
battle:蒋桂战争.note: The beginning of the wars among the new warlords. Nanjing launched a punitive expedition against the Guangxi Clique on the pretext of the Hunan Incident; Li Mingrui and other Guangxi Army commanders in Hubei were bought over and changed sides, Hu Zongduo and Tao Jun withdrew west with their troops, and on 5 April the Central Army entered Wuhan without a fight. The Guangxi Clique lost Hunan, Hubei and eastern Hebei.
battle:蒋桂战争.sides: Chiang Kai-shek's Central Army defeated New Guangxi Clique

battle:蒙达之战.note: US forces landed on New Georgia and fought hard in the jungle for more than a month to capture the Japanese airfield at Munda. Thereafter the Solomons campaign switched to island-hopping, bypassing Kolombangara and other heavily garrisoned Japanese islands.

battle:虎头要塞战斗.cmd: Zakhvatayev vs. Japanese 15th Border Garrison Unit
battle:虎头要塞战斗.note: The Hutou Fortress faced the Soviet town of Iman across the Ussuri River. The Japanese garrison and the Japanese civilians who had taken refuge there refused to believe the news of the surrender and held out until 26 August, when almost all were wiped out. It is called “the place where the Second World War ended”.

battle:衡宝战役.note: The Fourth Field Army wiped out more than 40,000 men of Bai Chongxi's group, including its main force, the 7th Army, between Hengyang and Baoqing; Bai Chongxi's forces fell back into Guangxi, and most of Hunan was liberated.
battle:衡宝战役.sides: Fourth Field Army defeated Bai Chongxi's forces

battle:衡阳之战（1930）.cmd: Jiang Guangnai and Cai Tingkai vs. Li Zongren, Bai Chongxi and Zhang Fakui
battle:衡阳之战（1930）.note: The Guangxi–Zhang Fakui Army marched north in support of Yan and Feng, taking Changsha and Yueyang in quick succession in early June; the Guangdong Army struck into the gap behind it and seized Hengyang, cutting its line of retreat. The Guangxi–Zhang Fakui Army turned back and stormed Hengyang without success, suffering heavy casualties, and withdrew to Guangxi.
battle:衡阳之战（1930）.sides: Guangdong Army defeated Guangxi–Zhang Fakui Army

battle:衡阳保卫战.note: Fang Xianjue's Tenth Army, more than 10,000 strong, held the isolated city to the death for forty-seven days, inflicting more than 10,000 casualties on the Japanese; relief never came, and on 8 August Fang Xianjue and others ceased resistance. It was the longest defence of a city by Chinese forces in the War of Resistance.

battle:襄樊战役.note: The Central Plains Field Army took Xiangyang and Fancheng and captured Kang Ze, commander of the 15th Pacification Zone; northern Hubei and southwestern Henan were joined into one.
battle:襄樊战役.sides: Central Plains Field Army defeated KMT forces

battle:西北战役.note: Three divisions of the Vietnam People's Army crossed the Red River and took Nghĩa Lộ on 17 October; the French abandoned Sơn La and other posts and fell back to Nà Sản, and the Vietnamese forces entered Điện Biên Phủ at the end of November. Most of the Thái areas of the northwest were liberated, leaving the French only Nà Sản and Lai Châu, and the Vietnamese opened the road into Upper Laos.
battle:西北战役.sides: Vietnam People's Army defeated French forces

battle:西安起义.cmd: Zhang Fenghui and Qian Ding vs. Wenrui
battle:西安起义.note: The New Army and the Elder Brothers Society rose in response to the Wuchang Uprising and stormed the Manchu quarter; Wenrui, the Xi'an General, drowned himself in a well. Shaanxi was the first province in the north to be won for the revolution; holding Tong Pass to the east and keeping the Gansu Army at bay to the west, it tied the Qing court down with worries on its western flank.

battle:西征.cmd: Peng Dehuai vs. Ma Hongkui and Ma Hongbin
battle:西征.note: On its Western Expedition into the Shaanxi–Gansu–Ningxia border area, the Red First Front Army took Dingbian, Yanchi, Yuwang and other towns, nearly doubling the size of the Soviet Area, and around Yuwang prepared to receive the Second and Fourth Front Armies coming north.
battle:西征.sides: Red Army defeated Ningxia Ma army

battle:西昌战役.cmd: Chen Geng vs. Hu Zongnan and He Guoguang
battle:西昌战役.note: The Second Field Army closed in on Xichang along several routes; Hu Zongnan flew out on 26 March, and Xichang was liberated on 27 March. Resistance by organized KMT formations on the mainland was essentially at an end.

battle:西路讨贼之役.cmd: Yang Ximin, Liu Zhenhuan and Shen Hongying vs. Chen Jiongming and Ye Ju
battle:西路讨贼之役.note: Sun Yat-sen formed the Western Route Anti-Rebel Army from Yang Ximin's Yunnan Army and the Guangxi Armies of Liu Zhenhuan and Shen Hongying; it moved east down the Xi River from Wuzhou, part of the Guangdong Army rose in support in Guangzhou, and Chen Jiongming withdrew to Huizhou on 15 January. Sun Yat-sen returned to Guangdong in February, and from then on the Yunnan and Guangxi guest armies entrenched themselves in Guangzhou.

battle:讨石之战.cmd: Zhang Xueliang and Yu Xuezhong vs. Shi Yousan
battle:讨石之战.note: Commissioned by the Guangzhou Nationalist Government, Shi Yousan attacked north from Shunde towards Baoding, aiming to seize Beiping and Tianjin; the Northeastern Army and the Central Army coming north attacked him from north and south, Shi's forces collapsed in early August, and Shi Yousan fled alone to Shandong.
battle:讨石之战.sides: Northeastern Army and Central Army defeated Shi Yousan's forces

battle:讨贼之役（四川）.cmd: Yang Sen, Liu Xiang, Deng Xihou and Yuan Zuming vs. Xiong Kewu, Liu Chengxun and Lai Xinhui
battle:讨贼之役（四川）.note: Appointed by Sun Yat-sen commander-in-chief of the Sichuan Anti-Rebel Army, Xiong Kewu fought back and forth over Chengdu and Chongqing with Yang Sen, Liu Xiang and Yuan Zuming's Guizhou Army, who were backed by Wu Peifu. In early 1924 the Anti-Rebel Army was defeated and Xiong Kewu led his troops through Guizhou into Hunan, while Yang Sen entered Chengdu as military superintendent.
battle:讨贼之役（四川）.sides: Yang Sen and Liu Xiang defeated Xiong Kewu

battle:讨逆之战.cmd: Duan Qirui, Duan Zhigui and Cao Kun vs. Zhang Xun
battle:讨逆之战.note: Zhang Xun restored Puyi to the throne on 1 July; on 3 July Duan Qirui swore in the Anti-Restoration Army at Machang, and it attacked Langfang and Fengtai along separate routes and broke into Beijing on 12 July; Zhang Xun fled into the Netherlands Legation. Styling himself the man who had “recreated the Republic”, Duan Qirui took charge of the government again, but soon refused to restore the parliament and the Provisional Constitution, setting off the Constitution Protection Movement.

battle:诺门罕战役.mod: Khalkhin Gol, Dornod Province, Mongolia (east of Nomonhan, New Barag Left Banner, Inner Mongolia)
battle:诺门罕战役.note: Known in the Soviet Union as the Battle of Khalkhin Gol. Japan's Kwantung Army provoked a border conflict and fought Soviet and Mongolian forces on a large scale on both banks of the Khalkhin Gol; on 20 August Zhukov encircled the Japanese 23rd Division with massed tanks and all but annihilated it. A ceasefire took effect on 16 September, and Japan thereafter turned to the “southern advance”.
battle:诺门罕战役.sides: Soviet Union and Mongolia defeated Japan and Puppet Manchukuo

battle:谅山之战.note: On the night the Franco-Japanese agreement was signed, the 5th Division of the Japanese invading troops crossed the border from Zhennan Pass in Guangxi into northern Vietnam and besieged Đồng Đăng and Lạng Sơn; the French surrendered after several hundred casualties. The Japanese then landed at Hải Phòng, and the supply route to China along the Yunnan–Vietnam Railway was cut.

battle:谭赵战争.cmd: Zhao Hengti vs. Tan Yankai and Lu Diping
battle:谭赵战争.note: Appointed by Sun Yat-sen Civil Governor of Hunan and commander-in-chief of the Hunan Anti-Rebel Army, Tan Yankai joined forces with the Hunan Army units opposed to Zhao and briefly broke into Changsha in August; Wu Peifu sent troops to Zhao's aid, and Tan's army was defeated and fell back, entering Guangdong in November, where it was later reorganized as the Hunan National Construction Army.

battle:象岛海战.note: The French light cruiser Lamotte-Picquet led a small squadron in a surprise attack on the Ko Chang anchorage, crippling the Thai coastal defence ship Thonburi, which ran aground, and sinking two torpedo boats without loss to itself. Though France won at sea, Thailand's gains on land were still confirmed through Japanese mediation.

battle:豫东战役（睢杞）.cmd: Su Yu vs. Ou Shounian and Huang Baitao
battle:豫东战役（睢杞）.note: Seizing the chance offered by the KMT reinforcement of Kaifeng, the East China Field Army encircled and wiped out Ou Shounian's army group between Suixian and Qixian, capturing Ou Shounian; Huang Baitao's army group came to the rescue, and after fierce fighting the two sides broke contact. In all, the Eastern Henan Campaign wiped out more than 90,000 of the KMT forces.
battle:豫东战役（睢杞）.sides: East China Field Army defeated KMT forces

battle:豫中会战.cmd: Jiang Dingwen and Tang Enbo vs. Okamura Yasuji
battle:豫中会战.note: The first phase of the Henan–Hunan–Guangxi Campaign (Operation Ichi-gō to the Japanese): Japanese forces crossed the river from Zhongmu, took Zhengzhou, Xuchang, Dengfeng and Luoyang in succession, and linked up at Queshan with the enemy coming north from Xinyang, opening up the Beiping–Hankou Railway. In thirty-odd days the KMT forces lost more than thirty towns, and routed soldiers were disarmed by starving peasants.

battle:豫南会战.cmd: Tang Enbo and Li Zongren vs. Sonobe Waichirō
battle:豫南会战.note: The Japanese 11th Army drove north from Xinyang along the Beiping–Hankou Railway, seeking to encircle and destroy Tang Enbo's army group. The Chinese forces avoided a head-on clash and struck at the enemy's flanks and rear; after taking Wuyang, Shangcai and other places Japanese forces returned to their original positions.

battle:豫西鄂北会战.cmd: Liu Zhi and Hu Zongnan vs. Takamori Takashi
battle:豫西鄂北会战.note: The Japanese 12th Army attacked Xixiakou and Laohekou in several columns, aiming to destroy the US airfield at Laohekou. Laohekou fell on 8 April; Chinese forces held off the attack on the Xixiakou line and counter-attacked to retake some positions.
battle:豫西鄂北会战.old: Battle of Western Henan and Northern Hubei

battle:贝尔谢巴—加沙之战.cmd: Allenby and Chauvel vs. Kress von Kressenstein
battle:贝尔谢巴—加沙之战.note: On 31 October the 4th Australian Light Horse Brigade charged at dusk to seize the wells of Beersheba, turning the flank of Gaza; on 7 November the Ottoman forces abandoned Gaza and withdrew north, and on the 16th the British entered Jaffa.
battle:贝尔谢巴—加沙之战.sides: Britain defeated Ottoman Empire and Germany

battle:贝里琉之战.note: The island had been expected to fall within days, but the Japanese changed their tactics and held positions in depth in caves in the coral rock, and the US 1st Marine Division suffered more than 6,500 casualties. It took more than two months of hard fighting to clear the whole island, and the Japanese on Iwo Jima and Okinawa later adopted the same protracted defence.

battle:贺胜桥战役.cmd: Chen Keyu and Li Zongren vs. Wu Peifu
battle:贺胜桥战役.note: Wu Peifu came in person to direct the battle and had broadsword squads cut down retreating soldiers, but still could not hold back the fierce attack of the Fourth and Seventh Armies; his whole army fled back to Wuchang, and the Northern Expedition Army soon stood before the three cities of Wuhan.
battle:贺胜桥战役.sides: National Revolutionary Army defeated Wu Peifu's army

battle:赣州战役.note: Carrying out the “Left” policy of “seizing key cities”, the Central Bureau of the Soviet Areas ordered the Red First Front Army to attack Ganzhou; repeated assaults with tunnel mines failed, and when Chen Cheng's relief forces arrived the siege was lifted. Afterwards Mao Zedong's views prevailed for a time, and the Red Army marched east on Zhangzhou.

battle:赤塔战役.note: The People's Revolutionary Army twice attacked Chita without success; under the Gongota armistice the Japanese withdrew from Transbaikalia on 15 October, and on the 22nd the People's Revolutionary Army liberated Chita, Semyonov escaping by aeroplane. The “Chita cork” was pulled out, and the Far Eastern Republic moved its capital to Chita.

battle:车桥战役.cmd: Su Yu vs. Japanese and puppet troops
battle:车桥战役.note: The New Fourth Army's 1st Division took the Cheqiao strongpoint between Huai'an and Baoying and, striking at the relief force, wiped out part of the Japanese troops. It was the New Fourth Army's first assault on a fortified position on its own initiative, and from then on the Central Jiangsu and Huaihai anti-Japanese base areas were joined into one.
battle:车桥战役.sides: New Fourth Army defeated Japanese and puppet troops

battle:车里雅宾斯克战役.note: Kolchak's army tried to let the Red Army into the city and then encircle it, but was itself broken by the Red 5th Army, and its main force was badly weakened. From then on the Whites could not hold the Urals and fell back towards the Tobol River and Omsk.

battle:边界战役.cmd: Võ Nguyên Giáp vs. Carpentier, Lepage and Charton
battle:边界战役.note: With the assistance of the Chinese Military Advisory Group (Chen Geng), the Vietnam People's Army concentrated its main force to take Đông Khê, then on the Cao Bằng–Thất Khê road encircled and wiped out the Charton column withdrawing from Cao Bằng and the Lepage column coming north to meet it; the French lost about 5,000 men and then abandoned Lạng Sơn and Lào Cai. The Sino-Vietnamese border was opened, and the Vietnam People's Army went over to large-scale mobile warfare.
battle:边界战役.sides: Vietnam People's Army defeated French forces

battle:辽西围歼战.note: Liao Yaoxiang's army group, advancing west towards Jinzhou, was held up at Heishan and Dahushan and could not fall back to Yingkou in time; it was encircled and wiped out in western Liaoning by the main force of the Northeast Field Army, and Liao Yaoxiang was captured. Shenyang was liberated on 2 November, ending the Liaoshen Campaign.
battle:辽西围歼战.sides: Northeast Field Army defeated KMT forces

battle:迈兹赖阿之战.note: Druze rebels ambushed a French column marching to relieve Suwayda, inflicting heavy losses on the French. The great victory spread the uprising to Damascus and Hama, turning it into the Great Syrian Revolt.

battle:迈萨隆之战.cmd: Gouraud and Goybet vs. Yusuf al-Azma
battle:迈萨隆之战.note: On the basis of the San Remo resolution France sent an ultimatum to Faisal; the Syrian defence minister, Yusuf al-Azma, led the remnants of the army and volunteers to resist the French invading army at the Maysalun Pass, and was defeated and killed. On 25 July French troops entered Damascus, and Faisal went into exile.

battle:迪化之围.cmd: Sheng Shicai (with Soviet support) vs. Ma Zhongying
battle:迪化之围.note: Ma Zhongying besieged Dihua for the second time; Sheng Shicai appealed to the Soviet Union for help, and Soviet forces entered Xinjiang with aircraft and armoured cars and routed Ma's forces at the Toutun River. Ma Zhongying went south to Kashi; thereafter Sheng Shicai pursued a pro-Soviet policy, relying on the Soviet Union to consolidate his rule in Xinjiang.

battle:遵义战役.cmd: Peng Dehuai and Lin Biao vs. Wu Qiwei and Wang Jialie
battle:遵义战役.note: The Red Army occupied Zunyi again, routing the Guizhou Army at Laoyashan and Honghuagang and mauling two divisions of Wu Qiwei's Central Army column; it was the biggest victory since the start of the Long March.

battle:那产之战.note: Salan built an entrenched camp around the airfield at Nà Sản southeast of Sơn La, supplied entirely by air. Vietnamese night attacks at the end of November and in early December were twice repulsed; the French believed they had found the way to deal with the Vietnamese forces and copied the model at Điện Biên Phủ the following year, while Nà Sản itself was evacuated by air in August 1953.
battle:那产之战.sides: French forces defeated Vietnam People's Army

battle:邯郸战役.cmd: Liu Bocheng and Deng Xiaoping vs. Ma Fawu and Gao Shuxun
battle:邯郸战役.note: Also called the Beiping–Hankou Campaign. Three KMT armies advancing north along the Beiping–Hankou Railway were encircled on the Zhang River south of Handan; on 30 October Gao Shuxun, commander of the New 8th Army, led his forces in an uprising, Ma Fawu was captured, and the KMT plan to open the Beiping–Hankou Railway was thwarted.
battle:邯郸战役.sides: Eighth Route Army defeated KMT forces

battle:郭松龄反奉.cmd: Zhang Zuolin, Zhang Xueliang and Wu Junsheng vs. Guo Songling
battle:郭松龄反奉.note: Guo Songling, a Fengtian Army general, denounced Fengtian by circular telegram at Luanzhou and concluded a pact with Feng Yuxiang against Zhang; he took Shanhaiguan and Jinzhou and advanced to Juliuhe. The Japanese Kwantung Army intervened, blocking his advance on the grounds of the neutrality of the South Manchuria Railway Zone; Wu Junsheng's cavalry raided his rear at Baiqibao, Guo's army collapsed, and Guo Songling was captured on 24 December and killed on 25 December.

battle:鄂木斯克失陷.note: The Whites abandoned their “capital”, Omsk, and large numbers of men and quantities of supplies fell into Red Army hands; the Kolchak government had already moved east to Irkutsk, and the Whites retreated in disorder along the Trans-Siberian Railway in the depths of winter—the “Great Siberian Ice March”.

battle:鄂西会战.cmd: Chen Cheng (Sun Lianzhong) vs. Yokoyama Isamu
battle:鄂西会战.note: Japanese forces sought to destroy the Sixth War Zone forces on the south bank of the Yangtze and seize the shipping on the river. Hu Lian's 11th Division held Shipai Fortress to the death, and the Japanese, stalled before it, returned to their original positions. Shipai commanded the mouth of the Three Gorges and was the gateway to Chongqing.

battle:金城战役.note: The last large-scale offensive campaign before the armistice. The CPV 20th Army Group and other units broke through the lines of four ROK divisions in a single night and straightened out the salient south of Kumsong, gaining, according to Chinese statistics, from over 100 to more than 200 square kilometres of ground, and helping to bring about the signing of the Armistice Agreement on 27 July.
battle:金城战役.sides: Chinese People's Volunteers defeated ROK Army

battle:金宝之战.note: The 11th Indian Division used the hills at Kampar to hold off the Japanese 5th Division tenaciously for four days, the best battle the British fought in the Malayan campaign. The Japanese outflanked them by sea, the British were forced to withdraw south, and Kuala Lumpur could not be held either.

battle:金门战斗.cmd: Tang Enbo and Hu Lian vs. Ye Fei
battle:金门战斗.note: Three regiments of the Third Field Army's 28th Army and other units crossed the sea and landed at Guningtou on Kinmen; for lack of boats and with no follow-up support, the more than 9,000 men who landed were all killed in action or captured. Kinmen remained occupied by KMT forces for a long time afterwards.

battle:锦州之战.cmd: Rong Zhen (Northeastern Army) vs. Honjō Shigeru
battle:锦州之战.note: After Zhang Xueliang's Liaoning provincial government moved west to Jinzhou, the Japanese Kwantung Army pushed west in the name of “bandit suppression”; the Northeastern Army withdrew inside the Great Wall on orders, and on 3 January Japanese forces seized Jinzhou. With the gateway to western Liaoning lost, the main cities of the Three Northeastern Provinces fell one after another.

battle:锦州战役.cmd: Lin Biao and Luo Ronghuan vs. Fan Hanjie
battle:锦州战役.note: The Northeast Field Army took Jinzhou and captured Fan Hanjie, shutting the door through which the KMT forces in the Northeast could withdraw along the Beining Railway into North China; it was the key battle of the Liaoshen Campaign.
battle:锦州战役.sides: Northeast Field Army defeated KMT forces

battle:长乐村战斗.cmd: Liu Bocheng and Xu Xiangqian vs. Tomabechi Brigade, Japanese 108th Division
battle:长乐村战斗.note: Japanese forces attacked the Southeastern Shanxi Anti-Japanese Base Area along nine routes with 30,000 troops; the Eighth Route Army's 129th Division pursued and wiped out withdrawing Japanese troops at Changlecun, the other Japanese columns then fell back, and the Eighth Route Army followed up to recover more than ten county towns in southeastern Shanxi.
battle:长乐村战斗.sides: Eighth Route Army defeated Japanese forces

battle:长岭寨战斗.cmd: Zhu De and Mao Zedong vs. Guo Fengming
battle:长岭寨战斗.note: The Red Fourth Army's first battle in Fujian: at Changlingzhai outside Changting it wiped out the brigade of the local warlord Guo Fengming, killing Guo Fengming, and took Changting for the first time, raising a large sum for army pay and issuing new uniforms to the whole army.
battle:长岭寨战斗.sides: Red Fourth Army defeated Fujian Army

battle:长津湖战役.note: Eastern front of the Second Campaign. In bitter cold of more than thirty degrees below zero the CPV 9th Army Group besieged the US 1st Marine Division and part of the 7th Division beside Changjin Lake, destroying most of the 31st Regimental Combat Team; the 1st Marine Division broke out and withdrew south to Hungnam. The CPV suffered very heavy losses from frostbite, and the “UN Command” forces were driven out of northeastern Korea.
battle:长津湖战役.sides: Chinese People's Volunteers defeated US forces

battle:长衡会战.note: The second phase of the Henan–Hunan–Guangxi Campaign: the Japanese 11th Army drove south with eight divisions, took Changsha on 18 June and turned to attack Hengyang. Of the four battles of Changsha, Chinese forces won three and lost one; the gateways to northern and central Hunan lay wide open.

battle:阜宁战役.note: The 3rd Division of the New Fourth Army took the town of Funing, the central Japanese and puppet stronghold in the Yan-Fu area, joining the Yan-Fu Anti-Japanese Base Area into one and preparing for the capture of the towns of northern Jiangsu in the great counter-offensive of August.
battle:阜宁战役.sides: New Fourth Army defeated puppet troops

battle:阳夏战役.cmd: Feng Guozhang and Duan Qirui vs. Li Yuanhong and Huang Xing
battle:阳夏战役.note: Qing forces took Liujiamiao on 27 October, set fire to and sacked Hankou on 1 November and captured Hanyang on 27 November, but lacked the strength to cross the river and attack Wuchang. The revolutionary army held out for 41 days, buying time for the provinces to rise in response; Yuan Shikai, for his part, used the fighting to press the revolutionaries into peace talks under the threat of force.

battle:阿图岛之战.cmd: Kinkaid and Brown vs. Yamazaki Yasuyo
battle:阿图岛之战.note: The US 7th Infantry Division landed in icy fog; on the night of 29 May the remnants of the Japanese garrison launched a suicide charge, and of about 2,600 defenders only 28 were taken prisoner. For the first time Japan used the word “gyokusai” (“shattered jade”) in publicizing the annihilation of a garrison.

battle:阿德里安堡之围.cmd: Ivanov and Stepanović vs. Şükrü Pasha
battle:阿德里安堡之围.note: In the First Balkan War Bulgarian and Serbian forces besieged Edirne for five months, and the garrison surrendered on 26 March. In July of the same year, during the Second Balkan War, Enver seized the opening to recover the city, and the Ottomans kept Eastern Thrace.
battle:阿德里安堡之围.sides: Bulgaria and Serbia defeated Ottoman Empire

battle:阿扬战役.note: The White general Pepelyayev landed at Ayan with the Siberian Volunteer Army in September 1922, and his winter march into Yakutia was checked; the Red Army made a surprise attack on Ayan from the sea, and on 17 June Pepelyayev surrendered. It was one of the last actions of the Russian Civil War.
battle:阿扬战役.sides: Red Army defeated Siberian Volunteer Army

battle:陇海线会战.cmd: Chiang Kai-shek, Liu Zhi and Gu Zhutong vs. Feng Yuxiang, Sun Liangcheng and Ji Hongchang
battle:陇海线会战.note: The main battlefield of the Central Plains War, the largest of the wars among the new warlords. Several hundred thousand troops on the two sides surged back and forth among Guide, Lanfeng, Qixian and Taikang; at one point Northwestern Army cavalry raided Liuhe station and nearly captured Chiang Kai-shek. In August the Central Army launched a general offensive, and in early October it took Kaifeng and Zhengzhou.
battle:陇海线会战.sides: Chiang Kai-shek's Central Army defeated Northwestern and Shanxi Armies

battle:陈官庄战役.note: Du Yuming led the three army groups at Xuzhou out of the city and withdrew west, only to be encircled around Chenguanzhuang in Yongcheng; after more than a month trapped in wind and snow, Qiu Qingquan was killed and Du Yuming captured. The Huaihai Campaign ended in victory, and the KMT's crack forces north of the Yangtze River were all but wiped out.
battle:陈官庄战役.sides: East China Field Army defeated KMT forces

battle:陈庄战斗.cmd: He Long and Guan Xiangying vs. Mizuhara Yoshishige
battle:陈庄战斗.note: Japanese forces made a lightning raid on Chenzhuang, in the rear of the Shanxi-Chahar-Hebei Border Region; the Eighth Route Army's 120th Division and Shanxi-Chahar-Hebei units laid an ambush on their return route and wiped out more than 1,000 of the enemy, wounding the brigade commander Mizuhara.
battle:陈庄战斗.sides: Eighth Route Army defeated Japanese forces

battle:陕西靖国之战.cmd: Yu Youren, Hu Jingyi and Guo Jian vs. Chen Shufan, Liu Zhenhua and Xu Lanzhou
battle:陕西靖国之战.note: The Shaanxi Constitution Protection Army rose north of the Wei River; in August Yu Youren took office as commander-in-chief of the National Pacification Army, based at Sanyuan. Chen Shufan brought the Zhensong Army and the Fengtian Army into Shaanxi to attack it together, and the National Pacification Army held out with difficulty for three years; after the Zhili Clique entered Shaanxi in 1921, Hu Jingyi accepted reorganization and the rest of the army fell apart.

battle:随枣会战.note: Japanese forces attacked the Fifth War Zone between the Dahong Mountains and the Tongbai Mountains and for a time took Zaoyang, but fell back to the Suixian–Zhongxiang line in the face of Chinese counter-attacks; the two sides largely returned to their positions before the battle.

battle:雁宿崖、黄土岭战斗.note: Shanxi-Chahar-Hebei forces first wiped out a Japanese battalion at Yansuya, then ambushed the enemy force sent in retaliation at Huangtuling, killing Lieutenant-General Abe Norihide, commander of the Japanese 2nd Independent Mixed Brigade, with mortar fire.
battle:雁宿崖、黄土岭战斗.sides: Eighth Route Army defeated Japanese forces

battle:雁门关伏击战.cmd: He Long and He Bingyan vs. Japanese transport unit
battle:雁门关伏击战.note: The 716th Regiment of the Eighth Route Army's 120th Division twice ambushed Japanese transport columns travelling from Datong to Xinkou on the road south of Yanmen Pass, cutting their rear supply lines in support of the Battle of Xinkou on the frontal battlefield.
battle:雁门关伏击战.sides: Eighth Route Army defeated Japanese forces

battle:集宁之战.cmd: Nie Rongzhen and He Long vs. Fu Zuoyi
battle:集宁之战.note: While Shanxi-Chahar-Hebei and Shanxi-Suiyuan troops were besieging Datong, Fu Zuoyi came east from Guisui to its relief and occupied Jining on 13 September; the Shanxi-Chahar-Hebei and Shanxi-Suiyuan troops lifted the siege of Datong, and the western gateway to Zhangjiakou lay wide open.
battle:集宁之战.sides: Fu Zuoyi's forces defeated Shanxi-Chahar-Hebei and Shanxi-Suiyuan forces

battle:霍雷夫行动.cmd: Yigal Allon vs. Egyptian Expeditionary Force
battle:霍雷夫行动.note: Israeli forces outflanked Auja and for a time pushed into Sinai as far as the vicinity of El Arish, withdrawing under British pressure. Egypt agreed to negotiate, and on 24 February 1949 an armistice agreement was signed on Rhodes, placing the Gaza Strip under Egyptian administration.

battle:青化砭、羊马河、蟠龙之战.note: The Northwest Field Corps won three victories in three battles at Qinghuabian, Yangmahe and Panlong, wiping out the 31st Brigade, the 135th Brigade and the Panlong supply base; Hu Zongnan's plan to “settle the Northwest question in three months” collapsed.
battle:青化砭、羊马河、蟠龙之战.old: Battles of Qinghuabian, Yangmahe and Panlong
battle:青化砭、羊马河、蟠龙之战.sides: Northwest Field Corps defeated KMT forces

battle:青岛之战.note: Using its declaration of war on Germany as a pretext, Japan sent troops into Shandong; landing at Longkou, they crossed beyond the war zone designated by China and advanced west along the Qingdao–Jinan Railway. At the end of October, together with British forces, they besieged the fortress of Qingdao, and the Germans surrendered on 7 November. Japan thereby seized Qingdao by force and grabbed Germany's rights and interests in Shandong.

battle:靖国之役（四川）.cmd: Xiong Kewu, Gu Pinzhen and Wang Wenhua vs. Liu Cunhou, Wu Guangxin and Zhou Daogang
battle:靖国之役（四川）.note: Tang Jiyao formed the Yunnan-Guizhou National Pacification Allied Army and entered Sichuan to protect the Constitution, joining Xiong Kewu's Sichuan Army in attacking Liu Cunhou and Wu Guangxin, who stood with Beijing. In December the National Pacification Army took Chongqing and Wu Guangxin fled east; in February 1918 the Sichuan troops in Chengdu changed sides, Liu Cunhou retreated north to southern Shaanxi, and Xiong Kewu was appointed Military Governor of Sichuan by the Military Government.
battle:靖国之役（四川）.sides: National Pacification Army defeated Liu Cunhou and Wu Guangxin

battle:韦岗伏击战.cmd: Su Yu vs. Japanese truck convoy
battle:韦岗伏击战.note: The New Fourth Army's Advance Detachment ambushed a Japanese convoy on the Zhenjiang–Jurong road; it was the New Fourth Army's first battle after pushing behind enemy lines south of the Yangtze, and it raised the curtain on the creation of the Maoshan Anti-Japanese Base Area.
battle:韦岗伏击战.sides: New Fourth Army defeated Japanese forces

battle:韶关之战.cmd: Ye Ju and Hong Zhaolin vs. Xu Chongzhi, Li Fulin and Zhu Peide
battle:韶关之战.note: After Chen Jiongming's rebellion, Sun Yat-sen ordered the Northern Expedition Army in Jiangxi to turn back and punish Chen; Xu Chongzhi and others returned from southern Jiangxi to attack Shaoguan, fought Ye Ju's forces fiercely for more than a month without success, and moved off into Fujian and Guangxi; Sun Yat-sen left Guangdong for Shanghai on 9 August.
battle:韶关之战.sides: Chen Jiongming's forces defeated Northern Expedition Army

battle:飞夺泸定桥.cmd: Wang Kaixiang and Yang Chengwu vs. Li Quanshan (Liu Wenhui's forces)
battle:飞夺泸定桥.note: The Red 4th Regiment raced 120 kilometres in a day and a night to reach Luding; 22 assault troops clambered along the iron chains of Luding Bridge, whose planks had been removed, and seized the bridgehead, and the Central Red Army thus crossed the Dadu River.

battle:香港保卫战.cmd: Young and Maltby vs. Sakai Takashi
battle:香港保卫战.note: On the same day as Japan's surprise attack on Pearl Harbor, the Japanese 23rd Army crossed the Shenzhen River and attacked Kowloon, broke through the Gin Drinkers' Line on 10 December and landed on Hong Kong Island on 18 December. On Christmas Day Governor Young surrendered; Hong Kong fell and entered three years and eight months of Japanese occupation.

battle:马尼拉战役.cmd: Griswold and Beightler vs. Iwabuchi Sanji
battle:马尼拉战役.note: Japanese naval troops, disregarding Yamashita Tomoyuki's order to withdraw, held Manila to the last, and US forces fought for it street by street and house by house for a month; the Intramuros district was left almost entirely in ruins. About 100,000 civilians died in the fighting and in Japanese massacres, and Manila became one of the most heavily destroyed cities of the Second World War.
battle:马尼拉战役.sides: United States and the Philippines defeated Japan

battle:马当要塞之战.note: Madang was a fortress on the Yangtze barrier line; the Japanese Hada Detachment landed and struck it from the flank, the defending commander mishandled the situation, the fortress fell within two days, and the gateway to Jiujiang lay wide open.

battle:马拉什之战.note: After taking over the garrison of Marash, French troops fought three weeks of street battles with the local Turkish militia and withdrew on the night of 11 February; the Armenian refugees who went with them suffered heavy losses. It was the Turkish national movement's first victory on the southern front.

battle:马来海战.note: Land-based Japanese navy bombers sank the British battleship Prince of Wales and the battlecruiser Repulse off Kuantan, and Phillips went down with his ship. It was the first time capital ships under way at sea had been sunk by aircraft, and Britain was left with no capital ships in the Far East.

battle:高兴圩战斗.cmd: Mao Zedong and Zhu De vs. Jiang Guangnai and Cai Tingkai
battle:高兴圩战斗.note: The Red Army attacked the 19th Route Army at Gaoxingxu in Xingguo; both sides suffered more than 3,000 casualties, and the Red Army failed to wipe out its opponent. It was the most savage battle of the third counter-“encirclement” campaign.

battle:高台战斗.cmd: Dong Zhentang and Yang Keming vs. Ma Yuanhai
battle:高台战斗.note: More than 3,000 men of the Western Route Army's Fifth Army held Gaotai and were besieged by more than 20,000 of Ma Bufang's troops; the town fell, and the army commander Dong Zhentang and the political commissar Yang Keming died heroically.
battle:高台战斗.sides: Ma Bufang's forces defeated Western Route Army

battle:高邮战役.note: The Central China Field Army took Gaoyou, held by Japanese and puppet troops who refused to surrender to the New Fourth Army; more than 1,000 Japanese surrendered. It was the New Fourth Army's last large-scale operation against the Japanese after the end of the War of Resistance.
battle:高邮战役.sides: New Fourth Army defeated Japanese and puppet troops

battle:鲁南战役.cmd: Chen Yi and Su Yu vs. Ma Liwu
battle:鲁南战役.note: The East China Field Army wiped out the Reorganized 26th Division and the 1st Rapid Column, capturing large numbers of tanks and heavy guns; it liberated Zaozhuang on 20 January and formed a Special Arms Column.
battle:鲁南战役.sides: East China Field Army defeated KMT forces

battle:鲁西南战役.cmd: Liu Bocheng and Deng Xiaoping vs. Wang Jingjiu
battle:鲁西南战役.note: The Liu-Deng Army crossed the Yellow River by night and wiped out nine and a half KMT brigades at Yuncheng, Dingtao, Liuyingji and Yangshanji, opening the way south; it then made its thousand-li thrust into the Dabie Mountains.
battle:鲁西南战役.sides: Shanxi-Hebei-Shandong-Henan Field Army defeated KMT forces

battle:黄安战役.cmd: Xu Xiangqian and Chen Changhao vs. Zhao Guanying
battle:黄安战役.note: The first battle of the Red Fourth Front Army after its founding on 7 November: it besieged Huang'an for more than forty days, beat off the relief forces and broke into the town on 22 December, capturing Zhao Guanying, commander of the 69th Division. The Hubei-Henan-Anhui Soviet Area was joined up into a single whole.
battle:黄安战役.sides: Red Fourth Front Army defeated KMT 69th Division

battle:黄崖洞保卫战.cmd: Peng Dehuai (Ou Zhifu) vs. Japanese 36th Division
battle:黄崖洞保卫战.note: Huangyadong was the Eighth Route Army's largest arsenal. The Special Task Regiment of Eighth Route Army Headquarters held it behind its natural defences for eight days and nights, killing or wounding nearly 1,000 Japanese and covering the removal of the factory's equipment; it was a model of positional defence in which the Eighth Route Army defeated a larger force with a smaller one.
battle:黄崖洞保卫战.sides: Eighth Route Army defeated Japanese forces

battle:黄桥战役.cmd: Chen Yi and Su Yu vs. Han Deqin (Li Shouwei)
battle:黄桥战役.note: Han Deqin of the KMT diehards attacked Huangqiao with more than 30,000 men; the New Fourth Army's Northern Jiangsu Command struck back in self-defence with 7,000 men and defeated him, and Li Shouwei, commander of the 89th Army, drowned. The New Fourth Army then joined up at Baiju, Yancheng, with Huang Kecheng's Eighth Route Army forces coming south, laying the foundation of the Northern Jiangsu Anti-Japanese Base Area.
battle:黄桥战役.sides: New Fourth Army defeated KMT forces under Han Deqin

battle:黄洋界保卫战.cmd: Zhu Yunqing and He Tingying vs. KMT forces of Hunan and Jiangxi
battle:黄洋界保卫战.note: With the main force of the Red Fourth Army far away in southern Hunan, the rearguard, less than a battalion strong, held the natural barrier of Huangyangjie with positions of bamboo spikes and rolling stones and beat off four regiments of KMT forces of Hunan and Jiangxi; Mao Zedong commemorated it in his poem Jinggangshan, to the tune of Xijiangyue.
battle:黄洋界保卫战.sides: Red Fourth Army defeated KMT forces of Hunan and Jiangxi

battle:黄陂战斗.cmd: Zhou Enlai and Zhu De vs. Chen Cheng (Li Ming and Chen Shiji)
battle:黄陂战斗.note: The first battle of the fourth counter-“encirclement” campaign: the Red First Front Army ambushed two divisions of Chen Cheng's Central Route Army in the hills south of Huangpi and captured the division commanders Li Ming and Chen Shiji. Annihilating the enemy by large-formation ambush was typical of this phase.
battle:黄陂战斗.sides: Red First Front Army defeated KMT forces

battle:黄麻起义.cmd: Pan Zhongru, Wu Guanghao and Dai Kemin vs. Huang'an county militia
battle:黄麻起义.note: In the small hours of 14 November the peasant self-defence army of Huang'an and Macheng took the county town of Huang'an and set up the Huang'an Peasants' Government; on 5 December KMT forces broke into the town in a night raid, Pan Zhongru was killed in action, and the remaining forces moved to Mount Mulan, the beginning of the Hubei-Henan-Anhui Revolutionary Base Area.
battle:黄麻起义.sides: Huangma Uprising forces defeated Huang'an county garrison

battle:齐会战斗.cmd: He Long and Guan Xiangying vs. Yoshida Battalion, Japanese 27th Division
battle:齐会战斗.note: The Eighth Route Army's 120th Division encircled and wiped out a Japanese battalion at Qihui, Hejian, in central Hebei; it was an example of the Eighth Route Army fighting a battle of annihilation on the plains, and it consolidated the Central Hebei Anti-Japanese Base Area.
battle:齐会战斗.sides: Eighth Route Army defeated Japanese forces

battle:龙冈战斗.cmd: Mao Zedong and Zhu De vs. Zhang Huizan
battle:龙冈战斗.note: The first battle of the first counter-“encirclement” campaign. The Red Army concentrated its forces in an ambush at Longgang and wiped out the headquarters and two brigades of the KMT 18th Division, which had rashly pushed ahead, more than 9,000 men in all, capturing the division commander Zhang Huizan alive; the front-line command centre of the “encirclement” forces collapsed.
battle:龙冈战斗.sides: Red First Front Army defeated KMT 18th Division

battle:龙州起义.cmd: Li Mingrui and Yu Zuoyu vs. Guangxi Army
battle:龙州起义.note: On 1 February Yu Zuoyu and others rose at Longzhou and set up the Red Eighth Army and the Zuojiang Revolutionary Committee, with Li Mingrui as commander-in-chief, opening up the Zuojiang Revolutionary Base Area; in late March the Guangxi Clique turned back to counter-attack and Longzhou fell, and the remnants of the Red Eighth Army moved to the Youjiang area and merged into the Red Seventh Army.
battle:龙州起义.sides: Guangxi Army defeated Red Eighth Army

battle:龙源口战斗.cmd: Zhu De and Chen Yi vs. Yang Chisheng and Yang Ruxuan
battle:龙源口战斗.note: The Red Fourth Army routed the two Jiangxi Army divisions of Yang Chisheng and Yang Ruxuan along the line of the New and Old Qixi Ridges and went on to occupy Yongxin; the independent regime on the Hunan–Jiangxi border reached its greatest extent.
battle:龙源口战斗.sides: Red Fourth Army defeated Jiangxi Army

battle:龙潭战役.cmd: Li Zongren, He Yingqin and Bai Chongxi vs. Sun Chuanfang
battle:龙潭战役.note: Taking advantage of Chiang Kai-shek's resignation, Sun Chuanfang led more than 60,000 men in a forced crossing from the north bank of the Yangtze and for a time cut the Shanghai–Nanjing Railway; the First and Seventh Armies attacked him from east and west, the greater part of Sun's forces was wiped out, and he was never again able to strike south.
battle:龙潭战役.sides: National Revolutionary Army defeated Sun Chuanfang's army

battle:龙陵会战.note: Longling was the hub of the Japanese 56th Division in western Yunnan; Chinese forces attacked the town three times and Japanese forces twice counter-attacked with reinforcements, and it was taken only after five months of seesaw fighting. Mangshi and Zhefang were then recovered in succession.

canal:大运河.note: After grain transport on the canal was abolished in the late Qing, most of the northern section silted up and fell out of use; the southern section remained navigable.

canal:苏伊士运河.note: Links the Mediterranean and the Red Sea; Britain's lifeline to India and the Far East; it was not taken back by Egypt until 1956.

capital:万象@伊沙拉.note: Seat of the Lao Issara provisional government; French forces entered the city on 24 April 1946.

capital:万象@老挝.note: Seat of the French Résident supérieur in Laos; the king still lived at Luang Prabang in the north.

capital:上乌金斯克@远东共和国.note: The Far Eastern Republic was proclaimed here and made it its first capital, until it moved its capital to Chita after Semyonov had been driven out.

capital:上海@中共.note: In July 1921 the First National Congress of the CPC was held in Shanghai; the Central Committee long operated in secret in Shanghai (in April–September 1927 it was for a time in Wuhan), and moved to Ruijin in early 1933.

capital:东京@日本.note: After the Meiji Restoration Edo was renamed Tokyo and the Emperor moved here, and it has been Japan's capital ever since; from September 1945 the US occupation authorities (Allied General Headquarters) were also based here.

capital:丰原（桦太厅）@桦太.note: The Karafuto Agency moved here from Odomari in 1908, and the town was laid out in a grid of streets on the model of Sapporo; in 1946 the Soviet Union renamed it Yuzhno-Sakhalinsk.

capital:亚历山德罗夫斯克@北桦太.note: Called Ako by the Japanese; the military administration of the Sakhalin Expeditionary Army was set up here to rule northern Sakhalin.

capital:京城（朝鲜总督府）@朝鲜.note: After annexing Korea, Japan renamed Seoul as Keijo; the Government-General of Korea was set up in October 1910 and in 1926 moved into its new building in front of Gyeongbokgung Palace.

capital:仰光@缅甸国.note: Seat of Ba Maw's Japanese-backed puppet government, which moved with the Japanese forces to Moulmein in late April 1945.

capital:仰光@缅甸联邦.note: Capital of the Union of Burma; in 1949 Karen armed forces at one point came close to its northern outskirts.

capital:仰光@英属缅甸.note: Capital of British Burma, site of the Shwedagon Pagoda and the great port of the Irrawaddy delta.

capital:伊宁@东突厥斯坦共和国.note: Centre of the Three Districts Revolution. After the Yining Uprising of November 1944 a provisional government was set up, holding the three districts of Ili, Tacheng and Ashan; in 1946 it joined the Xinjiang provincial coalition government, and the three districts remained autonomous in practice until Xinjiang's peaceful liberation at the end of 1949.

capital:伊尔库茨克@高尔察克政府.note: Kolchak's government moved east to Irkutsk before the fall of Omsk; after the Political Centre uprising of January 1920, power changed hands.

capital:伊斯坦布尔@奥斯曼.note: Capital of the Ottoman Empire; occupied by the Entente Powers in 1918–1923.

capital:伏龙芝@吉尔吉斯.note: Originally named Pishpek; renamed in 1926 after the Red Army commander Frunze, who was born here.

capital:保安@中共.note: In July 1936 the CPC Central Committee moved to Bao'an, where Snow interviewed Mao Zedong; it moved to Yan'an in January 1937.

capital:克孜勒@唐努乌梁海.note: In August 1921 the “Tannu Tuva People's Republic” was set up with Soviet Russian backing, with its capital at Khem-Beldyr (renamed Kyzyl in 1926); in October 1944 it was incorporated into the Soviet Union.

capital:克孜勒奥尔达@草原.note: Originally named Perovsk; capital of the Kazakh Autonomous Republic from 1925 to 1929.

capital:利雅得@沙特.note: In 1902 Ibn Saud recaptured the city, and from here the Saudi state revived.

capital:加尔各答@英国.note: Capital of British India from 1772; the Delhi Durbar of 1911 announced the move of the capital, after which it remained the capital of Bengal Province.

capital:加德满都@尼泊尔.note: Capital of the Shah dynasty, site of the Singha Durbar, palace of the Rana prime ministers.

capital:北京@中共.note: In March 1949 the CPC Central Committee moved from Xibaipo into Beiping; in September the First Plenary Session of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference decided to make Beiping the capital and rename it Beijing; on 1 October the People's Republic of China was founded and the founding ceremony was held.

capital:北京@北洋政府.note: Yuan Shikai took office as Provisional President in Beijing in March 1912; the Beiyang Government had its capital here until June 1928, when the Fengtian Army withdrew beyond Shanhaiguan.

capital:北京@华北临时政府.note: In December 1937 Wang Kemin set up the Puppet North China Provisional Government in Beiping and renamed Beiping as Beijing; in March 1940 it was merged into the Wang Jingwei Puppet Regime and renamed the Puppet North China Political Council.

capital:北京@清.note: Capital of the Qing dynasty. On 12 February 1912 Empress Dowager Longyu issued the edict of abdication and the Qing fell; Puyi went on living in the Forbidden City until 1924.

capital:北平@扩大会议.note: In July 1930 Yan Xishan, Wang Jingwei and others convened the Enlarged Conference in Beiping, and in September set up a separate Nationalist Government; it collapsed after Zhang Xueliang's forces entered North China through Shanhaiguan.

capital:南京@国民政府.note: On 18 April 1927 Chiang Kai-shek set up the Nationalist Government in Nanjing; it moved to Chongqing in November 1937 and returned to the capital in May 1946; Nanjing was liberated on 23 April 1949.

capital:南京@汪伪.note: On 30 March 1940 Wang Jingwei made his “return to the capital” at Nanjing and set up the Puppet Nationalist Government; it announced its dissolution on 16 August 1945.

capital:南京@维新政府.note: In March 1938 Liang Hongzhi set up the Puppet Reformed Government in Nanjing, governing the occupied areas of Jiangsu, Zhejiang and Anhui; in March 1940 it was merged into the Wang Jingwei Puppet Regime.

capital:南京@讨袁军.note: In July 1913 Huang Xing declared a campaign against Yuan Shikai in Nanjing; on 1 September Zhang Xun's forces broke into Nanjing and the Second Revolution failed.

capital:南京@革命军.note: On 1 January 1912 Sun Yat-sen took office as Provisional President and the Nanjing Provisional Government was established; in April the Provisional Senate resolved to move the government to Beijing.

capital:卡拉奇@巴基斯坦.note: Pakistan's capital at its founding; large numbers of Muslim refugees poured in, and the population doubled within a few years.

capital:厚和@蒙疆.note: In October 1937 the Japanese occupied Guisui and renamed it “Houhehaote”; the Puppet Mongol United Autonomous Government was set up here.

capital:古晋@沙捞越.note: Site of the Astana, palace of the Brooke Raj; capital of the British colony of Sarawak after 1946.

capital:台北（国民党当局驻地）@国民政府.note: In December 1949 the KMT authorities retreated to Taiwan and made Taipei their seat.

capital:吉达@汉志.note: After Mecca fell, King Ali held out here for a year.

capital:吉隆坡@马来亚.note: Capital of the Malayan Union and of the Federation of Malaya.

capital:吉隆坡@马来联邦.note: Capital of the Federated Malay States; a Chinese city that grew up on tin mining.

capital:哈伊勒@拉希德.note: Capital of the House of Rashid; surrendered to Ibn Saud in November 1921.

capital:唐山@冀东政府.note: In August 1937 the Puppet East Hebei Government moved to Tangshan; in February 1938 it was merged into the Puppet North China Provisional Government.

capital:喀什@东突厥斯坦伊斯兰共和国.note: In November 1933 separatist forces in southern Xinjiang set up the so-called “Islamic Republic of East Turkestan” at Kashi; it collapsed after Ma Zhongying's forces broke into Kashi in February 1934.

capital:喀布尔@萨卡维.note: In 1929 Kalakani held Kabul and ruled as Emir for nine months.

capital:喀布尔@阿富汗.note: Capital of the Barakzai dynasty; Amanullah built the new town of Darul Aman on its western outskirts.

capital:埃里温@亚美尼亚.note: In July 1918 the Armenian government moved here from Tiflis.

capital:塔什干@突厥斯坦.note: Seat of the Governor-General of Russian Turkestan and of the Turkestan Autonomous Soviet Republic; capital of Uzbekistan from 1930.

capital:大不里士@阿塞拜疆人民政府.note: Capital of the Azerbaijan People's Government; formerly the seat of the Qajar crown prince.

capital:大马士革@叙利亚.note: Seat of Faisal's Arab government in 1918–1920, then capital of Syria under the French mandate.

capital:安卡拉@土耳其.note: Seat of the Grand National Assembly in 1920; made the capital on 13 October 1923.

capital:安曼@约旦.note: Only a small town when Abdullah made it the capital of Transjordan in 1921.

capital:安汶@南马鲁古共和国.note: Where the so-called “Republic of South Maluku” was proclaimed; it was taken by Indonesian forces in November.

capital:尼兹瓦@阿曼伊玛目.note: Seat of the Ibadi Imam of the interior.

capital:山打根@北婆罗洲.note: Capital of North Borneo under the British North Borneo Company; the town was destroyed in the war, and the capital moved to Jesselton.

capital:巴库@阿塞拜疆.note: The oil capital on the Caspian; in September 1918 the Azerbaijani government moved here from Ganja.

capital:巴格达@伊拉克.note: Occupied by British forces in March 1917; capital of the Kingdom of Iraq from 1921.

capital:巴达维亚@爪哇.note: Capital of the Netherlands East Indies; the Governor-General usually resided at the palace in Bogor.

capital:布哈拉@布哈拉.note: Capital of the Emirate and of the Bukharan People's Soviet Republic; a centre of Islamic learning in Central Asia.

capital:希瓦@希瓦.note: Capital of the Khanate of Khiva and of the Khorezm People's Soviet Republic.

capital:帝力@葡属帝汶.note: Seat of the Governor of Portuguese Timor.

capital:平壤@朝鲜民主主义人民共和国.note: Capital of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea. Taken by the “UN Command” forces on 19 October 1950 and recovered by Chinese and Korean forces on 6 December; in the later stages of the war it was repeatedly bombed by the US Air Force and reduced almost to ruins.

capital:平壤（北朝鲜临时人民委员会）@苏军占领区.note: Headquarters of the Soviet 25th Army; the Provisional People's Committee for North Korea was set up here in February 1946 and became the People's Committee of North Korea the following year.
capital:平壤（北朝鲜临时人民委员会）@苏军占领区.old: Pyongyang (Provisional People's Committee for North Korea)

capital:广州@国民政府.note: Seat of the Constitution Protection Military Government (1917), the Generalissimo's Headquarters (1923) and the Nationalist Government (July 1925); in April–October 1949, around the time of Nanjing's liberation, the KMT government moved to Guangzhou.

capital:广州@广州国民政府.note: In May 1931, over the Tangshan Incident, the anti-Chiang factions set up a separate Nationalist Government in Guangzhou; after the September 18 Incident, Nanjing and Guangzhou made peace, and it was abolished on New Year's Day 1932.

capital:库伦@外蒙古.note: In December 1911, instigated by tsarist Russia, the Jebtsundamba Khutughtu declared “independence” at Urga and proclaimed himself emperor; in November 1924 the Mongolian People's Republic was founded and the city was renamed Ulan Bator.

capital:延安@中共.note: Seat of the CPC Central Committee from January 1937 to March 1947 and capital of the Shaanxi-Gansu-Ningxia Border Region; in March 1947, when KMT forces launched their concentrated attack on northern Shaanxi, the CPC Central Committee withdrew on its own initiative, and on the 19th Hu Zongnan's forces occupied Yan'an.

capital:张家口@蒙疆.note: In November 1937 the Puppet Mengjiang United Committee was set up here; in September 1939 the Puppet Mengjiang United Autonomous Government was established, with Prince De as chairman.

capital:德化@蒙疆.note: In May 1936, with the backing of the Kwantung Army, Prince De set up the Puppet Mongol Military Government at Jiabusi (renamed Dehua).

capital:德里@英国.note: Proclaimed the new capital of British India in December 1911; the government moved here in 1912 and was temporarily housed north of the old city, while a site to the south was chosen for building New Delhi.

capital:德黑兰@伊朗.note: Capital of the Qajar and Pahlavi dynasties; the Tehran Conference was held here in 1943.

capital:成都@国民政府.note: At the end of November 1949 the KMT government moved from Chongqing to Chengdu, and on 7 December decided to move to Taiwan.

capital:拉什特@吉兰.note: Capital of the Gilan Soviet Republic.

capital:拉萨@西藏.note: In early 1913 the 13th Dalai Lama returned to Lhasa, and after the “expulsion of the Han” had driven out the Sichuan Army the Kashag ran the government on its own; Lhasa was the seat of the Local Government of Xizang in the Republican period.

capital:撒马尔罕@突厥斯坦.note: Capital of the Uzbek Soviet Socialist Republic from 1924 to 1930.

capital:斯利那加@克什米尔.note: Summer capital of Jammu and Kashmir; Indian troops were airlifted here in October 1947.

capital:新京@伪满洲国.note: In March 1932 Puppet Manchukuo made Changchun its “capital” and renamed it “Xinjing”; in August 1945 the Soviet Red Army occupied it and Puppet Manchukuo collapsed.

capital:新加坡@海峡殖民地.note: Capital of the Straits Settlements and also seat of the British High Commissioner for the Malay States; site of the Far East naval base.

capital:新德里@印度.note: India became independent on 15 August 1947, Nehru raised the flag at the Red Fort on the 16th, and New Delhi became the capital of India.

capital:新德里@英国.note: The new capital designed by Lutyens and Baker, inaugurated in February 1931, with the Viceroy's House at its centre.

capital:日惹@印度尼西亚.note: Sultan Hamengkubuwono IX supported the Republic, and Yogyakarta became the revolutionary capital; it was taken by Dutch airborne troops in December 1948.

capital:昆明@护国军.note: On 25 December 1915 Tang Jiyao and Cai E declared Yunnan independent in Kunming and formed the National Protection Army to fight Yuan Shikai.

capital:普那卡@不丹.note: Winter capital of the Wangchuck dynasty, where the first king was enthroned in 1907.

capital:曼谷@暹罗.note: Capital of the Chakri dynasty; the port and political centre on the lower Menam.

capital:望加锡@东印度尼西亚邦.note: Capital of the State of East Indonesia.

capital:杜尚别@塔吉克.note: Originally a market village of Eastern Bukhara; made the capital of Tajikistan in 1924 and renamed Stalinabad in 1929.

capital:桑怒@巴特寮.note: After the Vietnam People's Army and Pathet Lao forces occupied it in April 1953, Souphanouvong's Lao Resistance Government was based in the mountains around Sam Neua.

capital:梯弗里斯@格鲁吉亚.note: Seat of the Russian Viceroy of the Caucasus and from 1918 the capital of Georgia; renamed Tbilisi in 1936.

capital:武吉丁宜@印度尼西亚.note: After Yogyakarta fell, Sjafruddin set up an emergency government in West Sumatra and held out, moving from place to place, in the mountains around Bukittinggi.

capital:武昌@革命军.note: The Wuchang Uprising broke out on 10 October 1911; the next day the Hubei Military Government was set up with Li Yuanhong as military governor, and the provinces rose in response one after another.

capital:汉口@国民政府.note: In December 1926 the Nationalist Government moved north to Wuhan, and from New Year's Day of the following year it conducted business in Hankou.

capital:汉口@武汉国民政府.note: After the April 12 Counter-revolutionary Coup, Wang Jingwei headed the Wuhan Nationalist Government in opposition to Nanjing; with the July 15 “purge of Communists” the first KMT–CPC cooperation broke down, and in September the Nanjing and Wuhan governments merged.

capital:汉城（大韩民国）@大韩民国.note: Capital of the Republic of Korea. Occupied by the Korean People's Army on 28 June 1950 and retaken by the “UN Command” forces on 28 September; Chinese and Korean forces entered it on 4 January 1951 and withdrew on their own initiative on 15 March; Syngman Rhee's government returned to the capital in August 1953.

capital:汉城（美军政厅）@美占朝鲜.note: The military government of the US Army Forces in Korea was housed in the former Government-General of Korea building; it handed over power to the Republic of Korea in August 1948.

capital:江界（临时首都）@朝鲜民主主义人民共和国.note: After Pyongyang fell, the DPRK government withdrew north to Kanggye, a mountain town near the Yalu River, and held out behind its natural defences, returning to Pyongyang at the end of the year.

capital:河内@北圻.note: Seat of the Governor-General of French Indochina, and also of the Résident supérieur of Tonkin.

capital:河内@越南民主共和国.note: Capital of the Democratic Republic of Vietnam after the August Revolution; the government left the city after the Vietnamese people's war of resistance against France broke out in full in December 1946, and the central authorities moved back after the takeover in October 1954.

capital:海参崴（滨海诸政府）@日占西伯利亚.note: While garrisoned by the Japanese intervention forces, it was in turn the seat of the Primorye Regional Zemstvo Government (January 1920), Merkulov's Provisional Priamurye Government (May 1921) and Diterikhs's “Amur Zemsky Krai” (July 1922).

capital:海得拉巴@海得拉巴.note: Capital of the Nizam's state; Indian forces entered the city in September 1948.

capital:特拉维夫@以色列.note: Where the founding of the state was proclaimed on 14 May 1948; seat of the provisional government.

capital:瑞金@中共.note: In November 1931 the Provisional Central Government of the Chinese Soviet Republic was established at Yeping, Ruijin; in October 1934 the Central Red Army set out on the Long March and withdrew from Ruijin.

capital:瓦窑堡@中共.note: The CPC Central Committee moved here in November 1935, and in December the Wayaobu Meeting set the policy of the anti-Japanese national united front; the Committee left in June 1936.

capital:碧瑶@菲律宾第二共和国.note: The summer capital in the American period. In December 1944 Laurel's puppet government withdrew here with Yamashita Tomoyuki, and in late March 1945 Laurel left from here for Japan.

capital:福州@福建人民政府.note: In November 1933 Li Jishen, Jiang Guangnai and Cai Tingkai led the 19th Route Army in setting up the “People's Revolutionary Government of the Chinese Republic” in Fuzhou; it failed in January the following year.

capital:科伦坡@锡兰.note: Capital of British Ceylon, and from 1948 the capital of the Dominion of Ceylon.

capital:耶路撒冷@巴勒斯坦.note: Seat of the British Mandate government of Palestine; the High Commissioner's residence was at first on the Mount of Olives, and in 1933 moved to the newly built Government House on the southern outskirts.

capital:肇庆@护国军.note: In May 1916 the National Protection provinces set up the Military Affairs Council at Zhaoqing, with Tang Jiyao as Chief Commander and Cen Chunxuan acting in his place; it was abolished in July, after Yuan's death.

capital:腊包尔@新几内亚.note: Capital of Australian-administered New Guinea; after the volcanic eruption of 1937 it was decided to move the capital to Lae. Under Japanese occupation it was the largest Japanese base in the South Pacific.

capital:苏莱曼尼亚@苏莱曼尼亚.note: Barzanji's seat when he proclaimed himself King of Kurdistan.

capital:莫尔兹比港@巴布亚.note: Capital of Australian Papua; the target of Japanese attacks by sea and by land in 1942, it never fell.

capital:萨那@也门.note: Capital of the Ottoman Yemen Vilayet; after the Ottoman withdrawal in 1918 Imam Yahya entered the city.

capital:西柏坡@中共.note: The CPC Central Committee moved here in May 1948 and from here directed the three great campaigns of Liaoshen, Huaihai and Pingjin; in March 1949, after the Second Plenary Session of the Seventh Central Committee, it moved to Beiping.

capital:西耶路撒冷@以色列.note: In December 1949 Israel declared Jerusalem its capital, and the parliament moved into the western city.

capital:西贡@南圻.note: Seat of Cochinchina, the most prosperous French colonial city in Southeast Asia, joined to Chợ Lớn, where the Chinese community was concentrated.

capital:西贡@越南国.note: Seat of the government of the State of Vietnam; Bảo Đại mostly stayed at Đà Lạt.

capital:贝鲁特@黎巴嫩.note: Capital of Greater Lebanon and of the Lebanese Republic; seat of the French High Commissioner.

capital:赤塔（谢苗诺夫）@谢苗诺夫.note: Semyonov took the city in September 1918 and, under Japanese protection, controlled the Transbaikal railway; he fled in October 1920.

capital:赤塔（远东共和国）@远东共和国.note: After its liberation by the People's Revolutionary Army in October 1920 it became the capital of the Far Eastern Republic, until the republic merged into Soviet Russia in November 1922.

capital:越北根据地@越南民主共和国.note: During the war of resistance against France, the central organs of the Democratic Republic of Vietnam were based in the “safe zone” in the mountains where the provinces of Thái Nguyên, Tuyên Quang and Bắc Kạn meet, centred on Định Hóa.

capital:迪化@新疆.note: Capital of Xinjiang Province. Governed in turn by Yang Zengxin (1912–1928), Jin Shuren and Sheng Shicai; on 25 September 1949 Tao Zhiyue announced an uprising by circular telegram, and Xinjiang was peacefully liberated.

capital:通州@冀东政府.note: In November 1935 Yin Rugeng set up the Puppet East Hebei Anti-Communist Autonomous Committee at Tongxian, renamed a government in December; in July 1937, after the puppet peace preservation corps rose in revolt (the Tongzhou Incident), it moved to Tangshan.

capital:鄂木斯克@高尔察克政府.note: Seat of the Provisional Siberian Government and of Kolchak's White Government, called the “capital of Siberia” by the White Russians; it was taken by the Red Army on 14 November 1919.

capital:重庆@国民政府.note: The Nationalist Government announced its move to Chongqing on 20 November 1937, and in 1940 the city was designated the auxiliary capital; in October 1949 the KMT government moved again from Guangzhou to Chongqing.

capital:金边@柬埔寨.note: Royal capital of Cambodia, seat of the French Résident.

capital:釜山（临时首都）@大韩民国.note: After Seoul fell, Syngman Rhee's government moved south by way of Daejeon and Daegu and came to Busan on 18 August 1950, holding out behind the perimeter; it moved here again on 3 January 1951, and the city was thereafter the provisional capital until the government returned to Seoul in August 1953.

capital:阿什哈巴德@土库曼.note: Capital of the Transcaspian Oblast and from 1924 the capital of Turkmenistan; called Poltoratsk from 1919 to 1927.

capital:阿拉木图@草原.note: Originally named Verny; capital of Kazakhstan from 1929; the Turkestan–Siberia Railway opened in 1930.

capital:雅加达@印度尼西亚.note: Where independence was proclaimed; in January 1946 the government moved to Yogyakarta because Dutch forces had reoccupied the city, and it moved back after the transfer of sovereignty.

capital:顺化@中圻.note: Capital of the Nguyễn dynasty, where the Emperor of Annam lived under French protection.

capital:顺化@越南帝国.note: The Japanese-backed Empire of Vietnam had its capital at Huế; Bảo Đại abdicated at the Meridian Gate on 30 August.

capital:马尼拉@菲律宾.note: Capital of the American Philippines; the Governor-General and the President of the Commonwealth resided at Malacañang Palace.

capital:马尼拉@菲律宾共和国.note: Capital of the Republic of the Philippines; in 1948 the official capital was moved to neighbouring Quezon City.

capital:马尼拉@菲律宾第二共和国.note: Seat of Laurel's Japanese-backed puppet government.

capital:马斯喀特@阿曼.note: Seat of the Sultan, and of the British Political Agent.

capital:麦加@汉志.note: Seat of Sharif Hussein, where the Arab Revolt began in 1916.

conc:上海公共租界.note: Formed in 1863 by merging the British and American settlements; the Municipal Council was dominated by British and American residents. In the early part of the War of Resistance it was the “solitary island”; in December 1941 Japanese forces moved in, and on 1 August 1943 it was taken over by the Wang Jingwei Puppet Regime.

conc:上海法租界.note: Established in 1849; its Municipal Council was controlled by the French Consul-General. The First National Congress of the CPC was held here; in the “solitary island” period it sheltered large numbers of refugees. On 30 July 1943 Vichy France handed it over to the Wang Jingwei Puppet Regime.

conc:东交民巷使馆界.note: In 1901 the Qing government was forced to sign the Boxer Protocol, which made this a legation quarter in which Britain, the United States, France, Japan, Russia, Italy and other countries stationed troops and governed themselves, and where Chinese were not allowed to live. In 1943 Britain and the United States gave it up under the new treaties, and in March that year Japan handed its part over to the Wang Jingwei Puppet Regime.

conc:中东铁路附属地（哈尔滨）.note: In 1898 the Chinese Eastern Railway Bureau was set up in Harbin, and the railway zone was administered and garrisoned by the Russians. In 1920 the Beijing Government recovered administrative and judicial power over the zone and set up the Special District of the Eastern Provinces.

conc:九江英租界.note: Established in 1861. In January 1927, after the Hankou Incident, crowds in Jiujiang stormed into the concession and the Northern Expedition Army took it over; an agreement for its return was signed in March.

conc:九龙.note: In 1860 the Qing government was forced to sign the Convention of Beijing, ceding the Kowloon Peninsula south of Boundary Street and Stonecutters Island; the Qing court still kept officials in the Kowloon Walled City, and the sovereignty dispute continued into the Republican era.

conc:亚南.note: A small enclave of French India near the mouth of the Godavari; in June 1954 the pro-merger faction seized power locally, and it was transferred de facto to India on 1 November.

conc:关东州.note: After the Russo-Japanese War Japan seized Russia's leased territory at Lüda, and in 1915, through the Twenty-One Demands, extended the lease to 99 years. The Kwantung Army took its name from it, and the September 18 Incident was launched from here.

conc:刘公岛.note: When Weihaiwei was returned, the British navy kept the lease on part of the facilities on Liugong Island for another ten years as the summer anchorage of its Far East fleet; after the Japanese occupied Weihai in 1938 the British navy stayed on until 1940.

conc:卡来卡尔.note: One of the five enclaves of French India, on the Coromandel Coast; transferred de facto to India in November 1954.

conc:厦门英租界.note: Established in 1852 at Haihoutan; very small in area. Recovered by the Nationalist Government on 17 September 1930.

conc:哈巴尼亚空军基地.note: A Royal Air Force base retained under the Anglo-Iraqi Treaty of 1930; besieged by Iraqi forces in May 1941.

conc:天津俄租界.note: Marked out on the east bank of the Hai River after the war of 1900. Recovered in September 1920 after the Beijing Government stopped recognizing the diplomats and consuls of the former Russian government; the Soviet Union formally gave it up in 1924. The Belgian Concession to its south (established 1902) was returned in January 1931.

conc:天津德租界.note: Established in 1895. Recovered when the Beijing Government broke off relations with Germany in March 1917, and made Special District No. 1; in August that year China declared war on Austria-Hungary, and the Austro-Hungarian Concession east of the river (established 1902) was also recovered.

conc:天津日租界.note: Established in 1898; a base of Japan's North China Garrison Army and its special service agencies; Puyi slipped away from here to the Northeast in November 1931; in March 1943 Japan handed it over to the Wang Jingwei Puppet Regime.

conc:天津法租界.note: Established in 1861; its forcible seizure of Laoxikai in 1916 sparked the “Laoxikai Incident”; in June 1943 Vichy France handed it over to the Wang Jingwei Puppet Regime. East of the river lay the Italian Concession (1902–1943; taken over by the Japanese after the Italian armistice, and formally given up by Italy in 1947).

conc:天津英租界.note: The largest and most prosperous of the nine foreign concessions. In 1939 the Japanese blockaded the British Concession on the pretext of the “Cheng Xigeng case”; in December 1941 Japanese forces moved in, and in 1943 Britain gave it up under the new treaty.

conc:威海卫.note: A territory forcibly leased by Britain, facing Lüshun across the sea. Returned on 1 October 1930 under the Convention for the Rendition of Weihaiwei and made the Weihaiwei Administrative Region.

conc:广州湾.note: A territory forcibly leased by France and attached to French Indochina, with its capital at Fort-Bayard. During the War of Resistance it was South China's outlet to the outside world; in February 1943 Japanese forces moved in; in August 1945 China and France signed an agreement for its return, and it was renamed Zhanjiang.

conc:新界.mod: Tai Po, New Territories, Hong Kong
conc:新界.note: In 1898 Britain, by the Convention for the Extension of Hong Kong Territory, forcibly leased the land south of the Shenzhen River and north of Boundary Street, together with the outlying islands, for 99 years; when British forces took over the following year they met armed resistance from the villagers.

conc:旅大（苏）.note: In August 1945 Soviet forces occupied Lüda; under the Sino-Soviet Treaty of Friendship and Alliance concluded between the Nationalist Government and the Soviet Union, Lüshun was to be a naval base shared by the two countries and Dalian a free port, but in practice both were under Soviet military control. In February 1950 the Sino-Soviet Treaty of Friendship, Alliance and Mutual Assistance and the Agreement on the Chinese Changchun Railway, Lüshun and Dalian provided for Soviet withdrawal from Lüshun by the end of 1952, which was postponed at China's request because of the War to Resist US Aggression and Aid Korea; in October 1954 the withdrawal was agreed, and in May 1955 Soviet forces left and the facilities were handed over to China.

conc:本地治里.note: Capital of French India; together with Chandernagor and the others, five enclaves in all, it made up French India. Transferred de facto to India in 1954.

conc:杭州日租界.note: Under the Treaty of Shimonoseki Hangzhou was opened as a trading port, and a Japanese concession was set up around Gongchenqiao, where business remained slack. Hangzhou fell in December 1937, and in March 1943 Japan handed the concession over to the Wang Jingwei Puppet Regime.

conc:汉口俄租界.note: Established in 1896. The Beijing Government took over its administration in September 1920 and made it Special District No. 2; the Soviet Union gave it up in the Sino-Soviet Agreement of 1924.

conc:汉口德租界.note: Established in 1895, the first new concession opened by the Powers in Hankou after the Sino-Japanese War of 1894–1895. Recovered after relations with Germany were broken off in March 1917, and made Special District No. 1.

conc:汉口日租界.note: The northernmost of the five concessions. The Japanese residents left in August 1937 and China took it over the following year; after Wuhan fell in October 1938 the Japanese reoccupied it, and in March 1943 it was handed over to the Wang Jingwei Puppet Regime.

conc:汉口法租界.note: Established in 1896, wedged between the Russian and German concessions. In June 1943 Vichy France handed it over to the Wang Jingwei Puppet Regime; France formally gave it up in the new Sino-French treaty of February 1946.

conc:汉口英租界.note: At the height of the Great Revolution, on 3 January 1927, crowds in Hankou clashed with British sailors, and the Wuhan Nationalist Government promptly took over the concession; the Chen–O'Malley Agreement was signed on 19 February, and it was formally returned in March, the first British concession recovered through diplomacy.

conc:江孜商务代表处.note: After British forces invaded Lhasa in 1904, a trade agency with a guard was set up at Gyangze under the Treaty of Lhasa, and Yadong was also opened as a trading post; after India's independence in August 1947, India took them over.

conc:沙面法租界.note: The eastern fifth of Shamian was the French Concession; in 1943 Vichy France handed it over to the Wang Jingwei Puppet Regime, and France formally gave it up in the new Sino-French treaty of February 1946.

conc:沙面英租界.note: Reclaimed from a sandbank from 1859, its western four-fifths forming the British Concession. The Shaji Massacre of June 1925 took place on the bank opposite the concession. In December 1941 Japanese forces moved in.

conc:满铁附属地（奉天）.note: The South Manchuria Railway's zone around Fengtian station, where Japan held administrative, police and garrison rights; the September 18 Incident was launched from here. In December 1937 Japan abolished its extraterritoriality, and administration of the railway zone passed to Puppet Manchukuo.
