conc:满铁附属地（长春）.note: The northern terminus of the South Manchuria Railway, where a new town was laid out south of Kuanchengzi. In 1932 Puppet Manchukuo designated Changchun as “Xinjing”, and the railway zone was handed over to Puppet Manchukuo in December 1937.

conc:澳门.note: Gradually occupied by Portugal from the mid-16th century; in 1887 the Qing government was forced to sign the Sino-Portuguese Treaty of Amity and Commerce, recognizing Portugal's “perpetual occupation and government”. Portugal was neutral in the Pacific War, so Macao was not occupied by the Japanese and became a gathering place for refugees.

conc:牯岭.note: In 1895 the British missionary Little leased Guniuling on Mount Lu to build a summer resort, run by the foreign-dominated Guling Company; the Nationalist Government recovered it in January 1936.

conc:第乌.note: A Portuguese island fortress at the southern tip of the Kathiawar Peninsula; Indian forces entered it in December 1961.

conc:纳加尔哈维利.note: A Portuguese inland enclave with its capital at Silvassa, acquired from the Maratha Empire under a treaty of 1779; seized on 2 August 1954 by volunteers seeking union with India, it formed a joint autonomous administration with Dadra.

conc:胶州湾（德）.note: In March 1898 Germany forced the Qing government to sign the Jiao'ao Lease Treaty for a term of 99 years, and built the port of Qingdao and the Qingdao–Jinan Railway. On 7 November 1914 a combined Japanese and British force took Qingdao.

conc:胶州湾（日）.note: After capturing it Japan imposed military rule; the Paris Peace Conference transferred Germany's rights in Shandong to Japan, triggering the patriotic May Fourth Movement; it was returned on 10 December 1922 under the treaty of the Washington Conference.

conc:苏州日租界.mod: outside Pan Gate, Gusu District, Suzhou, Jiangsu
conc:苏州日租界.note: Under the Treaty of Shimonoseki Suzhou was opened as a trading port, and in 1897 a Japanese concession was set up at Qingyangdi outside Pan Gate. In March 1943 Japan handed it over to the Wang Jingwei Puppet Regime.

conc:达德拉.note: A small inland enclave of Portuguese India east of Damão, ceded to Portugal by the Maratha Empire at the end of the 18th century under a treaty of 1779; seized on 22 July 1954 by volunteers seeking union with India.

conc:达曼.note: The northern enclave of Portuguese India; Indian forces entered it in December 1961.

conc:重庆日租界.note: Established in 1901 at Wangjiatuo on the south bank; the Japanese did little with it, and after 1931 the people of Chongqing repeatedly demanded its recovery; in August 1937, after the nationwide War of Resistance had begun, the Japanese residents left and China recovered it.

conc:金德讷格尔.note: The enclave of French India in Bengal, near Calcutta. In a referendum in 1949 it voted to join India, and it was transferred de facto in May 1950.

conc:镇江英租界.note: Established in 1861 outside the Yinshan Gate at Xijindu. Recovered by the Nationalist Government on 15 November 1929.

conc:青岛美军基地.note: In October 1945 the US Marines landed at Qingdao to accept the Japanese surrender, after which it was the station of the US Western Pacific Fleet; they left in May 1949, on the eve of Qingdao's liberation.

conc:香港岛.mod: Central and Western District, Hong Kong
conc:香港岛.note: Forcibly occupied by British forces in January 1841; in 1842 the Qing government was forced to cede it in the Treaty of Nanjing, and Victoria City was the seat of the British colonial government of Hong Kong. Occupied by the Japanese on 25 December 1941; British forces returned on 30 August 1945.

conc:马埃.note: The enclave of French India on the Malabar Coast; from June 1954 it was controlled by groups seeking union with India, and it was transferred de facto to India on 1 November.

conc:鼓浪屿公共租界.note: In 1902 Britain, the United States, Japan and other countries concluded an agreement with the Qing court, and the Municipal Council was set up the following year; Gulangyu was the only international settlement on an island. Japanese forces landed on the island in December 1941; the Wang Jingwei Puppet Regime took it over in 1943, and the Nationalist Government recovered it in September 1945.

event:“一〇一号作战”轰炸重庆.note: Japanese army and navy air units flying from Hankou, Yichang and elsewhere bombed Chongqing and Chengdu continuously for more than 100 days in an attempt to force the Nationalist Government to submit.

event:“东突厥斯坦伊斯兰共和国”成立.note: A handful of separatists in southern Xinjiang cobbled together the so-called “Islamic Republic of East Turkestan” in Kashi, with Sabit Damolla as “prime minister” and Khoja Niyaz set up as “president”. This separatist regime was crushed by the Tungan army within a few months.
event:“东突厥斯坦伊斯兰共和国”成立.old: Founding of the “Islamic Republic of East Turkestan”

event:“日台条约”.note: A few hours before the San Francisco Peace Treaty took effect, the Taiwan authorities and Japan signed a so-called “peace treaty” in Taipei; Japan confirmed its renunciation of Taiwan and Penghu, and the Taiwan authorities waived claims to war reparations. The Chinese government did not recognize it; diplomatic relations between China and Japan were not established until 1972.

event:“蒙古人民共和国”成立.note: After the Bogd Khan died in May, the Mongolian People's Party abolished the monarchy, and the First State Great Khural proclaimed the “Mongolian People's Republic”, renamed Urga Ulan Bator and adopted a constitution. The Republic of China did not recognize it.

event:一二·九运动.note: Led by the Communist Party of China, several thousand students in Beiping braved the cold to stage an anti-Japanese, national-salvation demonstration against “North China autonomy”; a second great march on the 16th forced the postponement of the founding of the Hebei-Chahar Political Council. The December 9 Movement set off a new upsurge of the nationwide movement to resist Japan and save the nation.

event:七一五“分共”.note: The Wang Jingwei clique presided over a meeting of the KMT Central Committee in Wuhan that formally decided on the “purge of Communists”, followed by mass arrests and killings of Communists and revolutionary masses. The first KMT–CPC cooperation broke down completely, the National Revolution failed, and the CPC turned to armed resistance against the KMT reactionaries.

event:七七事变.note: Japanese troops holding night exercises near the Lugou Bridge demanded entry into Wanping Fortress on the pretext of searching for a missing soldier; when refused, they shelled Wanping, and Ji Xingwen's regiment of the 29th Army rose to resist. The Lugou Bridge Incident marked the beginning of the Nationwide War of Resistance.

event:七届四中全会.note: The Fourth Plenary Session of the Seventh CPC Central Committee adopted the Resolution on Strengthening Party Unity; after the session the activities of Gao Gang and Rao Shushi in splitting the Party and seeking to usurp the supreme power of the Party and the state were exposed and criticized. Gao Gang committed suicide in August; in March 1955 both were expelled from the Party, and Rao Shushi was subsequently arrested.
event:七届四中全会.old: Fourth Plenary Session of the Seventh CPC Central Committee

event:万县惨案.note: Yang Sen's forces detained British merchant steamers that had run down and sunk wooden boats; British warships then shelled the city of Wanxian for two or three hours, perpetrating the Wanxian Massacre, in which over a thousand soldiers and civilians were killed or wounded, and stirring up a nationwide wave of anti-imperialist protest.

event:万宝山事件.note: Japan incited Korean settlers outside Changchun to dig an irrigation channel, leading to clashes with local farmers, and Japanese police intervened with gunfire. The Japanese side then distorted and sensationalized the affair in Korea, stirring up anti-Chinese riots in many places that killed or wounded hundreds of overseas Chinese; it became an important provocation before Japan launched the September 18 Incident.

event:三一八惨案.note: After the Guominjun fired on Japanese warships forcing their way into Dagukou, Japan joined Britain, the United States and other powers, eight in all, to issue an ultimatum demanding the removal of the Dagu defences. On 18 March crowds in Beijing who had come to petition in protest were fired on and massacred outside the Executive Government's gates by the guards of Duan Qirui's Executive Government; more than forty were killed, among them Liu Hezhen.

event:三一运动.note: A national independence movement of the Korean people against Japanese colonial rule. National representatives read out the Declaration of Independence in Keijo and students rallied in Tapgol Park; demonstrations quickly spread across all Korea, and suppression by Japanese troops and police left thousands dead. Afterwards Japan switched to “cultural rule”.

event:三八线以北地区行政权移交.note: The areas north of the 38th parallel but south of the military demarcation line, including Cheorwon, Hwacheon, Yanggu, Inje, Goseong and Yangyang (called the “recovered areas” in South Korea), remained under the military administration of the “UN Command” after the armistice; in November administration was handed over to South Korea, and they were incorporated into the provinces of Gyeonggi and Gangwon.
event:三八线以北地区行政权移交.old: Handover of administration north of the 38th parallel

event:三反五反.note: Within Party and government organs, a campaign against corruption, waste and bureaucracy; in private industry and commerce, a campaign against bribery, tax evasion, theft of state property, cheating on labour and materials, and theft of state economic intelligence. The major embezzlers Liu Qingshan and Zhang Zishan were executed according to law, and large numbers of law-breaking industrialists and merchants were investigated and dealt with.

event:三湾改编.note: Mao Zedong reorganized the Autumn Harvest Uprising forces at Sanwan into the 1st Regiment, 1st Division, First Army of the Workers' and Peasants' Revolutionary Army, establishing Party branches at company level, Party representatives at company level and above, and soldiers' committees. This established organizationally the Party's leadership over the army and was an important beginning in building a new type of people's army.

event:上海南北和会.note: Zhu Qiqian for the Beijing Government and Tang Shaoyi for the Military Government held peace talks in Shanghai but deadlocked over a ceasefire in Shaanxi, the parliament and the Shandong Question; on 13 May Tang Shaoyi's eight conditions were rejected, and the talks broke down.

event:东三省“自治”.note: After Fengtian's defeat in the First Zhili–Fengtian War, the Beijing Government stripped Zhang Zuolin of all his posts; Zhang Zuolin declared the “autonomy” of the Three Northeastern Provinces and was acclaimed Commander-in-Chief of Peace Preservation of the Three Northeastern Provinces. No longer taking orders from Beijing, he rebuilt and drilled his army, and in 1924 entered North China once again.

event:东京大空袭.note: More than 300 US B-29s made a low-level night incendiary raid on the Shitamachi district of Tokyo; about 100,000 people died and a million were left homeless. Incendiary bombing of Japan's major cities followed.

event:东京审判宣判.note: The tribunal sentenced seven men, including Tōjō Hideki, Doihara Kenji and Matsui Iwane, to death by hanging, and most of the rest to life imprisonment; the executions were carried out on 23 December.

event:东京审判开庭.note: The International Military Tribunal for the Far East opened at Ichigaya, Tokyo, to try twenty-eight Class-A war crimes suspects, including Tōjō Hideki, for crimes against peace and other charges. The tribunal was made up of judges from eleven countries; the Chinese judge was Mei Ru'ao.

event:东北人民政府成立.note: The Northeast People's Representative Conference in Shenyang elected the Northeast People's Government, with Gao Gang as chairman, the earliest established of the greater administrative regions of the People's Republic of China.

event:东北易帜.note: Defying Japanese obstruction, Zhang Xueliang announced by circular telegram that the three northeastern provinces and Rehe would fly the Blue Sky, White Sun flag and submit to the Nationalist Government; Nanjing appointed him Commander of the Northeastern Frontier Defence Army, and the Nationalist Government thus nominally unified the country.

event:东江纵队成立.note: The Guangdong People's Anti-Japanese Guerrillas proclaimed the formation of the Dongjiang Column at Tuyang Village in Huiyang, with Zeng Sheng as commander and Lin Ping as political commissar, and openly declared that they accepted the leadership of the Communist Party of China.

event:两广事变.note: Chen Jitang, together with Li Zongren and Bai Chongxi, sent troops into Hunan in the name of “going north to resist Japan”. Chiang Kai-shek split and bought off his opponents; the Guangdong air force and Yu Hanmou went over to the central government one after the other, and on 18 July Chen Jitang left for Hong Kong. In September Guangxi made peace with Nanjing. The semi-independence of the Southwest came to an end.

event:两广统一.note: Wang Jingwei and Tan Yankai of the Nationalist Government held talks at Wuzhou with Li Zongren and Huang Shaohong and agreed that Guangxi's military and civil affairs would be unified under the Nationalist Government; in March the Guangxi forces were reorganized as the Seventh Army of the National Revolutionary Army, with Li Zongren as commander, laying the groundwork for the Northern Expedition.

event:两河口会议.note: A meeting of the Political Bureau set the strategic policy of moving north to establish a Sichuan-Shaanxi-Gansu base area; Zhang Guotao agreed on the surface but soon, on the grounds of “unified command”, contended with the Party for the leadership of the Red Army.

event:中东路事件.note: On 10 July the Northeastern authorities took back by force the Chinese Eastern Railway, jointly run by China and the Soviet Union, and expelled the Soviet staff; the Soviet Union broke off relations and sent in troops, the Northeastern Army was heavily defeated at Jalainur and Manzhouli, and on 22 December the Khabarovsk Protocol was signed, restoring the railway's former status.

event:中亚民族划界.note: The Soviet Union redrew Central Asia along national lines: the Turkestan Autonomous Republic and the Bukharan and Khorezm People's Republics were abolished, and the Uzbek and Turkmen union republics were created, together with Tajik, Kirghiz, Karakalpak and other autonomous units, laying the basis for the borders of today's five countries.

event:中亚起义.note: Tsarist Russia's conscription of Central Asian Muslims for wartime labour service provoked uprisings among the peoples of Jizzakh, Semirechye and other regions, the risings of the Kazakhs and Kirghiz being the fiercest. Deaths in the tsarist suppression ran into the hundreds of thousands, and large numbers of Kirghiz fled to Xinjiang, China.

event:中俄声明.note: China and Russia exchanged declarations: tsarist Russia recognized China's suzerainty over Outer Mongolia, and China recognized Outer Mongolian “autonomy” and undertook not to station troops or settle colonists there. This laid the groundwork for the 1915 Kyakhta Agreement.

event:中俄蒙协约.note: China, Russia and Outer Mongolia signed a tripartite agreement at Kyakhta: Outer Mongolia renounced its “independence” and recognized Chinese suzerainty; China recognized Outer Mongolian “autonomy”, invested the Bogd Khan with his title and stationed a High Commissioner at Urga.

event:中共一大.note: The First National Congress of the Communist Party of China opened on 23 July in the Shanghai French Concession; after a search by the concession police it moved to a red boat on South Lake in Jiaxing, Zhejiang, where it closed. It adopted the Party programme, elected Chen Duxiu Secretary of the Central Bureau and proclaimed the founding of the Communist Party of China. This was an epoch-making event.
event:中共一大.old: First National Congress of the CPC

event:中共七大.note: At the Seventh National Congress of the CPC, Mao Zedong delivered the report On Coalition Government; the congress established Mao Zedong Thought as the Party's guiding ideology and wrote it into the Party Constitution, and elected a Central Committee headed by Mao Zedong. Party membership had passed 1.2 million.
event:中共七大.old: Seventh National Congress of the CPC

event:中共中央移驻西柏坡.note: The CPC Central Committee and the Central Military Commission crossed the Yellow River eastward and moved to Xibaipo in Pingshan, from where they directed the three great campaigns of Liaoshen, Huaihai and Pingjin; in March 1949, after holding the Second Plenary Session of the Seventh CPC Central Committee, they moved to Beiping.
event:中共中央移驻西柏坡.old: CPC Central Committee moves to Xibaipo

event:中共中央进驻延安.note: After the Xi'an Incident the Northeastern Army handed over Yan'an, and the CPC Central Committee and the Central Military Commission moved in from Bao'an; for the next ten years Yan'an remained the seat of the CPC Central Committee.
event:中共中央进驻延安.old: CPC Central Committee moves into Yan'an

event:中共六届六中全会.note: The plenary session endorsed Mao Zedong's political line, called on “the whole Party and the whole army to expand behind enemy lines in North and Central China”, and set the policy of making the anti-Japanese base areas behind enemy lines the focus.
event:中共六届六中全会.old: Sixth Plenary Session of the Sixth CPC Central Committee

event:中华人民共和国成立.note: On the Tian'anmen rostrum Mao Zedong proclaimed the founding of the Central People's Government of the People's Republic of China; the New Democratic Revolution had won a great victory. The Soviet Union recognized it the next day, the countries of Eastern Europe, Burma and India followed, and Britain recognized it in January 1950.
event:中华人民共和国成立.old: Founding of the People's Republic of China

event:中华工农兵苏维埃第一次全国代表大会.note: Held at Yeping in Ruijin, the congress proclaimed the founding of the Provisional Central Government of the Chinese Soviet Republic, with Mao Zedong as Chairman of the Central Executive Committee and Chairman of the Council of People's Commissars; Ruijin was renamed Ruijing. This was an important attempt by the Communist Party of China to exercise state power in a part of the country.
event:中华工农兵苏维埃第一次全国代表大会.old: First National Congress of the Chinese Workers', Peasants' and Soldiers' Soviets

event:中华民国成立.note: Sun Yat-sen was inaugurated in Nanjing as Provisional President, proclaiming the founding of the Republic of China; the Gregorian calendar was adopted, with that year as Minguo 1. The Nanjing Provisional Government was a regime of bourgeois-republican character, but it was short of funds and its orders carried little weight.
event:中华民国成立.old: Founding of the Republic of China

event:中华苏维埃对日宣战.note: The Provisional Central Government issued a declaration of war on Japan in Mao Zedong's name, calling on the people of the whole country to drive Japanese imperialism out of China and demonstrating the Communist Party of China's firm stand of resisting Japan.
event:中华苏维埃对日宣战.old: Chinese Soviet Republic declares war on Japan

event:中印公路通车.note: After the Chinese Army in India and the Expeditionary Force met at Mong Yu, the China–India Road (Stilwell Road) was open along its whole length, and an opening ceremony was held at Wanding. The first convoy reached Kunming on 4 February, and an oil pipeline was laid at the same time.

event:中印西藏通商交通协定.note: China and India signed the Agreement on Trade and Intercourse between the Xizang Region of China and India; India withdrew its troops stationed at Yadong and Gyangze and handed over its postal and telegraph facilities. The preamble wrote in, for the first time, the Five Principles of mutual respect for each other's territorial integrity and sovereignty, mutual non-aggression, mutual non-interference in each other's internal affairs, equality and mutual benefit, and peaceful coexistence.
event:中印西藏通商交通协定.old: Sino-Indian Agreement on Trade and Intercourse with Xizang

event:中国人民志愿军入朝作战.mod: Dandong, Liaoning – Sinuiju, North Korea (Yalu River)
event:中国人民志愿军入朝作战.note: To resist US aggression and aid Korea, and to protect their homes and defend their country, the Chinese People's Volunteers, led by Peng Dehuai, crossed the Yalu River at Andong, Changdian Hekou, Ji'an and other points; on the 25th they fought their first battle at Onjong and Ryangsu-dong, opening the First Campaign.
event:中国人民志愿军入朝作战.old: Chinese People's Volunteers enter the war in Korea

event:中国人民政治协商会议.note: Its first plenary session adopted the Common Program and the Organic Law of the Central People's Government, made Beiping the capital and renamed it Beijing, adopted the Five-Star Red Flag as the national flag, and elected Mao Zedong Chairman of the Central People's Government.

event:中国土地法大纲.note: The CPC National Land Conference met at Pingshan, and on 10 October the Outline Land Law of China was promulgated, abolishing the land system of feudal and semi-feudal exploitation, applying the principle of land to the tiller and distributing land equally by head of population; the land reform movement spread widely through the Liberated Areas.

event:中央红军开始长征.note: After the failure of the fifth counter-“encirclement” campaign, the CPC Central Committee and the Central Revolutionary Military Commission led the 86,000 men of the Red First Front Army in a forced strategic shift, setting out from Ruijin and Yudu, crossing the Yudu River on pontoon bridges and heading west; Xiang Ying, Chen Yi and others stayed behind in the south with 16,000 men to carry on guerrilla warfare.
event:中央红军开始长征.old: Central Red Army sets out on the Long March

event:中央红军抵吴起镇.note: The Shaanxi-Gansu Detachment, more than 7,000 strong, reached Wuqizhen in the Shaanxi-Gansu Soviet Area, victoriously concluding the Central Red Army's year-long Long March of 25,000 li. In November it joined the Red 15th Army Group at Xiangbiziwan in Ganquan and resumed the designation of Red First Front Army.

event:中山舰事件.note: When the warship Zhongshan arrived at Huangpu, Chiang Kai-shek seized on it to accuse the CPC and the Soviet advisers falsely of plotting against him; he declared martial law in Guangzhou, detained the ship's captain, the Communist Li Zhilong, surrounded the Soviet advisers' residences and struck at the Communists. Wang Jingwei then went abroad, and Chiang Kai-shek took control of party and army.

event:中朝军队进占汉城.note: As Chinese and Korean forces closed in during the Third Campaign, the Syngman Rhee government moved again to Busan on 3 January, and Seoul's residents fled south in great numbers; on the 4th the “UN Command” forces withdrew from Seoul and blew up the pontoon bridges over the Han River, and Chinese and Korean forces entered Seoul (known in South Korea as the “January Fourth Retreat”). Busan thereafter served as the provisional capital until August 1953.
event:中朝军队进占汉城.old: Chinese and Korean forces enter Seoul

event:中美中英新约.note: China signed new treaties with the United States and with Britain: the two powers gave up consular jurisdiction, the legation quarter and the right to station troops, and returned their concessions, abolishing some of the privileges the powers had held in China since the beginning of modern times; Britain refused to return the Kowloon leased territory.
event:中美中英新约.old: New treaties with the United States and Britain

event:中苏互不侵犯条约.note: China and the Soviet Union signed the pact in Nanjing; the Soviet Union then supplied aircraft and artillery on credit and sent a volunteer air group to China, the most important foreign aid in the early period of the War of Resistance.

event:中苏友好同盟互助条约.note: During Mao Zedong's two-month visit to the Soviet Union, Zhou Enlai and Vyshinsky signed the new treaty, replacing the 1945 treaty. The Soviet Union undertook to return the Chinese Changchun Railway and withdraw from Lüshun before the end of 1952, and to provide a loan of US$300 million.
event:中苏友好同盟互助条约.old: Sino-Soviet Treaty of Friendship, Alliance and Mutual Assistance

event:中苏友好同盟条约.note: Wang Shijie and Molotov signed the treaty: China agreed that Outer Mongolia would decide on independence by plebiscite; the Chinese Changchun Railway would be jointly managed by China and the Soviet Union; Lüshun would be a naval base shared by the two countries and Dalian a free port. The Soviet Union undertook to give aid only to the Nationalist Government and to withdraw its troops from the Northeast within three months.
event:中苏友好同盟条约.old: Sino-Soviet Treaty of Friendship and Alliance

event:中苏解决悬案大纲.note: Wellington Koo and Karakhan signed the agreement, and China and the Soviet Union established diplomatic relations; the Soviet Union recognized Outer Mongolia as part of Chinese territory and agreed to withdraw its troops, and the Chinese Eastern Railway was placed under joint Sino-Soviet management.

event:中长铁路移交.note: Under the 1950 Sino-Soviet agreement, the Soviet Union handed over to China, free of charge, the jointly managed Chinese Changchun Railway and its property, with a handover ceremony in Harbin; at China's request, the withdrawal of the Soviet troops at Lüshun was postponed.
event:中长铁路移交.old: Handover of the Chinese Changchun Railway

event:临时约法.note: The Senate in Nanjing promulgated the Provisional Constitution of the Republic of China, China's first constitutional document of a bourgeois-republican character; it replaced the presidential system with a cabinet system in order to restrain Yuan Shikai. In April the Provisional Government and the Senate moved north to Beijing.

event:丽水·顺天事件.note: Ordered to Jeju for suppression duties, the 14th Regiment of the Korea Constabulary refused to go, staged an uprising at Yeosu and seized Yeosu and Suncheon, but was soon crushed. Afterwards South Korea enacted the National Security Act and carried out a large-scale purge of leftists in the army.

event:义静苏维埃.note: The Indochinese Communist Party led starving peasants in the provinces of Nghệ An and Hà Tĩnh to rise in struggle, drive out local officials and set up peasant-association soviets. The French colonial army suppressed them with aerial bombing; more than a thousand died, and the Party organization was almost destroyed.

event:乔里乔拉事件.note: During the non-violent Non-cooperation Movement, a crowd set fire to the police station at Chauri Chaura, and more than twenty policemen died. Gandhi called off the movement on the grounds that it had strayed from non-violence; he was arrested in March and sentenced to six years.

event:九一八事变.note: The Japanese Kwantung Army deliberately blew up a section of the South Manchuria Railway near Liutiaohu, falsely blamed Chinese troops, and attacked the Beidaying barracks and the city of Shenyang. The Northeastern Army was under orders not to resist; the next day the Japanese occupied Shenyang and Changchun, and within ten days the key points of Liaoning and Jilin provinces had fallen. The September 18 Incident marked the start of the Chinese People's War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression.

event:九三炮战.note: The PLA heavily shelled Kinmen from Xiamen and Dadeng; two US military advisers were killed that day, and the shelling continued intermittently for several months; KMT forces struck back at the Xiamen area with aircraft and artillery. The First Taiwan Strait Crisis thus broke out, and the United States and the Taiwan authorities stepped up their moves towards a treaty.

event:九世班禅圆寂.note: Choekyi Nyima, the 9th Panchen Lama, a patriotic religious leader, had left for the interior in 1923; on his way back to Xizang he was held up at Yushu by the obstruction of Britain and of pro-British forces in the Xizang local authorities, and he passed away there. His coffin and escort later remained stranded in Xikang.

event:也门政变.note: Imam Yahya was assassinated, and the “Free Yemenis” installed Abdullah of the al-Wazir family as imam; Crown Prince Ahmad rallied tribal forces and retook Sanaa, and the coup failed.

event:二二八事件.note: A clash during a crackdown on contraband cigarettes in Taipei set off a struggle by the people of Taiwan against the autocratic rule of the KMT authorities, which quickly spread across the whole island. On 8 March KMT reinforcements landed at Keelung and launched suppression and countryside purges, causing heavy casualties. Chen Yi was removed from office, and in May a Taiwan Provincial Government was set up in place of the previous administration.

event:二二六事件.note: Young officers of the Imperial Way Faction led some 1,400 soldiers in attacks that killed Lord Keeper of the Privy Seal Saitō Makoto, Finance Minister Takahashi Korekiyo and others, and occupied the Nagatacho area. The emperor ordered the revolt suppressed, and it was put down in four days; the Control Faction seized the opportunity for a purge, and the military fascists' grip on the government grew tighter still.

event:二十一条.note: The Japanese Minister Hioki Eki presented the “Twenty-One Demands” to Yuan Shikai. On 7 May Japan issued an ultimatum; on the 9th Yuan Shikai's government, seeking Japanese support for his bid to become emperor, accepted them (Group Five being left for later negotiation), and on the 25th the Minguo 4 Treaties were signed. The Chinese people marked 9 May as National Humiliation Day.

event:云南起义.note: Yunnan Provincial Chairman Lu Han issued a circular telegram at Kunming announcing his uprising and detained Zhang Qun and others; the KMT 8th and 26th Armies counter-attacked Kunming but failed to take it, withdrew south to southern Yunnan and were wiped out in early 1950, part of them retreating into Burma.

event:五一五事件.note: Young fascist naval officers attacked the Prime Minister's official residence and shot Prime Minister Inukai Tsuyoshi dead. Party cabinets came to an end and were replaced by “national unity” cabinets, and the influence of the military grew steadily.

event:五三、五四大轰炸.note: Japanese aircraft bombed central Chongqing with incendiary bombs on two consecutive days, killing or wounding more than 6,000 people, one of the most devastating Japanese air raids on Chongqing during the War of Resistance.

event:五卅运动.note: The fatal shooting of Gu Zhenghong, a worker and Communist, at a Japanese cotton mill in Shanghai sparked protests; on 30 May British police of the International Settlement opened fire on demonstrating students and crowds on Nanjing Road, killing or wounding dozens and perpetrating the May Thirtieth Massacre. Strikes by workers, students and merchants swept the country, an anti-imperialist patriotic movement spread everywhere, and the high tide of the Great Revolution arrived.

event:五原誓师.note: Back from the Soviet Union, Feng Yuxiang took office at Wuyuan as commander-in-chief of the Guominjun Allied Army and announced that the entire army would join the KMT en masse, in support of the Northern Expedition; it soon marched east via Ningxia and Gansu, and in November lifted the siege of Xi'an.

event:五四运动.note: On 4 May students in Beijing rallied in front of Tian'anmen under the slogan “Fight for sovereignty abroad, root out the traitors at home” and marched to Zhaojialou, where they set fire to Cao Rulin's residence. In June Shanghai workers went on strike and merchants closed their shops; the Beijing Government was forced to dismiss Cao Rulin, Zhang Zongxiang and Lu Zongyu and refused to sign the peace treaty. The May Fourth Movement marked the beginning of China's New Democratic Revolution.

event:井冈山会师.note: Zhu De and Chen Yi brought the remnants of the Nanchang Uprising forces and the peasant forces of southern Hunan to Longshi in Ninggang, where they joined Mao Zedong's forces. Together they were reorganized as the Fourth Army of the Workers' and Peasants' Revolutionary Army (soon renamed the Red Fourth Army), with Zhu De as commander and Mao Zedong as Party representative, greatly strengthening the Jinggangshan Revolutionary Base Area.

event:亚美尼亚大屠杀.note: On 24 April 1915 Armenian intellectuals in Istanbul were arrested; Armenians in the eastern provinces were then killed en masse, and the survivors were deported across the desert to the Deir ez-Zor area. Estimates of the dead range from 600,000 to 1.5 million.

event:亚齐起事.note: Daud Beureu'eh, the religious leader of Aceh, resenting Aceh's incorporation into the province of North Sumatra, declared Aceh part of Kartosuwiryo's “Islamic State of Indonesia” and raised forces to attack the towns; driven back, the rebels withdrew into the mountains, and the revolt gradually subsided after Aceh gained special-region status in 1959.

event:京汉铁路大罢工（二七惨案）.note: When the warlords obstructed the founding of the Beijing–Hankou Railway General Trade Union, workers along the whole line, led by the Communist Party of China, launched a general strike on 4 February; on the 7th Wu Peifu and Xiao Yaonan bloodily suppressed it at Jiang'an, Changxindian and elsewhere, and Lin Xiangqian, Shi Yang and others laid down their lives heroically. The labour movement entered a low ebb, prompting the CPC to seek cooperation with the KMT.

event:人民解放军进驻拉萨.note: The advance detachment of the 18th Army reached Lhasa first, on 9 September, and Zhang Guohua and Tan Guansan led the main force into the city on 26 October; a Xinjiang cavalry advance company had entered Gartok in Ngari in August. In the summer of 1952 troops were stationed at Xigaze, Gyangze, Yadong and other places.

event:以色列建国.note: A few hours before the British mandate ended, Ben-Gurion read the declaration of independence in Tel Aviv, and the United States and the Soviet Union promptly recognized the new state; the next day the armies of the Arab states moved in, and the First Middle East War broke out in full.

event:伊宁起义·三区革命爆发.note: The people of all ethnic groups in Ili, resisting reactionary KMT rule, rose in revolt with Soviet support and stormed the city of Yining, and the Three Districts Revolution broke out; it was part of China's New Democratic Revolution. In its early stage the leadership of the uprising was for a time seized by separatists such as Alikhan Töre, and on 12 November the so-called “East Turkestan Republic” was set up.
event:伊宁起义·三区革命爆发.old: Yining Uprising: the Three Districts Revolution begins

event:伊拉克反英大起义.note: In opposition to the British mandate (colonial rule), Shiite clerics and the tribes of the middle Euphrates River took up arms and for a time controlled Najaf, Karbala and other places. British forces brought in reinforcements and used aerial bombing to suppress the revolt, which led Britain to switch to indirect rule by installing Faisal.

event:伊拉克独立.note: Under the Anglo-Iraqi Treaty of 1930, Iraq ended the mandate and joined the League of Nations, the first mandated territory to become independent; Britain kept the air bases at Habbaniya and Shaibah and rights of transit.

event:伊斯兰联盟成立.note: Reorganized from an association of Javanese batik merchants in Solo, it began by boycotting Chinese merchants and defending Muslim interests; by the end of the 1910s it had several hundred thousand members, and it was Indonesia's first mass national movement organization.

event:伊朗改国名.note: Reza Shah asked foreign countries to call the country “Iran” instead of “Persia” from Nowruz onwards.

event:伊朗政变（1953）.note: US and British intelligence agencies incited army officers and street crowds to overthrow Mosaddegh: the first attempt on the 15th failed and the shah fled the country; on the 19th Zahedi led troops to seize the capital, and Mosaddegh was arrested and put on trial. The shah returned to rule in person, and the next year signed an agreement with an international oil consortium to resume exports.

event:伊朗石油国有化.note: In March the Iranian parliament passed the bill nationalizing the oil industry, recovering sovereignty over the country's oil; at the end of April Mosaddegh became prime minister and took over the Anglo-Iranian Oil Company. Britain applied pressure with an embargo and naval power; on 4 October the British staff left the Abadan refinery, and Iran's oil exports came almost to a halt.

event:伊本·沙特去世.note: Abdulaziz Ibn Saud, the founding monarch of Saudi Arabia, died of illness at Taif; his eldest surviving son Saud succeeded him, with Faisal as crown prince. A Council of Ministers had been set up only a month before his death, and oil revenues had already swelled the royal finances.

event:伊犁起义.note: The Ili New Army rose under Yang Zuanxu and others, stormed the Ili General's yamen at Huiyuan and killed the Ili General Zhirui; the next day it set up the Xin-Yi Grand Military Governorate and pushed east to confront Dihua.

event:会宁会师.note: The headquarters of the Red Fourth Front Army reached Huining and joined the Red First Front Army; on the 22nd the Red Second Front Army met the Red First Front Army at Jiangtaibao. With the three main forces of the Red Army united, the Long March ended in victory. The Long March was a great feat in human history.

event:伦维尔协定.note: Signed aboard the US transport Renville, anchored in Batavia harbour: a ceasefire was fixed along the “Van Mook Line” drawn by the Dutch, the Republican army withdrew from its guerrilla pockets inside Dutch-held territory, and the area under Republican control shrank to Central Java and the interior of Sumatra.

event:伪冀东防共自治政府.note: Instigated by Japan, Yin Rugeng declared at Tongzhou that the twenty-two counties of eastern Hebei were breaking away from the central government and formed the East Hebei Anti-Communist Autonomous Council, renamed a government on 25 December; it was the first puppet regime Japan set up as it engineered the North China Incident and instigated “North China autonomy”.
event:伪冀东防共自治政府.old: Puppet East Hebei Anti-Communist Autonomous Government

event:伪华北临时政府成立.note: The Japanese North China Area Army installed Wang Kemin and others in Beiping as the Puppet “Provisional Government of the Republic of China”, renamed Beiping Beijing, and the following February absorbed the Puppet East Hebei regime.
event:伪华北临时政府成立.old: Puppet North China Provisional Government established

event:伪华北政务委员会成立.note: The Puppet Provisional Government was reorganized as the Puppet North China Political Council, with Wang Kemin as chairman; nominally subordinate to the Wang Jingwei Puppet Regime but in fact controlled by the Japanese North China Area Army, it kept a high degree of independence.
event:伪华北政务委员会成立.old: Puppet North China Political Council established

event:伪察南自治政府成立.note: After occupying Zhangjiakou, the Kwantung Army backed Yu Pinqing and others in setting up the Puppet South Chahar Autonomous Government, which later became part of the Puppet Mengjiang regime.
event:伪察南自治政府成立.old: Puppet South Chahar Autonomous Government established

event:伪满改行帝制.note: Puyi performed the suburban sacrifice at Xinghuacun in Changchun and proclaimed himself emperor; Puppet Manchukuo was renamed the “Empire of Manchukuo”, with the era name Kangde, but real power remained in the hands of the Japanese Kwantung Army and Japanese officials.

event:伪满洲国成立.note: Japanese imperialism installed Puyi as “Chief Executive”, with the era name Datong and Changchun as “Xinjing”, and the people of the Northeast fell under Japanese colonial rule. Puppet Manchukuo was a puppet regime of the Japanese aggressors, and the League of Nations, too, refused to recognize it.

event:伪满洲国解体.note: Puyi withdrew with the Kwantung Army to Dalizigou in Tonghua, where he read out his abdication edict, and Puppet Manchukuo was dissolved. On the 19th Puyi was captured by Soviet troops at Shenyang airfield as he was about to fly to Japan.

event:伪维新政府成立.note: The Japanese Central China Expeditionary Army installed Liang Hongzhi and others in Nanjing as the Puppet “Reformed Government of the Republic of China”, ruling the occupied areas of Jiangsu, Zhejiang and Anhui alongside the Puppet Provisional Government in Beijing.

event:伪蒙古军政府成立.note: With the backing of the Japanese Kwantung Army, Prince De set up the Puppet Mongol Military Government at Jiabusi (renamed Dehua), with Prince Yun as chairman, Prince De as director-general and Li Shouxin as minister of military affairs, and adopted the Genghis Khan era for dating years.

event:伪蒙古联盟自治政府成立.note: After occupying Guisui, the Japanese renamed it Houhehaote and backed Prince De and others in setting up the Puppet Mongol United Autonomous Government; in November it joined with the Puppet South Chahar and Puppet North Shanxi regimes to form the Puppet Mengjiang United Committee.
event:伪蒙古联盟自治政府成立.old: Puppet Mongol United Autonomous Government established

event:伪蒙疆联合自治政府成立.note: The three regimes of Puppet South Chahar, Puppet North Shanxi and the Puppet Mongol United Autonomous Government merged into the Puppet Mengjiang United Autonomous Government, with Prince De as chairman and its seat at Zhangjiakou; in 1941 it was renamed the Puppet Mongol Autonomous State.
event:伪蒙疆联合自治政府成立.old: Puppet Mengjiang United Autonomous Government established

event:何梅协定.note: Using the Hebei Incident as a pretext, Umezu Yoshijirō, commander of the Japanese North China Garrison Army, applied coercion; He Yingqin gave verbal consent and confirmed it by letter on 6 July: Yu Xuezhong would be replaced, the Central Army and the 51st Army of the Northeastern Army withdrawn, and the Hebei provincial party headquarters abolished. The Nationalist Government bowed to Japan, and the gates of North China were thrown wide open.

event:侯赛因—麦克马洪通信.note: Sharif Hussein of Mecca and McMahon, the British High Commissioner in Egypt, exchanged ten letters; the British promised in principle to support Arab independence, but the wording on boundaries and on the status of Palestine was vague, giving rise to endless disputes later.

event:俄界会议.note: Having gone north on its own with the First and Third Army Groups, the Central Committee held a meeting at Ejie and adopted the Decision on the Errors of Comrade Zhang Guotao; the northbound forces were reorganized as the Shaanxi-Gansu Detachment, with Peng Dehuai as commander and Mao Zedong as political commissar.

event:俄蒙协约.note: Tsarist Russia and the “independent” Outer Mongolian regime privately concluded the Russo-Mongolian Agreement and its commercial protocol; on the pretext of “assisting” Outer Mongolian “autonomy” and barring Chinese troops and settlers, Russia seized privileges in Mongolia. The Beijing Government protested and refused to recognize it.

event:光州学生运动.note: A clash between Korean and Japanese students in Gwangju set off anti-Japanese demonstrations by Korean students that spread to more than 190 schools across Korea; it was the largest anti-Japanese national movement since the March First Movement.

event:克伦起事.note: The Karen National Defence Organisation rose at Insein in the northern outskirts of Rangoon and fought government troops for more than a hundred days, also holding Toungoo and other places; the Communist Party of Burma and the People's Volunteer Organisation each launched armed struggles as well, and for a time the Burmese government controlled only the area around Rangoon.

event:八七会议.note: The CPC Central Committee held an emergency meeting in secret in Hankou, which corrected and ended Chen Duxiu's Right deviationist errors and set the general policy of agrarian revolution and armed resistance against the KMT reactionaries; Mao Zedong put forward the view that “political power is obtained from the barrel of a gun”. The meeting was the turning point from the failure of the Great Revolution to the rise of the Agrarian Revolutionary War.

event:八月革命.note: After Japan's surrender, the Indochinese Communist Party led the Viet Minh in a general uprising, taking Hà Nội on the 19th, Huế on the 23rd and Sài Gòn on the 25th; on the 30th Bảo Đại handed over the imperial seal at the Meridian Gate in Huế and abdicated.

event:八路军收复张家口.note: After the Japanese Mongolia Garrison Army withdrew south, the Shanxi-Chahar-Hebei forces recovered Zhangjiakou, the first provincial capital recovered by the Eighth Route Army in the War of Resistance. The leading bodies of the Shanxi-Chahar-Hebei Border Region moved in at once, and Zhangjiakou became the CPC's political centre in North China.

event:关东大地震.note: A magnitude 7.9 earthquake struck Sagami Bay, and fires swept Tokyo and Yokohama, leaving about 105,000 people dead or missing. Rumours spread after the quake, and vigilante groups, troops and police massacred large numbers of Koreans and some Chinese; the anarchist Ōsugi Sakae was murdered by the military police.

event:兴南撤退.note: After the Battle of Changjin Lake, the US X Corps withdrew from Hungnam by sea; together with ROK forces and nearly 100,000 refugees, more than 200,000 people were shipped south, and the port facilities were blown up once the evacuation was complete.

event:冀东抗日大暴动.note: The CPC's Hebei-Rehe Border Special Committee and the Eighth Route Army detachment of Song Shilun and Deng Hua launched an anti-Japanese uprising of the people in more than twenty counties of eastern Hebei and formed the Eastern Hebei Anti-Japanese Allied Army; it later failed after setbacks during a westward withdrawal.

event:冀察政务委员会.note: Set up by Nanjing to deal with Japan's demands for “North China autonomy”, with Song Zheyuan as chairman, it governed Hebei, Chahar, Beiping and Tianjin; semi-independent of the central government, it served as a buffer between Japan and Nanjing.

event:军务院成立.note: The independent provinces set up the Military Affairs Council at Zhaoqing, with Tang Jiyao as chief commander and Cen Chunxuan as deputy chief commander; recognizing Li Yuanhong as the lawful president, it stood against Beijing.

event:军政府改组.note: The Guangxi Clique and the Political Study Clique manipulated the Extraordinary Parliament into replacing the generalissimo system with a collegial directorate of seven Directors-General; Sun Yat-sen resigned in indignation and on 21 May left Guangdong for Shanghai. Cen Chunxuan became Chairman of the Directorate, and real power passed to the Guangxi Clique. The Constitution Protection Movement failed, and Sun Yat-sen came to see that “the South and the North are jackals from the same lair”.

event:凯末尔登陆萨姆松.note: Mustafa Kemal arrived at Samsun as Inspector of the Ninth Army; he soon issued the Amasya Circular and convened the Erzurum and Sivas congresses to organize national resistance. Turkey regards this day as the start of its War of National Liberation (War of Independence).

event:利亚卡特遇刺.note: Liaquat Ali Khan, Pakistan's first prime minister, was shot dead at a mass rally in the Company Bagh in Rawalpindi, and the assassin was shot dead on the spot. Thereafter Governor-General Ghulam Muhammad, the bureaucracy and the military gradually took real power.

event:制宪国民大会.note: Tearing up the resolutions of the Political Consultative Conference, the KMT unilaterally convened the National Assembly, which adopted the Constitution of the Republic of China, promulgated on 1 January 1947 and in force from 25 December 1947. The CPC and the China Democratic League refused to attend, and the door to KMT–CPC peace talks closed.

event:加利卜继任伊玛目.note: The Ibadi imam of the interior, Muhammad al-Khalili, died and Ghalib al-Hinai was chosen as imam; his brother Talib had close dealings with Saudi Arabia. The Sultan of Muscat sent troops into the interior to support prospecting at the Fahud oilfield, and the confrontation between the two sides intensified.

event:勒拿金矿惨案.note: Workers at the Lena goldfields went on strike and petitioned; the tsarist government's gendarmes opened fire on them, killing and wounding several hundred. The news shook all Russia, protest strikes broke out everywhere, and the revolutionary movement surged anew.

event:北京兵变·袁世凯就职.note: Special envoys went north from Nanjing to escort Yuan south for his inauguration; on 29 February a mutiny broke out in Beijing, and Yuan Shikai, citing instability in the north, stayed in Beijing. On 10 March he was inaugurated there as Provisional President, the government then moved north, and the fruits of the 1911 Revolution fell into Yuan Shikai's hands.
event:北京兵变·袁世凯就职.old: Beijing mutiny and Yuan Shikai's inauguration

event:北京政变.note: Feng Yuxiang, with Hu Jingyi and Sun Yue, turned back from the Rehe front and entered Beijing on 23 October, imprisoned Cao Kun, the president elected by bribery, and renamed their forces the Guominjun; on 5 November they revised the Articles of Favourable Treatment and expelled Puyi from the Forbidden City. The Beijing Government controlled by the Zhili Clique collapsed.

event:北伐军进入北京.note: Shang Zhen's forces of the Shanxi Army entered Beijing, marking the end of Beiyang warlord rule; in late June Nanjing renamed Zhili Province Hebei and Beijing the Special Municipality of Beiping, with the capital fixed at Nanjing.

event:北伐誓师.note: Driven by KMT–CPC cooperation, the National Revolutionary Army took its oath at Dongxiaochang in Guangzhou, with Chiang Kai-shek sworn in as commander-in-chief; about 100,000 men advanced north by several routes with the aim of overthrowing the three great imperialist-backed warlords, Wu Peifu, Sun Chuanfang and Zhang Zuolin.

event:北平和平解放.note: Fu Zuoyi signed an agreement with the CPC on the peaceful settlement of the Beiping question; more than 200,000 defending troops left the city to be reorganized, and on the 31st the Northeast Field Army entered the city. Beiping was peacefully liberated and the ancient capital was spared the ravages of war.

event:北平和谈.note: Zhang Zhizhong led the Nanjing government's delegation to Beiping for negotiations. On 15 April the CPC presented the final revised draft of the Agreement on Internal Peace; on the 20th the KMT government in Nanjing refused to sign, and that night the Yangtze River Crossing Campaign began. Most of the delegation stayed on in Beiping.

event:北平扩大会议.note: Wang Jingwei's Reorganization Clique, the Western Hills Group, and Yan and Feng jointly formed the Enlarged Conference of the KMT Central Party Headquarters, and on 9 September set up a separate Beiping Nationalist Government with Yan Xishan as chairman; after the Northeastern Army entered North China it moved to Taiyuan and soon dissolved.

event:北方居民南迁.note: The Geneva Accords allowed free movement for 300 days; 800,000 to a million northerners (mostly Catholics) moved south via Hải Phòng and other points on French and American ships and aircraft, in what the Americans called “Operation Passage to Freedom”; in the other direction more than 100,000 Viet Minh officers, soldiers and their families moved north from the south.
event:北方居民南迁.old: Migration from the North to the South

event:北朝鲜临时人民委员会.note: Set up under Soviet occupation with Kim Il Sung as chairman, it promptly carried out a land reform of confiscation without compensation and distribution free of charge, and nationalized key industries, laying the foundations for the state founded later.
event:北朝鲜临时人民委员会.old: Provisional People's Committee for North Korea

event:十七条协议.note: Li Weihan, Ngapoi Ngawang Jigme and others signed in Beijing the Agreement of the Central People's Government and the Local Government of Xizang on Measures for the Peaceful Liberation of Xizang. Xizang was peacefully liberated: the Local Government of Xizang came under the unified leadership of the Central Government, the PLA was to enter and be stationed in Xizang, the existing political system and the status of the Dalai Lama and the Panchen Lama were to remain unchanged, and reforms were to be carried out by the local authorities of Xizang of their own accord.

event:十三世达赖喇嘛圆寂.note: Thubten Gyatso, who had pursued new policies and built up the Tibetan army, passed away, and Reting Rinpoche became regent. The next year the Nationalist Government sent Huang Musong to Xizang to offer condolences; he left a commissioner and a radio station permanently in Lhasa, and direct ties between the central government and the Xizang local authorities were restored.

event:华北人民政府成立.note: The Shanxi-Chahar-Hebei and Shanxi-Hebei-Shandong-Henan Border Regions merged to form the North China People's Government, with Dong Biwu as chairman and its seat at Pingshan; from February 1949 it worked in Beiping, and many of its organs were the forerunners of ministries of the later Central People's Government.

event:华盛顿会议.mod: Washington, DC, United States (shown at Qingdao, the Shandong question it settled)
event:华盛顿会议.note: Nine powers, including the United States, Britain, Japan and China, met in Washington and signed the Nine-Power Treaty, which through the “Open Door” returned China to joint domination by the powers. Outside the conference, China and Japan concluded the Treaty for the Settlement of Outstanding Questions relative to Shandong, under which Japan agreed to return the Jiaozhou Bay leased territory and the Qingdao–Jinan Railway to China.

event:协约国出兵西伯利亚.note: Allied armed intervention against Soviet Russia: British troops landed first at Vladivostok, on 3 August; Japan announced its expedition on the 2nd and began landing from the 11th, and US troops landed from the 16th. The Japanese far exceeded the agreed troop strength, pushed west along the railway to Lake Baikal, and stayed longest of all the intervening powers.

event:南京国民政府成立.note: After the April 12 Counter-revolutionary Coup, Chiang Kai-shek, Hu Hanmin and others set up a separate Nationalist Government in Nanjing, opposed to the Wuhan Nationalist Government headed by Wang Jingwei, in what is known as the Nanjing–Wuhan split; together with Zhang Zuolin's Beiyang Government in Beijing, three governments existed side by side.

event:南京大屠杀.note: After capturing Nanjing, the Japanese invading troops carried out a bloody massacre of Chinese soldiers who had laid down their arms and of civilians over six weeks, accompanied by mass rape, looting and arson; more than 300,000 compatriots were killed. After the war both the International Military Tribunal for the Far East and the Nanjing Military Tribunal for the Trial of War Criminals established this crime.

event:南京惨案（1927）.note: As the Northern Expedition Army fought its way into Nanjing, foreign consulates and residents were looted; British and American warships, in the name of protecting their nationals, shelled the city, causing heavy Chinese military and civilian casualties. The imperialists used the incident to apply pressure, hastening the anti-Communist moves of the Chiang Kai-shek clique.

event:南北议和.note: Tang Shaoyi for the North and Wu Tingfang for the South negotiated in Shanghai and agreed to convene a National Convention to decide the form of state; the talks then turned into direct dealings between Yuan Shikai and the South, trading the forced abdication of the Qing emperor for Yuan's election as president.

event:南岳军事会议.note: Chiang Kai-shek convened his generals at Nanyue, announced that the War of Resistance had entered its second phase, readjusted the war zones, put forward the principle that “guerrilla warfare is more important than regular warfare”, and reorganized and retrained the troops.

event:南泥湾大生产.note: KMT diehards cut off the Eighth Route Army's pay and blockaded the Shaanxi-Gansu-Ningxia Border Region, and the Border Region launched the great production campaign. Wang Zhen's 359th Brigade moved into desolate Nanniwan to reclaim the land; by 1943 it was more than self-sufficient in grain and had become the standard-bearer of the great production campaign.

event:南洋厅成立.note: Japan abolished the navy's Provisional South Seas Islands Defence Force and set up the South Seas Government at Koror, with six branch offices; large numbers of migrants from Okinawa and the home islands came to grow sugar cane and mine phosphate.

event:卡斯托行动.note: Navarre ordered an airborne assault on Điện Biên Phủ; six parachute battalions were dropped within three days, drove out the Vietnamese garrison troops and repaired the airfield built by the Japanese during the Second World War, creating a fortified camp to block the Vietnamese army's route into Laos. In December French forces evacuated Lai Châu, and the Tai units moved to Điện Biên Phủ.

event:印尼主权移交.note: The Hague Round Table Conference reached agreement on 2 November; the Queen of the Netherlands in Amsterdam and the Dutch High Representative of the Crown in Djakarta signed simultaneously, transferring sovereignty to the Republic of the United States of Indonesia, with the exception of western New Guinea. Sukarno returned to Djakarta on the 28th.

event:印尼共产党起义.note: The Communist Party of Indonesia launched anti-Dutch uprisings, first at Banten in West Java and then at Silungkang in West Sumatra; they were soon crushed by the Dutch colonial authorities, and more than 1,000 people were exiled to the Boven Digoel concentration camp in western New Guinea.

event:印尼民族党成立.note: Founded in Bandung by Sukarno and others, it advocated non-cooperation and complete independence. On 28 October 1928 the Youth Congress in Batavia issued the “Youth Pledge”, affirming one motherland, one nation and one language (Indonesian).

event:印巴分治与旁遮普迁徙.note: Britain carried out the partition of India into India and Pakistan under the “Mountbatten Plan”; Pakistan and India became independent on 14 and 15 August respectively, but the Radcliffe Line was not made public until the 17th. More than ten million people in Punjab and Bengal crossed the new borders amid killings along the way; estimates of the dead range from 200,000 to more than a million.
event:印巴分治与旁遮普迁徙.old: Partition of India and the Punjab migrations

event:印度共和国成立.note: The constitution, drafted under Ambedkar's chairmanship, took effect; India became a federal parliamentary republic, with Prasad as its first president, and remained in the Commonwealth.

event:印度尼西亚单一共和国.note: Within half a year the member states of the federation merged one after another into the Republic; on the fifth anniversary of independence the federation was dissolved and replaced by the unitary Republic of Indonesia, with its capital at Djakarta.

event:印度尼西亚独立宣言.note: Two days after Japan's surrender, Sukarno and Hatta read the proclamation of independence in front of the house at Jalan Pegangsaan Timur 56 in Djakarta; the next day they were chosen as president and vice-president, and the 1945 Constitution and the five founding principles (Pancasila) were adopted.

event:印度政府法.note: Passed by the British Parliament, it widened the franchise, introduced provincial autonomy and proposed an all-India federation including the princely states (never realized); it took effect in April 1937, when Burma and Aden were also separated from India. The Indian National Congress won a majority of the provinces in that year's provincial elections.

event:印度非法侵占达旺.note: The Indian authorities in Assam sent Ralengnao Khathing with the Assam Rifles into Tawang, forcing the local Xizang officials to withdraw and illegally occupying the area. The Chinese government has never recognized the illegal “McMahon Line”, drawn by Britain and Xizang in a private exchange of notes during the Simla Conference of 1914, and the Tawang area became a focal point of the later China–India boundary dispute.

event:印度首次大选.note: Under the new constitution, the House of the People and the state legislatures were elected by universal adult suffrage; the electorate numbered more than 170 million, and voting was held in stages over nearly four months. The Indian National Congress won over 70 per cent of the seats in the House of the People, and Nehru continued as prime minister.

event:印缅分治.note: The Government of India Act 1935 took effect; Burma was separated from British India, with its own governor and a bicameral legislature, and Ba Maw became its first premier.

event:印锡条约.note: India and Sikkim signed a peace treaty making Sikkim an Indian protectorate: India took responsibility for its defence, external affairs and external communications, while the Chogyal retained autonomy in internal affairs.

event:双十协定.note: KMT and CPC representatives signed the Summary of Conversations between the Representatives of the Government and the CPC, confirming the policy of “peaceful national reconstruction” and agreeing to convene the Political Consultative Conference; the CPC made concessions, agreeing to give up eight Liberated Areas, including those in Guangdong, Zhejiang, southern Jiangsu and southern Anhui.

event:叙利亚军事政变.note: Chief of Staff Husni al-Za'im staged a coup on 30 March, the first military coup in the post-war Arab world; in August he was overthrown and executed by Hinnawi, and in December Shishakli staged another coup.

event:古田会议.note: The Ninth Party Congress of the Red Fourth Army met at Gutian and adopted the resolution drafted by Mao Zedong, establishing the principles of building the Party ideologically and the army politically and of the Party's absolute leadership over the army—an important milestone in the history of building the Party and the people's army.

event:台湾光复.note: Chen Yi, Administrative Executive of Taiwan Province, accepted the surrender of Andō Rikichi, commander of the Japanese Tenth Area Army, at Taipei Public Hall, and announced that Taiwan and Penghu had returned to Chinese territory; the Taiwan Provincial Administrative Executive Office was set up.

event:台湾戒严.note: Chen Cheng, Chairman of Taiwan Province and Commander-in-Chief of the Garrison Command, declared martial law throughout the province; that year saw mass arrests of Communists and progressives, and the White Terror began. Martial law remained in force until 1987.

event:史迪威被召回.note: After the heavy defeat of KMT forces in the Henan–Hunan–Guangxi Campaign, the Americans demanded that Stilwell command all Chinese forces, which Chiang Kai-shek flatly refused. Roosevelt agreed to recall Stilwell, Wedemeyer took over as chief of staff of the China theatre, and the China–Burma–India theatre was split in two.

event:吉兰苏维埃共和国成立.note: In May the Caspian Flotilla of Soviet Russia landed at Enzeli in pursuit of White ships; Kuchik Khan and Iranian communists then proclaimed the Persian Socialist Soviet Republic at Rasht.

event:吉达条约.note: Britain recognized the complete independence of Ibn Saud's Kingdom of Hejaz and Nejd, superseding the Treaty of Darin of 1915; Ibn Saud recognized Britain's special relations with the Gulf sheikhdoms.

event:吐噶喇列岛归还.note: The Tokara Islands (Toshima Village), lying between 29° and 30° N, were returned to Japan before the peace treaty took effect, the first part of the US-administered Nansei Islands to be returned.

event:呼伦贝尔“独立”.note: Instigated by tsarist Russia, the Barga, Solun and other tribal elites headed by Shengfu drove out the Qing officials, held Hailar and Manzhouli and declared “independence”, attaching themselves to Outer Mongolia. In 1915 the area was made a Special Region.

event:哈塔伊并入土耳其.note: To win Turkey over to the Anglo-French side in a European war, France agreed to the incorporation of Hatay State into Turkey; large numbers of Armenians and Arabs moved to Syria.

event:哈密事变.note: Jin Shuren, chairman of Xinjiang Province, abolished the Hami Muslim princedom and replaced hereditary rule with regular administration, provoking an uprising of the Uygur people, who besieged the city of Hami; Ma Zhongying of Gansu accepted an invitation to lead his forces into Xinjiang, and Xinjiang sank into prolonged turmoil.

event:哈达铺.note: Emerging from the Min Mountains, the Shaanxi-Gansu Detachment reached Hadapu, where old newspapers at the post office revealed that Liu Zhidan's Red Army and a Soviet Area existed in northern Shaanxi; the decision was then made to settle in northern Shaanxi.

event:唐努乌梁海“独立”.note: After the Soviet Russian Red Army had driven out the Chinese garrison, the banner elites of Uriankhai, backed by Soviet Russia, held an assembly that proclaimed the so-called “Tannu Tuva People's Republic” and its separation from China. The Republic of China never recognized it.

event:唐努乌梁海被并入苏联.note: At the Soviet Union's direction, the Little Khural of the “Tuvan People's Republic” requested admission to the Soviet Union in August, and in October the Supreme Soviet of the USSR admitted it as the Tuvan Autonomous Oblast. The Nationalist Government did not recognize this, and official maps long continued to show the region as Chinese territory.
event:唐努乌梁海被并入苏联.old: Tannu Uriankhai annexed by the USSR

event:四一二反革命政变.note: In Shanghai, Chiang Kai-shek had armed Green Gang men attack and disarm the workers' pickets; the next day petitioning crowds were fired on and massacred, and large numbers of Communists, labour leaders and revolutionary masses were arrested and killed. Guangzhou and other places soon carried out a “party purge”, and the National Revolution suffered a grave setback.

event:四川独立.note: On 22 November the Shu Military Government was set up in Chongqing; on the 27th Zhao Erfeng handed over power and the Great Han Sichuan Military Government was established in Chengdu. After a mutiny in Chengdu on 8 December, Yin Changheng became military governor, and on the 22nd Zhao Erfeng was executed. The two military governments merged in 1912.

event:国共合作宣言公布.note: The KMT's Central News Agency published the CPC Central Committee's Declaration on the Publication of KMT–CPC Cooperation; the next day Chiang Kai-shek issued a statement recognizing the CPC's legal status. The second KMT–CPC cooperation formally took shape, and the Anti-Japanese National United Front was formally established.

event:国民会议.note: The Nationalist Government convened the National Convention, which adopted the Provisional Constitution of the Republic of China for the Period of Political Tutelage, promulgated and put into effect on 1 June, establishing one-party tutelage by the KMT.

event:国民党一大.note: Sun Yat-sen presided over the First National Congress of the Kuomintang of China, which reorganized the KMT, gave a new interpretation of the Three People's Principles and established the Three Great Policies of alliance with Soviet Russia, cooperation with the Communist Party and assistance to the peasants and workers. Communists joined the KMT as individuals, and the first KMT–CPC cooperation formally took shape.
event:国民党一大.old: First National Congress of the KMT

event:国民党临时全国代表大会.note: The congress adopted the Programme of Armed Resistance and National Reconstruction, elected Chiang Kai-shek Director-General of the KMT and Wang Jingwei Deputy Director-General, and decided to set up the People's Political Council and the Three People's Principles Youth League.

event:国民党五届五中全会.note: The plenary session set up the Supreme National Defence Council and adopted the policy of “dissolving, guarding against and restricting the Communists”; thereafter the focus of KMT policy gradually shifted to anti-Communism, and friction between the KMT and the CPC increased.
event:国民党五届五中全会.old: Fifth Plenary Session of the Fifth KMT Central Executive Committee

event:国民党六大.note: The Sixth National Congress of the KMT decided to convene a National Assembly in November and adopted a resolution on the CPC question, holding fast to one-party dictatorship. The struggle between the KMT and the CPC over the future of post-war China came into the open.
event:国民党六大.old: Sixth National Congress of the KMT

event:国民党当局退踞台湾.note: The KMT government had already moved from Nanjing to Guangzhou, Chongqing and Chengdu; on 7 December its Executive Yuan resolved to move to Taipei, began working in Taiwan the next day, and retreated to entrench itself in Taiwan. On 1 March 1950 Chiang Kai-shek resumed office in Taipei.

event:国民党残军撤台.note: Under arrangements made by a four-party military commission of the United States, Thailand, Burma and the Taiwan authorities, the remnant troops and their dependants passed through Thailand in three batches and were flown out to Taiwan from Chiang Rai; on 30 May Li Mi announced the disbandment of the “Yunnan Anti-Communist National Salvation Army”, but several thousand men remained in Burma.
event:国民党残军撤台.old: KMT remnant troops evacuated to Taiwan

event:国民党残军盘踞掸邦.note: The KMT remnant forces of Li Mi made Mong Hsat their headquarters and built an airfield for links with Taiwan; in 1951 they twice invaded Yunnan and were driven back by the PLA, then built up their strength east of the Salween River, and repeated attacks by the Burmese army failed to dislodge them. In March 1953 Burma announced that it would stop accepting US aid and took the matter to the United Nations; on 23 April the UN General Assembly passed a resolution demanding that the foreign troops leave Burma.
event:国民党残军盘踞掸邦.old: KMT remnant troops entrench in the Shan States

event:国民参政会成立.note: The highest wartime body for consulting public opinion opened in Hankou, with the KMT, the CPC, the Young China Party, the National Socialist Party of China and non-party figures taking part, reflecting unity in the War of Resistance.

event:国民政府对日德意宣战.note: The day after the attack on Pearl Harbor, the Nationalist Government formally declared war on Japan, and also on Germany and Italy. After more than four years of the Nationwide War of Resistance, the “incident” at last became a formally declared war, and China became an ally of the United States, Britain and other countries.
event:国民政府对日德意宣战.old: Nationalist Government declares war on Japan, Germany and Italy

event:国民政府承认外蒙古独立.note: The Nationalist Government announced its recognition of Outer Mongolia's independence, and the two countries established diplomatic relations in February. In 1953 the Taiwan authorities revoked the recognition on the grounds that the Soviet Union had violated the treaty.
event:国民政府承认外蒙古独立.old: Nationalist Government recognizes Outer Mongolian independence

event:国民政府移驻重庆.note: The Nationalist Government issued its declaration on moving to Chongqing, and Lin Sen and others arrived there at the end of the month; the military high command and most ministries were based in Wuhan at first and all moved to Chongqing from the autumn of 1938.

event:国民政府迁都武汉.note: Members of the KMT Central Committee and of the Nationalist Government formed a provisional joint council in Hankou, and the government formally began work in Wuhan on 1 January 1927. Chiang Kai-shek wanted it to remain at Nanchang for the time being, and so began the dispute over the move of the capital.

event:国民政府还都南京.note: The Nationalist Government moved its capital back from Chongqing to Nanjing and held a ceremony for the return of the capital; Chongqing remained the auxiliary capital.

event:土地改革法.note: The Central People's Government promulgated the Agrarian Reform Law of the People's Republic of China, abolishing the landlord class's system of feudal exploitative land ownership and preserving the rich-peasant economy. From the winter of 1950 it was carried out in stages in the newly liberated areas of East China, Central-South China, Southwest China and Northwest China, and was basically completed by the end of 1952.

event:土耳其共和国成立.note: The Grand National Assembly proclaimed Turkey a republic and elected Mustafa Kemal president, with İsmet as prime minister; on 13 October Ankara had been made the capital.

event:土耳其加入北约.note: Turkey sent troops to join the US-led “UN Command” forces in the Korean War and, with US support, joined the North Atlantic Treaty Organization at the same time as Greece; in April 1954 it also concluded a cooperation agreement with Pakistan, paving the way for the Baghdad Pact the following year.

event:基斯卡撤退.note: Under cover of thick fog, Japanese cruisers and destroyers evacuated the more than 5,000-strong garrison within an hour; when combined US and Canadian forces landed on 15 August, the island was deserted.

event:塘沽协定.note: Signed by Xiong Bin for the Nationalist Government and Okamura Yasuji for the Japanese Kwantung Army. Chinese troops withdrew west and south of the Yanqing–Tongzhou–Ninghe line, and the twenty-two counties of eastern Hebei south of the Great Wall were made a demilitarized zone, in effect recognizing Japan's occupation of the Northeast and Rehe.

event:塞兰岛游击战.note: After the loss of Ambon, the remnants of the “Republic of South Maluku” retreated into the mountain forests of Seram to wage guerrilla warfare, while Indonesian troops held the coastal towns. Its leader Soumokil was captured in December 1962 and executed in 1966.

event:外蒙古“独立”.note: Instigated by tsarist Russia, the princes and senior lamas of Outer Mongolia declared “independence” and expelled Sanduo, the Amban at Urga; on the 29th they enthroned the Jebtsundamba Khutughtu as Bogd Khan, with the era name “Gongdai”.

event:外蒙古取消自治.note: Xu Shuzheng, the Northwest Frontier Commissioner, led the Frontier Defence Army into Urga, and the Outer Mongolian princes petitioned to renounce “autonomy”. On 22 November the Beijing Government formally decreed the end of Outer Mongolian “autonomy”; the arrangements set by the Kyakhta Agreement were abolished, and jurisdiction over Outer Mongolia was restored.

event:外蒙古独立公投.note: Under the notes exchanged with the Sino-Soviet Treaty of Friendship and Alliance, Outer Mongolia held a plebiscite on independence, observed by Lei Fazhang, Vice-Minister of the Interior, sent by the Nationalist Government; officially, every voter was announced to have voted for independence.

event:外高加索三国独立.note: The Transcaucasian Democratic Federative Republic broke up after little more than a month; Georgia declared independence on 26 May, followed by Armenia and Azerbaijan on the 28th.
event:外高加索三国独立.old: Independence of the three Transcaucasian states

event:大元帅府成立.note: After Chen Jiongming had been driven out of Guangzhou, Sun Yat-sen returned to Guangdong on 21 February and on 2 March set up the Army and Navy Generalissimo's Headquarters at the Cement Works; no longer styling himself president, he commanded the Yunnan, Guangxi, Guangdong and Hunan armies as Generalissimo.

event:大国民议会开幕.note: After the Allies formally occupied Istanbul in March and dissolved the Ottoman parliament, nationalist deputies convened a separate Grand National Assembly in Ankara; Kemal was elected its speaker, setting up a rival authority to the sultan's government in Istanbul.

event:大逆事件.note: On the pretext of a plot to assassinate Emperor Meiji, the Japanese government fabricated a case and carried out mass arrests of socialists and anarchists; twelve people, including Kōtoku Shūsui, were executed in January 1911, and the socialist movement entered a “winter period”.

event:大韩民国临时政府成立.note: After the March First Movement, Korean independence activists in exile set up a provisional government in the Shanghai French Concession, with Syngman Rhee as premier and later president. After 1932 it moved successively to Hangzhou, Changsha, Guangzhou and Chongqing; in November 1945 Kim Ku and others returned home.
event:大韩民国临时政府成立.old: Provisional Government of the Republic of Korea established

event:大韩民国成立.note: With US backing, a constitution was drawn up after the separate southern election of 10 May; Syngman Rhee was elected president, the establishment of the government of the Republic of Korea was proclaimed on 15 August, and the US Army Military Government handed over power.

event:天津事变.note: The Japanese secret agent Doihara Kenji organized a riot by plainclothes squads in Tianjin and, in the confusion, secretly spirited Puyi out of Tianjin via Yingkou to Lüshun, in preparation for setting up Puppet Manchukuo.

event:天津租界危机.note: Claiming that the British Concession was sheltering anti-Japanese elements, Japanese troops blockaded the British and French concessions in Tianjin; in the Arita–Craigie Agreement Britain acknowledged the “special requirements” of the Japanese army in China, compromising with Japan.

event:太原起义.note: New Army regimental commander Yan Xishan and others rose in revolt, killed Governor Lu Zhongqi and set up the Shanxi Military Government. As Shanxi commanded the flank and rear of the capital region, the Qing court hurriedly sent the Beiyang Army into Shanxi.

event:奄美群岛归还.note: From 1951 a reversion movement swept the Amami islands, with many people joining hunger-strike petitions. The United States and Japan signed an agreement, and on 25 December the Amami Islands were returned to Japan and restored to Kagoshima Prefecture; Okinawa remained under US administration.

event:奥斯曼帝国参战.note: The Ottoman fleet (including the Goeben, handed over by Germany) bombarded Russian Black Sea ports on 29 October; in November the Allies declared war on the Ottoman Empire, and on the 14th the sultan-caliph proclaimed a holy war.

event:孙中山北上与逝世.note: Invited north to discuss affairs of state, Sun Yat-sen travelled via Shanghai and Kobe, Japan, to Tianjin and Beijing, calling for a National Convention and the abolition of the unequal treaties in opposition to Duan Qirui's Rehabilitation Conference; he died of illness in Beijing on 12 March 1925.
event:孙中山北上与逝世.old: Sun Yat-sen's journey north and death

event:孙中山就任非常大总统.note: After the Guangdong Army returned to Guangdong, the Extraordinary Parliament in Guangzhou elected Sun Yat-sen Extraordinary President of the Republic of China; he took office on 5 May in opposition to the Beijing Government. Sun Yat-sen soon began planning a Northern Expedition, and his differences with Chen Jiongming, who advocated a “federation of self-governing provinces”, grew ever deeper.

event:孙文越飞宣言.note: Sun Yat-sen and the Soviet Russian envoy Joffe issued a joint manifesto in Shanghai: Soviet Russia declared that it had no intention of introducing the communist system into China and renounced the privileges of tsarist Russia in China. Sun Yat-sen adopted the policy of alliance with Soviet Russia, and Soviet advisers and aid then arrived in Guangzhou.

event:孟加拉大饥荒.note: The fall of Burma cut off rice supplies; with the British colonial authorities' wartime procurement and hoarding compounded by a cyclone disaster, rice prices in Bengal soared, and some two to three million people died of starvation and disease.

event:孟加拉语运动.note: Students in East Bengal, opposing Urdu as the sole national language, demonstrated near Dacca University, and police opened fire, killing several people. The 1956 constitution recognized Bengali as one of the national languages, and the day was later designated International Mother Language Day.

event:宁汉合流.note: After Wuhan's “purge of Communists”, the Nanjing, Wuhan and Western Hills factions formed the Special Central Committee of the Kuomintang of China and reorganized the Nationalist Government, and the Wuhan Nationalist Government came to an end soon after.
event:宁汉合流.old: Merger of the Nanjing and Wuhan governments

event:宁粤和谈.note: After the September 18 Incident, Nanjing and Guangzhou held peace talks in Shanghai and agreed that each would hold its own Fourth National Congress of the KMT and then jointly form a new central leadership; in December Chiang Kai-shek resigned and the Guangzhou Nationalist Government was abolished.

event:宁粤对立·广州国民政府.note: Wang Jingwei, Sun Fo, Chen Jitang, Li Zongren and others convened an Extraordinary Conference of members of the Central Executive and Supervisory Committees in Guangzhou and set up a separate Nationalist Government in confrontation with Nanjing, known as the Nanjing–Guangzhou split; it was abolished after Chiang Kai-shek resigned in December.
event:宁粤对立·广州国民政府.old: Nanjing–Guangzhou split: the Guangzhou Nationalist Government
