event:宁都会议.note: The Central Bureau of the Soviet Areas met at Xiaoyuan in Ningdu, where the “Left” leaders wrongly criticized Mao Zedong as “Rightist” and removed him as general political commissar of the Red First Front Army, a post taken over by Zhou Enlai; from then until the Zunyi Meeting, Mao Zedong was out of the Red Army's leadership.

event:安国军政府成立.note: The Fengtian warlord Zhang Zuolin took office in Beijing as Generalissimo of the Army and Navy of the Republic of China and formed the Anguojun Military Government, the last central government of the Beiyang warlords; it ended in June 1928 when he withdrew to the Northeast.

event:安得拉邦成立.note: Potti Sriramulu, a leader of the Telugu-language movement, died after a 58-day fast, setting off riots; Nehru agreed to carve the Telugu-speaking areas out of Madras State to form Andhra State, with its capital at Kurnool, the beginning of the redrawing of India's state boundaries along linguistic lines.

event:安沛起义.note: The Vietnamese Nationalist Party launched an uprising of the Vietnamese soldiers of the Yên Bái garrison, which French forces crushed within days; Nguyễn Thái Học and twelve others were executed. Thereafter leadership of the Vietnamese national movement passed to the Communist Party of Vietnam (Indochinese Communist Party), founded in Hong Kong the same month.

event:宋教仁案.note: Song Jiaoren, acting chairman of the Kuomintang, was shot at the Shanghai–Nanjing Railway station by an assassin sent by Yuan Shikai and died on the 22nd. The Kuomintang had just won the parliamentary elections. In April Yuan Shikai went on to bypass parliament and sign the Reorganization Loan; Sun Yat-sen resolved to take up arms against Yuan, and North and South split.

event:定重庆为陪都.note: The Nationalist Government formally designated Chongqing the auxiliary capital, signalling its resolve to wage a protracted war of resistance; Chongqing kept the title of auxiliary capital after the government returned to Nanjing in May 1946.

event:宜昌大撤退.note: Around the fall of Wuhan, Lu Zuofu's Minsheng Company organized fleets at Yichang to ship the stranded personnel and arsenal equipment into Sichuan before the Yangtze River's low-water season.

event:密苏里号受降.note: Japanese representatives Shigemitsu Mamoru and Umezu Yoshijirō signed the instrument of unconditional surrender aboard the US warship Missouri in Tokyo Bay; MacArthur accepted the surrender on behalf of the Allies, and Xu Yongchang signed for China. The Second World War came to an end.

event:富田事变.note: During the purge of the “AB League”, the General Front Committee of the Red First Front Army arrested local Red Army and soviet cadres in Jiangxi; part of the Red 20th Army rose at Futian and freed those arrested. The incident was branded counter-revolutionary at the time, and the campaign to eliminate counter-revolutionaries in southwestern Jiangxi was then seriously overextended.

event:察哈尔民众抗日同盟军成立.note: In cooperation with the Communist Party of China, Feng Yuxiang announced by circular telegram at Zhangjiakou that he had taken up the post of commander-in-chief, and Ji Hongchang, Fang Zhenwu and others joined him to resist Japan together; the Nanjing Nationalist Government, however, denounced it as “undermining unity”.
event:察哈尔民众抗日同盟军成立.old: Chahar People's Anti-Japanese Allied Army formed

event:对德奥宣战.note: Duan Qirui's government declared war on Germany and Austria-Hungary, bringing China in on the side of the Allies; it took back the German and Austro-Hungarian concessions in China and stopped paying their Boxer Indemnity. In the name of entering the war, Duan Qirui borrowed heavily from Japan to raise and train the War Participation Army, building up the strength of the Anhui Clique.
event:对德奥宣战.old: China declares war on Germany and Austria-Hungary

event:对日和约生效.note: The one-sided San Francisco Peace Treaty and the US–Japan Security Treaty took effect; Allied General Headquarters was abolished, the US occupation of six years and eight months came to an end, and Japan regained its sovereignty. Okinawa and the Bonin Islands remained under US administration.
event:对日和约生效.old: Peace treaty with Japan takes effect

event:尼泊尔 1950 年革命.note: King Tribhuvan took refuge in the Indian embassy and then left for New Delhi, and the Nepali Congress launched an armed rising from the Indian border; with Indian mediation a coalition government was formed in February 1951, ending more than a century of dictatorship by the hereditary prime ministers of the Rana family.

event:尼港事件.note: Tryapitsyn's partisans occupied Nikolayevsk; a Japanese night attack on 12 March failed, and several hundred Japanese soldiers and residents were killed. Before withdrawing at the end of May, the partisans burned the town and executed their hostages. Japan used this as grounds to occupy northern Sakhalin.

event:山东独立与取消.note: Under pressure from all quarters, Governor Sun Baoqi declared independence, only to revoke it 11 days later under coercion from officers of the Beiyang 5th Division. Shandong became a province that declared and then revoked its independence; only the Yantai area remained with the revolutionary army.

event:山东问题（巴黎和会）.note: The Paris Peace Conference was manipulated by the imperialist powers; on 30 April the three-power council of Britain, the United States and France decided to transfer Germany's rights in Shandong to Japan. China's diplomatic failure sparked the May Fourth Movement, and on 28 June the Chinese delegation refused to sign the peace treaty with Germany.

event:山打根死亡行军.note: The Japanese marched Australian and British prisoners from the Sandakan POW camp inland to Ranau in three groups; more than 2,400 died on the marches and in the camps, and the only survivors were six men who escaped.

event:川人治川.note: After the Yunnan and Guizhou Armies withdrew, the Sichuan Army generals declared Sichuan self-governing by circular telegram, rejecting appointments from both North and South. In June 1921 they made Liu Xiang commander-in-chief of the Sichuan Army and provincial governor; each army raised its own funds within its own garrison zone, giving rise to the warlord garrison-zone system that lasted for many years.

event:川军入拉萨.note: Zhong Ying led 2,000 men of the Sichuan Army into Lhasa; the 13th Dalai Lama fled overnight to India, and the Qing court stripped him of his title. Qing central administration in Xizang reached its peak, while Britain seized the chance to court the Dalai Lama.

event:巴丹死亡行军.note: More than 70,000 American and Filipino prisoners who had surrendered on Bataan were marched more than 100 km under the blazing sun to San Fernando and then taken on to Camp O'Donnell; along the way thousands died of hunger, thirst and disease or were bayoneted.

event:巴列维王朝建立.note: On 31 October parliament deposed the Qajar dynasty, and on 12 December a Constituent Assembly made Reza Khan shah; he was crowned the following April and pursued centralizing and secularizing reforms.

event:布赖米争端.note: Saudi Arabia sent Turki ibn Ataishan with a few dozen men to occupy the Buraimi Oasis and claim sovereignty; Abu Dhabi and Muscat protested with British support. In 1954 the two sides agreed to submit the dispute to international arbitration, and in October 1955 the British drove out the Saudi personnel with the Trucial Oman Levies.

event:希腊军登陆士麦那.note: The Paris Peace Conference allowed Greece to send troops to occupy Smyrna, and on the day of the landing they clashed with the Turkish inhabitants. This roused national resistance across Anatolia, and the Turkish national liberation movement arose from it.

event:平江惨案.note: KMT diehards had troops of the 27th Army Group surround the New Fourth Army's liaison office in Pingjiang and murder Tu Zhengkun and others, a grave anti-Communist incident engineered by the KMT diehards.

event:平顶山惨案.note: After the Liaoning People's Self-Defence Army raided the Japanese mining district at Fushun, Japanese troops, on the charge of “colluding with bandits”, drove more than 3,000 villagers of Pingdingshan to the foot of the hill and machine-gunned them, then burned the bodies to destroy the evidence, perpetrating the Pingdingshan Massacre.

event:广岛原子弹.note: The US B-29 Enola Gay dropped the uranium bomb “Little Boy” on Hiroshima; by the end of the year about 140,000 people had died.

event:广州商团叛乱.note: Chen Lianbo and others of the Guangzhou Merchants' Corps, backed by British imperialism, had their smuggled arms impounded; they colluded with Chen Jiongming in a plot to overthrow the revolutionary government. On 10 October the Corps opened fire on a commemorative procession, and on the 15th the Whampoa student army, the Workers' Corps and other forces, on Sun Yat-sen's orders, put down the Merchants' Corps rebellion in Xiguan.

event:广州国民政府成立.note: The Kuomintang of China reorganized the Generalissimo's Headquarters as the Nationalist Government of the Republic of China, with Wang Jingwei as chairman and a collegial committee system; in August its armies were unified as the First to Fifth Armies of the National Revolutionary Army. The Guangdong revolutionary base was thereby consolidated.

event:广西独立.note: Following Guizhou, Lu Rongting declared Guangxi independent, and the Guangxi Army advanced east into Guangdong. Having lost his southwestern shield, Yuan Shikai was forced to abolish the monarchy a week later.

event:庐山谈话.note: At the Lushan talks, Chiang Kai-shek declared: “Once war breaks out, then, whether north or south, old or young, every person, whoever he may be, has the duty to defend our land and resist.”

event:府院之争.note: President Li Yuanhong and Premier Duan Qirui were deadlocked over the bill to enter the war against Germany; parliament refused to consider it, and Duan's side had the Military Governors' Corps apply pressure. On 23 May Li Yuanhong dismissed Duan Qirui, the Anhui Clique provinces declared independence, and Li Yuanhong summoned Zhang Xun to Beijing to mediate.
event:府院之争.old: Dispute between the President and the Cabinet

event:废除哈里发.note: The Grand National Assembly abolished the caliphate and expelled the Ottoman dynasty, at the same time abolishing the religious courts and the Ministry of Religious Affairs. A few days later King Hussein of Hejaz proclaimed himself caliph, hastening his downfall.

event:废除苏丹制.note: The Grand National Assembly voted to abolish the sultanate, keeping the caliphate as a purely religious office. The last sultan, Mehmed VI, left aboard a British warship on 17 November, and Abdülmecid II was chosen caliph.

event:廖仲恺遇刺.note: Liao Zhongkai, a leader of the KMT left, was assassinated by the KMT right outside the Central Party Headquarters. As the case implicated relatives of Hu Hanmin and Guangdong Army generals, Hu Hanmin went abroad and Xu Chongzhi was forced to leave Guangdong in September, leaving Chiang Kai-shek in control of the armed forces in Guangdong.

event:延安总部受降令·全面反攻.note: In the name of the Yan'an headquarters, Zhu De issued seven orders in succession, directing the forces of all the Liberated Areas to deliver ultimatums to the Japanese and puppet troops to lay down their arms by a deadline, and sending troops into the Northeast, Chahar and Suiyuan. Chiang Kai-shek, for his part, ordered the Eighth Route Army to “stay where it is and await orders”, in an attempt to monopolize the right to accept the surrender.
event:延安总部受降令·全面反攻.old: Yan'an headquarters' orders to accept surrender: general counter-offensive

event:延安整风.note: Mao Zedong gave the report Rectify the Style of Study, the Party's Style of Work and the Style of Writing, and the whole Party launched the Rectification Movement against subjectivism, sectarianism and stereotyped Party writing; during the 1943 screening of cadres a deviation occurred for a time in the form of the “rescue campaign”. With the adoption of the historical resolution at the Seventh Plenary Session of the Sixth Central Committee, the whole Party achieved unprecedented unity on the basis of Mao Zedong Thought.

event:开城停战谈判.note: After Soviet representative Malik proposed a ceasefire on 23 June, the delegates of the two sides opened armistice talks at Laebongjang in Kaesong and agreed to put the question of the military demarcation line first on the agenda; on 23 August the Chinese–Korean side broke off the talks because the Kaesong neutral zone had been attacked.

event:开罗会议.note: Roosevelt, Churchill and Chiang Kai-shek conferred on the war against Japan and post-war arrangements. The Cairo Declaration, issued on 1 December, stated that the Chinese territories Japan had stolen, such as the Northeast, Taiwan and the Penghu Islands, should be restored to China, and that Korea should become independent in due course.

event:张勋复辟.note: Zhang Xun led his Pigtail Army into Beijing, forced Li Yuanhong to dissolve parliament and on 1 July restored Puyi to the throne, declaring the year Xuantong 9. The restoration met nationwide opposition; twelve days later the Anti-Restoration Army entered Beijing, and Puyi abdicated a second time.

event:张学良通电入关.note: Zhang Xueliang declared by circular telegram his support for the central government and called for a ceasefire; the Northeastern Army promptly entered North China and took over Beiping and Tianjin. With Yan and Feng now attacked from front and rear, the outcome of the Central Plains War was decided at once; Zhang Xueliang became Deputy Commander-in-Chief of the Army, Navy and Air Force and took up his post in Beiping.
event:张学良通电入关.old: Zhang Xueliang's circular telegram and entry into North China

event:张自忠殉国.note: During the Battle of Zaoyang–Yichang, Zhang Zizhong, commander-in-chief of the 33rd Army Group, crossed the Han River to intercept the Japanese and died for his country after fierce fighting at Nanguadian, one of the highest-ranking commanders to die for the country in the War of Resistance.
event:张自忠殉国.old: Zhang Zizhong dies for his country

event:彝海结盟.note: Liu Bocheng and Xiao Yedan, chief of the Guoji clan of the Yi people, swore an alliance in blood on the shore of Yihai Lake; the Red Army was able to pass peacefully through the Yi area and reach the Dadu River ahead of the KMT forces—a successful application of the Party's ethnic policy.

event:彭县起义.note: Liu Wenhui, Deng Xihou and Pan Wenhua issued a joint circular telegram at Pengxian announcing their uprising; Xikang and northwestern Sichuan were peacefully liberated, and the KMT forces at Chengdu were caught between attacks from front and rear.

event:徐州会议.note: Feng Yuxiang first conferred with the Wuhan side at Zhengzhou, then went on to Xuzhou for talks with Chiang Kai-shek; he switched to supporting Nanjing and demanded that Wuhan “purge the Communists”, and from then on the balance between Nanjing and Wuhan tipped towards Nanjing.

event:德拉特尔防线.note: De Lattre built a line of concrete blockhouses along the outer edge of the Red River Delta, from Quảng Yên through Bắc Ninh and Vĩnh Yên to Ninh Bình and Phát Diệm; the delta thus became the core area held by French forces, though many Viet Minh guerrilla zones remained inside the line.

event:德里杜尔巴.note: King George V of Britain, as Emperor of India, received homage at Delhi and announced that the capital of British India would move from Calcutta to Delhi, and that the 1905 partition of Bengal would be revoked.

event:德黑兰会议.note: Roosevelt, Stalin and Churchill met for the first time, agreed to open a second front in France in 1944, and issued a declaration guaranteeing Iran's independence and territorial integrity after the war.

event:懋功会师.note: The Central Red Army crossed Jiajin Mountain; its vanguard joined the Red Fourth Front Army at Dawei on the 12th, and the central leaders reached Maogong on the 18th. The two armies together numbered more than 100,000.

event:成都血案.note: In May the Qing government proclaimed the “nationalization of railways”, selling off railway rights in return for foreign loans, and the people of Sichuan rose to protect the railways. Viceroy of Sichuan Zhao Erfeng lured and arrested Pu Dianjun and other leaders of the Railway Protection Comrades' Association and opened fire on the petitioning crowd; Comrades' Armies rose on all sides and besieged Chengdu, and the Qing court sent Hubei New Army troops into Sichuan, leaving Wuchang thinly defended.

event:所谓“南马鲁古共和国”成立.note: Ambonese former officers and soldiers of the Netherlands East Indies colonial army and local leaders, opposed to incorporation into a unitary state, proclaimed “independence”, splitting Indonesia. Indonesian troops captured the town of Ambon in November; after 1951 some of the Ambonese soldiers moved to the Netherlands with the Dutch army.

event:扎西会议.note: The Political Bureau held a series of meetings around Zhaxi; Zhang Wentian replaced Bo Gu in overall charge, the Central Red Army was streamlined into sixteen regiments, and it was decided to turn back to northern Guizhou.

event:护国起义.note: Tang Jiyao, Cai E and Li Liejun announced Yunnan's independence by circular telegram and formed the National Protection Army to fight Yuan, in three armies: Cai E's First Army to enter Sichuan, Li Liejun's Second Army to advance into Guangdong and Guangxi, and Tang Jiyao's Third Army to hold the home base. Thus began the National Protection War.

event:护法军政府成立.note: Members of parliament went south and held an Extraordinary Session in Guangzhou, which on 1 September elected Sun Yat-sen Generalissimo of the Army and Navy of the Military Government of the Republic of China, with Tang Jiyao and Lu Rongting as marshals. Sun Yat-sen took office on the 10th, rallying the country to uphold the Provisional Constitution and restore parliament; thus began the Constitution Protection Movement.

event:拉合尔决议.note: Under Jinnah's presidency, the All-India Muslim League passed a resolution demanding “independent states” in the Muslim-majority areas of the north-west and east, commonly known as the “Pakistan Resolution”.

event:拉合尔完全独立决议.note: At its Lahore session, presided over by Nehru, the Indian National Congress passed the “complete independence” resolution, and on the night of 31 December the tricolour was raised on the bank of the Ravi River; 26 January 1930 was declared “Independence Day”, which later became India's Republic Day.

event:挺进大别山.note: Liu Bocheng and Deng Xiaoping led the main force of the Shanxi-Hebei-Shandong-Henan Field Army south from southwestern Shandong, across the Longhai Railway, the Yellow River flooded area and the Ru and Huai rivers, in a thousand-li leap into the Dabie Mountains, raising the curtain on the PLA's strategic offensive.

event:捷克军团叛乱.note: After a clash at Chelyabinsk station, the Soviet authorities ordered the Czechoslovak Legion, some 40,000 men withdrawing east along the Trans-Siberian Railway, to be disarmed; at the instigation of the Allies the Legion revolted, Soviet power from the Volga River to Vladivostok was overthrown in place after place within weeks, and the Civil War broke out in full.

event:接管河内.note: Within the 80-day deadline set by the Geneva Accords, French forces left Hà Nội on 9 October, and the Vietnam People's Army 308th Division entered the city the next day to take it over; the central organs of the Democratic Republic of Vietnam then moved back from Việt Bắc. At the end of October French forces also withdrew from Hải Dương, leaving only the Hải Phòng area in the north, which they evacuated completely in May 1955.

event:摩苏尔问题解决.note: In December 1925 the League of Nations awarded the province of Mosul to Iraq; Turkey accepted this in the Treaty of Ankara with Britain and Iraq, in return for 10 per cent of Mosul's oil revenues for twenty-five years.

event:收回威海卫.note: Under the Sino-British agreement of April 1930, Britain returned Weihaiwei, which it had leased for thirty-two years; the Nationalist Government set up the Weihaiwei Administrative Office under its direct control, while Liugong Island remained on loan to the British navy for ten more years.

event:收回汉口、九江英租界.note: British sailors stabbed and wounded members of the crowd outside the Jianghan Customs House in Hankou, and the people stormed into the British Concession; the Nationalist Government promptly took over the British Concessions at Hankou and Jiujiang and formally recovered them by agreement in February. It was the first time in modern history that the Chinese people had recovered concessions through mass struggle and diplomatic negotiation, a major victory in the anti-imperialist struggle.
event:收回汉口、九江英租界.old: Recovery of the British Concessions at Hankou and Jiujiang

event:政治协商会议.note: Thirty-eight delegates of the KMT, the CPC, the China Democratic League, the Young China Party and prominent public figures met and adopted five agreements, on the organization of the government, the programme for peaceful national reconstruction, military questions, the draft constitution and the National Assembly; they were soon wrecked by the KMT and never implemented.

event:文夕大火.note: After the fall of Yueyang, the KMT authorities in Changsha misjudged the enemy situation and set fires prematurely under the “scorched-earth resistance” plan; most of the city burned, and thousands were killed or injured.

event:斯大林逝世.note: Stalin died at his dacha outside Moscow, and Malenkov, Beria, Khrushchev and others formed a collective leadership. The Soviet Union promptly helped bring about a turn in the Korean armistice talks, and at the end of March the Chinese and Korean side agreed to an advance exchange of sick and wounded prisoners of war.

event:新四军组建.note: The Red Army guerrillas in eight southern provinces were reorganized as the New Fourth Army of the National Revolutionary Army, with Ye Ting as commander and Xiang Ying as deputy commander; its headquarters was set up in Hankou on 25 December and early the following year moved to Nanchang and southern Anhui.

event:新四军重建军部.note: The Central Military Commission of the CPC ordered the headquarters of the New Fourth Army re-established, with Chen Yi as acting commander and Liu Shaoqi as political commissar; the army was reorganized into seven divisions and one brigade, kept up the War of Resistance behind enemy lines in Central China, and grew steadily stronger.

event:新生活运动.note: Launched by Chiang Kai-shek at his Nanchang Field Headquarters, the movement sought to regulate food, clothing, housing and travel by the virtues of “propriety, righteousness, integrity and sense of shame”, serving the political and social control of the “Communist suppression” campaigns; it was later extended to the whole country.

event:新疆和平起义.note: Xinjiang Garrison Commander-in-Chief Tao Zhiyue and Provincial Chairman Burhan Shahidi issued circular telegrams announcing their uprising one after the other, and Xinjiang was peacefully liberated; on 20 October the First Field Army entered Dihua. Earlier, Ehmetjan Qasimi and other leaders of the Three Districts Revolution, invited to Beiping to attend the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, had been killed in a plane crash on the way.

event:新疆联合政府.note: Zhang Zhizhong signed peace terms with representatives of the Three Districts Revolutionary Government, and in July the Xinjiang Province coalition government was formed, with Ehmetjan Qasimi as vice-chairman. In 1947 the coalition government broke down, and the Three Districts kept up the revolution until the peaceful liberation of Xinjiang in 1949.

event:日内瓦协议.mod: Hiền Lương Bridge, Quảng Trị, Vietnam
event:日内瓦协议.note: The Geneva Conference took up Indochina from 8 May, and on 20–21 July armistice agreements were signed, restoring peace in Indochina. In Vietnam, the Bến Hải River near the 17th parallel became the provisional military demarcation line; the forces of the two sides were to regroup to the north and south within 300 days, and nationwide elections were to be held in July 1956. Pathet Lao forces were to regroup in Sam Neua and Phongsaly, and no regroupment zone was designated in Cambodia. The United States issued a unilateral declaration, and the State of Vietnam objected.

event:日军侵占广州湾.note: Japanese troops landed in the French leased territory of Guangzhouwan, where the Vichy French authorities signed an agreement with Japan for “joint defence”; the Japanese also occupied the Leizhou Peninsula. In August 1945 China and France signed an agreement for the return of Guangzhouwan.

event:日军侵占海南岛.note: Japanese troops landed near Haikou and soon took Sanya; Hainan was placed under the long-term direct rule of the Japanese navy and became a base for the southward advance, while the Qiongya anti-Japanese forces and the KMT defenders withdrew into the mountains.

event:日军侵占阿图、基斯卡.note: At the same time as the Midway operation, Japanese forces seized the islands of Kiska and Attu in the western Aleutians to tie down US forces in the North Pacific, causing alarm on the US mainland.

event:日军撤出海参崴.note: Under pressure at the Washington Conference and criticism at home, Japan was forced to withdraw its troops; the last Japanese troops left Vladivostok on 25 October, and the People's Revolutionary Army entered the city the same day. The armed intervention, which had lasted more than four years at enormous cost, ended in failure.

event:日军进占上海租界.note: On the day the Pacific War broke out, Japanese troops marched into the Shanghai International Settlement, ending the “Isolated Island” period; British and American residents were later interned. The French Concession survived for the time being because Vichy France collaborated with Japan.

event:日军进驻越北.note: Decoux, Vichy France's Governor-General of Indochina, was forced to sign an agreement with the Japanese allowing Japanese troops to be stationed at airfields in northern Vietnam and to pass through; all transport to China on the Yunnan–Vietnam Railway stopped. The United States promptly imposed an embargo on scrap iron and steel to Japan.

event:日军进驻越南南部.note: Under the Franco-Japanese joint defence agreement, Japanese troops moved into Cochinchina and Cambodia, occupying Cam Ranh Bay and the Sài Gòn airfields and pointing straight at Malaya and the Dutch East Indies. On 1 August the United States imposed a total oil embargo on Japan, and Japan resolved to advance south.

event:日军龙口登陆.note: China had declared neutrality and marked out a war zone, yet Japanese troops brazenly landed at Longkou and pushed west, seizing Jinan station on 6 October and taking control of the entire Qingdao–Jinan Railway. Thus arose the Shandong Question.

event:日本侵占北库页岛.note: Using the Nikolayevsk Incident as a pretext, Japan sent troops into the northern part of Sakhalin Island in the name of a “guarantee occupation”, set up a military administration and prospected the Okha oilfield; the occupation lasted until 1925.

event:日本吞并朝鲜.note: Japan forced the Korean Empire to sign the Japan–Korea Annexation Treaty, signed on 22 August and promulgated on the 29th; the Korean Empire perished and Korea was reduced to a Japanese colony. On 1 October the Government-General of Korea was set up, with Terauchi Masatake as the first Governor-General.

event:日本国宪法施行.note: The new constitution promulgated in November 1946 took effect: the emperor became the symbol of the unity of the people, sovereignty rested with the people, and Article 9 renounced war and the maintenance of war potential.

event:日本夺取南洋群岛.note: After the outbreak of the First World War, Japanese navy South Seas squadrons seized in succession the German Marshall, Caroline, Palau and Mariana Islands; after the war Japan held them as a League of Nations mandate, known as the South Seas Islands.
event:日本夺取南洋群岛.old: Japan seizes the South Seas Islands

event:日本宣布无条件投降.note: The Japanese Emperor broadcast the Imperial Rescript on the Termination of the War, announcing acceptance of the Potsdam Proclamation and unconditional surrender. After fourteen years of resistance (eight years of the Nationwide War of Resistance), the Chinese people won a great victory in the War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression.

event:日本对美英宣战.note: In the early hours of 8 December, Japan time, Japanese forces made a surprise attack on Pearl Harbor and invaded Malaya; the same day Japan declared war on the United States and Britain, and the Pacific War broke out.
event:日本对美英宣战.old: Japan declares war on the United States and Britain

event:日本扶植“缅甸国”.note: Backed by Japan, Ba Maw proclaimed Burma's “independence” and declared war on Britain and the United States, and a Japan–Burma treaty of alliance was signed the same day. Aung San became Minister of Defence, and his Burma National Army later became the main force of the anti-Japanese uprising.
event:日本扶植“缅甸国”.old: Japan sets up the “State of Burma”

event:日本扶植菲律宾傀儡政府.note: Japan installed Laurel as president of the puppet “Republic of the Philippines”, which concluded a treaty of alliance with Japan the same day. Neither the anti-Japanese guerrillas on the islands nor the Commonwealth government in exile in the United States recognized it.
event:日本扶植菲律宾傀儡政府.old: Japan sets up a Philippine puppet government

event:日汪密约.note: The Wang Jingwei clique and the Japanese signed the Outline for Adjusting New Japan–China Relations in Shanghai, selling out a great deal of national sovereignty; in January the following year Gao Zongwu and Tao Xisheng made the full text public in Hong Kong.

event:日泰同盟.note: On 8 December Japanese troops landed at Singora and Pattani and passed through Bangkok; Thai forces resisted for a few hours before a ceasefire. On the 21st Luang Phibun concluded a treaty of alliance with Japan, and in January 1942 Thailand declared war on Britain and the United States; Seni Pramoj, the minister in Washington, refused to deliver the declaration of war and organized the “Free Thai” movement.

event:日满议定书.note: Japan formally “recognized” Puppet Manchukuo; Puppet Manchukuo confirmed all Japan's rights and interests in the Northeast and allowed Japanese troops to be stationed there, and the commander of the Kwantung Army doubled as ambassador to “Manchukuo”.

event:日苏基本条约.note: On 20 January Japan and the Soviet Union signed the Basic Convention in Beijing and established diplomatic relations; Japan recognized the Soviet Union and in May withdrew from northern Sakhalin, in exchange for oil and coal concessions in northern Sakhalin.

event:旧金山对日和约.mod: Tokyo, Japan (signed in San Francisco, United States)
event:旧金山对日和约.note: Shutting China out, the United States rounded up 48 countries to sign a one-sided peace treaty with Japan in San Francisco. Japan renounced Korea, Taiwan, Penghu, the Kurils, southern Sakhalin and other territories, and the Ryukyu and Bonin Islands were placed under US administration. China was excluded; the government of the People's Republic of China declared that it would not recognize the treaty, and the Soviet Union refused to sign. The US–Japan Security Treaty was signed the same day, and US forces remained stationed in Japan.
event:旧金山对日和约.old: San Francisco Peace Treaty with Japan

event:昂山遇刺.note: Gunmen sent by the former premier U Saw burst into a meeting of the Executive Council and killed Aung San, aged only 32, and six ministers. U Nu took his place, and Burma became independent half a year later.

event:昌都地区人民解放委员会.note: Formed after the liberation of Qamdo from 18th Army cadres and members of the Qamdo religious and secular upper strata such as Pagbalha Geleg Namgyai, it was directly under the Central People's Government and not subject to the Kashag; in 1956 it was brought, together with the Kashag and the Panchen Kampus Assembly, into the Preparatory Committee for the Xizang Autonomous Region.

event:明号作战.note: Fearing that the French colonial army would support an Allied landing, the Japanese staged a sudden coup on 9 March, disarming and interning French troops and officials overnight; French troops who resisted at Lạng Sơn and elsewhere were massacred, and some French forces retreated into Yunnan. Japan then backed the “independence” of Vietnam, Cambodia and Luang Prabang.

event:明治天皇逝世.note: Emperor Meiji died; Emperor Taishō ascended the throne and the era name was changed. That winter the First Movement to Protect Constitutional Government arose; the following year the Katsura Tarō cabinet fell, and party politics gradually took hold.

event:晋察冀边区政府成立.note: The Shanxi-Chahar-Hebei Congress of Military, Government and People's Representatives at Fuping elected the Border Region Provisional Administrative Committee, which was recognized by the Nationalist Government: the first unified anti-Japanese democratic government behind enemy lines.

event:晋西事变.note: Yan Xishan launched the Western Shanxi Incident, ordering his old army to attack the Death-Defying Corps of the Shanxi New Army; supported by the Eighth Route Army, the New Army struck back, northwestern Shanxi became an anti-Japanese base area, Yan Xishan fell back to southwestern Shanxi, and the “Sacrifice League” system collapsed.

event:暹罗改国名泰国.note: Luang Phibun promoted “state-ism”, replacing “Siam” with “land of the Thai”, and advocated the recovery of lost territories and Pan-Thaiism. The name reverted to Siam in September 1945 and was changed again to Thailand in May 1949.

event:暹罗立宪革命.note: The People's Party, formed by young military officers and civil officials who had studied in France, including Pridi Banomyong and Luang Phibun, staged a coup, forcing King Prajadhipok to accept a constitution and ending absolute monarchy. The king abdicated in 1935.

event:曹锟贿选.note: In June the Zhili Clique drove out Li Yuanhong and bought members of parliament at 5,000 yuan a vote; on 5 October Cao Kun was elected President, and on the 10th he took office and promulgated the Constitution of the Republic of China. Public opinion was outraged, and Sun Yat-sen, Lu Yongxiang and Zhang Zuolin formed an anti-Zhili triangular alliance.

event:曼哈顿叛乱.note: Young Thai naval officers seized Prime Minister Luang Phibun at the ceremony for the handover of the dredger Manhattan, a gift from the United States; the army and air force struck back, Luang Phibun escaped by swimming amid the gunfire, and the revolt was put down within three days. The navy's power never recovered.

event:朝鲜停战协定.note: Clark, Commander-in-Chief of the “UN Command”, Kim Il Sung, Supreme Commander of the Korean People's Army, and Peng Dehuai, Commander of the Chinese People's Volunteers, each signed the Armistice Agreement, which took effect at 10 p.m. that night; the War to Resist US Aggression and Aid Korea ended in victory. The actual line of contact became the military demarcation line, with each side pulling back 2 km to create a demilitarized zone; South Korea did not sign.

event:朝鲜内战爆发.note: Before dawn the Korean People's Army advanced south along the whole length of the 38th parallel, and the Korean civil war broke out. The United States manipulated the UN Security Council into passing resolutions in the absence of the Soviet Union, promptly intervened militarily in Korea, and sent the Seventh Fleet to intrude into the Taiwan Strait.
event:朝鲜内战爆发.old: Outbreak of the Korean civil war

event:朝鲜南部受降.note: The day after landing at Incheon, the US XXIV Corps accepted the Japanese surrender at the Government-General of Korea and lowered the Hinomaru flag; north of the 38th parallel, Soviet troops had already reached Pyongyang in late August.

event:朝鲜民主主义人民共和国成立.note: After the elections to the Supreme People's Assembly in August, the founding of the state was proclaimed on 9 September, with Kim Il Sung as premier; Soviet troops withdrew by the end of the year, and the Korean Peninsula was formally divided between two regimes.
event:朝鲜民主主义人民共和国成立.old: Democratic People's Republic of Korea established

event:木黄会师.note: On its Western March, the Red Sixth Army Group joined He Long's and Guan Xiangying's Red Third Army at Muhuang; the Red Third Army resumed its designation as the Red Second Army Group, and the two army groups then advanced east into western Hunan, opening up the Hunan-Hubei-Sichuan-Guizhou Base Area.

event:李大钊就义.note: On 6 April the Fengtian warlord Zhang Zuolin sent troops and police to raid the former barracks of the Soviet embassy, arresting Li Dazhao, one of the founders of the CPC, and others, who were put to death on the 28th. Li Dazhao died a heroic martyr, and the CPC's northern organization was badly damaged.

event:李闻惨案.note: Li Gongpu and Wen Yiduo of the China Democratic League were assassinated one after the other in Kunming by KMT secret agents; public opinion was shaken, and relations between the democratic parties and the KMT government deteriorated sharply.
event:李闻惨案.old: Assassinations of Li Gongpu and Wen Yiduo

event:李顿报告书.note: The League of Nations Commission of Enquiry signed its report in Beiping and published it in Geneva. It found that the September 18 Incident was not Japanese self-defence and that Puppet Manchukuo did not arise from the will of the people, yet it proposed “autonomy” for the Northeast, in effect favouring Japan. When the League Assembly adopted the report the following February, Japan withdrew from the League.

event:杜立特空袭.note: Lieutenant Colonel Doolittle led sixteen B-25s off the aircraft carrier Hornet; after bombing Tokyo, Nagoya, Kobe and other places they flew on to make forced landings in the Zhejiang area of China. Japan was shaken; it resolved to attack Midway and launched the Battle of Zhejiang–Jiangxi in retaliation.

event:杨增新遇刺.note: Yang Zengxin, who had ruled Xinjiang for seventeen years, changed to the Nationalist flag on 1 July and was assassinated by Fan Yaonan at a banquet on the 7th; Jin Shuren put down the revolt and succeeded him as provincial chairman.

event:杨靖宇殉国.note: Yang Jingyu, commander-in-chief of the First Route Army of the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army, fought Japanese and puppet troops single-handed at Sandaowaizi in Mengjiang and died a hero's death for his country; when the Japanese cut open his stomach they found only grass roots and cotton wadding. Mengjiang County was later renamed Jingyu County.
event:杨靖宇殉国.old: Yang Jingyu dies for his country

event:板门店谈判.note: On 25 October the talks resumed at Panmunjom, southeast of Kaesong, and in November agreement was reached on taking the actual line of contact as the demarcation line; the talks then deadlocked for a year and a half over the repatriation of prisoners of war, with repeated adjournments.

event:林芽椰蒂协定.note: The Dutch and Indonesian sides initialled the agreement near Cirebon: the Netherlands recognized the Republic's de facto authority over Java, Sumatra and Madura, and the two sides agreed to form a United States of Indonesia by 1949. It was formally signed in March 1947; in July the Netherlands tore up the agreement and launched an offensive.

event:柬埔寨独立.note: King Sihanouk left for Bangkok and Siem Reap, pressing France with his “Royal Crusade for Independence”; the French gradually handed over judicial, police and military command powers, and at a handover ceremony in Phnom Penh on 9 November Cambodia became fully independent.

event:格尼遇刺.note: Gurney, the British High Commissioner in Malaya, was killed in a Malayan Communist Party ambush on his way to the hill resort of Fraser's Hill. The next year Templer took charge of both military and civil affairs and pursued the “New Villages” and “hearts and minds” policies, and the Malayan Communist Party was gradually driven deep into the mountains.

event:武昌起义.note: The Engineer Battalion of the Hubei New Army, led by the revolutionary societies the Literary Society and the Progressive Association, rose first and took the viceroy's yamen in a single night; the next day the Hubei Military Government was set up, with Li Yuanhong as military governor. Thus broke out the 1911 Revolution.

event:段祺瑞临时执政.note: The Fengtian Clique and the Guominjun jointly brought Duan Qirui to Beijing as Provisional Chief Executive of the Republic of China, with neither president nor premier; his government wavered between the Fengtian Clique and the Guominjun until he fled in April 1926.
event:段祺瑞临时执政.old: Duan Qirui becomes Provisional Chief Executive

event:毛泽东赴重庆谈判.note: Invited by Chiang Kai-shek in three telegrams, Mao Zedong, striving for peace, flew to Chongqing accompanied by Hurley and Zhang Zhizhong and negotiated with the KMT for more than forty days, signing the Double Tenth Agreement on 10 October.
event:毛泽东赴重庆谈判.old: Mao Zedong goes to Chongqing for negotiations

event:永坪会师.note: The Red 25th Army, arriving on its Long March, reached Yongping and joined the Red 26th and 27th Armies of northern Shaanxi; together they were reorganized as the Red 15th Army Group, with Xu Haidong as commander and Liu Zhidan as deputy commander.

event:江淮大水.note: Months of torrential rain over the Yangtze and Huai river basins burst the dykes; the three cities of Wuhan were under water for more than a month, eight provinces were stricken and tens of millions of people affected—one of the worst floods in twentieth-century China.

event:江苏独立.note: Governor Cheng Dequan declared independence at Suzhou, having a few eave tiles knocked off his yamen to signal “revolution”. Officials of the old regime “came over” one after another, and the southeast as a whole swung to the side of the revolution.

event:汤山事件.note: Hu Hanmin, president of the Legislative Yuan, opposed Chiang Kai-shek's plan to draw up a provisional constitution and was placed under house arrest at Tangshan in Nanjing; the Guangdong Clique, the Guangxi Clique and KMT elders rose against Chiang, leading to the Nanjing–Guangzhou split.

event:汪伪国民政府成立.note: Under the name of “returning the capital”, Wang Jingwei set up the Puppet Nationalist Government in Nanjing, into which the Puppet Reformed Government was merged; it kept the Blue Sky, White Sun flag but added a yellow triangular pennant to distinguish it.
event:汪伪国民政府成立.old: Wang Jingwei Puppet Nationalist Government established

event:汪伪政权解体.note: Chen Gongbo announced the dissolution of the Wang Jingwei Puppet Nationalist Government and set up a “Nanjing Provisional Political Affairs Committee” in its place; he soon fled to Japan and was later extradited and executed. The Puppet North China Political Council and the Puppet Mengjiang regime collapsed at the same time.
event:汪伪政权解体.old: Collapse of the Wang Jingwei Puppet Regime

event:汪精卫出逃投敌.note: KMT Deputy Director-General Wang Jingwei left Chongqing and fled via Kunming to Hà Nội; on the 29th he issued the Yan Telegram endorsing the Konoe Statement, openly defecting to the enemy, and in January the following year he was expelled from the KMT.
event:汪精卫出逃投敌.old: Wang Jingwei flees and defects to the enemy

event:汪精卫病死.note: When an old wound flared up, Wang Jingwei went to Japan for treatment and died at Nagoya Imperial University Hospital. Chen Gongbo succeeded him as acting chairman of the Wang Jingwei Puppet Nationalist Government.

event:沙俄“保护”乌梁海.note: The Tsar approved placing the banners of Uriankhai under Russian “protection”, establishing the Uriankhai Krai and building the town of Belotsarsk at present-day Kyzyl, in effect annexing the region. The Beijing Government protested but was powerless to stop it.

event:沙特攻取哈萨.note: Taking advantage of the Ottomans' entanglement in the Balkan Wars, Ibn Saud made a night attack on Hofuf, drove out the Ottoman garrison and took Hasa on the Persian Gulf, giving Nejd an outlet to the sea.

event:沙特阿拉伯王国成立.note: Ibn Saud merged Hejaz and Nejd and named the state the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. In 1938 a commercial oilfield was discovered at Dhahran, worked under concession by the Standard Oil Company of California.

event:河南大饥荒.note: Henan suffered years of drought and locusts, yet the KMT government continued to levy grain in kind at the full quota; famine spread to more than 100 counties, millions starved to death, and three million people fled to Shaanxi. The Ta Kung Pao was suspended for three days for reporting it, and the reports of the American journalist Theodore White drew international attention.

event:法军撤出三角洲南部.note: After the fall of Điện Biên Phủ, French forces abandoned Phát Diệm, Nam Định and other places in the southern Red River Delta in Operation Auvergne and pulled back into the Hà Nội–Hải Phòng corridor; large numbers of Catholics moved north with them to Hải Phòng and Hà Nội.
event:法军撤出三角洲南部.old: French withdraw from the southern Delta

event:法属印度事实移交.note: After Indo-French negotiations, elected representatives of Pondichéry and the other territories voted at Kizhoor on 18 October in favour of merger with India; on 1 November the four territories of Pondichéry, Karikal, Mahé and Yanaon were transferred de facto, while the de jure cession was not completed until 1962.
event:法属印度事实移交.old: De facto transfer of French India

event:法币改革.note: The Nationalist Government nationalized silver and made the notes of three banks—the Central Bank of China, the Bank of China and the Bank of Communications (later joined by the Farmers Bank of China)—the legal tender, or fabi, pegged to sterling and the US dollar, unifying the national currency.

event:法越初步协定.note: Hồ Chí Minh signed an agreement with the French representative Sainteny: France recognized the Democratic Republic of Vietnam as a “free state” within the French Union, and the Vietnamese side agreed to let 15,000 French troops enter northern Vietnam to relieve the Chinese troops, to be withdrawn within five years. The status of Cochinchina was left to a referendum; the negotiations later broke down.

event:洛川会议.note: An enlarged meeting of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee laid down the line of a total war of resistance, decided to wage mountain guerrilla warfare independently behind enemy lines, and adopted the Ten-Point Programme for Resisting Japan and Saving the Nation.

event:洛桑条约.note: Turkey and the Allies signed the treaty at Lausanne, superseding the Treaty of Sèvres: Turkey recovered Eastern Thrace and the whole of Anatolia, consular jurisdiction was abolished, the Straits were demilitarized, and the Mosul question was left for later. Allied troops left Istanbul in October.

event:济南惨案.note: On the pretext of protecting its nationals, Japanese imperialism sent troops into Shandong to obstruct the Northern Expedition. From 3 May they massacred Chinese soldiers and civilians, brutally murdering the negotiator Cai Gongshi, and on the 11th stormed the city of Jinan; thousands of soldiers and civilians died. Japanese troops occupied Jinan until May 1929.

event:济州四三事件.note: The Jeju organization of the Workers' Party of South Korea launched an armed uprising against separate elections in the south; the troops and police of the Syngman Rhee authorities and right-wing youth groups waged a long “punitive campaign”, killing islanders indiscriminately, and by 1954 about 30,000 people had died.

event:海陆丰苏维埃.note: Peng Pai led the peasants of Haifeng and Lufeng in their third armed uprising, and in November soviet governments were set up in the two counties, among the earliest county-level soviet regimes in the country; they were overrun by the Guangdong Army at the end of February 1928.

event:淞沪停战协定.note: Signed by the Nationalist Government and Japan under British, American, French and Italian mediation. Japanese troops withdrew to the International Settlement and the extra-settlement roads area, but Chinese troops were barred from the area between Shanghai and the Suzhou–Kunshan line, and the 19th Route Army was transferred to Fujian.

event:清帝退位.note: Empress Dowager Longyu issued the abdication edict in the name of the Xuantong Emperor, granting Yuan Shikai full powers to organize a provisional republican government; the Qing imperial house received the Articles of Favourable Treatment. Qing rule came to an end, and with it the feudal autocratic monarchy of more than 2,000 years.

event:湖南和平起义.note: Hunan Provincial Chairman Cheng Qian and Chen Mingren, commander of the 1st Army Group, issued a circular telegram at Changsha announcing their uprising and their break with the KMT government; the next day the Fourth Field Army entered the city, and Changsha was peacefully liberated.

event:湖南自治.note: After expelling Zhang Jingyao, Tan Yankai called by circular telegram for “Hunan ruled by Hunanese” and proclaimed Hunan self-government; his successor Zhao Hengti championed a federation of self-governing provinces and on 1 January 1922 promulgated the Hunan Provincial Constitution, the first provincial constitution of the Republic, and Hunan stood on its own between North and South.

event:滇缅公路通车.note: Running from Kunming to Wanding to link with the railway at Lashio in Burma, the road was built in nine months with crude tools by labourers of all ethnic groups in western Yunnan, and became China's most important international route after the coast was blockaded.

event:滦州兵谏.note: Zhang Shaozeng, commander of the 20th Division, and others jointly telegraphed the throne a twelve-article political programme, demanding the convening of a parliament, the drafting of a constitution and a ban on members of the imperial clan serving as ministers of state. The Qing court was forced to promulgate the Nineteen Articles on 3 November.

event:炸断惠通桥.note: Pursuing the routed Chinese Expeditionary Force along the Burma Road, the Japanese reached the Nu River; Chinese engineers blew up the Huitong Bridge as the Japanese vanguard was crossing, and Song Xilian's forces then arrived to hold the east bank, so that the Japanese could not cross to the east. For the next two years Chinese and Japanese forces faced each other across the Nu River.

event:犹太自治州设立.note: The Soviet Union set up the Jewish Autonomous Oblast on the left bank of the Heilong River, centred on Birobidzhan, with the aims both of settling Jewish migrants and of populating the Sino-Soviet border region.

event:狼牙山五壮士.note: During the Shanxi-Chahar-Hebei autumn counter-“mopping-up” campaign, five soldiers of the 6th Squad, 7th Company, of the Eighth Route Army's 1st Sub-district covered the withdrawal of the main force and the local people, luring the Japanese onto a dead end on Langya Mountain; when their ammunition ran out they leapt heroically from the cliff. Three died, and two survived when they were caught in tree branches.

event:班禅返藏.note: The 10th Panchen Erdeni travelled from Qinghai via Nagqu and reached Lhasa in April; after meeting the Dalai Lama he returned in June to Tashilhunpo Monastery in Xigaze, and the Panchen Kampus Assembly resumed jurisdiction over parts of Tsang.

event:瓦窑堡会议.note: A meeting of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee decided to build a broad anti-Japanese national united front and to change the “workers' and peasants' republic” into a “people's republic”, laying the groundwork for later alliance with Zhang Xueliang and Yang Hucheng and for promoting the second KMT–CPC cooperation.

event:甘地遇刺.note: On his way to evening prayers at Birla House in New Delhi, Gandhi was shot dead by the Hindu nationalist Godse.

event:甘孜会师.note: The Red Second and Sixth Army Groups reached Garze and joined the Red Fourth Front Army; on the 5th the Red Second Front Army was formed, with He Long as commander-in-chief. Zhu De and Liu Bocheng, together with He Long and Ren Bishi, pressed Zhang Guotao to go north with them.

event:白朗起义.note: Bai Lang, a peasant of Baofeng, Henan, gathered a following and rose in revolt under the banner “Support the Han, punish Yuan”; in 1914 he fought his way through five provinces—Henan, Hubei, Anhui, Shaanxi and Gansu—storming Laohekou and other towns, and was defeated around Baofeng in August. The Beiyang Army mustered troops from several provinces to suppress the uprising, which took a year to put down.

event:白沙起义.note: Unable to bear the oppression of the local KMT military and administration, the Li leader Wang Guoxing led the Li and Miao people in an uprising that drove KMT forces out of the Baisha area; he then made contact with the Qiongya Column, and the Wuzhi Mountains area gradually became an anti-Japanese base area led by the CPC.

event:百色起义.note: Deng Xiaoping and Zhang Yunyi led the 4th Battalion of the Guangxi Garrison and the Youjiang peasant forces in an uprising at Baise, founding the Red Seventh Army and the Youjiang Soviet Government and opening up the Youjiang Revolutionary Base Area.

event:皇姑屯事件.note: In a plot devised by Kōmoto Daisaku, a staff officer of the Japanese Kwantung Army, explosives were laid at Sandongqiao, where the Beijing–Fengtian and South Manchuria Railways crossed, blowing up Zhang Zuolin's special train; Zhang Zuolin was gravely wounded and died. The Kwantung Army had planned to exploit the chaos to send in troops and seize the Northeast, but was thwarted when the Fengtian side kept his death secret.

event:皖南事变.note: An anti-Communist incident engineered by the KMT diehards, it was the climax of the second anti-Communist upsurge. Ordered to move north, the headquarters of the New Fourth Army and its forces in southern Anhui, more than 9,000 men, were besieged at Maolin by seven divisions of the KMT Third War Zone, and most were killed or captured; Commander Ye Ting was detained when he went to negotiate, and Deputy Commander Xiang Ying was murdered after breaking out. The Nationalist Government announced the abolition of the New Fourth Army's designation.

event:盛世才四一二政变.note: The Naturalized Army (White Russian troops) staged a coup; Jin Shuren fled, and his chief of staff Sheng Shicai was chosen as provisional commissioner, beginning his eleven-year rule.

event:盛世才投靠国民党.note: Seeing the Soviet Union's reverses in the Soviet–German war, Sheng Shicai went over to the KMT. On 29 August Soong Mei-ling flew to Dihua, and Xinjiang submitted to the Nationalist Government; the Soviet Union then withdrew its advisers and its garrison at Hami, the KMT set up party headquarters in Xinjiang, and Sheng Shicai carried out mass arrests of the Communists working in Xinjiang. Mao Zemin and others were secretly put to death in 1943.
event:盛世才投靠国民党.old: Sheng Shicai goes over to the KMT

event:盛世才调离新疆.note: Seeing the success of the Soviet counter-offensive, Sheng Shicai sought to turn back to the Soviet Union but was rebuffed, and he carried out mass arrests of KMT personnel. The Nationalist Government transferred him to be Minister of Agriculture and Forestry; he left Dihua in September, Wu Zhongxin succeeded him as chairman of Xinjiang Province, and Sheng Shicai's eleven-year rule over Xinjiang came to an end.
event:盛世才调离新疆.old: Sheng Shicai transferred out of Xinjiang

event:直接行动日.note: The Muslim League called for “direct action” to win Pakistan; massive communal killings between Hindus and Muslims broke out in Calcutta, leaving thousands dead within days. The riots then spread to Noakhali and Bihar, and partition became a foregone conclusion.

event:省港大罢工.note: From 19 June workers in Hong Kong and Shamian struck in support of the May Thirtieth Movement; on the 23rd a procession passing Shaji was fired on and massacred by British and French forces, leaving more than fifty dead. Led by the CPC, the strike lasted sixteen months and blockaded Hong Kong, and the workers' pickets became an important force in consolidating the revolutionary regime in Guangdong.

event:礼萨汗政变.note: Reza Khan, an officer of the Cossack Division, and the journalist Seyyed Zia led more than 3,000 men into Tehran and formed a new cabinet; Reza Khan became Minister of War, then prime minister in 1923, and deposed the Qajar dynasty in 1925.

event:福州第一次沦陷.note: To blockade the mouth of the Min River, Japanese troops landed at Lianjiang and Changle and occupied Fuzhou on 21 April, withdrawing on 3 September. The Fujian provincial capital had already moved to Yong'an for the duration of the war.

event:福州第二次沦陷.note: To guard against a US landing in East China, Japanese troops occupied Fuzhou again; they withdrew on 18 May 1945, and Chinese troops recovered the city.

event:福建事变.note: Based on the 19th Route Army, Li Jishen, Chen Mingshu, Jiang Guangnai and Cai Tingkai set up the People's Revolutionary Government of the Chinese Republic in Fuzhou, abolished the Blue Sky, White Sun flag and called for resisting Japan and opposing Chiang; they had already concluded a preliminary anti-Japanese, anti-Chiang agreement with the Red Army. Two months later the government was defeated by the attack of Chiang Kai-shek's Central Army.

event:科伦坡会议.note: The prime ministers of five countries, Ceylon, India, Pakistan, Burma and Indonesia, met in Colombo and called for a ceasefire in Indochina; the Indonesian prime minister, Ali Sastroamidjojo, proposed an Asian–African conference.

event:秦土协定.note: Using the Zhangbei Incident as a pretext, Doihara Kenji forced Qin Dechun, acting chairman of Chahar Province, to sign: Song Zheyuan was dismissed, the 29th Army withdrew from northern Chahar, and eastern and northern Chahar were left to “peace preservation corps”, paving the way for the Puppet Mongol Army to enter Chahar later.

event:突袭高门.note: Enver of the Committee of Union and Progress led a band into the Grand Vizier's offices, shot the Minister of War dead and forced the Grand Vizier to resign. Thereafter the “Three Pashas”, Enver, Talaat and Djemal, ruled as a dictatorship until defeat in 1918.

event:立三“左”倾错误.note: The Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee adopted a resolution drawn up under Li Lisan that called for initial victory in one or more provinces and ordered the Red Army to attack key cities such as Changsha, Nanchang and Wuhan, giving rise to the “Left” adventurist error; it was corrected at the Third Plenary Session of the Sixth Central Committee in September.

event:竹沟事变.note: KMT diehards had local armed forces attack the New Fourth Army's rear office at Zhugou, killing more than 200 sick and wounded soldiers and family members; the CPC Central Plains Bureau then moved to eastern Anhui.

event:第一个五年计划.note: Centred on the 156 key projects built with Soviet aid, it concentrated resources on giving priority to the development of heavy industry; work began in succession at Anshan Iron and Steel, the First Automobile Works in Changchun and elsewhere. At the end of 1953 the CPC Central Committee announced the General Line for the Transition Period, and the socialist transformation of agriculture, handicrafts and capitalist industry and commerce followed.

event:第一届全国人民代表大会.note: On 20 September it adopted the Constitution of the People's Republic of China; it elected Mao Zedong Chairman of the People's Republic of China and Liu Shaoqi Chairman of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress, and Zhou Enlai became Premier of the State Council. Both the Dalai Lama and the Panchen Lama attended. The Central People's Government was thereby replaced by the State Council and the other constitutional bodies.

event:第三次反共高潮.note: Taking advantage of the dissolution of the Communist International, the KMT diehards whipped up the third anti-Communist upsurge, and Hu Zongnan moved his river-defence troops to prepare a lightning strike on the Shaanxi-Gansu-Ningxia Border Region. The CPC publicly exposed the plot and rallied public opinion, Britain and the United States also expressed concern, and Chiang Kai-shek was forced to order the attack called off.

event:第五福龙丸事件.note: The United States tested a hydrogen bomb at Bikini Atoll; the Japanese deep-sea fishing boat Lucky Dragon No. 5, outside the danger zone, was contaminated by radioactive fallout, and one of its crew died half a year later. The incident set off a movement in Japan to ban atomic and hydrogen bombs.

event:米骚动.note: Women in a fishing village in Toyama tried to stop rice from being shipped out, setting off mass struggles to seize rice across the whole country; the government sent in troops to suppress them. The Terauchi cabinet fell, and Hara Takashi formed Japan's first true party cabinet.

event:紫石英号事件.note: The British warship HMS Amethyst intruded into the PLA's river-crossing front line, exchanged fire with the crossing troops, was damaged and ran aground; trapped for a hundred days, it slipped away down the river on the night of 30 July. The history of imperialist warships running rampant on the Yangtze River thereby came to an end.

event:红军改编为八路军.note: The main Red Army forces in the Northwest were reorganized as the Eighth Route Army of the National Revolutionary Army, with Zhu De as commander-in-chief and Peng Dehuai as deputy, comprising the 115th, 120th and 129th Divisions; in September it was redesignated the 18th Army Group.
event:红军改编为八路军.old: Red Army reorganized as the Eighth Route Army

event:绒坝岔停战.note: The British Vice-Consul Teichman meddled in the Sichuan–Xizang conflict in the name of “mediation”: a ceasefire agreement was concluded at Qamdo on 19 August, and a supplementary agreement on troop withdrawal at Rongbatsa in October. The line ran roughly along the Jinsha River; Dege, Baiyu and several other counties east of the river were held by the Tibetan army, while Batang, Garze and the lands to the east went to the Sichuan Frontier.

event:绥远起义.note: Suiyuan Provincial Chairman Dong Qiwu and others, 39 in all, issued a circular telegram at Baotou announcing their uprising, and their troops were reorganized into the PLA; the “Suiyuan Way”, named alongside the “Beiping Way”, was thus realized, and Suiyuan was peacefully liberated.

event:缅甸国民军抗日起义.note: Aung San led the Burma National Army out of Rangoon on the pretext of going to the front, then turned on the Japanese and, together with the Anti-Fascist Organisation, worked with the British forces. Burma later made this day its Armed Forces Day.
event:缅甸国民军抗日起义.old: Burma National Army rises against Japan

event:缅甸独立.note: Under the 1947 Aung San–Attlee Agreement, the Union of Burma proclaimed its independence at 4.20 a.m., without joining the Commonwealth; Sao Shwe Thaik became president and U Nu prime minister.

event:编遣会议.note: The Nationalist Government summoned the heads of the army groups to discuss troop reductions; Chiang Kai-shek sought to cut the armies of the regional power-holders, and Feng, Yan and Li left the conference one after another. It ended without result and became the fuse for the wars among the new warlords.

event:罗得岛停战协定.note: Through the mediation of Acting UN Mediator Bunche, Israel signed armistice agreements in turn with Egypt (February), Lebanon (March), Jordan (April) and Syria (July), drawing what later came to be called the “Green Line”.

event:美军登陆华北.note: More than 50,000 men of the US Marine Corps' III Amphibious Corps landed at Tanggu, Qinhuangdao and Qingdao to guard ports, railways and coal mines, and used ships and aircraft to carry KMT forces north to grab territory.
event:美军登陆华北.old: US forces land in North China

event:美军观察组抵延安.note: Barrett led the US Army Observation Group (the “Dixie Mission”) by air to Yan'an; the US side thus established formal contact with the CPC for the first time, to look into the situation of the Eighth Route Army and the possibilities for cooperation.
event:美军观察组抵延安.old: US Army Observation Group arrives at Yan'an

event:美台“共同防御条约”.mod: Taipei, Taiwan (signed in Washington, DC, United States)
event:美台“共同防御条约”.note: The United States and the Taiwan authorities signed the so-called “Mutual Defense Treaty”, whose scope was limited to Taiwan and Penghu; Kinmen, Matsu and the other offshore islands were not expressly covered. The treaty took effect in March 1955 and was terminated in 1980.

event:美国第七舰队侵入台湾海峡.note: After the outbreak of the Korean civil war, Truman announced that the Seventh Fleet would prevent any attack on Taiwan and put forward the theory of the “undetermined status of Taiwan”, obstructing the Chinese people's liberation of Taiwan; the PLA's plan to attack Taiwan had to be shelved.
event:美国第七舰队侵入台湾海峡.old: US Seventh Fleet intrudes into the Taiwan Strait

event:美韩共同防御条约.mod: Seoul, South Korea (signed in Washington, DC, United States)
event:美韩共同防御条约.note: Syngman Rhee pressured the United States by refusing the armistice and by detaining and unilaterally “releasing” prisoners of war, and obtained this treaty in return: the United States pledged mutual defence and the stationing of US troops in South Korea. The treaty took effect in November 1954.

event:老挝宣布独立.note: The Lao Issara movement led by Prince Phetsarath formed a provisional government and proclaimed the independence and unity of Laos. In March–May 1946 French forces reoccupied Laos, and the government went into exile in Bangkok.

event:老挝独立.note: France and Laos signed the Treaty of Amity and Association in Paris, which recognized Laos as a fully independent sovereign state within the French Union; the French handed over their remaining powers.

event:联合国分治决议.note: The UN General Assembly adopted Resolution 181, dividing Palestine into an Arab state and a Jewish state, with Jerusalem under international administration. The Jewish Agency accepted it and the Arab side rejected it; civil war broke out the next day.

event:胡克运动受挫.note: In October 1950 Philippine government forces rounded up the Politburo of the Communist Party of the Philippines in Manila; Defence Secretary Magsaysay combined suppression with conciliation, using land resettlement to induce the Huks to surrender. Magsaysay was elected president in 1953, and on 17 May 1954 the Huk leader Taruc surrendered.

event:自卫队成立.note: Under the two defence laws, the National Police Reserve set up in 1950 (renamed the National Safety Force in 1952) was reorganized into the Ground, Maritime and Air Self-Defense Forces, under a newly established Defense Agency.

event:自由印度临时政府.note: Proclaimed by Subhas Chandra Bose in Syonan (Singapore), it commanded the Indian National Army, made up of Indian Army prisoners of war, which fought alongside the Japanese in the Battle of Imphal; Japan nominally placed the Andaman and Nicobar Islands under its administration.

event:舟山群岛解放.note: To concentrate forces for the defence of Taiwan, the KMT authorities secretly withdrew the more than 120,000-strong Zhoushan garrison to Taiwan; the PLA promptly landed, and on 19 May the Zhoushan Islands were liberated.

event:色佛尔条约.note: The sultan's government was forced to sign this predatory treaty near Paris: the Arab provinces were ceded, Eastern Thrace and the administration of Smyrna went to Greece, the Straits were placed under international control, Armenia's independence was recognized and Kurdish autonomy was promised. Ankara refused to recognize it, and the treaty never took effect.

event:花园口决堤.note: To stop the Japanese advancing west on Zhengzhou, KMT forces breached the Yellow River dyke at Huayuankou; the Yellow River changed course and took over the Huai, creating the Yellow River flooded area across Henan, Anhui and Jiangsu, where hundreds of thousands died and over ten million were affected.

event:芷江洽降.note: Imai Takeo, deputy chief of staff of the Japanese invading troops' China Expeditionary Army, flew to Zhijiang, handed over maps of Japanese troop dispositions to Xiao Yisu, chief of staff of the Chinese Army General Headquarters, and received the memorandum on the surrender. Zhijiang has since been known as the “City of Surrender Acceptance”.

event:苏军撤出东北.note: After dismantling and shipping off large quantities of industrial and mining equipment from the Northeast, Soviet troops withdrew from south to north, beginning at Shenyang; the last contingent left on 3 May, leaving troops only at Lüda. The KMT and the CPC at once contested the cities they had vacated.
event:苏军撤出东北.old: Soviet troops withdraw from Northeast China

event:苏浙军区成立.note: Su Yu led the main force of the New Fourth Army's 1st Division south across the Yangtze River and at Changxing combined with the forces of southern Jiangsu and eastern Zhejiang to form the Jiangsu-Zhejiang Military Region, preparing to support a possible Allied landing on the southeast coast; in the Tianmu Mountains area it struck back against attacks by the forces of the KMT diehard Gu Zhutong.

event:苏联对日宣战.note: Under the Yalta Agreement, the Soviet Union declared war on Japan three months after the end of the war in Europe; in the early hours of the 9th Soviet troops attacked into Northeast China. Outer Mongolia followed by declaring war on Japan on the 10th.
event:苏联对日宣战.old: Soviet Union declares war on Japan

event:英军重返香港.note: Rear Admiral Harcourt of the British Pacific Fleet led his squadron into Victoria Harbour, restoring colonial rule over Hong Kong ahead of Chinese troops, and accepted the Japanese surrender in Hong Kong on 16 September.
event:英军重返香港.old: British forces return to Hong Kong

event:英国吞并塞浦路斯.note: After the Ottoman entry into the war, Britain announced the annexation of Cyprus, which it had administered since 1878; in December it also declared Egypt a protectorate and deposed the pro-Ottoman Khedive Abbas II.

event:英国封闭滇缅公路.note: Under Japanese pressure, Britain closed the Burma Road for three months, at the same time as French Indochina halted transit, cutting China off almost entirely from overseas supplies; the road reopened in October.

event:茂物会议.note: The prime ministers of five countries, Indonesia, India, Burma, Ceylon and Pakistan, conferred at Bogor and decided to hold an Asian–African Conference in Bandung in April of the following year, inviting more than twenty countries, including the People's Republic of China.

event:茉莉芬事件.note: The Communist Party of Indonesia and left-wing troops seized power in Madiun, and Musso, just back from the Soviet Union, was named as their leader. The Hatta government sent the Siliwangi Division to suppress them and retook Madiun at the end of the month; Musso was killed, thousands died, and the Communist Party suffered a heavy blow.

event:荣县独立.note: Wu Yuzhang and Wang Tianjie of the Tongmenghui led the Comrades' Army in seizing Rongxian and declared it independent of the Qing government; it was the earliest revolutionary county government established in 1911.

event:荷兰迪亚建港.note: The Netherlands set up a post on Humboldt Bay on the north coast of New Guinea, named it Hollandia, and asserted its rule over the western half of New Guinea. In 1944 MacArthur set up his Southwest Pacific headquarters here.

event:莫普拉起义.note: During the Khilafat Movement, Muslim Moplah peasants in Malabar rose in revolt, attacking British government offices and Hindu landlords; the rising turned into communal conflict and was crushed by British troops, with thousands dead. More than sixty prisoners suffocated to death while being transported in a closed goods wagon.

event:菲律宾独立.note: As agreed, the United States recognized the independence of the Republic of the Philippines, with Roxas as president. At the same time the Philippines was forced to accept the Bell Trade Act, which gave Americans “parity” rights in business, and in 1947 it signed a military bases agreement; economically and militarily it remained under US control.

event:菲律宾自治邦成立.note: Under the US Tydings–McDuffie Act of 1934, the Philippines drew up a constitution and Quezon took office as President of the Commonwealth, with independence promised after a ten-year transition; foreign affairs and defence remained with the United States.

event:萨卡维攻陷喀布尔.note: Amanullah's reforms provoked revolts by tribes and clerics; in January Amanullah abdicated and fled, and the Tajik Kalakani broke into Kabul and proclaimed himself emir. In October Nadir Khan captured Kabul and took the throne.

event:萨耶山起义.note: Saya San, a former monk, proclaimed himself “Galon King” and led peasants against the colonial authorities' capitation tax; the rising spread to many districts of Lower Burma. The British brought in Indian troops to suppress it; Saya San was captured in August 1931 and executed in November.

event:蒋介石“引退”.note: Chiang Kai-shek announced his “retirement” and returned to Xikou in Fenghua; Li Zongren, as vice-president, acted as president and sought peace talks with the CPC. As Director-General of the KMT, Chiang still controlled military and political affairs and Taiwan from behind the scenes.

event:蒋介石下野.note: After the setback at Xuzhou, under pressure from both the Guangxi Clique and the Wuhan side, Chiang Kai-shek resigned as commander-in-chief by circular telegram, returned to Fenghua and then went to Japan; Sun Chuanfang seized the chance to cross the Yangtze River, leading to the Battle of Longtan.

event:蒋介石任国民政府主席.note: Lin Sen, Chairman of the Nationalist Government, was injured in a car accident in May and died on 1 August; in September the Eleventh Plenary Session of the Fifth KMT Central Executive Committee chose Chiang Kai-shek to succeed him and amended the Organic Law to give the chairman real power, concentrating supreme party, government and military power in his hands.
event:蒋介石任国民政府主席.old: Chiang Kai-shek becomes Chairman of the Nationalist Government

event:蒙古人民政府成立.note: The Soviet Russian Red Army and Sükhbaatar's Mongolian People's Army entered Urga on 6 July, and on the 11th the Mongolian People's Government was set up, keeping the Bogd Khan as a limited monarch; Outer Mongolia declared “independence” once again. Ungern was captured in August and executed in September. From then on Outer Mongolia was beyond the control of the Chinese government.

event:蒙德罗斯停战.note: Ottoman representatives signed aboard the British warship Agamemnon: the Straits were to be opened, and the Allies gained the right to occupy any strategic point. The Ottoman Empire left the First World War, and the “Three Pashas” fled.

event:蒙政会成立.mod: Bailingmiao, Darhan Muminggan United Banner, Inner Mongolia
event:蒙政会成立.note: The Nationalist Government approved the establishment of the Mongolian Local Autonomy Political Council, with Prince Yun as chairman and Prince De as secretary-general; the so-called “high degree of autonomy” advocated by Prince De received nominal recognition.
event:蒙政会成立.old: Mongolian Local Autonomy Political Council established

event:行宪国民大会.note: The KMT convened the First National Assembly, which elected Chiang Kai-shek president and Li Zongren vice-president and adopted the Temporary Provisions for the Period of Mobilization for the Suppression of Rebellion, granting the president emergency powers.
event:行宪国民大会.old: First National Assembly under the Constitution

event:袁世凯之死.note: Yuan Shikai died amid the condemnation of the whole nation. Li Yuanhong succeeded him as President and Duan Qirui controlled the cabinet. Having lost their common master, the Beiyang warlords split into cliques, and China sank into fragmentation and fighting among the warlords.

event:袁世凯复辟帝制.note: In August Yang Du and others founded the Society to Plan for Stability to promote monarchy; in December the Council of State “acclaimed” Yuan, and on the 12th Yuan Shikai accepted the throne, designating 1916 as “Hongxian 1”. With the National Protection War breaking out and Beiyang generals turning away from him, Yuan Shikai was forced to abolish the monarchy on 22 March.

event:袁世凯当选正式大总统.note: With parliament surrounded by a “citizens' corps”, it elected Yuan Shikai formal President. In November Yuan ordered the Kuomintang dissolved and its members' parliamentary credentials confiscated; left without a quorum, parliament was suspended in January 1914.

event:西南联合大学成立.note: Peking University, Tsinghua University and Nankai University first combined as a temporary university in Changsha, then moved west on foot to Kunming, where they were renamed National Southwestern Associated University; they returned to their home campuses in 1946.

event:西卜条约.note: Through the mediation of the British Political Agent in Muscat, the sultan concluded an agreement with the Ibadi tribes of the interior: the sultan would not interfere in the affairs of the interior, and the Imamate became autonomous in practice.

event:西姆拉会议.note: Britain engineered a tripartite conference of China, Britain and the Xizang local authorities in an attempt to split Xizang from China, proposing a division into “Inner Xizang” and “Outer Xizang”. The Chinese representative Chen Yifan was forced to initial the draft in April, but was at once repudiated by the Beijing Government; the British and Xizang sides secretly exchanged notes to concoct the illegal “McMahon Line”, which the Chinese government never recognized.

event:西安事变.note: To press Chiang into resisting Japan, Zhang Xueliang and Yang Hucheng staged a military remonstrance, detaining Chiang Kai-shek and demanding by circular telegram an end to the civil war and united resistance against Japan. In Nanjing the advocates of a punitive expedition and those of a peaceful solution were at a standoff; the CPC called for a peaceful settlement and sent Zhou Enlai and others to Xi'an to negotiate. Chiang Kai-shek was forced to accept the demands to stop the civil war and unite with the CPC against Japan, and was released on the 25th; Zhang Xueliang escorted him back to Nanjing and was then detained. The peaceful settlement of the Xi'an Incident became the pivot of the change in the national situation.

event:西山会议.note: Zou Lu, Xie Chi, Lin Sen and other right-wingers of the KMT met before Sun Yat-sen's coffin in the Western Hills outside Beijing; opposing alliance with Soviet Russia and cooperation with the Communists, they declared the Communists expelled from the party and Borodin dismissed, and set up a separate Central Committee in Shanghai, forming the Western Hills Group and splitting the KMT.

event:西康建省.note: The Xikang provincial government was set up at Kangding with Liu Wenhui as chairman, governing the Kang, Ya and Ning areas; the lands west of the Jinsha River were nominally included as well.

event:西藏代表团新德里接触.note: Shakabpa and other members of the Kashag delegation held contacts in New Delhi with Yuan Zhongxian, the Chinese ambassador to India, but reached no agreement; after the Qamdo Campaign the Kashag sent Ngapoi Ngawang Jigme to Beijing instead, and the 17-Article Agreement was signed the following year.
event:西藏代表团新德里接触.old: Xizang delegation's contacts in New Delhi

event:谢赫·阿卜杜拉被捕.note: Sheikh Abdullah, Prime Minister of Jammu and Kashmir, who leaned towards autonomy and had grown distant from New Delhi, was dismissed and arrested by the head of state, Karan Singh, and Bakshi Ghulam Mohammad succeeded him; in February 1954 the state's Constituent Assembly ratified accession to India.

event:贝尔福宣言.note: British Foreign Secretary Balfour wrote to Lord Rothschild expressing support for the establishment in Palestine of a “national home” for the Jewish people, provided that nothing be done to prejudice the civil and religious rights of the existing non-Jewish communities there. It was later written into the Mandate.

event:赛克斯—皮科协定.note: Britain and France secretly carved up the Ottoman Empire's Asian territories: coastal Syria and Cilicia were to go to France, Baghdad and Basra to Britain, Palestine was to be under international administration, and Arab states within British and French spheres of influence were to be set up in the interior. Soviet Russia made the agreement public in 1917.

event:赫鲁晓夫访华.note: Khrushchev led a delegation to the celebrations of the fifth anniversary of National Day; the two sides agreed that Soviet troops would withdraw from the Lüshunkou naval base by the end of May 1955, that the Soviet shares in four Sino-Soviet joint-stock companies would be transferred to China, and that loans and aid projects would be increased.
