route:广东战役.note: The Fourth Field Army's 15th Army Group and the Second Field Army's 4th Army Group entered Guangdong from southern Jiangxi and launched the Guangdong Campaign in early October, liberating Shaoguan on the 7th, advancing south along the Bei River and liberating Guangzhou on the 14th; Yu Hanmou's forces withdrew to western Guangdong and Hainan.

route:新三十八师退入印度.note: On 19 April the 113th Regiment of Sun Liren's New 38th Division drove back the Japanese at Yenangyaung, relieving the encircled British 1st Burma Division. After Lashio fell the whole force retreated; Sun Liren, having turned back at Wuntho to rescue friendly forces, did not take the Yeren Mountains route but crossed the Chindwin River westward on bamboo rafts at Paungbyin on the night of 18 May, entering Imphal, India, relatively intact on the 27th; the division later became the backbone of the Chinese Army in India.

route:新疆骑兵先遣连进阿里.note: The advance company of the Xinjiang Military Region's Independent Cavalry Division (Li Disan and more than 130 others) set out from Pulu Village, Yutian, on 1 August 1950, crossed the Kunlun Mountains and entered Gerze in Ngari in September; it wintered at Zhamamangbao, cut off from supplies and ravaged by altitude sickness, and more than sixty men laid down their lives; in June 1951 it advanced west with the follow-up forces and on 3 August took up station at Gartok. The location of Zhamamangbao is approximate.
route:新疆骑兵先遣连进阿里.old: Xinjiang cavalry advance company enters Ngari

route:日军大亚湾登陆攻广州.note: To cut the supply line from Hong Kong to the interior, the Japanese 21st Army landed at Daya Bay on 12 October; Yu Hanmou's defending forces were thinly spread, and the Japanese drove on through Danshui, Huizhou and Zengcheng to occupy Guangzhou on the 21st, in less than ten days in all.
route:日军大亚湾登陆攻广州.old: Japanese land at Daya Bay and attack Guangzhou

route:日军沿平汉路南下.note: After Beiping and Tianjin fell, the First Army of the Japanese North China Area Army advanced south along the Beiping–Hankou Railway, broke through the Yongding River line in September, occupied Baoding on the 24th and Shijiazhuang on 10 October, and halted for a time on the line of the Zhang River and Anyang in early November; in February 1938 it attacked northern Henan again, occupying Xinxiang and reaching the north bank of the Yellow River.
route:日军沿平汉路南下.old: Japanese advance south along the Beiping–Hankou Railway

route:日军沿平绥路西进.note: The Japanese 5th Division attacked Nankou in early August, and Tang Enbo's forces held out stubbornly for half a month; the Kwantung Army's Chahar Expeditionary Force came south from Zhangbei and occupied Zhangjiakou on the 27th. Datong fell on 13 September, and the Japanese advanced west along the Beiping–Suiyuan Railway, occupying Guisui on 14 October and Baotou on the 17th, and set up the Puppet Mengjiang regime.
route:日军沿平绥路西进.old: Japanese advance west along the Beiping–Suiyuan Railway

route:日军沿沪宁路进攻南京.note: The Battle of Songhu lasted three months; in mid-November Chinese forces withdrew west, and the Japanese Shanghai Expeditionary Army pursued them along the Shanghai–Nanjing Railway, occupying Suzhou on the 19th and taking Wuxi and Changzhou in quick succession in late November; in December it pressed on Nanjing via Danyang and Jurong; Nanjing fell on the 13th, and the Japanese then perpetrated the Nanjing Massacre, in which more than 300,000 compatriots were killed.
route:日军沿沪宁路进攻南京.old: Japanese advance on Nanjing along the Shanghai–Nanjing Railway

route:日军沿津浦路北进.note: After Nanjing fell, the Japanese 13th Division and other units advanced north from Pukou, occupying Bengbu in early February 1938, and were stopped on the Huai River line by the forces of Yu Xuezhong and Zhang Zizhong; in May the northern and southern Japanese columns converged on Xuzhou, the southern column advancing north from Mengcheng and Suxian, and Xuzhou fell on the 19th.
route:日军沿津浦路北进.old: Japanese advance north along the Tianjin–Pukou Railway

route:日军沿津浦路南下.note: The Japanese Second Army advanced south along the Tianjin–Pukou Railway, occupied Dezhou on 3 October and paused on the north bank of the Yellow River; on 23 December it crossed the river at Jiyang, and Han Fuju abandoned Jinan and Tai'an and withdrew south. In March 1938 the Japanese drove south into southern Shandong and were checked in the two battles of Tengxian and Tai'erzhuang; in May they brought up reinforcements to encircle Xuzhou, which fell on the 19th, and the main body of the Chinese forces broke out.
route:日军沿津浦路南下.old: Japanese advance south along the Tianjin–Pukou Railway

route:日军第十军杭州湾登陆.note: On 5 November the Japanese Tenth Army landed at Jinshanwei on Hangzhou Bay, outflanking the Songhu defenders from the rear and forcing the Chinese forces to withdraw west along the whole front; it then advanced west via Jiaxing and Huzhou along the southern shore of Lake Tai, and in December came north from Lishui to attack Nanjing's Zhonghua Gate from the south.
route:日军第十军杭州湾登陆.old: Japanese Tenth Army lands at Hangzhou Bay

route:日军缅甸作战·仰光至曼德勒.note: The Japanese 15th Army crossed the border from Thailand on 20 January and occupied Moulmein on the 31st; on 23 February the British blew up the Sittang Bridge, cutting off most of their troops east of it. Rangoon fell on 8 March, and the Japanese advanced north up the Sittang valley, fighting the Chinese Expeditionary Force's 200th Division at Toungoo for twelve days, and occupied Mandalay on 1 May.
route:日军缅甸作战·仰光至曼德勒.old: Japanese Burma campaign: Rangoon to Mandalay

route:日军缅甸作战·奔袭腊戍.note: The Japanese 56th Division drove east from Toungoo into the Shan States with motorized units, racing via Loikaw and Loilem to occupy Lashio on 29 April and cut the Expeditionary Force's line of retreat; it then entered Yunnan along the Burma Road, occupying Wanding on 3 May and reaching Huitong Bridge over the Nu River on the 5th, where the defenders blew up the bridge and the Japanese were held on the west bank of the Nu.
route:日军缅甸作战·奔袭腊戍.old: Japanese Burma campaign: drive on Lashio

route:日军缅甸作战·进占密支那.note: Part of the Japanese 56th Division advanced north from Lashio via Namhkam and Bhamo, occupying Myitkyina on 8 May and blocking the Chinese Expeditionary Force's way home through northern Burma; the Fifth Army was forced to take the route through the Yeren Mountains instead.
route:日军缅甸作战·进占密支那.old: Japanese Burma campaign: occupation of Myitkyina

route:日军菲律宾作战.note: Homma Masaharu's 14th Army landed at Lingayen Gulf on 22 December and another force at Lamon Bay, attacking from north and south; MacArthur declared Manila an open city, and the Japanese entered it on 2 January 1942. US and Filipino forces withdrew to the Bataan Peninsula and surrendered on 9 April, followed by the Bataan Death March; the Corregidor fortress surrendered on 6 May.

route:日军进攻太原（东路）.note: The Japanese 20th Division advanced west from Shijiazhuang along the Zhengding–Taiyuan Railway, fighting fiercely with Sun Lianzhong's and other forces holding Niangzi Pass; in late October it broke through Niangzi Pass and drove straight on Taiyuan via Yangquan and Yuci, closing in together with the Japanese on the northern route and forcing the defenders of Xinkou to withdraw.

route:日军进攻太原（北路）.note: Itagaki Seishirō's 5th Division entered Shanxi from southern Chahar, and on 25 September was ambushed at Pingxing Pass by the Eighth Route Army's 115th Division, which won the Pingxingguan Victory; part of the Kwantung Army came south from Datong to Yanmen Pass. In October Chinese forces held the Japanese at Xinkou for more than twenty days; after Niangzi Pass fell they were attacked front and rear and withdrew south, and Taiyuan fell on 8 November.

route:日军马来亚东海岸.note: One of the first landings of the Pacific War: the Japanese Takumi Detachment landed at Kota Bharu in the early hours of 8 December, slightly before the air raid on Pearl Harbor; it then moved south along the east coast and occupied Kuantan airfield in early January 1942.
route:日军马来亚东海岸.old: Japanese advance down the east coast of Malaya

route:日军马来亚作战.note: Yamashita Tomoyuki's 25th Army landed at Singora, Pattani and Kota Bharu on 8 December and drove south along the west coast road with bicycle infantry and tanks, defeating the British Indian forces in turn at Jitra, Kampar and Slim River; it occupied Kuala Lumpur on 11 January, and on the 31st the British withdrew across the Strait of Johore; on 8 February the Japanese crossed to the island, and on the 15th the British forces in Singapore surrendered.

route:昌都战役.note: The main force of the 18th Army crossed the Jinsha River around Dege on 6–7 October, while a southern column from Batang and Qinghai cavalry from Yushu advanced separately to converge on the enemy; Qamdo was liberated on the 19th, and in late October the Governor of Qamdo, Ngapoi Ngawang Jigme, led the Tibetan army in laying down its arms, creating the conditions for the signing of the 17-Article Agreement and the peaceful liberation of Xizang the following year.

route:朝鲜人民军南下.mod: Yeoncheon – Waegwan on the Nakdong River, South Korea
route:朝鲜人民军南下.note: The Korean civil war broke out on 25 June; the Korean People's Army crossed the 38th parallel and occupied Seoul on the 28th; the United States intervened militarily, and the US Task Force Smith was defeated in its first engagement, at Osan on 5 July; Daejeon fell on the 20th, and Dean, commander of the US 24th Division, became separated during the breakout and was captured in late August. In early August the People's Army advanced to the Nakdong River line, and the “UN Command” forces fell back on the Busan Perimeter.

route:朝鲜人民军西南迂回.note: The Korean People's Army's 6th Division went south from Seoul in a wide envelopment through the west of the peninsula, occupying Jeonju around 20 July, Gwangju on the 23rd and Jinju on the 31st, and in August closed on Masan, threatening Busan from the west.

route:朱德、陈毅部湘南起义上井冈山.note: About 800 survivors of the Nanchang Uprising forces, led by Zhu De and Chen Yi, fought their way through southern Jiangxi; after reorganization they took cover in northern Guangdong under the designation of Fan Shisheng's forces; in January 1928 they took Yizhang by a ruse and launched the Southern Hunan Uprising, holding Chenzhou and Leiyang in February; in April, caught between Hunan and Guangdong forces, they withdrew east, and around the 28th joined Mao Zedong's forces at Longshi, Ninggang, forming the Fourth Army of the Workers' and Peasants' Revolutionary Army (soon renamed the Red Fourth Army).
route:朱德、陈毅部湘南起义上井冈山.old: Zhu De's and Chen Yi's forces: Southern Hunan Uprising and march to Jinggangshan

route:武汉会战·日军大别山北麓.note: The Japanese Second Army advanced west from Hefei, occupying Lu'an on 28 August; it met stubborn resistance at Fujinshan and Huangchuan in September, occupied Xinyang on 12 October and cut the Beiping–Hankou Railway, then advanced south along the line; part of the 13th Division crossed the Dabie Mountains at Xiaojieling towards Macheng. Hankou fell on 25 October.
route:武汉会战·日军大别山北麓.old: Battle of Wuhan: Japanese advance north of the Dabie Mountains

route:武汉会战·日军长江南岸.note: The Japanese 11th Army and the navy advanced west up the Yangtze, occupying Anqing on 12 June, breaking through the Madang fortress on the 26th and occupying Jiujiang on 26 July; the army then advanced west along the south bank via Ruichang and Yangxin, while another force was surrounded and badly mauled by Xue Yue's forces at Wanjialing, De'an (the Wanjialing Victory). Wuchang fell on 26 October.
route:武汉会战·日军长江南岸.old: Battle of Wuhan: Japanese advance south of the Yangtze

route:法军第 100 机动群撤出安溪.mod: An Khê, Gia Lai – Pleiku, Vietnam
route:法军第 100 机动群撤出安溪.note: Groupement Mobile 100 was ordered to abandon An Khê and withdraw west along Route 19 to Pleiku; on 24 June, the very day it set out, it was ambushed and lost most of its vehicles and guns, and the remnants reached Pleiku after hard fighting through the Mang Yang Pass.
route:法军第 100 机动群撤出安溪.old: French Groupement Mobile 100 withdraws from An Khê

route:海南岛战役.note: The Fourth Field Army's 40th and 43rd Armies, relying mainly on wooden sailing junks, first sent small units across secretly in March to join the Qiongya Column; on the night of 16 April the main force forced a crossing of the Qiongzhou Strait from the Leizhou Peninsula and landed at Cape Lingao and elsewhere; it liberated Haikou on the 23rd and reached Yulin and Sanya on 1 May; the whole of Hainan Island was liberated, and Xue Yue's forces withdrew to Taiwan.

route:渡江战役·东集团与上海战役.note: The Eastern Group crossed the Yangtze around Jiangyin on 21 April, where the garrison of the Jiangyin Fortress staged an uprising; it then advanced east along the Nanjing–Shanghai Railway and liberated Suzhou on the 27th; from 12 May it launched the Shanghai Campaign, Tang Enbo's forces withdrew via Wusong to Zhoushan and Taiwan, and Shanghai was liberated on the 27th.
route:渡江战役·东集团与上海战役.old: Yangtze River Crossing Campaign: Eastern Group and the Shanghai Campaign

route:渡江战役·中集团.note: The KMT government refused to sign the Agreement on Internal Peace; on the night of 20 April the Central Group of the Third Field Army was the first to cross the Yangtze, around Digang west of Wuhu, then advanced east via Xuancheng and Guangde to meet the Eastern Group at Wuxing, encircling the KMT forces withdrawing south from Nanjing and Wuhu; Hangzhou was liberated on 3 May.
route:渡江战役·中集团.old: Yangtze River Crossing Campaign: Central Group

route:滇西反攻·腾冲.note: Huo Kuizhang's 20th Army Group forced a crossing of the Nu River on 11 May and attacked up the Gaoligong Mountains, reaching the walls of Tengchong in late July; after fighting from house to house, it wiped out the garrison on 14 September, recovering the first county town in western Yunnan.

route:滇西反攻·龙陵至畹町.mod: Huitong Bridge, Yunnan – Mong Yu, Myanmar
route:滇西反攻·龙陵至畹町.note: Song Xilian's 11th Army Group crossed the Nu River in early June and besieged the Songshan fortress for three months, taking it on 7 September and opening the Burma Road; it took Longling on 3 November and Mangshi on the 20th, took Wanding on 20 January 1945, and joined the Chinese Army in India at Mong Yu on the 27th.
route:滇西反攻·龙陵至畹町.old: Western Yunnan counter-offensive: Longling to Wanding

route:秋收起义军上井冈山.note: Mao Zedong led the Autumn Harvest Uprising on the Hunan–Jiangxi border; from 9 September the regiments set out separately from Xiushui, Anyuan and Tonggu to attack Pingjiang, Pingxiang and Liuyang; after setbacks they assembled at Wenjiashi, Liuyang, on the 19th and turned south into the Luoxiao Mountains; on the 29th they were reorganized at Sanwan, Yongxin, reached Ninggang in October, and on the 27th went up Jinggangshan to Ciping, founding the Jinggangshan Revolutionary Base Area.
route:秋收起义军上井冈山.old: Autumn Harvest Uprising forces march to Jinggangshan

route:第三次战役（西线）.mod: Imjin River, Paju – Suwon, South Korea
route:第三次战役（西线）.note: At dusk on 31 December the CPV 13th Army Group and the Korean People's Army I Corps broke through all along the line of the Imjin River and the Hantan River; on 3 January 1951 they reached Uijeongbu, on the 4th entered Seoul and on the 5th crossed the Han River, the People's Army occupying Incheon the same day; the “UN Command” forces withdrew south, and the Volunteers reached the Suwon area around the 7th and halted the pursuit on the 8th.

route:第五军野人山撤退.note: After Myitkyina fell, Du Yuming led the Fifth Army headquarters and the New 22nd Division through the primeval forest of the Yeren Mountains in northern Burma instead; it was the rainy season, and very many died of tropical disease, hunger and flash floods; from July the survivors reached Ledo, India, one group after another; on the 200th Division's way back east, Dai Anlan died of his wounds for his country.
route:第五军野人山撤退.old: Fifth Army's retreat through the Yeren Mountains

route:第十八军进军拉萨.note: After the signing of the Agreement on Measures for the Peaceful Liberation of Xizang (the 17-Article Agreement), the main force of the 18th Army marched into Xizang, advancing west along the old post road from Qamdo via Shopado, Banbar, Lhari and Taizhao to Lhasa, crossing many passes above 5,000 metres and building the road as it marched; the advance detachment reached Lhasa first, on 9 September, and Zhang Guohua and Tan Guansan led the main force into the city on 26 October. The dates for the stages along the way can be fixed only to the month.

route:红二、六军团长征.note: He Long and Ren Bishi led the Red Second and Sixth Army Groups out from Liujiaping, Sangzhi, on 19 November 1935, first into central Hunan, then turning into eastern and western Guizhou and manoeuvring back and forth in the Wumeng Mountains; on 25–28 April 1936 they crossed the Jinsha River at Shigu, Lijiang, crossed snowy mountains by way of Zhongdian and Batang, and in July reached Garze and joined the Red Fourth Front Army, being renamed the Red Second Front Army; after going north they joined the Red First Front Army at Jiangtaibao on 22 October; with the three main forces of the Red Army joined up, the Long March ended in victory.
route:红二、六军团长征.old: Long March of the Red Second and Sixth Army Groups

p.渡沅江（沅陵东）: Crossing the Yuan River (east of Yuanling)

route:红二十五军长征.note: Wu Huanxian and Xu Haidong led the Red 25th Army, about 2,900 strong, out from Hejiachong, Luoshan, on 16 November 1934, broke out through the snow at Dushu Town and entered southern Shaanxi to build the Hubei-Henan-Shaanxi Base Area; in July 1935 it left through Fengyukou, marching west and then north via Liangdang, Tianshui and Qin'an into eastern Gansu; Wu Huanxian was killed in action at Jingchuan on 21 August, and on 15 September the army reached Yongping, the first Long March force to arrive in northern Shaanxi.
route:红二十五军长征.old: Long March of the Red 25th Army

route:红六军团西征.note: Ren Bishi, Xiao Ke and Wang Zhen led the Red Sixth Army Group to scout the way for the Central Red Army. On 7 August it broke out of the Hunan-Jiangxi Base Area and headed west, crossing the Xiang River at Jieshou, Xing'an, in early September; after entering Guizhou it was surrounded at Ganxi, Shiqian, on 7 October by KMT forces of the three provinces of Hunan, Guangxi and Guizhou, broke out in scattered groups, and on 24 October joined He Long's Red Third Army at Muhuang, Yinjiang.
route:红六军团西征.old: Western March of the Red Sixth Army Group

route:红四方面军长征.note: Abandoning the Sichuan-Shaanxi Base Area, the Red Fourth Front Army crossed the Jialing River westward at the end of March 1935, entered northwestern Sichuan via Jiangyou and Maoxian, and joined the Central Red Army at Maogong in June. Zhang Guotao, opposing the Central Committee's policy of going north, led the Left Column south from Ngawa; checked in the Battle of Baizhangguan in November, it withdrew west to Dawu, Luhuo and Garze in February 1936; after joining the Red Second and Sixth Army Groups in July it went north, reaching Huining on 9 October.
route:红四方面军长征.old: Long March of the Red Fourth Front Army

route:美军中太平洋跳岛.note: Nimitz's thrust began in the Gilbert Islands, attacking Tarawa in November 1943 and taking the Marshall Islands in February 1944; it landed on Saipan in June, and after the Battle of the Philippine Sea took Guam and Tinian, from which B-29s bombed the Japanese home islands; it attacked Peleliu in September and Iwo Jima in February 1945, and landed on Okinawa on 1 April.
route:美军中太平洋跳岛.old: US island-hopping in the Central Pacific

route:美军西南太平洋反攻.mod: Buna, Papua New Guinea – Manila, Philippines
route:美军西南太平洋反攻.note: MacArthur's thrust leapt forward stage by stage along the north coast of New Guinea, bypassing Rabaul and other strongly held Japanese bases; it landed at Hollandia in April 1944 and took Morotai in September; on 20 October it landed on Leyte, followed at once by the Battle of Leyte Gulf; on 9 January 1945 it landed at Lingayen Gulf and in February entered Manila, where street fighting went on for a month.
route:美军西南太平洋反攻.old: US counter-offensive in the Southwest Pacific

p.吕宋西岸海上: Off the west coast of Luzon

route:苏军外贝加尔方面军·坦克集团军.note: At midnight on 9 August three Soviet Red Army fronts crossed the border simultaneously, sending troops into Northeast China to fight Japan. The Transbaikal Front's 6th Guards Tank Army set out from eastern Mongolia and within two days crossed the Greater Hinggan Mountains, which the Japanese had thought impassable, entering the Songliao Plain; short of fuel, it halted for two days around Lubei waiting for fuel to be airlifted, and resumed its advance on the 15th; on the 19th airborne troops landed at Shenyang, and around the 20th ground forces entered Shenyang and Changchun.

route:苏军外贝加尔方面军·第三十九集团军.note: From the eastern tip of Mongolia the 39th Army broke in at Halun Arxan, crossed the Greater Hinggan Mountains, attacked Solun and Wangyemiao, and pushed via Taonan towards Changchun; Soviet airborne troops landed at Changchun, the capital of Puppet Manchukuo, on the 19th, and Japan's Kwantung Army was then ordered to surrender.

route:苏军远东第一方面军.note: Meretskov's 1st Far Eastern Front advanced west from Primorye, broke through the Kwantung Army's permanent fortifications around Dongning and Suifenhe, took Mudanjiang on 16 August, and then headed along the Chinese Eastern Railway towards Harbin, with part of its forces heading via Dunhua towards Jilin; on the 18th Soviet airborne troops landed at Harbin.

route:苏军远东第一方面军（趋吉林）.note: After taking Mudanjiang, part of the 1st Far Eastern Front went south down the Mudan River valley to Dunhua, then pushed west towards Jilin, joining the Soviet troops airlanded at Jilin; the Kwantung Army had already been ordered to cease fire and lay down its arms. This line shows only the general movement; the specific units and dates remain to be verified.

route:苏军远东第二方面军.note: The 2nd Far Eastern Front's 15th Army, supported by the Amur Flotilla, crossed the Heilong River from Leninskoye to take Tongjiang, then went up the Songhua River via Fujin, Jiamusi and Yilan, reaching Harbin around 20 August.

route:苏蒙联军骑兵机械化集群.note: The Soviet-Mongolian Cavalry-Mechanized Group under Pliyev crossed the Gobi southward from southeastern Mongolia, one wing heading via Duolun towards Rehe and the other closing on Zhangjiakou via Dehua and Zhangbei, where it fought fierce battles with the Japanese Mongolia Garrison Army; after the Japanese withdrew, the Eighth Route Army entered Zhangjiakou.

route:西路军西征.note: More than 21,000 men of the Red Fourth Front Army's 5th, 9th and 30th Armies crossed the Yellow River westward at Hubaokou, Jingyuan, in late October 1936, and in November were named the Western Route Army; advancing west along the Hexi Corridor, they fought bloody battles against the forces of Ma Bufang and Ma Buqing at Gulang, Yongchang, Gaotai and Nijiayingzi, and were defeated in the Qilian Mountains in March 1937; Li Xiannian led the Left Detachment of more than 400 men westward, reaching Xingxingxia in late April and going on via Hami to Dihua.
route:西路军西征.old: Western Expedition of the Western Route Army

route:越南人民军第三〇八师入上寮.mod: Điện Biên Phủ, Vietnam – north of Luang Prabang, Laos
route:越南人民军第三〇八师入上寮.note: To tie down the French reserves, Võ Nguyên Giáp sent the 308th Division south from Điện Biên Phủ down the Nam Ou in late January, sweeping away the posts along the way; in February, after closing on Luang Prabang, it returned to Điện Biên Phủ.
route:越南人民军第三〇八师入上寮.old: Vietnam People's Army 308th Division enters Upper Laos

route:越南人民军进军上寮·南乌江.mod: Điện Biên Phủ, Vietnam – outskirts of Luang Prabang, Laos
route:越南人民军进军上寮·南乌江.note: The western route of the Upper Laos Campaign: the Vietnam People's Army went south from Điện Biên Phủ down the Nam Ou valley, surrounded Muang Khoua and reached the outskirts of Luang Prabang, pulling back before the rainy season in May.
route:越南人民军进军上寮·南乌江.old: Vietnam People's Army in Upper Laos: Nam Ou valley

route:越南人民军进军上寮·桑怒至石缸平原.mod: Mộc Châu, Sơn La, Vietnam – Plain of Jars, Xiangkhouang, Laos
route:越南人民军进军上寮·桑怒至石缸平原.note: The eastern route of the Upper Laos Campaign: the Vietnam People's Army crossed the border from the Mộc Châu area in the northwest, drove out the Sam Neua garrison in mid-April and went south to the Plain of Jars, where the French airlifted in troops and built a fortified camp to hold the plain; Souphanouvong's resistance government moved into Sam Neua with the army.
route:越南人民军进军上寮·桑怒至石缸平原.old: Vietnam People's Army in Upper Laos: Sam Neua to the Plain of Jars

route:越南人民军进军中寮.mod: Mụ Giạ Pass on the Vietnam–Laos border – Thakhek, Laos
route:越南人民军进军中寮.note: Part of the Vietnam People's Army, with Lao forces, crossed the Mụ Giạ Pass westward from Quảng Bình and advanced west along Route 12; on 23 December the French and Lao forces abandoned Thakhek, and the Vietnamese forces reached the bank of the Mekong.
route:越南人民军进军中寮.old: Vietnam People's Army in Central Laos

route:陈谢兵团挺进豫西.note: Chen Geng and Xie Fuzhi led part of the Shanxi-Hebei-Shandong-Henan Field Army in forcing a crossing of the Yellow River from southern Shanxi from 22 August, entered western Henan, liberated Shanxian, Lingbao and other places and threatened Tongguan and Luoyang, deploying in the Central Plains in a triangular formation with the Liu-Deng Army and Chen Yi's and Su Yu's forces of the East China Field Army.
route:陈谢兵团挺进豫西.old: Chen-Xie Group thrusts into western Henan
